title: ‘Runner’ Review: Alan Ritchson and Owen Wilson Lend Some Personality to a Good-Enough Action Thriller
summary: Are movie stars okay? Between the recent explosion of celebrity spokesperson roles (such as Ben Affleck finally doing Aflac commercials) and a steady growth in star-driven straight-to-streaming fare, actors the general public would consider “successful” seem to be hustling for work — any work — harder than ever. Owen Wilson, for example, has recently appeared […]
content:
Are movie stars okay? Between the recent explosion of celebrity spokesperson roles (such as Ben Affleck finally doing Aflac commercials) and a steady growth in star-driven straight-to-streaming fare, actors the general public would consider “successful” seem to be hustling for work — any work — harder than ever. Owen Wilson, for example, has recently appeared in a big-budget Disney movie (“Haunted Mansion”), played a high-profile character within the Marvel Cinematic Universe, and is soon set to return to his scene-stealing role in the “Fockers” franchise. So why is he in Angel Studios’ “Runner?”

Truth be told, Scott Waugh’s action thriller, co-starring Alan Ritchson (“Reacher”), is actually pretty entertaining, with the good sense to clock in at an efficient 98 minutes. But there’s something dispiriting about the middle-tier existence of a skillful meat-and-potatoes crowdpleaser like this, which is neither polished enough to hold up against proper studio fare, nor scrappy enough to thrive as Roger Corman-style exploitation. Supported by Waugh’s muscular direction, Wilson and Ritchson work well together in a chase film whose thinly sketched premise barely sustains its wall-to-wall action sequences.

Popular on Variety

Ritchson plays Hank Malone, a “big American war hero” turned courier in Brisbane, Australia who just collected his AA coin for a year of sobriety and is teaching himself French in his late daughter’s honor. When his employer gives him a short-term job, picking up a donated liver being transported from the U.S., Hank gets more than he bargained for when the organ shows up under the arm of Ben Bishop (Wilson), a chatty messenger determined to accompany it to its final destination.

With a limited amount of time before the organ loses its viability, Ben directs Hank to drive directly to a Gold Coast hospital about an hour away, where anxious mother Kate (Leila George) awaits the liver for her sick daughter Ellie (Scarlett Crabtree). But after spotting a motorcade of black-clad vehicles creeping through city traffic after their car, Hank gathers that another party that considers the organ valuable. What he soon discovers is that the other party is led by Damian Zaldívar (Rodrigo Santoro), the ruthless son of a drug lord (Cecilia Toussaint) who also needs the liver to stay alive, and has instructed Damian to kill anyone who interferes with him obtaining it.

Starring and co-produced by Ritchson, “Runner” is really a showcase for him, a talented actor with real screen presence who hasn’t demonstrated a ton of versatility, but has been on the cusp of stardom for several years. This doesn’t feel likely to bump him up to the big leagues — it barely feels like a movie made for theaters — but the most complimentary comparison to make is that it feels like his version of “The Rundown,” Dwayne Johnson’s underappreciated 2003 star vehicle from when he was still The Rock. In both cases, the characters at least initially try to avoid violence, and harbor aspirations more personal than pummelling opponents ad nauseam. Even without a tearful backstory that parallels the circumstances of Hank’s current assignment with an almost cartoonish precision, Ritchson makes Hank likable with a performance that’s thoughtful, human and drily funny.

Opposite Ritchson in full “butterscotch stallion” mode is Wilson, testing Ben’s likability with a motor-mouthed performance he’s given a few dozen times. Whether the actor is improvising or sticking closely to the script by Miles Hubley and Tommy White, Wilson’s talent and experience maintain the charm of a character who practically talks nonstop but in other hands could simply be obnoxious. In the buddy-movie “action guy-funny guy” formula, Wilson makes Ritchson’s half of that balance a little less lopsided, enabling the audience to enjoy the duo’s frantic, noble determination to deliver the organ, even amidst chaotic violence that will likely be the reason that many see the film.

Waugh, named a 2012 Director to Watch by Variety, last helmed the dismal “Expend4bles.” He redeems himself with this project, perhaps because he’s serving the needs of only two main actors and not a smorgasbord of stars, but he’s clear in delivering what this film needs to accomplish. Sure, it’s simplistic and frequently silly, but most of the laughs are intentional, and the action is sturdy and exciting.

Even so, you feel like corners have been cut. Is this the first production in history unable to license “Spirit in the Sky”? Norman Greenbaum’s ubiquitous 1969 single isn’t the only song replaced by a cover or soundalike. The setting of Brisbane serves no purpose other than to highlight what must have been significant tax incentives. And the moving backgrounds outside the windows of every conveyance on screen needed at least one more visual effects pass. Sadly, that’s the stuff that makes all the good work done elsewhere seem chintzy or inadequate.

Perhaps ironically, the actors are clearly having fun, which can elevate even the cheapest-looking entertainment to classic status. This clunky vehicle doesn’t transcend its limitations — Wilson and Ritchson’s efforts are the duct tape holding it together — but it’s much better than anyone could have expected. It even makes you want to see them together on screen again in something a bit slicker and more sophisticated. That’s probably the opposite feeling that the film’s producers would like to elicit, but “Runner” is precisely the kind of for-hire work that proves its stars deserve better.

title: Jon Stewart Uses Nathan Fielder’s ‘You Can See Everything’ Trailer to Troll Donald Trump and His ‘Human Printer’ Aide
summary: Jon Stewart returned to “The Daily Show” desk Tuesday night and used the trailer for Nathan Fielder’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” to troll President Donald Trump and his most dedicated aide, known to some as “the human printer.” After attacking Trump for living in a “reality distortion field,” often rejecting the views […]
content:
Jon Stewart returned to “The Daily Show” desk Tuesday night and used the trailer for Nathan Fielder’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” to troll President Donald Trump and his most dedicated aide, known to some as “the human printer.”

After attacking Trump for living in a “reality distortion field,” often rejecting the views and facts of experts and journalists in favor of his own outlook, Stewart mused, “Maybe it’s just better to be the guy in ‘The Matrix,’ going, ‘Oh, this blue pill’s not so bad! That reality has steak!’ But I know too much. How do I get there? Who would give me the blue pill?”

Through a series of news clips, Stewart introduced the audience to Trump staffer Natalie Harp. She earned the nickname “the human printer” because “she follows the president everywhere with a laptop and printer, feeding him a steady stream of positive news stories,” according to one sound bite.

Popular on Variety

In another clip presented by Stewart, CNN reported that she “once jumped in the trunk of an SUV to ensure she would be able to be with the president for a court appearance.” She also, according to a TMZ sound bite, “wrote [Trump] letters that can only be described as love letters.”

“Can we even trust her?” Stewart joked. “Well, decide for yourselves. Because tonight, here on ‘The Daily Show,’ we are premiering exclusive footage. We lived with Natalie Harp and the president for a month to determine what their relationship was really like. Let’s take a quick preview.”

The show then cut to the viral “You Can See Everything” trailer, except with Trump superimposed over Fielder’s face. In the preview, Holmes says, “Why would I deceive you? There’s no — there’s no reason for me to do that.”

“You Can See Everything,” which debuted at Telluride Film Festival at a secret screening, follows Fielder and a reluctant camera crew as they capture Holmes in her house in the weeks before she reports to prison. Holmes was sentenced to more than 11 years in jail in 2022 for defrauding investors through her Theranos health startup.

Watch Stewart’s entire monologue below.

title: Jon Stewart Likens Donald Trump Aide Natalie Harp To Elizabeth Holmes In Viral ‘You Can See Everything’ Trailer
summary: Jon Stewart returned for an all-new episode of The Daily Show following a month-long hiatus. The comedian and Comedy Central host didn’t waste any time trolling Donald Trump and the chaos he’s caused over the last few weeks, like renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America. Toward the end of his opening monologue, he likened Trump […]
content:
Jon Stewart returned for an all-new episode of The Daily Show following a month-long hiatus.

The comedian and Comedy Central host didn’t waste any time trolling Donald Trump and the chaos he’s caused over the last few weeks, like renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America.

Toward the end of his opening monologue, he likened Trump aide Natalie Harp to Elizabeth Holmes following the viral trailer for the documentary You Can See Everything.

Stewart showed a clip from CNN where they displayed one of the letters she wrote Trump, in which she allegedly says, “I never want to bring you anything but you.”

The show host added, “For the sake of my own sanity, I’m going to pretend that’s referring to the dishwashing liquid.”

Watch on Deadline

Stewart did not stop there and added, “This is unbelievable. The outside world is somehow fed into this woman — a single conduit. And from there, she is the filter to all the information that is directly fed into Donald Trump’s psyche.”

This brought up the trailer for the Nathan Fielder doc, with Stewart noting it was “exclusive footage” of Trump and Harp to “determine what their relationship was really like.”

The clip superimposed Trump’s face onto Fielder’s body as Elizabeth Holmes (playing Harp), asked him, “Why would I deceive you? There’s no reason for me to do that.”

A24 premiered Fielder’s doc about Elizabeth Holmes at the Telluride Film Festival and released a clip of the film. The preview went viral for how intense Holmes looked at Fielder and how they were having an intense conversation while she rocked her baby with her foot, a revelation made when the shot went wide.

Stewart is not the only Comedy Central personality taking swipes at Trump. South Park announced it was changing its name to South America after Trump ordered Lake Ontario renamed Lake America.

Watch The Daily Show in the video below.

title: Jeff Lowell Dies: ‘John Tucker Must Die’ Writer & ‘The Crew’ Creator Was 52
summary: Veteran film and TV comedy writer Jeff Lowell died on August 24 in Virginia after a brief illness. He was 52. Lowell started his career as a sitcom writer in the mid 1990s, working on such series as The George Carlin Show, Bless This House and The Drew Carey Show. He went on to serve […]
content:
Veteran film and TV comedy writer Jeff Lowell died on August 24 in Virginia after a brief illness. He was 52.

Lowell started his career as a sitcom writer in the mid 1990s, working on such series as The George Carlin Show, Bless This House and The Drew Carey Show. He went on to serve as writer-producer on Cybil, Spin City, Sports Night, Just Shoot Me!, Inside Schwartz and hourlong comedy-drama Common Law.

In 2014, a half-hour script Lowell had originally developed three seasons prior was picked up to pilot by ABC. Titled Manhattan Love Story, the single-camera comedy starring Jake McDorman and Lio Tipton went to series which ran for one season.

Lowell continued to work steadily in television with stints on CBS’ Two and a Half Men; TV Land’s The Jim Gaffigan Show, which he executive produced; and Netflix’s The Ranch, created by 2.5 Men veterans Don Reo and Jim Patterson, on which he rose to executive producer.

Watch on Deadline

Most recently, Lowell created, executive produced and served as showrunner on the multi-camera Netflix comedy series The Crew, starring Kevin James.

Lowell made his feature debut with the screenplay for the 2006 movie John Tucker Must Die, directed by Betty Thomas. His followup was the 2008 film Over Her Dead Body, which he wrote and directed. Other feature credits include Hotel For Dogs, which Lowell co-wrote, and Kevin James’ Home Team, which he produced.

He is survived by his wife and two children.

title: Federal Film & TV Tax Credits Not A Done Deal, Adam Schiff Says; White House Involved: “Negotiations Are Ongoing”
summary: EXCLUSIVE The elusive goal is in sight but the finish line is still a way off in the race to get a federal film and TV tax incentive bill passed and signed into law by Donald Trump, California’s junior senator says.  “Over the past two years, Senator Adam Schiff has been working to build bipartisan […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE The elusive goal is in sight but the finish line is still a way off in the race to get a federal film and TV tax incentive bill passed and signed into law by Donald Trump, California’s junior senator says.

“Over the past two years, Senator Adam Schiff has been working to build bipartisan support for his federal film tax incentive legislation,” a spokesperson for the man once known as the Congressman from Hollywood told Deadline this evening.

“There is bill language, and currently, leaders in the Senate, House, and Trump administration are engaging in conversations to finalize text,” the aide added, confirming a dramatic turn of events in just the last few days.

“Negotiations are ongoing.”

Watch on Deadline

To that, the working figure on the Trump-coined Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act is a 20% tax credit. That credit could rise at least another 5% to 10% if filming occurs in rural areas or the production wealth for the same project is spread among several states, sources tell me.

Still, talks are fraught with expectations that all regions of the country will get something out of any new program. There is hope that the incentives are flexible and rich enough to bring production to states that had previously seen very little filming in their borders.

California Democrats Linda Sanchez and Laura Friedman are spearheading the effort in the House of Representatives, Deadline has confirmed. Our corporate cousin Variety earlier today first mentioned Ways and Means committee member Sanchez and ex-Rysher Entertainment executive Friedman, the successor to Schiff in Burbank, in relation to the potential legislation. Republicans Nathaniel Moran (R-TX) and Brian Jack (R-GA) are also in the mix, though the degree of their participation, even with Trump’s vehement backing of the incentive, is unclear.

“A lot of details are being worked out, what the priorities are,” a Hollywood political operative with strong industry and DC ties said today of the state of any possible legislation.

Indications are that the bulk of what is being discussed behind closed doors is based in large part of the format and execution of California’s now $750 million annual program.

Like the Golden State incentives under outgoing Governor — and likely 2028 White House candidate — Gavin Newsom, who has been advocating for a 20 – 25% federal tax credit for awhile, will allow producers and studios/streamers a menu of methods by which to redeem the incentives over a number of years — some potentially faster than others. Another big component of any federal incentive is to snag relocating productions. Series or films first made outside the country or content that had already been assured foreign credits but haven’t yet started production will be strongly encouraged to come Stateside.

It also seems some of the language circulating in draft form is lifted from suggestions put forth earlier by Paramount CEO David Ellison in private get-togethers with Congressional members. Reps for Paramount did not respond to Deadline’s request for comment or clarity on Ellison’s influence in the tax credits scheme.

What is also clear is that for Dems, the emphasis is on keeping production and jobs in the home of Hollywood and in New York. Equally crystal at this juncture is that for the GOP, which is having a midterms centric mini-convention in Dallas starting Wednesday, the key states for entertainment industry consolidation and growth are Texas and Georgia. Almost more than the Golden State, the one time home of The Walking Dead and every Marvel movie has been hit hard by big budget productions moving to overseas jurisdictions with even more lucrative incentives than the uncapped Peach State.

“Georgia is in play now in almost every election, and Republicans get that the movie industry is a strong source of jobs and pride,” the political operative stated. “It’s an easy sell, even to people who hate liberal Hollywood.”

Of course, as fickle as Trump can be, having the former Apprentice host now loudly backing his pal Jon Voight’s plan makes the shift (no pun intended) more palatable for most GOPers and their MAGA base.

At the same time, for all the hoopla the past two weeks around any federal program to increase production, bring back lost entertainment industry jobs and businesses, and fill state coffers with tax revenue, the pathway to Trump’s Oval Office desk is not so smooth — even with bipartisan backing and unexpected bedfellows.

Both chambers of the current Republican controlled Congress are set to put a “Close for the midterms” sign up on their respective doors in a matter of days. Add to that the expectation that DC will be a ghost town from October to the second week of November for the pivotal election, a lot of Republicans will be in the Lone Star state the rest of this week for the Dallas 2026 confab.

As the calendar and other political realities constrict passage of any significant federal incentive, there is also the procedural requirement that the measure go to the Joint Committee on Taxation.

Chaired by Sen. Mike Crapo (R-ID), the theoretically nonpartisan assortment of five Senate Finance Committee members and five House Ways and Means Committee members is charged with assessing what a program could cost and what it could bring into the IRS. Specifically to this matter, the Committee is tasked with looking at any and all tax credit initiatives that exceed $2 million — which the multi-billion dollar Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act will certainly surpass many times over.

So, as Hollywood sees boffo box office this summer but tens of thousand of jobs are lost in and around L.A. and worries of more layoffs from a Paramount-Warner Bros Discovery merger loom, the mantra around federal tax credits may be quite simple: Hurry up and wait, for now.

Ted Johnson contributed to this report

title: ‘DAU’ Director Ilya Khrzhanovsky Responds to Ukraine Backlash at Venice: I Wish for the Ukrainian Government to ‘Save the Country and Win This War’
summary: Dissident Russian director Ilya Khrzhanovsky, who is at the Venice Film Festival with competition title “DAU” countered claims by Ukrainian officials that the film has Russian state links and took a clear position on the ongoing war. “Look, my position about Russia-Ukrainian war has been very clear from the beginning of the war,” he said. […]
content:
Dissident Russian director Ilya Khrzhanovsky, who is at the Venice Film Festival with competition title “DAU” countered claims by Ukrainian officials that the film has Russian state links and took a clear position on the ongoing war.

“Look, my position about Russia-Ukrainian war has been very clear from the beginning of the war,” he said. “Actually even [from] before the full invasion in 2022, my position was clear. I commented many times,” Khrzhanovsky added.

“The only thing I can wish for is peace and success for the Ukrainian government to succeed in the best possible way, to save the country and to win this war,” the director continued.

Popular on Variety

Regarding his ties to Sergei Adoniev, the Russian oligarch who originally bankrolled the project, Khrzhanovsky specified that “he was the first financier,” adding: “He financed the ‘DAU’ project from 2008 to 2019 and his generous support was great and very important for the art project,” noting that. at the time Russia was not on any sanction lists. But “Over the past seven years, the project has had a completely different life,” in terms of its financing. He said.

Asked whether he was critical of the film’s lead actor Teodor Currentzis, the Greek-Russian classical conductor who has refused to explicitly criticize Vladimir Putin or Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, Khrzhanovsky said: “Look, I can criticize myself for things. And I prefer to judge myself for things and try to act and behave in a way how I feel it should be and I try to be connected to my spirit and soul and choices.” But “Some people choose what I don’t like,” he added “And I think everyone is responsible for their own choices.”

Inspired by Soviet physicists who helped develop the atomic bomb, “DAU” follows the life of the titular scientist (Lev Landau, nicknamed Dau) across four decades in the Soviet Union, from 1928 to 1968. The 3-hour-and-15-minute film compiles two decades of work from Russian-born Khrzhanovsky’s “DAU” project, which stretches across the mediums of cinema, television and art. Two films from the project have already been released, “DAU. Degeneration” (2019) and “DAU. Natasha” (2020).

The film’s inclusion in Venice’s competition caused controversy in the lead-up to the festival, with the Ukraine Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Culture as well as the Ukrainian Embassy in Italy releasing a joint statement. “At the time when Russia is continuing its war of aggression against Ukraine, systematically destroying cities, cultural heritage and national identity, offering one of the world’s most prestigious cultural platforms to a project linked to the Russian state and its networks of influence sends a deeply worrying signal,” the statement said.

In a social media post last month, Venice artistic director Alberto Barbera defended his decision to include the film in competition, saying that Khrzhanovsky is “a Russian dissident who ended up on the regime’s blacklist as a terrorist and enemy of the state — a director who, from the very beginning, has taken a stand against the Russian invasion of Ukraine.” He added that critiques are part of an “inexplicable smear campaign against a film that its accusers have evidently not even seen yet.”

Beyond political criticism, “DAU. Natasha” also sparked questions ahead of its premiere at Berlin Film Festival in 2020 about unprofessional and unsafe conditions, especially relating to the treatment of actresses and use of unsimulated violence. Khrzhanovsky and members of his cast, including lead Natalia Berezhnaya, strongly denied these claims.

Maria Nafpliotou, who stars “DAU,” struck a similar note. “There was not a script, there were only some lines and we knew who we were [what characters we were playing],” she said, describing Khrzhanovsky’s unique directorial method. “Ilya sent people into set and we had to react. It reminded me what it means to be an actor, really. I was treated with respect and kindness.”

title: Law Kar-ying, Paw Hee-ching to Topline Sri Kishore’s Cantonese Opera Drama ‘The Grand Tribute’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Hong Kong screen veterans Law Kar-ying and Paw Hee-ching have been cast to lead “The Grand Tribute,” a Cantonese opera drama written and directed by Sri Kishore, the filmmaker behind 2021’s “My Indian Boyfriend.” “My Indian Boyfriend” was billed as Hong Kong’s first mainstream romantic drama with a South Asian male lead. “The Grand Tribute” […]
content:
Hong Kong screen veterans Law Kar-ying and Paw Hee-ching have been cast to lead “The Grand Tribute,” a Cantonese opera drama written and directed by Sri Kishore, the filmmaker behind 2021’s “My Indian Boyfriend.”

“My Indian Boyfriend” was billed as Hong Kong’s first mainstream romantic drama with a South Asian male lead. “The Grand Tribute” marks a shift from that contemporary intercultural romance toward a story rooted in traditional Cantonese performing arts, and is set entirely in Hong Kong.

The story follows a Cantonese opera performer in his 70s staging one final show as a farewell gesture of love for his terminally ill wife. Law Kar-ying, an accomplished Cantonese opera performer in real life, stars opposite Paw Hee-ching, whose casting anchors the film’s central relationship in lived experience of the art form.

Popular on Variety

“I am always fascinated by the love shared between elderly couples and the way they express their affection,” Sri Kishore said. “I want to capture that essence and bond between the couple, set against the backdrop of Cantonese opera, while incorporating many humorous and fun elements into the story.”

Rather than treating Cantonese opera as a fading tradition, Sri Kishore describes it as a form capable of connecting people across generations. “Cantonese opera is a universal canvas for human emotion,” he said. “This film explores intergenerational bonds, cultural celebration, and what it means to create art as an act of love. These themes transcend language and culture.”

Sri Kishore is writing, directing and producing the project. Dai Ming Tsui serves as co-producer and Nasrul Ekram as line producer. Dhiraj Gangaraju and Vamshi Sriramoju are co-executive producers, with Shiva Gorrella, Phaneendra Prasad and Satya Mantha as associate executive producers. The production banner is Sri Kishore Film Productions Limited.

The film also features a diverse, international supporting cast that mirrors Hong Kong’s multicultural makeup, alongside its Chinese lead pair. The production is aiming for a full theatrical run alongside distribution on international streaming services, with hopes of introducing the city’s artistic heritage to global audiences.

“‘The Grand Tribute’ is about legacy – about what we leave behind. Not just for our families, but for the cultures we inherit and the ones we choose to embrace,” Sri Kishore said.

Principal photography commences in October.

title: U.K. Broadcaster Channel 4’s Plan to Cut 28% of Workforce Prompts Parliamentary Scrutiny: ‘Today’s News Will Be Deeply Worrying’
summary: Channel 4’s plans to cut over a quarter of its workforce are set to be scrutinized by a parliamentary committee. The British public service broadcaster confirmed Wednesday it planned to slash around 340 roles, equivalent to 28% of its headcount, within the next few months. The move is partly aimed at protecting the network’s already […]
content:
Channel 4’s plans to cut over a quarter of its workforce are set to be scrutinized by a parliamentary committee.

The British public service broadcaster confirmed Wednesday it planned to slash around 340 roles, equivalent to 28% of its headcount, within the next few months.

The move is partly aimed at protecting the network’s already under-pressure commissioning budgets, with a press release about the news citing “a rapidly changing media landscape, including evolving audience habits, increasing global competition, a challenging consumer environment and a volatile advertising market.”

Channel 4’s CEO Priya Dogra, who joined the broadcaster six months ago, said: “The challenges we face require a fundamental transformation in how we work.”

Popular on Variety

In response to the news, the cross-party Parliamentary media committee confirmed it planned to “question” Channel 4 over its plans.

“Today’s news will be deeply worrying for the talented and dedicated people who work at Channel 4,” said MP Caroline Dinenage, who chairs the Culture, Media and Sport committee. “I’m sure that the committee will want to question Channel 4 about today’s news and how they will work with other public service broadcasters to ensure that they remain relevant and sustainable.”

Channel 4 is publicly-owned but ad-funded, meaning that unlike fellow publicly-owned broadcaster the BBC, it receives almost no public funding and instead relies on advertising. Under previous governments there were plans to sell off the broadcaster, which caused alarm within the U.K. industry. There are currently no plans to revisit those proposals.

Between the advertising downturn and proliferation in the number of U.S.-owned streaming platforms operating in the U.K. (HBO Max launched in the territory earlier this year, joining others including Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+ and Paramount+) not to mention the rise of YouTube, it has become an increasingly difficult environment for the PSBs to operate in without backing from a larger entity. The BBC is funded by the U.K. public, Channel 5 is owned by Paramount Skydance and ITV recently confirmed its linear and streaming operations would be acquired by Comcast-owned Sky.

It has been a particularly tough time for Channel 4, which has recently been rocked by a scandal surrounding one of its most popular shows, “Married at First Sight U.K.,” and is still searching for a new director of programs, with incumbent Ian Katz set to step down next month.

“The proposals announced today are intended to secure Channel 4’s future as a trusted, independent British broadcaster,” said Channel 4 chair Geoff Cooper. “By taking action now, it can build a more sustainable and resilient organisation, maximise investment in content and strengthen its ability to deliver public value for audiences, the creative industries and the UK for the years ahead.”

title: ‘Place to Be’ Helmer Kornél Mundruczó on Directing Ellen Burstyn, Taika Waititi and a Pigeon in an Unlikely Love Story
summary: Hungarian director Kornél Mundruczó first worked with Ellen Burstyn on his 2020 drama “Pieces of a Woman,” and immediately knew he wanted to make another movie with her. “She was [on set] for two or three days only, and I loved her,” Mundruczó tells Variety over Zoom from Budapest. “Of course, I love her movies, […]
content:
Hungarian director Kornél Mundruczó first worked with Ellen Burstyn on his 2020 drama “Pieces of a Woman,” and immediately knew he wanted to make another movie with her.

“She was [on set] for two or three days only, and I loved her,” Mundruczó tells Variety over Zoom from Budapest. “Of course, I love her movies, but just to work with her was on another level. I felt I was with a master.”

The Oscar-winning star of “The Exorcist” and “Requiem for a Dream” has built her 70-year career on roles in horror films and serious dramas, but Mundruczó envisioned something different. “I always wanted to give her a love story because her body of work is rather dark, you know?” he says. “I wanted to do kind of a light movie for her, that was also something very important and special for me, because I could easily be dark as well.”

Popular on Variety

Enter “Place to Be.” Premiering at Venice on Wednesday, the movie marks Mundruczó’s first time back at the festival since “Pieces of a Woman” — which wasn’t the “real Venice experience” due to COVID-19, he says — and is particularly special since Burstyn is being honored with a Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement.

In what Mundruczó describes as an “urban road movie,” Burstyn plays Brooke, a widowed woman whose children are trying to force her into a retirement home. When a pigeon flys through her window and refuses to leave, Brooke embarks on a cross-country road trip to return the bird to its owner, meeting divorcee Nelson (Taika Waititi) along the way. The two strike up an unlikely friendship with each other and the pigeon, learning that it’s never too late to start a new chapter in life.

Mundruczó says the idea struck him when he attended a pigeon race — a historic sport where specially trained pigeons are transported to a location and then released to fly home, with the winner being the bird that returns the fastest. “It was so beautiful,” he says. “It was like something forgotten, because pigeons were so important in the past — this is a messenger bird that comes from the Bible.” He also found within the pigeon a “great metaphor” for aging stars. “Once you had that kind of importance, and your importance is not there anymore but you’re still the same quality,” the director adds.

After Burstyn was on board, the next challenge was finding an actor to play opposite the Strasberg-trained actress. “I wanted to get someone who is a very strong personality and not an actor, in a way. I needed this real quality person. And then Taika popped up in my mind,” Mundruczó says. “Taika has kind of what Robin Williams had, like this sad clown. Someone who you feel this kind of true depth and complexity on this cheerful facade.”

When Burstyn and Waititi met, it was “immediately a big love,” he adds. “They were very connected and the chemistry between them was fantastic.”

In the supporting cast, Murray Bartlett and Pamela Anderson play Burstyn’s children, with all three actually bearing a striking resemblance to one another. “I mean genetically, it’s very close,” he says. “When you see them together, you completely believe that they are family, you know?”

But perhaps the biggest star of “Place to Be” is the pigeon itself. It was supremely important to Mundruczó that the film used real birds and as little CGI as possible. Seventeen pigeons played Intruder, the name that Burstyn’s character gives to her flying friend.

“Ellen fell in love with at least five of them,” Mundruczó says with a laugh. “It was a really beautiful experience and also just tells you how close you can be with animals.”

With several scenes showcasing flocks of pigeons, Mundruczó estimates that around 1,000 birds were used in the production — which filmed in Sydney, Australia and New York — with professional pigeon handlers present on set. “Part of the story that I’m really proud of is we didn’t lose a single pigeon!” Mundruczó says.

When audiences are able to see “Place to Be,” Mundruczó hopes they come away with hope — and perhaps a newfound love for pigeons.

“From Brooke’s perspective, she wants to help this little bird, but at one point the bird helps her. And that’s true as well for Nelson’s character,” he says. “This little bird is help for both of their lives.”

title: Netflix India Chief Monika Shergill Says ‘Specificity Can Be a Strength’ as Streamer Unveils Expanded Comedy Slate (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Monika Shergill, VP, content, Netflix India, says the streamer has moved comedy from a series of individual bets to a long-term programming pillar because of how many different audience needs the genre can serve. “Comedy is deeply personal and subjective. What makes one person laugh may not work for another, so our job is to […]
content:
Monika Shergill, VP, content, Netflix India, says the streamer has moved comedy from a series of individual bets to a long-term programming pillar because of how many different audience needs the genre can serve.

“Comedy is deeply personal and subjective. What makes one person laugh may not work for another, so our job is to super-serve audiences with a wide range of voices, formats and sensibilities,” Shergill tells Variety.

Netflix India will expand its comedy offering this season with a slate spanning film, scripted series, stand-up specials and unscripted formats, kicking off with the franchise film “Dhamaal 4” and the family comedy “Chumbak.” The lineup also includes Zakir Khan’s stand-up special “Papa Yaar,” “The Great Indian Kapil Show” Season 5, Bhuvan Bam’s “Dhindora” Season 2 and a new stand-up special from Sumukhi Suresh, who joins Netflix with “Hoemonal.” The slate additionally features more episodes of Samay Raina’s “India’s Got Latent,” including a recently released exclusive episode with Varun Dhawan.

Popular on Variety

“Chumbak” comes from J.D. Majethia and Aatish Kapadia, the makers of “Khichdi” and “Sarabhai vs Sarabhai.” The multi-generational family comedy is set in a Mumbai neighborhood and follows five families whose lives are intertwined by everyday favors, opinions and mishaps. “Papa Yaar” traces how Khan comes to see his father differently over time, moving past the parent-as-authority-figure framing toward a bond built on shared history and mutual understanding.

Shergill points to the streamer’s five specials with Vir Das, including the International Emmy-winning “Landing,” alongside the returning “The Great Indian Kapil Show” and “Single Papa,” which was renewed for a second season, as evidence of that range.

One lesson from the slate so far, Shergill says, is that audiences want both familiarity and discovery at once. “One of the clearest things we’ve learned is that audiences want both comfort and surprise,” she says. She points to “The Great Indian Kapil Show” renewing itself season after season with the same cast, against the eccentric courtroom world of “Maamla Legal Hai,” as two different routes to the same result. “What connects them is emotional recognition,” she says.

Asked what she looks for in a comic voice, Shergill says Netflix weighs three things: “a distinctive point of view, a strong idea and the potential for the creative relationship to grow.” A large following, she adds, “cannot substitute for the idea.” She cites Majethia and Kapadia’s “instinctive understanding of Indian families and communities that shapes ‘Chumbak'” as an example of a voice matched to the right project.

Shergill pushes back on the notion that Indian comedy audiences are splintering into narrower segments. “Audiences aren’t dividing, they’re diversifying their own taste,” she says, noting that the same viewer might watch Kapil Sharma with family and Zakir Khan on their own, depending on mood and company. That fluidity, she says, shapes the range of the slate itself, from the dark comedy “Darlings” to the crime caper “Dhoom Dhaam” to the workplace setting of “Maamla Legal Hai” to “Super Subbu,” which she says wraps a social issue in comic packaging so it lands with viewers.

On why now, Shergill says the timing reflects several factors converging at once rather than a single trigger. “It isn’t one signal; it is the combination of several,” she says, pointing to Bam’s “Dhindora” returning for a second season, Suresh’s “Hoemonal” arriving as a new voice, and Raina’s relationship with Netflix evolving from an appearance on Kapil Sharma’s show to “India’s Got Latent” Season 2 and now an exclusive special in development.

On international reach, Shergill says Indian humor does not need to be diluted to travel abroad. “Indian humor does not have to become less Indian to travel. In fact, specificity can be a strength,” she says. Das’s run of specials, capped by “Landing’s” International Emmy win for comedy in 2023, illustrates that dynamic, according to Shergill, who adds that “global reach is an opportunity that follows the work, not a requirement that shapes it.”

Looking ahead, Shergill says the next phase of growth will come from voices and comic worlds the platform has not yet tapped. “The biggest opportunity is in the voices and comic worlds we haven’t discovered yet,” she says. “The next breakout idea may not look like anything that came before it. Our job is to stay curious enough to find it and ambitious enough to back it.”

“Comedy remains an underserved genre in entertainment, so that combination of continuity and newness is what makes this the moment to invest further,” Shergill says.

title: ‘Wicked’ & ‘Wicked: For Good’ Live-To-Film Concerts To Kick Off 2027 Tour In San Francisco & New York
summary: EXCLUSIVE: A series of live-to-film concerts of Wicked and Wicked: For Good, with film screenings accompanied by a live symphony orchestra, will officially premiere at Radio City Music Hall on January 23, 2027, with a special preview set for January 16 in San Francisco. The first event will be Wicked: Part One In Concert. The […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: A series of live-to-film concerts of Wicked and Wicked: For Good, with film screenings accompanied by a live symphony orchestra, will officially premiere at Radio City Music Hall on January 23, 2027, with a special preview set for January 16 in San Francisco.

The first event will be Wicked: Part One In Concert.

The concerts are a collaboration between Universal Film and Universal Destinations & Experiences. See the announced tour dates below.

The “concert experiences” will feature the films projected on an HD screen while orchestras perform Stephen Schwartz’s songs and Schwartz’s and John Powell’s underscore live-to-picture. Universal Film has partnered with Justin Hurwitz’s company Hurwitz Concerts, which has toured La La Land in Concert and Whiplash in Concert since 2023, and which now makes its entry into producing concerts of films not scored by Hurwitz.

“When I’ve seen live concerts of film scores,” said Schwartz in a statement, “I’ve always found it an amazing experience, so I’m delighted that the Wicked movies are now becoming film concerts, especially under the expert direction of Oscar-winner Justin Hurwitz and his talented team.”

Watch on Deadline

“I absolutely love the live-to-film format and think the Wicked films are so perfect for it,” said Hurwitz. “It’s an honor for me to help bring Stephen Schwartz’s masterpiece musical and John Powell’s brilliant, cinematic underscore to concert venues around the world.”

Directed by Jon M. Chu, Wicked and Wicked: For Good star Cynthia Erivo as Elphaba and Ariana Grande as Glinda, alongside Jonathan Bailey, Michelle Yeoh, Jeff Goldblum, Ethan Slater, Bowen Yang, and Marissa Bode. Songs include “Defying Gravity,” “Popular,” and “For Good.”

The announced tour dates include the San Francisco preview, the Radio City premiere and Chicago (January 30); Mexico City (March 6); Guadalajara (April 17); Monterrey (April 24); Toronto (May 29); Montréal (July 17); and Vancouver (July 24).

More dates and cities will be announced.

title: Channel 4 Confirms Plans To Cut More Than A Quarter Of Its Workforce
summary: Channel 4 has announced the deepest round of layoffs in its 43-year history. The British network, home to shows including The Great British Bake Off and Taskmaster, is planning to cut 340 jobs by the end of 2026, meaning its workforce will shrink by more than a quarter. Channel 4 CEO Priya Dogra announced the […]
content:
Channel 4 has announced the deepest round of layoffs in its 43-year history.

The British network, home to shows including The Great British Bake Off and Taskmaster, is planning to cut 340 jobs by the end of 2026, meaning its workforce will shrink by more than a quarter.

Channel 4 CEO Priya Dogra announced the layoffs on Wednesday after spending recent months overseeing a strategic review of the commercial broadcaster.

She told employees that the redundancies — equivalent to 28% of Channel 4’s 1,276-strong workforce — will ensure that more of C4’s £1 billion ($1.3 billion) income is spent on screen.

The scale of the cuts has shocked insiders and others close to Channel 4. One source described it as a “very bad” day for the British broadcaster.

Watch on Deadline

Channel 4 finds itself increasingly isolated in a world in which it is dwarfed in size by some of its production suppliers, rival networks, and digital giants like YouTube.

The state-owned broadcaster is grappling with these forces at the same time as reckoning with ad market contraction and rising production costs.

Dogra has designed a new organizational structure, aimed at reducing management layers, removing duplication, and simplifying decision-making.

She is positioning the changes as “owning our future,” building on the work of her predecessor Alex Mahon in growing digital sales to 34% of Channel 4’s revenue.

Channel 4’s announcement was, however, light on details about the new structure, including how it will impact commissioning and the network’s fledgling in-house production plans.

A consultation process with staff will begin shortly. Channel 4 said further details will be announced about the plans in the coming months.

Dogra said: “Channel 4 is a precious asset which plays a unique role in the UK. We need to secure and own our future so we can continue to make shows others won’t, reach audiences others can’t, and thrive as a distinctive and disruptive British voice for future generations.

“Today marks the first phase of our transformation, ensuring Channel 4 is the right shape and size to deliver its future strategy and focus investment in the programmes audiences love.

“The challenges we face require a fundamental transformation in how we work. I know the proposals we are announcing today will be very difficult for many colleagues and will have a significant impact across the organisation. Many talented people who have made an enormous contribution to Channel 4 will be leaving as a result.

“These decisions have not been taken lightly, but I strongly believe they are necessary to create a simpler, more focused and more sustainable Channel 4 that can invest a greater proportion of revenues into distinctive content, back British creativity and deliver impact for audiences long into the future.”

Channel 4 chair Geoff Cooper added: “The proposals announced today are intended to secure Channel 4’s future as a trusted, independent British broadcaster.

“By taking action now, it can build a more sustainable and resilient organisation, maximise investment in content and strengthen its ability to deliver public value for audiences, the creative industries and the UK for the years ahead.”

Caroline Dinenage, chair of UK Parliament’s Culture, Media and Sport Committee, said the jobs cull was “deeply worrying” for Channel 4’s employees. “Channel 4 is a unique asset and must find ways to maintain independence and distinctiveness while capitalising on efficiencies and opportunities for collaboration,” she added.

Channel 4’s job cuts follow similar redundancies at the BBC, which has committed to reducing its workforce by 10%, equating to around 2,000 layoffs. Channel 4’s last major round of redundancies came in 2024 when 200 roles were closed.

Channel 4 cuts often spark conversations about the broadcaster’s executive pay, which reached record levels during Mahon’s tenure. Despite leaving Channel 4 in June 2025, Mahon’s total pay stood at £566,000, which is more than the BBC director-general earns in a year, despite running a considerably larger organization.

title: Netflix South Africa Slate Includes Latest ‘How To Ruin’, ‘Seriously Single’ & ‘Disaster Holiday’ Editions
summary: Netflix’s How to Ruin, Seriously Single and Disaster Holiday franchises are getting new editions as part of the streamer’s latest South African slate. Following the launch of Blood Legacy Season 2 on September 25, Netflix will debut Seriously Single Too, Another Disaster Holiday later this year, with Tuiskoms Season 2, Marked Season 2 and Meet […]
content:
Netflix‘s How to Ruin, Seriously Single and Disaster Holiday franchises are getting new editions as part of the streamer’s latest South African slate.

Following the launch of Blood Legacy Season 2 on September 25, Netflix will debut Seriously Single Too, Another Disaster Holiday later this year, with Tuiskoms Season 2, Marked Season 2 and Meet the Khumalos 2 also in production.

How to Ruin Diwali: Mee the Parents launches on October 30 and Dineo and Zothile ‘Solo Ntsizwa’ Langa have been confirmed as the hosts of Love is Blind: South Africa. Docuseries Stars & Vows: Anele and Buzza is another debuting in 2026.

How to Ruin Diwali: Meet The Parents comes from Burnt Onion Productions in collaboration with producer, Jayan Moodley. The show takes an irreverent look at an interracial couple whose engagement brings together two very different families and cultures. Moodley’s comedy The Kandasamys drew on similar South African Indian family tropes.

Watch on Deadline

Per the synopsis, it follows overachieving perfectionist Mmabatho Nkomo meeting her fiance’s traditional Indian family for the first time as her desperate attempt to impress backfires when she accidentally exposes her future father-in-law’s secret affair. With Diwali only days away, Mmabatho must navigate unfamiliar cultural territory and reunite the family she has torn apart without causing even more chaos.

Rosemary Zimu-Mnguni, Kyle Clark, Jailoshini Naidoo, Koobeshen Naidoo, Sonia Mbele, Meshack Mavuso, Luthando ‘BU’Mthembu, Denise Zimba and Ashish Gangapersad star.

Another Disaster Holiday, directed by Rethabile Ramaphakela, sees Joseph Ngema (Kenneth Nkosi) preparing to become a dad again at 50 and fighting to prove he is still father of the year. Per the preamble, “Under the guise of a romantic Sun City babymoon with a heavily pregnant Nandi, Joseph sets out to crash his children’s holiday with his ex-wife Dora and the hot younger boyfriend stealing his thunder. Enter Kay Sibiya, who joins the returning star-studded cast as Dora’s new bae and Joseph’s newest competition. Naturally, disaster follows.”

Seriously Single Too, also directed by Ramaphakela, sees Dineo (Fulu Mugovhani) and Noni (Tumi Morake) return, though their friendship may not last their latest trip. The pic follow what is supposed to be a wild bachelorette getaway in Cape Town for the now-estranged friends turn into a disastrous chain of events that leaves them on the brink. Also starring are Buntu Petse, Keke Mphuthi, Yonda Thomas and Thabiso Rammusi.



Romcom series Tuiskoms‘s second season sees Fleur (Amalia Uys) and Werner (Armand Aucamp) preparing for their wedding, before their carefully planned future takes an unexpected turn. Per the synopsis, “At the same time, a free-spirited woman with a complicated past returns to Wilderness after years away, hoping to reconnect with the family she left behind. Across the town, old wounds, new beginnings and unexpected connections reshape the lives of those who call it home.” Uys and Aucamp star alongside Kim Syster, Jane de Wet and Clint Brink.

Netflix recently found a hit out of South Africa in the shape of The Polygamist, which generated over 24 million views in its first weeks, reached the Top 10 in 62 countries and ranked first in 22 countries. The streamer is this week celebrating ten years in the country, and has trotted out several stats backing its performance there.

During a press showcase in Rosebank, Johannesburg, where Netflix executives, filmmakers and on-screen talent gathered to mark the occasion, the streamer claimed to have supported 8,000 jobs through partnerships with more than 30 local production companies. Its local originals have included Blood and Water, Silverton Siege, Fatal Seduction and most recent Umthetho, and have been filmed in 20 cities across eight provinces. Netflix claims to have offered more than 300 local titles in total over the past decade, including acquisitions.

“Ten years ago, we set out to share South African stories and voices with the world and today, we are proud to strengthen our partnership with the local creative industry and continue creating exciting stories that will entertain our members in South Africa and around the world,” said Ben Amadasun, VP of Content for Netflix Middle East and Africa.

“Our slate ahead keeps that ambition alive with the addition of established names alongside bold new production partners across genres from unscripted to thrillers, family dramas and comedy.”

Netflix also teased a new scripted series from Shaka iLembe maker The Bomb Shelter Film Productions and a multi-title partnership with The River producer Tshedza Pictures for four scripted series.

title: John Malkovich Cancels 2027 Tel Aviv Show & Says Producers Fabricated Quotes About The Performance
summary: John Malkovich has canceled a planned performance in Israel next year over what he described as the publication of an unauthorized press release to announce the show.  Malkovich was scheduled to perform The Music Critic in Tel Aviv next year. A press release was published last week quoting Malkovich saying he was “thrilled to return […]
content:
John Malkovich has canceled a planned performance in Israel next year over what he described as the publication of an unauthorized press release to announce the show.

Malkovich was scheduled to perform The Music Critic in Tel Aviv next year. A press release was published last week quoting Malkovich saying he was “thrilled to return to Israel” and looked “forward to meeting the warm Israeli audience once again, to whom I feel a strong closeness and solidarity.”

Malkovich has said he did not make those statements and was only aware of the announcement after reading press reports. In a statement to The Hollywood Reporter, which first reported on the story, the actor said it was all published without his agreement.

“A PR company hired by the Israeli promoter drafted a quote for the article that was attributed to me, though I never made the statements that were quoted, nor was I consulted before they were printed,” Malkovich said. “I did not utter these phrases, and they most certainly are not approved by me, nor do they reflect my feelings. The fact that they were printed as direct quotes from me is unacceptable and untenable. For this reason, I have decided I cannot participate in the Tel Aviv performance.”

Watch on Deadline

Malkovich added: “My appearance in any country, even my own, does not constitute approval of said country’s policies, nor actions, nor its elected or unelected leaders. My appearances would also not condone nor mean that I am in supposed ‘solidarity’ with any particular political cause, nor with the killing of innocents, nor with any acts of terrorism, nor any other kind of barbarity.”

The Israeli PR firm has since apologized for incorrectly attributing quotes to Malkovich.

“Mr. Malkovich did not make, provide, authorize or approve this statement, nor was it approved by his representatives,” the firm said in the statement. “We sincerely apologize to Mr. Malkovich and his representatives for the incorrect attribution and regret that this occurred.”

Malkovich is coming fresh off a buzzy showing in Venice, where his latest feature, Wild Horse Nine, landed a strong 14-minute ovation and quickly became the subject of awards chatter.

title: BBC Boss Matt Brittin Asked News Unit To Examine Jason Arday Coverage After Cambridge Professor’s Death
summary: EXCLUSIVE: The BBC’s new director general ordered the UK broadcaster’s news division to assess its coverage of Jason Arday after the academic died by suicide last month. The University of Cambridge professor was subjected to intense press scrutiny for days amid a spiralling plagiarism row. He was found dead at his home in August, prompting […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: The BBC‘s new director general ordered the UK broadcaster’s news division to assess its coverage of Jason Arday after the academic died by suicide last month.

The University of Cambridge professor was subjected to intense press scrutiny for days amid a spiralling plagiarism row. He was found dead at his home in August, prompting soul-searching in British media over whether the coverage of the Arday allegations was proportionate.

BBC boss Matt Brittin asked news chiefs to examine the volume of the corporation’s output on Arday in comparison with other UK media outlets. He told colleagues that it was right to take stock of the BBC’s coverage because the forensic media reporting appeared to contribute to Arday’s death. BBC News bosses stood by the broadcaster’s reporting, describing it as “fair and proportionate.”

Brittin revealed the Arday mini-review during an all-staff briefing on Tuesday, during which employees raised questions about the BBC’s reporting on the professor. “It’s obviously a terribly tragic story, and a horrible, horrible outcome,” he told employees. “I did ask the team to look at our coverage as a result of that, and see where we were compared with other media. I think we played the coverage very straight.”

Watch on Deadline

Brittin said other publications ran “hundreds of stories” about the Arday scandal, though he did not provide an equivalent figure for the BBC. “I felt like many people in the newsroom: This is something where coverage seems to have directly contributed to a tragedy, and there’s a responsibility on everyone in the media to look at themselves in those times,” he added.

Brittin, who has quickly earned a reputation for being very direct with colleagues, used the Arday issue to make a broader point about the BBC being more “critical” and less self-congratulatory about its output. He caveated his remarks by saying that the BBC is staffed by “brilliant professionals.”

“In a fast-changing world we need to be a culture where we learn and we’re curious. And I think one of the things I’d observe is that sometimes we can be quite sea of green about things,” Brittin explained.

“We’re very good at congratulating ourselves on what’s gone well. I’d like us also to be critical about what we could have done better, and are there things we could have learned from others out there in the media market?”

In a statement on BBC News’ Arday output, a spokesperson said: “Jason Arday was a prominent figure at one of the world’s most prestigious universities, and the allegations made against him and the wider implications for academia made this a public interest story.

“We believe we reported on the different aspects of this story in a fair and proportionate way and reflected a wide range of views in our coverage, including Mr Arday’s public statements and comment from supporters who spoke in his defence. When covering any story, we are always mindful to treat those involved with sensitivity.”

title: ‘Jackass: Best and Last’ Sets Paramount+ Release Date
summary: The joke’s over: “Jackass: Best and Last” will be available to stream on Paramount+ on Sept. 24. After the film’s theatrical release on June 26, the decades-long saga of pranks and tomfoolery is finally coming to an end. The “Jackass” crew’s wild ride from MTV show to five-part film series officially concludes with its move […]
content:
The joke’s over: “Jackass: Best and Last” will be available to stream on Paramount+ on Sept. 24.

After the film’s theatrical release on June 26, the decades-long saga of pranks and tomfoolery is finally coming to an end. The “Jackass” crew’s wild ride from MTV show to five-part film series officially concludes with its move to streaming.

The original cast members, including Johnny Knoxville, Bam Margera, Steve-O, Chris Pontius, Jason “Wee Man” Acuña, Dave England, Preston Lacy and Ehren McGhehey, all reunited for one last round of pranks in “Best and Last.” The film comes four years after “Jackass Forever,” in which the cast stuck to their debaucherous ways, while introducing a new generation of pranksters. During production of that movie, Knoxville was pummeled by a bull, leaving him with a brain hemorrhage, concussion, broken wrist and broken rib that forced him to semi-retire.

“I can’t do anything where I can get another concussion,” Knoxville said on the “Books That Changed My Life” podcast. “[I’m] way over my limit for concussions, but I don’t care about anything else. I just can’t get hit in the head anymore — but a lot of other guys can.”

Popular on Variety

While he successfully avoided head injuries this time around, Knoxville and his crew spent this film revisiting old stunts and experimenting with new extremes.

“My name is Johnny Knoxville, and I’m going to try to not get emotional,” the star said on the CinemaCon stage. “This is the last ‘Jackass’ film the world will ever see. ‘Jackass’ means a hell of a lot for me. We knew we were making the last one, so we went extra hard to make sure this was also our best ‘Jackass’ film ever.”

title: Thunder Road Films and Lit Entertainment Group Launch TR/AK, Media Company Focusing on Original Stories and Creators
summary: Thunder Road Films founder Basil Iwanyk and partner Erica Lee have partnered with Lit Entertainment Group founder Adam Kolbrenner to launch a new media company, TR/AK. The company will focus on creators and telling original stories, as well as commercially ambitious film and television projects targeted for global audiences. Thunder Road Films is behind the […]
content:
Thunder Road Films founder Basil Iwanyk and partner Erica Lee have partnered with Lit Entertainment Group founder Adam Kolbrenner to launch a new media company, TR/AK.

The company will focus on creators and telling original stories, as well as commercially ambitious film and television projects targeted for global audiences.

Thunder Road Films is behind the “John Wick” franchise and has supported Taylor Sheridan in his filmmaking endeavors, including “Wind River.” Lit Entertainment boasts a clientele that represents leading writers and creators including Justin Marks (“Shogun,” “Top Gun: Maverick”), Dave Andron (“Snowfall,” “Justified”), Zach Dean (“The Gorge,” “The Tomorrow War”), David Guggenheim (“Safe House,” “Designated Survivor”), Roshan Sethi (“The Surgeon”), Aaron Guzikowski (Prisoners), Matt Lieberman (Free Guy, Christmas Chronicles), Sascha Penn (“By Any Means,” “Raising Kanan”), Matt Lopez (“Father of the Bride,” “Sheriff Country”), Liz Garcia (“Purple Hearts”), Ben Jacoby (“Whisper Man”), and Justin Rhodes (“Liminal”).

Thunder Road’s films have collectively grossed more than $4.4 billion worldwide. Projects written by Lit clients have generated more than $7 billion at the global box office, in addition to thousands of hours of television.

Popular on Variety

In addition to the top-tier roster of clients, Lit also represents a dynamic library of more than 10,000 stories and characters through partnerships with NeoText, Weird Tales, Heavy Metal, Meridia Books, Weekly World News, Zenescope Comics and others.

Thunder Road and Lit brands will remain independent, though additional executive appointments are expected as the company builds out its finance, operations and corporate infrastructure.

“Erica and I have been thinking of how to grow Thunder Road for years and Adam is a longtime friend and collaborator with us,” said Iwanyk. “The more we talked, the more we realized we had a shared vision and ambition in creating the most expansive and dynamic independent company in town.”

The launch formalizes a long-standing collaboration among Iwanyk, Lee and Kolbrenner that most recently spans three high-profile films all from spec screenplays from Lit clients: Roshan Sethi’s “The Surgeon,” starring Michelle Yeoh and Martin Freeman, which will have its world premiere at this year’s Toronto International Film Festival; Marc Webb’s upcoming “Day Drinker” for Lionsgate written by Zach Dean starring Johnny Depp, Penélope Cruz and Madelyn Cline, set for release March 26, 2027; and “By Any Means,” starring Mark Wahlberg and Yahya Abdul-Mateen II.

“Basil, Erica and the Thunder Road team have built their company by trusting their instincts and doing the work required to get ambitious movies made,” said Kolbrenner. “That’s very much how we operate at Lit. TR/AK is about bringing those teams together, backing great writers and filmmakers for projects that can connect with audiences around the world.”

Thunder Road is currently in production on “Hivemind” starring Samara Weaving and Nicholas Braun. Its upcoming slate includes A24’s “The Peasant,” directed and starring Dev Patel; “The Kellys,” written and directed by Brad Peyton for Amazon and starring Arnold Schwarzenegger, Liam Hemsworth and Geena Davis; the Walton Goggins action vehicle “Mister”; and “Caine,” the latest in the John Wick franchise starring and directed by Donnie Yen.

CAA Media Finance-Evolution was a strategic advisor on the transaction.

title: Channing Tatum, Gemma Chan and a 9-Year-Old Front the ‘Josephine’ Oscar Campaign (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Every awards season has a film that dares you to look away. This year it’s carried by a nine-year-old girl. Sumerian Pictures will submit Beth de Araújo’s Sundance Film Festival winner “Josephine” across multiple categories for the upcoming awards season, Variety has learned exclusively. The push runs from best picture through the acting and crafts […]
content:
Every awards season has a film that dares you to look away. This year it’s carried by a nine-year-old girl.

Sumerian Pictures will submit Beth de Araújo’s Sundance Film Festival winner “Josephine” across multiple categories for the upcoming awards season, Variety has learned exclusively. The push runs from best picture through the acting and crafts races, and it’s the first campaign the young distributor has ever mounted.

Reeves will be submitted in lead actress, which drops a child into one of the season’s most competitive races for her debut film. Oscar history shows us that lead nominations for child actors are rare. Only two performers under 18 have ever been nominated for best actress: Wallis, who still holds the record as the youngest at age 9 and Keisha Castle-Hughes for “Whale Rider” (2003) at age 13. In contrast, the supporting actress category has been far more welcoming to young performers. But if there’s ever been a case for bucking that trend, Reeves makes it.

Popular on Variety

Co-stars Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan will both campaign in their respective supporting actor and supporting actress categories. They both produced the drama alongside David Kaplan, Josh Peters, de Araújo and Marina Stabile. Tatum and Chan are delivering some of the strongest acting works of their long careers.

As Damien, Josephine’s father, he channels a subdued, aching kind of masculinity — one unable to articulate emotion but desperate to protect. His portrayal recalls his quietly devastating work in Bennett Miller’s “Foxcatcher” (2014).

Courtesy Photo

At Sundance, “Josephine” was often the first title blurted out during the annual ritual of asking people what they’ve seen and liked. An award-winning screenwriter told Variety that Tatum has an opportunity to carve himself a niche position that someone like Ryan Gosling used to occupy: the sexy knockaround guy who learns something about life and himself, as evidenced by his work in “Josephine” and, last year, “Roofman.”

Opposite him, Chan delivers the finest performance of her career. As Josephine’s mother, Claire, Chan is luminous with quiet sorrow, conveying maternal guilt and helplessness with precision.

Written and directed by de Araújo, the film follows an eight-year-old, played by newcomer Reeves, who accidentally witnesses a crime in Golden Gate Park and starts acting out, hunting for any way back to feeling safe while every adult around her proves useless at consoling her.

“Josephine” premiered in U.S. Dramatic Competition at Sundance in January and left with both the Grand Jury Prize and the Audience Award, a double no film had managed since “Minari” in 2020 and “CODA” the year after it. “CODA” went on to win best picture. Variety called the film a “standout” of the festival, writing: “‘Josephine’ dares to confront the life-shattering intersection of sex and violence in our culture, facing the toughest of ‘adult situations’ with clear eyes.”

De Araújo, who is of Chinese and Brazilian descent, enters the directing and original screenplay races. No Latina has ever been nominated for directing, while the only Asian woman to be recognized is Chloe Zhao, who won for “Nomadland” (2020) and is one of two women to be nominated twice when she was recognized for “Hamnet” (2025). De Araújo’s crafts team will seek love as well. Greta Zozula in cinematography, editors Anisha Acharya, Nico Leunen and Kyle Reiter and Nina Henninger in casting, a category that has quickly become the place where films built on discoveries rather than stars make their stand, as “The Secret Agent,” “Sinners and eventual winner “One Battle After Another” did last year.

While Sundance crowns its winners in January and the Academy names its nominees the following January, the 12 months between them can have worthy contenders disappear. Sumerian is spending its first campaign on the proposition that a girl who wasn’t alive for “Beasts of the Southern Wild,” along with the talents surrounding her, can go the distance.

The full list of categories is below.

Final eligibility is determined by the Academy and any other relevant organizational bodies.

See all Academy Awards predictions
