title: Israel’s ‘Tell Me Everything’ Tops Ophir Awards,  Becomes Country’s Oscar Submission
summary: Moshe Rosenthal’s Tell Me Everything is Israel’s official submission to the 2027 Oscar Best International Feature race by virtue of its winning the Best Picture prize Thursday’s at Israel’s Ophir Awards. Tell Me Everything won a total of 10 Ophir trophies tonight, including Best Director and Best Screenplay for Rosenthal. It came into the night […]
content:
Moshe Rosenthal’s Tell Me Everything is Israel‘s official submission to the 2027 Oscar Best International Feature race by virtue of its winning the Best Picture prize Thursday’s at Israel’s Ophir Awards.

Tell Me Everything won a total of 10 Ophir trophies tonight, including Best Director and Best Screenplay for Rosenthal. It came into the night at Israel’s equivalent of the Academy Awards with a record 16 nominations.

In Israel, the Ophir Best Picture winner automatically qualifies to be the country’s submission to the Oscar category.

Rosenthal’s film (in Hebrew the title is Independence) is set in Israel in 1987, when 12-year-old Boaz (Yair Mazor) discovers that his father (Assi Cohen), whom he idolizes, is gay, shattering the family while the beginning of the AIDS pandemic looms as the backdrop. The two attempt to reconcile and heal a decade later. Ido Tako plays the older Boaz, and Keren Tzur, Neta Orbach and Mor Demari also star.

Watch on Deadline

The pic had its world premiere at this year’s Sundance Film Festival in the World Cinema Dramatic Competition. It bowed in Israeli theaters on September 1.

This year’s 15-film Oscar shortlist in the international feature category will be revealed December 15, with Oscar nominations to be announced January 21, 2027.

Israel has been nominated 10 times in Oscar’s international category, most recently in 2011 for Joseph Cedar’s Footnote. Since then, it made the 15-film shortlist in 2015 with Foxtrot and submitted Shai Carmeli-Pollak’s The Sea last year. It has never won the Oscar.

title: Fox Corp. COO John Nallen Says Roku Deal On Track To Close Despite “Entirely Expected” DOJ Scrutiny
summary: Fox Corp. President and Chief Operating Officer John Nallen said the company’s $22 billion acquisition of Roku is on track to close despite a new request for information from regulators. Speaking at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia conference in San Francisco on Wednesday, Nallen mentioned Fox’s regulatory filing earlier in the day noting the U.S. Department […]
content:
Fox Corp. President and Chief Operating Officer John Nallen said the company’s $22 billion acquisition of Roku is on track to close despite a new request for information from regulators.

Speaking at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia conference in San Francisco on Wednesday, Nallen mentioned Fox’s regulatory filing earlier in the day noting the U.S. Department of Justice‘s had asked for additional information.

Nallen called that request “entirely expected,” echoing language in the filing that the merging companies intend to “work co-operatively” with regulators. He said the previous estimate that the transaction will close in the first half of 2027 remains intact.

While the exec has plenty of reason to publicly project confidence, his characterization is well-founded in regulatory procedural norms. Even so, there is an unpredictable element now in the mix on any corporate transaction: President Trump.

Watch on Deadline

Unmentioned during the conference session was speculation about potential backlash from Trump over last week’s abrupt decision by Fox News to drop longtime host Maria Bartiromo. “Her fans, of which there are many, will not be happy,” Trump posted on social media. Bartiromo has hired well-established entertainment Bryan Freedman, planning to fight Fox over her terms of her dismissal.

Given Trump’s capricious handling of tariffs and FCC scrutiny of broadcast networks whose programming he doesn’t like, some observers have wondered if the president could stymie the Roku deal out of spite. Trump and Fox chairman emeritus Rupert Murdoch, still a key figure in determining the direction of Fox News, have had many bumpy periods in their longtime relationship. Murdoch did not endorse Trump in 2016 and also broke with him after on-air talent including Bartiromo created legal liability by airing lies about the validity of the 2020 election.

Nallen said Roku is at an “inflection point,” starting to accelerate growth, while Fox streaming platform Tubi has recently turned profitable while revenue keeps surging. Given that combination of entities on the upswing, Nallen said, “It’s going to end up as a superb transaction.”

Probed about the financials of the deal, Nallen said it won’t saddle the combined company with excess debt.

He said Fox expects to have a leverage ratio of 2.8 times trailing earnings and, with revenue growing significantly at both companies, “the de-leveraging that occurs is rapid.” Plans for a share buyback in the range of $1 billion to $1.5 billion will proceed “unabated,” a further sign of financial strength, Nallen added. Public companies often have to balance paying down debt with buying back their own stock, with the latter move often helping boost investor confidence.

The session touched on a number of other topics, including sports rights, talks with distributors and the first year of streaming flagship Fox One.

Asked about progress with Fox One since its launch last August, Nallen said the company has projected reaching between 3 million and 5 million subscribers in the first five years after launch. While Fox execs are stopping short of revising that forecast, Nallen said initial subscriber growth is “above expectations.”

Data from research firm Antenna showed last summer’s blockbuster World Cup broadcasts helped spur 2.8 million sign-ups to Fox One.

title: Imax Tops $600M In Q3 Box Office So Far On ‘The Odyssey’; CEO Shrugs Off Industry M&A – “Our Primary Relationships Are With Filmmakers”
summary: Imax big screens have passed $600 million in global box office receipts so far this quarter, says CEO Rich Gelfond, noting that it’s still early in September (Q4 runs through end of the month) and “our best quarter ever was in the mid-three hundreds.” That was in the third quarter of 2023. The company is […]
content:
Imax big screens have passed $600 million in global box office receipts so far this quarter, says CEO Rich Gelfond, noting that it’s still early in September (Q4 runs through end of the month) and “our best quarter ever was in the mid-three hundreds.”

That was in the third quarter of 2023.

The company is on a roll and “I think it’s really the beginning,” he said at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia media conference touting Imax’s terrific run with Universal and Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, an overall box office recovery and the company’s ability to leverage various revenue streams from global ticket sales to Imax installations to, more recently, popcorn buckets.

“When we looked at our slate for the year, I was the most bullish person in the company on The Odyssey.” Imax’s previous record for a single film was $230 million in global box office receipts for Avatar‘s initial run. “Keep in mind, that’s on 1% of the screens in the world. And today, we’re knocking on the door of a half a billion dollars. How many films do a half a billion, let alone an Imax only?”

Watch on Deadline

RELATED: The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office

Imax splits the box office take with movie theaters and sometimes studios depending the structure of the exhibitor deal, getting about 18 cents on the dollar.

The slate ahead includes a range of diverse studio films along with sports, music (Oasis concert coming) and local language fare. Imax released 120 pieces of content last year.

For the rest of this year and beyond, Gelfond touted, among others, good tracking on Sony’s Resident Evil, and Dune: Part Three, where tickets went on sale a few weeks ago. “If you stopped today, which is three months in advance of the film’s release, it would be one of the most highest pre-sales in our 60 year history.”

From Netflix, David Fincher’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth starring Brad Pitt debuts with an exclusive two-week Imax theatrical window on November 25, as does Narnia: The Musician’s Nephew by Greta Gerwig in early 2027. The Thomas Crown Affair from Amazon MGM directed by and starring Michael B Jordan follows in March. Sony’s four Beatles movies start rolling out in 2028, with Joseph Kosinski’s Miami Vice ’85.

He said the company is looking to a wider variety of film fare to drive brand loyalty. “As much as I still believe in superhero movies … I don’t think there’s anything so unique about [them] that says, wow, I’ve got to see this in Imax. And, to some extent, we’ve seen over the last few years, that some of that has run its course.” The goal is “for people to say, ‘What’s playing at the Imax theater?’ And I’m not saying we’re there yet, but I think … momentum is clearly happening.”

Fandom is showing up in merch, which is becoming a new focus after a test putting out 2,500 Imax popcorn buckets on sale “and within 90 minutes they were gone. And we kept putting more on sale and couldn’t keep up with the demand. “When you look at our plans for 2027, we’re going to lean into merchandising.”

Asked if he’s concerned about industry consolidation, Gelfond said “our primary relationships are with filmmakers. So, wherever the filmmakers end up … they’re the ones that we’re really talking to about the content.”

“We’ve built this business over 60 years and we have the relationships … Those relationships with the filmmakers are not going anywhere.”

Meanwhile, he said, studios are recognizing that Imax helps drive global box office, and streamers that it boosts streaming calculus, as per Apple’s F1 by Kosinski, and Phil Lord and Christopher Miller’s Hail Mary for Amazon MGM.

He called Warner Bros. “a great partner and said, “We’ve talked many times to David Ellison and Paramount where if [the merger] does happen, they’re going to certainly ramp up their Imax productions. We have a terrific relationship with [Paramount]. We’ve done the Mission Impossible movies, Top Gun: Maverick.”

He said Imax has been using its growing cash position to expand its network. “Our old model used to be, [exhibitors] would put up all the money and we would license our technology. Then we went more to a joint venture model, where we take a bigger percentage of the box office, but we put up more of the capital … And since they’ve been doing very well, the paybacks have been even better than we modeled.”

title: ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live!’ Returning to Brooklyn for Week of Shows
summary: Jimmy Kimmel is returning to Brooklyn for a week of “Live!” shows at the end of September, according to People. This marks the eighth time the late-night host has traveled to the borough to tape. The shows, which take place at the Academy of Music’s Howard Gilman Opera House, will be taped from Monday, Sept. […]
content:
Jimmy Kimmel is returning to Brooklyn for a week of “Live!” shows at the end of September, according to People. This marks the eighth time the late-night host has traveled to the borough to tape.

The shows, which take place at the Academy of Music’s Howard Gilman Opera House, will be taped from Monday, Sept. 28 to Friday, Oct. 2 in front of a live audience. Guests will be revealed at a later date.

Kimmel also did a round of “Live!” broadcasts from Brooklyn in 2025, notably hosting fellow “The Late Show” frontman Stephen Colbert, who at the time had recently been canceled by ABC. Kimmel first played the BAM in 2012 and returned to the venue in 2015, 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2022.

Popular on Variety

Kimmel recently returned from a three-month break from hosting “Jimmy Kimmel Live!,” which typically records at Hollywood’s El Capitan Entertainment Centre. In his place, Kimmel had Rosie O’Donnell, Colman Domingo, Jelly Roll, Tiffany Haddish, Anthony Anderson and Ike Barinholtz fill in as host. Tuesday, which saw Kimmel return, marked the 4,000th episode of “Live!”

On Monday night, Kimmel is competing at the Emmy Awards for outstanding variety series. It would be his fourth win if he takes home the 2026 prize. In an effort to drum up support for his former colleague, Colbert posted a video on Instagram in late August encouraging Academy members to vote for Kimmel, even though he is competing against him.

“Kind of a weird voting system this year, but you know, I think we can all agree that Jimmy Kimmel deserves an Emmy,” Colbert said. “I don’t care if you’ve never even seen his show, you know he deserves an Emmy.”

title: Suki Waterhouse Says She’d Be ‘Nepo-Babying’ Her Daughter With Robert Pattinson If She Wanted to Work in Hollywood
summary: Good news for Suki Waterhouse and Robert Pattinson’s two-year-old daughter: if she ever wants to pursue a career in the arts when she’s older, her mom is happy to help.  In a recent interview with Nylon, when asked if she’d ever invite her daughter into the industry, the musician responded, “Why would I advise against […]
content:
Good news for Suki Waterhouse and Robert Pattinson’s two-year-old daughter: if she ever wants to pursue a career in the arts when she’s older, her mom is happy to help.

In a recent interview with Nylon, when asked if she’d ever invite her daughter into the industry, the musician responded, “Why would I advise against it? I’d be nepo-babying the hell out of her… Oh no. Why didn’t I just keep that inside?”

While Waterhouse first gained attention as a model, the star pivoted to acting, appearing in films like “Love Rosie” and TV shows including “Daisy Jones and The Six.” As of late, though, Waterhouse is best known for her music; “Loveland,” her third album, came out in July.

Popular on Variety

Pattinson has been a fixture in the industry since he played Edward Cullen in “Twilight,” and before then, Cedric Diggory in “Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire.” Today, the actor is one of Hollywood’s top stars, having led films like “The Batman,” “Mickey 17” and “The Drama.” “Primetime,” Pattinson’s latest project in which he portrays “To Catch a Predator” host Chris Hansen, is set to hit theaters on Sept. 25.

In the interview, Waterhouse also discussed the whirlwind few weeks she experienced after welcoming her daughter in 2024, calling the pace “quite intense.” (She shot a British Vogue cover, headlined Coachella’s Gobi stage and opened for Taylor Swift’s Eras Tour in England.)

Speaking with Variety earlier this year, Waterhouse also described the time as “a dream.” “When I had her, I had so many incredible things going on,” she said. “Maybe if I have another one, it will be a more peaceful moment. But I just knew that this time it was going to be a whirlwind. And I think as a result, everything has been so real that it hurts. It’s been amusing and so tender and fragile and hilarious and all the things.”

title: Barry Melrose, Former ESPN Analyst and Hockey Pro, Dies at 70
summary: Barry Melrose, a former NHL player, coach and longtime ESPN analyst, died Wednesday. He was 70.  Melrose’s wife, Cindy, confirmed his death to ESPN.  “For decades, Barry Melrose was one of the most distinctive and trusted voices in hockey,” wrote ESPN in a statement. “His knowledge of the game was deep, his candor was refreshing, […]
content:
Barry Melrose, a former NHL player, coach and longtime ESPN analyst, died Wednesday. He was 70.

Melrose’s wife, Cindy, confirmed his death to ESPN.

“For decades, Barry Melrose was one of the most distinctive and trusted voices in hockey,” wrote ESPN in a statement. “His knowledge of the game was deep, his candor was refreshing, and his passion was unmistakable. He was a foundational part of ESPN’s hockey coverage, and fans and teammates truly appreciated his entertaining delivery and charismatic personality.”

The statement continued: “We send our deepest condolences to his loved ones. He always kept it interesting and he will be missed.”

Popular on Variety

Born in Kelvington, Saskatchewan, Canada, Melrose began his hockey career when he was selected in the second round of the NHL Draft by the Montreal Canadiens in 1976. His debut came in 1979 with the Winnipeg Jets. Melrose went on to play for teams including the Toronto Maple Leafs and the Detroit Red Wings until 1986. He began coaching the following year. Notably, Melrose coached star player Wayne Gretzky and the Los Angeles Kings, who made it to the Stanley Cup Final in 1993. (He coached the team for three seasons, from 1992 to 1995.)

Melrose joined ESPN in 1996, transitioning from a coach to an analyst. In 2023, Melrose received a Parkinson’s disease diagnosis, after which he retired from the network.

John Buccigross, whom Melrose worked with at ESPN, shared a statement to X calling the former coach his “best friend at ESPN.” “A big brother figure of rock solid values,” he continued. “I am shook to my core. Barry gave his life to hockey and some of his ESPN family, like me, learned of his shocking death today while at a hockey rink in Las Vegas preparing for the upcoming season. Chilling and fitting — the rink was Barry’s home. A more beloved ESPN institution there has not been. We love you, Barry. Forever.”

Melrose is survived by his wife and two sons, Tyrell and Adrien.

title: Hideo Kojima’s ‘Physint’ Moves From PlayStation to Xbox as ‘Death Stranding’ Creator Plots TV and Film Projects With New Publishing Partner
summary: Xbox is expanding its partnership with video game industry legend Hideo Kojima. The “Death Stranding” and “Metal Gear” creator has switched the publishing partner on his upcoming game “Physint” to Microsoft’s Xbox from its original home at Sony’s PlayStation, which decided to cancel the action-espionage project. The news was shared via a blog post published […]
content:
Xbox is expanding its partnership with video game industry legend Hideo Kojima.

The “Death Stranding” and “Metal Gear” creator has switched the publishing partner on his upcoming game “Physint” to Microsoft’s Xbox from its original home at Sony’s PlayStation, which decided to cancel the action-espionage project.

The news was shared via a blog post published by Xbox Wednesday, along with the reveal that this partnership will “extend beyond games, with Xbox and Kojima Productions collaborating across film and television to bring new stories to broader audiences.”

Popular on Variety

Xbox is already set to publish Kojima Productions’ next release, “OD,” a horror game made in collaboration with Jordan Peele, which does not yet have a launch date. The action-espionage game “Physint” is the Kojima title that’s up next after “OD” and it was previously set to be published by PlayStation. The shift of “Physint” to Xbox is particularly notable due to the long-standing relationship Kojima has had with PlayStation, including their collaboration on the “Death Stranding” franchise.

Kojima wrote in a statement on X that this move comes after PlayStation decided to scrap “Physint” back in June.

“As confirmed earlier through our official channels, in mid-June of this year, we unexpectedly received notice from PlayStation Studios that they would cancel the PHYSINT project,” Kojima wrote. “PHYSINT is an important project both to me personally and to KOJIMA PRODUCTIONS. Determined to keep the project alive, we have spent the last three months searching tirelessly for a new partner. In the course of seeking advice and pursuing negotiations with people across many fields, we found in XBOX a partner with whom we share a common vision for the future, and we have decided to team up with them once again. Please rest assured that development of PHYSINT, our genre-defining action-espionage title, is ongoing and will continue moving forward.”

Per PlayStation’s own statement posted on X: “After careful consideration, we have made the difficult decision to step away from collaborating with KOJIMA PRODUCTIONS on its project PHYSINT. We continue to have great admiration for Hideo Kojima’s vision for the game. Our relationship remains strong after three decades of industry-leading, genre-defining creative cooperation, and we look forward to continued close collaboration with Hideo Kojima and his award-winning independent studio in the future.”

News of Kojima’s partnership expansion with Xbox comes amid mounting discourse over PlayStation’s July announcement that it will cease production of physical discs for its games beginning with new titles releasing in 2028, but conversations between Kojima and Xbox have been ongoing since earlier in the year when new CEO Asha Sharma came on board to replace Phil Spencer.

Over the course of several months, Sharma and Kojima have had in-person meetings and ongoing discussions about his creative plans and ways they could work together across platforms, including IP development for TV and film.

“Creators have choices about where and how they bring their ideas to life,” Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said. “We’re honored that Kojima-san has chosen Xbox to work with Kojima Productions on ‘Physint.’ His ambition to challenge conventions reflects the kind of creativity we want to support at Xbox.”

“This expands our relationship with Xbox beyond ‘OD,” Kojima said. “As we move forward with the development of ‘Physint,’ we remain committed to redefining the action-espionage genre for players around the world.”

While the “Physint” news is sure to excite Kojima’s U.S.-based fans with Xbox consoles, Xbox’s expanded relationship with Kojima will also likely bolster the brand’s presence in Japan and other Asian markets, which have historically been a weaker point for Xbox.

No specific details were shared regarding what TV and film projects Xbox is plotting with Kojima as part of their expanded partnership, though “Death Stranding” is already being developed into a film at A24 and the game maker has expressed ambitions for more transmedia projects.

“Back in the day, movies and games were two different worlds. It was like analog vs digital. It didn’t mix well, like oil and water,” Kojima told Variety in a 2024 interview about his decision to sign with Hollywood talent agency WME. “Nowadays, movies are also digital, like being shot on digital cameras instead of film. The pre-production and post-production phases are digital, too. It’s even streamed digitally. There seems to be more understanding in the conversations I have with people in the filmmaking industry. That wasn’t always the case. Now, there are movies that use Unreal Engine to create their backgrounds and environments. They also use performance capture [PCap] like we do, so the technology is almost the same up to a certain point.”

title: ‘South Park’ Creators Apologize for the Years-Long Delay of Their Kendrick Lamar Movie: ‘We Still Believe in the Project’
summary: “South Park” co-creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone have released an official apology for delaying their mysterious film collaboration with Kendrick Lamar. “We take full responsibility for the schedule delay of this movie,” Parker and Stone said in a statement to The Ankler. “We apologize to our partners at pgLang and Paramount, and we appreciate […]
content:
“South Park” co-creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone have released an official apology for delaying their mysterious film collaboration with Kendrick Lamar.

“We take full responsibility for the schedule delay of this movie,” Parker and Stone said in a statement to The Ankler. “We apologize to our partners at pgLang and Paramount, and we appreciate their patience. ‘South Park’ and life’s circumstances have gotten in the way, but we still believe in the project.”

Reps for Paramount, Parker and Stone did not immediately respond to Variety’s request for comment.

Popular on Variety

The musical comedy movie, operating under the working title “Whitney Springs,” is in production at Paramount, which is also the home of “South Park.” Parker and Stone are working on the project under their Park County banner. Lamar is also producing alongside Dave Free and his pgLang company.

Early loglines stated that “Whitney Springs” follows a Black man working as a slave reenactor at a living history museum who discovers his white girlfriend’s family once owned his ancestors. The Ankler reported a slight variation on the story. The outlet claims that the film follows the Black slave reenactor as he clashes with the racist mayor of a Midwestern town, who will be played by Parker. Lamar, The Ankler said, has recorded several original songs for the project.

Parker and Stone debut “South Park” Season 29 on Sept. 16. Seasons 27 and 28 came after a two-year hiatus and shocked audiences with the inclusion of Donald Trump as a major antagonist. The show has continued to troll the president in the off season. Parker and Stone recently changed the name of “South Park” to “South America,” in an apparent jab at Trump for changing the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America and Lake Ontario to Lake America.

title: Barry Melrose Dies: Gretzky-Era L.A. Kings Coach And Longtime ESPN Hockey Analyst Was 70
summary: Barry Melrose, who coached the Wayne Gretzky-led Los Angeles Kings team that helped put the NHL and hockey on the map in the U.S., and who later became ESPN’s signature hockey analyst for almost two decades, died Wednesday. He was 70. Melrose retired from ESPN after an almost two-decade broadcasting career after he revealed just […]
content:
Barry Melrose, who coached the Wayne Gretzky-led Los Angeles Kings team that helped put the NHL and hockey on the map in the U.S., and who later became ESPN‘s signature hockey analyst for almost two decades, died Wednesday. He was 70.

Melrose retired from ESPN after an almost two-decade broadcasting career after he revealed just before the start of the 2023-24 NHL season that he had been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease.

“I’ve had over 50 extraordinary years playing, coaching and analyzing the world’s greatest game, hockey,” Melrose said in a statement at the time. “It’s now time to hang up my skates and focus on my health, my family, including my supportive wife Cindy, and whatever comes next.”

Melrose coached the L.A. Kings the franchise’s first Stanley Cup Finals appearance in 1993, Gretzky’s fifth season in Los Angeles after arriving in a monumental trade with Edmonton. It was Melrose’s first season with the club; he would coach two more seasons in L.A. before turning his attention to TV.

Sporting a mullet, big bright pinstriped suits and with plenty to say, the Saskatchewan-born Melrose became a favorite on ESPN’s hockey coverage almost from the beginning when he joined in 1994; the network’s coverage of the Stanley Cup playoffs that year won a Sports Emmy. He began a full-time role in October 1996, and he appeared regularly on SportsCenter and NHL studio shows often with ESPNers like Steve Levy and John Buccigross, and also called regular-season and playoff games for ESPN and ABC Sports.

He even parlayed his ESPN fame into other TV roles, playing himself in Mystery Alaska, the 1999 feature about a small-town hockey club playing the NHL’s New York Rangers. He also guested as himself in a 2001 episode of ABC’s Michael J. Fox sitcom Spin City and appeared in the 2002 sequel Slap Shot 2: Breaking the Ice.

Buccigross remembered Melrose on Wednesday evening,

“Barry was my best friend at ESPN,” Buccigross wrote on social media Wednesday night. “A big brother figure of rock solid values. I am shook to my core. Barry gave his life to hockey and some of his ESPN family, like me, learned of his shocking death today while at a hockey rink in Las Vegas preparing for the upcoming season. Chilling and fitting — the rink was Barry’s home. A more beloved ESPN institution there has not been. We love you, Barry. Forever.”

Barry was my best friend at ESPN. A big brother figure of rock solid values. I am shook to my core. Barry gave his life to hockey and some of his ESPN family, like me, learned of his shocking death today while at a hockey rink in Las Vegas preparing for the upcoming season.… pic.twitter.com/x1zV1b4z87 — BucciOT.Com (@Buccigross) September 10, 2026

Said Levy tonight: “For more than 30 years Barry was the unquestioned face/voice of hockey in the United States. He was a man of the people, a family man, a part of my family. Tonight I’ll toast the kid from Kelvington who made it big but never forgot his roots. Now he can drink all the Bud Lights, smoke all the cigars and play all the rounds of golf he wants to. Barry Melrose was the best of us.”

ESPN hockey voice Steve Levy on the passing of his longtime friend & co-worker Barry Melrose pic.twitter.com/QJ953Q81BC — ESPN PR (@ESPNPR) September 10, 2026

Melrose played in the NHL as a defenseman with the Winnipeg Jets, Toronto Maple Leafs and Detroit Red Wings from 1979-86. He also played three seasons with Cincinnati in the WHA (1976-79). He later transitioned to coaching, leading teams to Memorial Cup and Calder Cup trophies.

In addition to the Kings, he coached 16 games with the Tampa Bay Lightning in 2008-2009 before returning to ESPN.

title: Chinese Distributor Hishow Adds ‘Josephine’, ‘Ah Girl’ & ‘Rec’ Franchise To We Love Cinema Release Slate
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Beijing-based producer-distributor Hishow Entertainment is expanding its cinephile ‘We Love Cinema’ brand with a slate of new acquisitions including recent Sundance winner Josephine and Ah Girl from Singapore’s Ang Geck Geck Priscilla. Beth de Araújo’s Josephine, starring Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan, scooped both the Grand Jury Prize and the Audience Award in the […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Beijing-based producer-distributor Hishow Entertainment is expanding its cinephile ‘We Love Cinema’ brand with a slate of new acquisitions including recent Sundance winner Josephine and Ah Girl from Singapore’s Ang Geck Geck Priscilla.

Beth de Araújo’s Josephine, starring Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan, scooped both the Grand Jury Prize and the Audience Award in the US Dramatic Competition at this year’s Sundance Film Festival.

Ah Girl, about a seven-year-old girl navigating her parents’ separation, premiered at International Film Festival Rotterdam where it won the Youth Jury Award. It also screened at Shanghai International Film Festival, where it provoked a strong audience reaction, and consequently ranks among the top three highest rated Chinese-language films on Douban this year.

Hishow is also stepping into genre films by releasing all four installments in the Spanish zombie horror franchise Rec, co-directed by Jaume Balagueró and Paco Plaza.

Watch on Deadline

Produced by Filmax and Castelao Producciones, the franchise ran over seven years with episodes including Rec (2007), Rec 2 (2009), Rec 3: Genesis (2012) and Rec 4: Apocalypse (2014). Hishow described the acquisition of the franchise as “a strategic move to broaden its audience beyond conventional arthouse fare and embrace more commercially versatile genres”.

Hishow is also re-releasing Ron Howard’s 2013 Formula 1 racing drama Rush, tapping into the Chinese audience’s nostalgia for recent classics.

Alongside new acquisitions, Hishow has also been hosting the ‘We Love Cinema French Film Festival’ over the summer, at venues in Beijing and Shanghai, screening Cannes selections The Birthday Party and Ulysses, alongside works from Jacques Demy, Éric Rohmer and Jean-Pierre Melville, among others.

Hishow launched its We Love Cinema banner last year, reaching out to cinephiles through curated film events and innovative distribution networks. The company is building online communities on WeChat and other platforms through which members can access exclusive content, early screenings and limited edition merchandise. It also plans to develop offline film entertainment spaces combining cinema, art and new technologies.

“We are dedicated to expanding our We Love Cinema brand to a multidimensional experience, and further build on our innovative marketing and distribution systems to adapt to the fast-changing market,” said Hishow co-founder and CEO Wang Haiyi.

Releases under the banner over the past year have included Hélène Cattet and Bruno Forzani’s Reflection In A Dead Diamond and Adam Elliot’s Memoir Of A Snail and Mary And Max.

title: LA’s Film Liaison Gives Update On Local Production Woes, Asks Lawmakers For “Additional Support” During City Council Meeting
summary: Los Angeles elected officials spent several hours on Wednesday grilling city leaders on ways to streamline the region’s film and television production processes, and the answer largely came down to more funding. “I have approached this work with a simple principle: when a production wants to film in Los Angeles, we work with urgency to […]
content:
Los Angeles elected officials spent several hours on Wednesday grilling city leaders on ways to streamline the region’s film and television production processes, and the answer largely came down to more funding.

“I have approached this work with a simple principle: when a production wants to film in Los Angeles, we work with urgency to find a path to a solution and make that process as easy as possible,” the city’s chief film liaison Steve Kang said to the council members before providing an update on his work over the past year.

Led by chair Adrin Nazarian, the newly formed Ad Hoc Committee on Film, Entertainment and Creative Industry summoned Kang and leaders from the Los Angeles fire and police departments to its first meeting at city hall on Wednesday afternoon. The committee also includes vice chair Traci Park and member Imelda Padilla.

Kang, who is also the President of the Los Angeles Board of Public Works, was appointed by LA Mayor Karen Bass in August 2025 to develop a comprehensive strategy for keeping production in Los Angeles and, potentially, luring back productions that had left. Much of that work revolved around reducing friction in the permitting and regulatory processes, including with FilmLA and other nearby jurisdictions.

Watch on Deadline

In large part, city councilmembers reiterated the concerns of their constituents: progress is being made, but not very quickly. During his presentation to city councilmembers on Wednesday, Kang tried to explain the lengthy timeline for cleaning up LA’s production regulations and leaned on the success the city eventually found with Fox’s Baywatch reboot as proof that his efforts are working.

“It was quite a feat, and we have learned quite a bit of lessons, because in the beginning there were hiccups, of course,” Kang explained to local lawmakers. “In Venice, you needed not only the city, the county, [and] the state coastal commission. You needed the lifeguards, beaches and harbor, the film commission, and so much more, and at the end of the day, we came together as one, including our councilwoman, the mayor, and our supervisor, and many other stakeholders, to hold weekly meetings with Fremantle to discuss what their issues were, and I think we delivered pretty much every one of their requests in real time.”

As vice chair Park pointed out, the question plaguing lawmakers currently is how to replicate that experience with more productions, particularly independent productions with fewer resources.

“Now we know Baywatch is going to be back for Season 2…are there some things that we took from that experience, changes that we can make, and operational changes that might be helpful?” she asked Kang.

Stakeholders spent more than two hours working through the early stages of an answer on Wednesday.

Kang described the “concierge service” that Baywatch received not only to highlight the lengths he’s gone to but also to point out how difficult it would be to scale that level of service for all productions in need of navigating the current thorny system while local agencies work out redundancies and unnecessary roadblocks — especially when the city’s entire film liaison office is one guy: him.

While the city contracts its permitting services to FilmLA, Kang is currently the only local official tasked with coordinating between FilmLA, the city, and the dozens of other regional jurisdictions in the area.

Over the long term, it’s clear that the city needs to make the permitting and other regulatory processes simpler and more consistent. In the short term, Kang says he’s been putting out productions’ individual fires as they arise, as was the case with Baywatch.

“Here at the local level, [we] would love your support in identifying additional resources to really staff up the concierge service, and thank you all for your help in granting an extra position within the Board of Public Works. But unfortunately, that position was frozen until January due to some budgetary forecasts,” he said. “So, would love some additional support in the concierge service and ensure that we really move forward and work together to bring more filming back to Los Angeles.”

Nazarian acknowledged the staffing concerns and vowed to address them, though the committee did not take any votes on Wednesday about these updates, nor the updates provided by LAPD and LAFD. The police and fire departments presented on their own permitting processes and fee structures.

He also pushed Kang on the timeline for enacting the initiatives the council passed in March, including a free micro-shoot permit for smaller productions.

“The city’s current pace of implementation falls short of the industry needs. Quite frankly, it’s unacceptable,” Nazarian said. “So, what’s the exact timeline for making these initiatives available to productions?”

Kang assured that there was a draft of the micro-shoot permit ordinance being drafted imminently, but he said the implementation of the other initiatives have run into cost barriers. In addition to the need for funding for more staffing, Kang explained that some smaller city establishments are having trouble waiving fees with no way to recoup that money elsewhere.

“Many of our departments have not been able to identify the sources of funding to replace some of those funding streams that will be removed,” he said.

The efforts from local leaders come at a time when all eyes are on U.S.-based production. President Donald Trump recently backed a federal film tax incentive after more than a year of behind-the-scenes advocacy from key groups, but that effort still faces quite a few political hurdles before it might become a reality.

At the state level, lawmakers scrambled last month to allow film and television studios a few key exemptions from a recently enacted statewide restriction on corporate tax credits. The amendment allows studios to recoup old tax credits faster, but it doesn’t exempt the companies from the restriction altogether like production advocacy groups wanted. Stakeholders argue that it undercuts last year’s $750 million expansion of the California Film & TV Tax Credit Program. Also, the post production community is pushing for its own tax incentive despite little funding in the state budget.

The statewide incentive was also a brief topic of conversation. When councilmembers questioned why the program cannot be more inclusionary, Kang reasoned that it is already “oversubscribed.”

“There’s more productions applying than the money is available. So I am seeing that we need to at least double [the funding] or [have] no cap. So $1.5 billion is more suitable for our region versus $750 [million],” he said, calling the bump “a good start.”

“So those are some of the problems that we’re having and we’re trying to solve with our state legislators as well,” he said.

title: Beyond Fest 2026 Lineup Includes ‘Primetime’, ‘V/H/S/Mixtape’ And ‘Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother’
summary: Beyond Fest will open its 2026 edition with Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime and close with Bassam Tariq’s Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother as the Los Angeles-set genre festival revealed its full lineup Wednesday. The fest, which runs September 23-October 6, will feature 10 world premieres and four North American premieres within its 81-film lineup, which […]
content:
Beyond Fest will open its 2026 edition with Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime and close with Bassam Tariq’s Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother as the Los Angeles-set genre festival revealed its full lineup Wednesday.

The fest, which runs September 23-October 6, will feature 10 world premieres and four North American premieres within its 81-film lineup, which will include buzzy titles for the L.A. crowd that includes Victorian Psycho, Paper Tiger, 35mm screenings of Ken Russell’s The Devils, the first two episodes of Mike Flanagan’s Carrie and Alex Gibney’s new doc Musk.

Among the world premieres is V/H/S/Mixtape, the latest in the horror anthology series mashing filmmakers Ernest Dickerson, Flying Lotus, Tobias Forge, David Moreau, RZA and Renee Zhan

Watch on Deadline

Special features include Robert Eggers taking over the Egyptian Theatre in person to screen his horror pics The Witch, The Lighthouse, The Northman and Nosferatu in order, along with sneak-peeking his upcoming Werwulf. Organizers also said that among those expected to appear in-person are M. Night Shyamalan (with his own retrospective), Conor Oberst, Jamie Lee Curtis, Matt Berry, Michael Mann, Dolph Lundgren, Danny DeVito, Al Pacino, Martin Brest, Fede Álvarez, Bruce Dern, Rodo Sayagues, Stephen Lang and Jeremy Saulnier.

Restortation and recut screenings include 4K versions of David Lynch’s Wild at Heart, Michael Mann’s Miami Vice, Bong Joon Ho’s The Host and Jackie Chan’s Rumble in the Bronx as well as E. Elias Merhige’s Begotten and Michele Soavi’s The Goodbye Kiss.

Beyond Fest is presented by Mubi and programmed and produced in partnership with the American Cinematheque, with all ticket-sale proceeds going to the latter.

“Beyond Fest is at its most exciting when a world premiere, a radical new filmmaker, a 70mm epic and a once-in-a-lifetime tribute can all exist within the same program,” said Chris LeMaire, American Cinematheque’s Director of Programming. “This slate reflects the range, curiosity and complete commitment to theatrical cinema shared by Beyond Fest and the American Cinematheque.”

Events and screenings will take place at the Egyptian, the Mubi Theatre at the Aero, Directors Village and the Mubi Theatre at the Los Feliz 3.

title: Woody Norman, Malachi Kirby, Tuppence Middleton, Conrad Khan, Kola Bokinni to Star in Urban Horror Thriller ‘Skag & Bone’; Featuristic Produces, UTA on Board (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Woody Norman (“C’mon C’mon”), Malachi Kirby (“Small Axe”), Tuppence Middleton (“Downton Abbey”), Conrad Khan (“Sunny Dancer”) and Kola Bokinni (“Ted Lasso”) are set to star in the British urban horror thriller “Skag & Bone.” The film, which is described as “Top Boy” meets “Talk to Me,” “blends the propulsive energy of a youth-infused crime thriller […]
content:
Woody Norman (“C’mon C’mon”), Malachi Kirby (“Small Axe”), Tuppence Middleton (“Downton Abbey”), Conrad Khan (“Sunny Dancer”) and Kola Bokinni (“Ted Lasso”) are set to star in the British urban horror thriller “Skag & Bone.” The film, which is described as “Top Boy” meets “Talk to Me,” “blends the propulsive energy of a youth-infused crime thriller with supernatural horror,” the producers told Variety.

UTA Independent Film Group has boarded the project to package the film and arrange financing. The agency will also represent North American rights.

Conor Boru will direct from a screenplay he co-wrote with longtime collaborator Ed Hartland. The film marks their second feature together, following Boru’s directorial debut, horror comedy “When the Screaming Starts,” which premiered at FrightFest.

Popular on Variety

Julien Loeffler and James Kermack will produce through their production company Featuristic Films.

Norman will lead the film as Younger, a 16-year-old rehoused with his mother, Maria (played by Middleton), on the notorious Stonemore Estate. After a debilitating stroke leaves Maria unable to work, Younger is forced to become both provider and protector. While attempting to navigate the estate’s unforgiving world alongside his cousin Caleb (played by Khan), Younger is drawn into the orbit of local drug lord Anton (played by Bokinni). Anton offers him protection, money and a possible escape from Stonemore, while an enigmatic local preacher (played by Kirby), presents him with a very different path.

But as a violent gang war tightens its grip on the estate, residents begin disappearing without a trace. An entity known as the Skag & Bone Man is stalking the tower blocks, feeding on the fear, desperation and buried secrets of those who live there. Trapped between the encroaching criminal forces and a supernatural evil no one else will confront, Younger must fight to save his mother and survive the estate long enough to escape it.

Norman received BAFTA and Critics Choice Award nominations for his breakout performance opposite Joaquin Phoenix in Mike Mills’ A24 drama “C’mon C’mon.” His subsequent credits include Netflix’s “The Electric State,” horror feature “Cobweb” and Paul Greengrass’ next film “The Uprising,” where Norman stars alongside Andrew Garfield.

Kirby won the BAFTA Television Award for best supporting actor for his performance as Darcus Howe in Steve McQueen’s “Small Axe: Mangrove.” He currently stars opposite Stephen Graham in Steven Knight’s period drama “A Thousand Blows” for Disney+, and previously led the miniseries “Roots.”

Middleton starred as Lucy Smith in the “Downton Abbey” film franchise and as Riley Blue in Netflix’s “Sense8.” Her credits also include David Fincher’s “Mank,” the Wachowskis’ “Jupiter Ascending,” Netflix limited series “The Defeated” and recent period dramas “The Forsytes” and “Death by Lightning.”

Khan earned BAFTA and British Independent Film Award nominations for his breakout role in Henry Blake’s “County Lines.” His credits also include the final season of “Peaky Blinders,” in which he played Duke Shelby, and BBC crime drama “Baptiste.”

Bokinni is best known for playing AFC Richmond captain Isaac McAdoo in the Emmy-winning Apple TV+ comedy “Ted Lasso.” His additional credits include Netflix’s “Black Mirror,” BBC drama “The Split” and Sky’s “Top Boy.”

Featuristic Films’ recent credits include underwater survival thriller “Breathe Deep,” starring Ingrid Torelli (“Late Night With the Devil”), Michiel Huisman (“The Haunting of Hill House”) and Avani Gregg (“Spider Island”), and crime drama “Salvable,” starring Shia LaBeouf (“Fury”), Toby Kebbell (“RocknRolla”) and James Cosmo (“Braveheart”).

“Conor and Ed have created a world that feels culturally specific, emotionally authentic and internationally accessible,” Loeffler and Kermack said. “‘Skag & Bone’ brings a distinctive new supernatural mythology to the genre and with it announces a bold new voice emerging from within Conor Boru. The caliber of the cast reflects the strength of the screenplay and Conor’s vision, and we are delighted to have UTA joining us as we move towards production.”

“‘Skag & Bone’ is a deeply human coming-of-age story trapped inside a relentless urban nightmare,” Boru said. “At its heart is a boy being forced to grow up too quickly in a world that has abandoned him. Woody possesses the rare combination of vulnerability, intelligence and strength that Younger demands, while Malachi, Conrad, Kola and Tuppence bring extraordinary weight and complexity to the forces shaping his life. It is a dream ensemble, and UTA’s involvement gives us the opportunity to realize this world with the ambition and scale it deserves.”

title: Telekom Srbija’s Content Head on Blueprint for Turning Serbian Production Powerhouse Into Global Player
summary: Telecommunications giant Telekom Srbija is looking to position itself as not only the leading production hub in Serbia but a regional juggernaut for the countries of the former Yugoslavia, exporting local content while attracting international productions to the Balkan nation. “Our next chapter is a deeper connection with our international partners, and presenting not only […]
content:
Telecommunications giant Telekom Srbija is looking to position itself as not only the leading production hub in Serbia but a regional juggernaut for the countries of the former Yugoslavia, exporting local content while attracting international productions to the Balkan nation.

“Our next chapter is a deeper connection with our international partners, and presenting not only Telekom Srbija, but the whole Serbian creative industry, to the global market,” says the company’s chief multimedia and content officer, Aleksandra Martinović.

Speaking to Variety from Belgrade, Martinović outlines Telekom Srbija’s blueprint for the coming years, building on its explosive growth in the past decade, in which the company has produced more than 300 titles, including more than 180 seasons of scripted drama.

Popular on Variety

That output was part of a production boom in a country that’s been the dominant hub of film and television production in the Balkan region since the break-up of the former Yugoslavia. In recent years, the Serbian industry has grown by leaps and bounds, thanks in large part to competition between the telecom heavyweight and rivals including United Media and public broadcaster Radio Television of Serbia.

For Martinović, that period has witnessed a transition at Telekom Srbija from a “traditional ecosystem” for film and TV content to “a very open-minded and sophisticated regional production ecosystem in the last eight or nine years.”

In some respects, that’s meant scaling back, with the company producing fewer shows that are nevertheless more suited for the global market. That includes bigger swings on series like the Serbian Spanish crime drama “Scar,” an ambitious co-production created by Plano a Plano and produced by Cicatriz A.I.E. and Dopamine, in association with RTVE, Prime Video Spain, Telekom Srbija, Canal Plus Poland and RTL Hungary; or the forthcoming romantic dramedy “Crosscurrents,” which is filmed in Montenegro and produced as a regional co-production with that country’s public broadcaster, RTCG.

Such series illustrate what Martinović characterizes as a strategy “to make choices more wisely and make choices more oriented to potential international partnerships and potential distribution to international markets.” One of the company’s most successful shows, the spy thriller “Civil Servant” (pictured), which is now entering its fourth season, has sold to Disney+ Hotstar in India, Brazilian streamer Globoplay, Telemundo and FlixLatino.

Next up is perhaps the company’s biggest gamble to date: the English-language, post-apocalyptic thriller “Sanctuary,” featuring “The Handmaid’s Tale” star Nina Kiri.

Martinović describes the film, which is directed by Filip Kovačević (“Incarnation”) and has been acquired for North America by Vertical, as “a huge risk and a huge challenge” for the company. “It’s very challenging, not only in the sense of authenticity, but also financing,” she says, adding that “international partners and distributors recognizing the value of that project” has been a boon for its backers.

It also illustrates how Telekom Srbija is punching above its weight, according to Martinović. “We are completely aware that we come from a small country,” she says. “Having the kind of content which we were able to sell to HBO, Disney+ and others, for us is very important praise and proof [of what we can do].”

Telekom Srbija’s Aleksandra Martinović Courtesy Telekom Srbija

Along with its prolific production arm, TS Media, Telekom Srbija is betting big on its streaming platform, MOVE — described by Martinović as a “regional Balkan Netflix” — while also “investing more in every element of the production chain,” most notably with the acquisition earlier this year of the Belgrade-based Firefly Studios.

“We have a [360-degree] approach regarding production,” says Martinović. “It’s production, distribution, offering infrastructure through our Firefly Studios, and, of course, selling our own content to international partners.”

The Firefly purchase underscores Telekom Srbija’s ambition to become “a one-stop shop in this part of Europe,” Martinović says, highlighting Serbia’s 25% cash rebate on local spend and some of the most skilled and experienced crews in the region. Among the recent success stories to come out of the country is “Martin Scorsese Presents: The Saints,” the Fox Nation docudrama series executive produced and narrated by Scorsese and produced through Lionsgate Alternative Television. Parts of the project were filmed in Serbia, both at Firefly Studios and locations in and around Belgrade and Pančevo.

This has been a tumultuous time in Serbia, which has faced roiling protests for nearly two years in the wake of a devastating train station tragedy that claimed 16 lives. The turbulence has spread to the country’s film and television industries, with many professionals claiming they’ve been shut out by state-backed media over their political beliefs.

Martinović rejects such criticism. “We are completely aware of the social and political situation, but it doesn’t affect our general strategy,” she says. “We are fighting for the whole creative industry in Serbia. And we open the door for the whole creative industry in Serbia through international projects, through selling our own projects to international broadcasters, through trying to attract international partners…to come here and see what we have to offer.

“Not ‘we’ only as TS Media, but ‘we’ as the Serbian creative industry,” she continues. “We are fighting for all of us — not only for Telekom Srbija, but for all of us. Through Telekom Srbija, which is the biggest player, we are trying to [lift] our whole creative industry and to present them on the global scene.”

title: Serbian Sci-Fi Epic ‘Sanctuary,’ Starring ‘The Handmaid’s Tale’s’ Nina Kiri, Acquired for U.S. Distribution (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Vertical has acquired U.S. distribution rights to “Sanctuary,” an English-language, post-apocalyptic thriller starring “The Handmaid’s Tale’s” Nina Kiri. According to the synopsis, “Sanctuary” is set on a post-apocalyptic Earth, where the discovery of a cryogenically suspended woman provokes fear in a desperate village, sending a young warrior and the mysterious woman on a quest for […]
content:
Vertical has acquired U.S. distribution rights to “Sanctuary,” an English-language, post-apocalyptic thriller starring “The Handmaid’s Tale’s” Nina Kiri.

According to the synopsis, “Sanctuary” is set on a post-apocalyptic Earth, where the discovery of a cryogenically suspended woman provokes fear in a desperate village, sending a young warrior and the mysterious woman on a quest for a lost city and answers that could restore humanity.

Directed by Filip Kovačević (“Incarnation”), the film is produced by Đorđe Stanković, Filip Kovačević and Vukota Antunović for Void Pictures and TS Media, the production arm of telecommunications giant Telekom Srbija. It stars Kiri alongside Dutch actor Jonas Smulders (“Luka,” “Paradise Drifters”) and Serbia’s Darko Perić (“Money Heist”). World sales are being handled by Sublimity, which has also secured several other international deals.

Popular on Variety

Kovačević, who previously directed the 2016 action thriller “Incarnation,” described “Sanctuary” as an attempt to give “a fresh take on dystopian sci-fi, with an original story that takes place in a distinct ‘semi-far future.’”

“The time is near enough so the events that led to the collapse of civilization are still relevant, but far enough that they have been shrouded in mystery and myth,” the director said. “The intent was to make an entertaining genre film that explores the cyclical nature of history and the individual’s role inside it.”

Variety has been given access to an exclusive teaser for the film, which you can watch here:

Producer Đorđe Stanković, of Belgrade-based Void Pictures, said that the filmmakers “set out to make an ambitious science-fiction film from Serbia that could speak to an international audience without losing its own identity.”

“Producing the film was an enormous undertaking, but also proof that genre cinema of this scale can come from this part of Europe,” he said. “We’re incredibly proud of what the team created and excited for the film to now begin its journey to audiences around the world.”

Void’s Vukota Antunović added: “From the beginning, ‘Sanctuary’ was driven by a shared belief in the story and the world we were building. Bringing together an international and domestic cast and a remarkable Serbian crew allowed us to make something that feels both rooted here and genuinely global.”

The ambitious, English-language feature marks a big swing for Telekom Srbija’s TS Media. In a statement provided to Variety, the company said that “Sanctuary” “represents a notable shift in scale and ambition for Serbian production.”

“The film is also part of a wider strategic ambition: to move Serbian scripted production further into the international marketplace, not only as a filming destination but as a source of original IP, creative talent and globally marketable projects,” the statement read.

“With experienced international actors, an English-language screenplay, U.S. distribution already in place and global sales representation, the project offers a case study in how production companies from smaller European markets can approach international genre filmmaking from day one.”

Commenting on the acquisition, Sublimity co-founder Alfredo Lara Orbezo said: “We’re thrilled to have secured key international distribution partners and a terrific U.S. home for a film of ‘Sanctuary’s’ scope and ambition. Its immersive world-building, remarkable production values and unforgettable performances carry the spirit of iconic sci-fi cinema.

“Bringing this film to market alongside Telekom and Void Pictures has been an incredible journey, and we’re proud to share it with audiences worldwide soon.”

content:
Georgi M. Unkovski’s “DJ Ahmet” leads the contest in the cinema categories for the Adriatic Film and TV Awards, which honor the top films and series from Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Croatia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Slovenia and Serbia.

“DJ Ahmet” premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in the World Cinema Dramatic category, and won the Audience Award as well as the Special Jury Award for Creative Vision.

“DJ Ahmet” has seven Adriatic Awards nominations, followed by “Yugo Florida” with six, and “Wind, Talk to Me,” “Mother” and “God Will Not Help,” all with five.

Popular on Variety

“Black Sun” and “The Hollow” lead in the series categories with four nominations each, followed by “Komar” and “Shame,” with three each.

The nominations were decided by a vote by more than 800 members of the Film and TV Academy of the Adriatic Region, film and television professionals from those countries. They will now decide on the winners.

The awards will be presented on Oct. 24 in Porto Montenegro, Tivat, Montenegro.
