Watch on Deadline

“In 1976, Brian Mulroney launched a charm offensive the likes of which Canada had never seen, dismantling the political establishment one dad joke at a time,” notes a film synopsis. “In this psychedelic doomscroll through the mind of a master politician, filmmaker Matthew Rankin charts the flamboyant rise of Canada’s 18th prime minister. From the backwoods of Baie-Comeau to the backrooms of power, Mulroney plots his ascent, trouncing his enemies with a smile and preparing Canada for the unlimited prosperity and permanent unity we live in today.”

President Ronald Reagan and Canadian Prime Minister Brian Mulroney in Ottawa, April 1987. Dirck Halstead/Getty Images

Mulroney possessed a voice as deep as rumbling thunder and a jaw as wide as a dump truck. He came to power in Canada midway through the Reagan era south of the border, and there was a certain bonhomie between the two men who shared some ideological similarities (I went to college in Montreal while Mulroney was in office and distinctly remember seeing graffiti on a wall that suggested the artist’s discomfort with the political alignment of the leaders. The one-word scrawl read: Mulronnie.).

Alas, Mulroney (or Mulronnie, if you prefer) isn’t around to see his name in lights at the festival. He died in 2024 at the age of 84 in Palm Beach, FL, where many Canadian snowbirds are known to migrate. (Ironically, that’s also the Mar-a-Lago home of Donald Trump, a successor to Reagan who has declared a trade war on Canada).

‘Ladies and Gentlemen, Brian Mulroney’ National Film Board of Canada

“First of all,” Canadian filmmaker Matthew Rankin writes in a director’s statement, “I want to say that I think Brian Mulroney is completely amazing. This film is not the hagiography of blessed St-Brian-de-Baie-Comeau, but neither is it an ideological curb-stomping of the man. You can blame it on my Winnipeg upbringing perhaps, but I relate to the world through irony, and a skeptic has little to offer true believers. I am drawn to Mulroney because he was the prime minister when I was a kid and because of what he means as a cinematic phenomenon: I first understood him, as maybe most people did, as a character on television.

“From the many thousands of hours of Mulroney-related news footage and propaganda I have sorted through emerges the full televisual force of an astoundingly charismatic and almost vengefully ambitious man, capable of being duplicitous and even ruthless (but hey, that’s politics), uniquely able to dance so effortlessly between Canada’s notoriously parochial two solitudes and, above all, an astonishing, brilliant political genius.”

Director Matthew Rankin National Film Board of Canada

He writes more. You can read it here.

Ladies and Gentlemen, Brian Mulroney is a production of the National Film Board of Canada. Rankin wrote, directed and edited the film. The producer is Pierre-Mathieu Fortin; executive producer is Pierre-Mathieu Fortin. Cinematography is by Alexandre Lampron; the original score is composed by Christophe Lamarche-Ledoux.

Ladies and Gentlemen, Brian Mulroney premieres Tuesday (Sept. 15) at Royal Alexandra Theatre at 12:59 p.m.

title: Emmys Presenters: Matthew McConaughey, Shailene Woodley and ‘Baywatch’ Reboot Stars Join Lineup
summary: Matthew McConaughey and Shailene Woodley — as well as a selection of Fox’s “Baywatch” reboot stars — are among the names set to present at Monday night’s 78th Emmys on NBC and Peacock.  Also joining the Emmys presenters lineup are stars Jamie Lee Curtis, Stephen Amell, Awkwafina, Noah Beck, Jessica Belkin, Scott Caan, Emma D’Arcy, […]
content:
Matthew McConaughey and Shailene Woodley — as well as a selection of Fox’s “Baywatch” reboot stars — are among the names set to present at Monday night’s 78th Emmys on NBC and Peacock.

Also joining the Emmys presenters lineup are stars Jamie Lee Curtis, Stephen Amell, Awkwafina, Noah Beck, Jessica Belkin, Scott Caan, Emma D’Arcy, Julia Garner, LL Cool J, Woody Harrelson, Hassie Harrison, Paul Anthony Kelly, Thaddeus LaGrone, John Mulaney, Brooks Nader, Emmy Rossum and Sofía Vergara.

Belkin, Harrison, LaGrone, Amell, Beck, and Nader all star in the forthcoming reboot of the iconic 1989 show.

Popular on Variety

Woodley recently took home her first Emmy at the Creative Arts Emmy Awards on Sept. 6, winning the award for guest actress in a drama series for her portrayal of Annie Clay in Hulu’s “Paradise.” Curtis was nominated for outstanding guest actress in a comedy series for her role in FX’s “The Bear.”

As previously reported by Variety, these stars join the already announced presenter line-up, which includes Odessa A’zion, Linda Cardellini, Macaulay Culkin, Alan Cumming, Sally Field, Jon Hamm, David Harbour, Marcello Hernández, Peter Krause, Dan Levy, Julianna Margulies, Annie Murphy, Niecy Nash-Betts, Keke Palmer, Amanda Peet, Amy Poehler, Florence Pugh, Rachel Sennott and Zendaya.

David Boreanaz and Sarah Michelle Gellar will be representing “Buffy the Vampire Slayer” to celebrate the show’s 30th anniversary, as will Kate Jackson, Cheryl Ladd and Jaclyn Smith for the 50th anniversary of “Charlie’s Angels.”

Musician Noah Kahan will perform “Bridge Over Troubled Water” during the show’s In Memoriam segment.

Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon and Jeannae Rouzan-Clay of Jesse Collins Entertainment and Mariska Hargitay will serve as executive producers of the 78th Emmy Awards. As previously announced, Hargitay will host the evening.

title: Seth Rogen Tells TIFF the Best Advice He’s Ever Received: ‘Less Semen, More Emotion!’
summary: It’s extraordinary just how prolific Seth Rogen has been. He began performing stand-up comedy at clubs around his native Vancouver at the age of 13 — around the time he and his buddy Evan Goldberg would write the first draft of “Superbad” — before featuring in the Judd Apatow shows “Freaks and Geeks” and “Undeclared,” […]
content:
It’s extraordinary just how prolific Seth Rogen has been.

He began performing stand-up comedy at clubs around his native Vancouver at the age of 13 — around the time he and his buddy Evan Goldberg would write the first draft of “Superbad” — before featuring in the Judd Apatow shows “Freaks and Geeks” and “Undeclared,” also serving as a writer on the latter, all before the age of 20. Since then, he’s starred in over 40 movies, written 10 and directed two, while creating four TV series. Along with the aforementioned comedy classic “Superbad,” he’s the man behind “Pineapple Express,” “This Is the End” and “The Studio,” while acting in everything from “Donnie Darko” and “Knocked Up” to “Steve Jobs” and “The Invite.”

And that is why, at just 44, Rogen is being honored with the Norman Jewison Career Achievement Award at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival.

Popular on Variety

Prior to the ceremony, Rogen sat down for a career-spanning talk with Geoff Macnaughton, TIFF’s vice president of market programming at theatrical, at the fest’s John Bassett Theatre. The multi-hyphenate has two films at this year’s fest — “Babies,” an ensemble comedy directed by his wife Lauren Miller Rogen, and “Tangles,” an animated film which the Rogens produced. And it was quite the hot ticket (though that’s to be expected for the hometown hero).

The talk began with Macnaughton asking about Rogen’s beginning as a teenage stand-up in clubs around Vancouver.

“My first show was at a lesbian bar called The Lotus. It went very well,” he laughed. “I don’t know. I think I’m very lucky that from a very young age, I kind of knew what I wanted to do. As soon as I realized you could be funny for a living, and I loved films … and I wanted to make movies. I got a video camera and made movies with my dear friend Evan, who I still make movies with today. I was just very fortunate in that I had a very clear idea of what I wanted to do with my life, and my parents were very supportive of it.”

When it comes to the worst advice Rogen’s ever received, he pointed to an actor teacher he had when he was a kid — he entered adult acting classes as a youngster to challenge himself — and remembers her telling him, “Your voice is terrible. You should change your voice because you’ll never have a career sounding like that.”

As for the best advice his mentor Judd Apatow ever gave him, Rogen recalled a moment that “is going to sound crude at face value, but there’s actually a lot of depth to the advice.”

“At one time, when we were shooting ‘Knocked Up,’ we would improvise a lot, and we were improvising and Judd screamed from the other room, ‘Less semen, more emotion!’” Rogen shared. “And honestly, as I’ve gone on to make films, it’s amazing how much I come back to ‘Less semen, more emotion,’ and how many times I’m writing with my friends and we’re making ourselves laugh and then we stop and go, ‘You know what? Less semen, more emotion.’” Those words from Apatow taught Rogen, “That understanding of how to balance humor and emotion and reality and comedy and how to navigate tone.”

As for how productive Rogen has been, he mostly chalks it up to the love of the game and his lack of fear due to decades of training.

“I mean, I love what I do, so it’s not hard to motivate yourself when you really enjoy what you do,” he offered. “And it’s just what I do. If I’m sitting around on a weekend and there’s a thing I’m working on, I work on it, because I want to work on it, not because I have, like, an obligation to work on it.”

He continued: “When you love what you do, it’s easier to motivate yourself. I know a lot of people who love what they do and they do get in their own way creatively. I started so young and I’ve written so much that I don’t pressurize the act of writing. I have no fear — the blank page does not intimidate me. I’m sometimes excited by the blank page.”

Midway through the discussion, the talk moved to “The Studio,” Rogen and his creative partner Evan Goldberg’s Apple TV comedy series about a green studio head (Rogen) navigating the chaotic Hollywood landscape while trying to balance creative fulfillment and the profit motive.

When Rogen was asked if the Emmy-winning show, which satirizes a number of his real-life interactions with Hollywood figures, has complicated his relationship with the industry and its power players, Rogen paused.

“Um … I don’t … Not … I’ve felt it change a little bit my role in Hollywood, I think because we’ve made this thing that is so referential to the specific people that we work with and the specific people in our world,” he reasoned. “It’s funny making a thing where I think, ‘Oh, everyone in Hollywood watches this.’”

“I think in general everything’s the same, but people probably treat us very differently,” he added. “I think for 20 years people just didn’t think we were paying that much attention, like, ‘Oh, these guys are stoned.’”

title: Teary-Eyed Kaley Cuoco Recalls Death of Her ‘8 Simple Rules’ TV Dad John Ritter: ‘One of the Worst Days of My Life’
summary: Kaley Cuoco stepped out Saturday night to pay tribute to her TV dad, John Ritter. She was starring as the television sitcom icon’s daughter on “8 Simple Rules” in 2003 when Ritter suffered a fatal thoracic aortic dissection – a tearing of the heart’s main artery — while on set. “I always cry when I […]
content:
Kaley Cuoco stepped out Saturday night to pay tribute to her TV dad, John Ritter.

She was starring as the television sitcom icon’s daughter on “8 Simple Rules” in 2003 when Ritter suffered a fatal thoracic aortic dissection – a tearing of the heart’s main artery — while on set. “I always cry when I talk about him,” Cuoco said, choking up.

Speaking at the John Ritter Foundation for Aortic Health’s annual Evening From the Heart Gala, Cuoco, who is pregnant with her and fiancé Tom Pelphrey’s second child, recalled meeting Ritter for the first time at a table read for “8 Simple Rules.” She was 16 and playing the “hot girl before I was knocked up,” Cuoco cracked while pointing to her belly. “Young and cool and hot, so I wore like the hottest outfit I could ever find for this table read, like nothing. It had these little spaghetti straps, just ridiculous.”

Popular on Variety

When the Emmy-winning Ritter walked over to her at the table, Cuoco introduced herself. “He gives me a big hug, and he looks at me, and he takes off his jacket, and he puts it on me and says, ‘Don’t ever wear that again,’” Cuoco said, smiling. “It was the best.”

Kaley Cuoco tears up as she recalls the death of her "8 Simple Rules" TV dad, John Ritter. https://t.co/mKOrXGRkwN pic.twitter.com/D1qiWzXu4M — Variety (@Variety) September 13, 2026

Ritter appeared in the first season of “8 Simple Rules” and three episodes of the second before his untimely passing at age 54.

“When he passed away, I don’t want to get dramatic, but I can truly say that was one of the worst days of my life,” Cuoco said. “I remember having to remind myself that I wasn’t his kid. I remember for weeks after, I was like, ‘Gosh, I feel like I lost my dad.’”

Cuoco said Ritter’s talent and on-set leadership continue to inspire.

“He was so funny,” she said. “I took all that with me in life and the jobs I had after. He always has been the north star in my career and somebody who I adore.”

The gala was hosted by Ritter’s widow, Amy Yasbeck, and his son, Tyler Ritter. Yasbeck reunited with her co-stars from the sitcom “Wings” – Tim Daly, Steve Webber and Tony Shalhoub – for a Q&A moderated by Variety’s Marc Malkin. Writer and producer Steve Levitan also joined the panel and recalled how “Wings” was his first writing job in Hollywood.

Ritter’s “Three’s Company” co-star Joyce DeWitt made a surprise appearance to announce a nationwide tour of “Three’s Company” table reads to benefit the foundation. Tyler said that the organization is also hosting a fundraising dinner in October at the original Brady Bunch house in Los Angeles with the show’s Maureen McCormick as host.

According to JRF, 20,000 people suffer an aortic dissection every year in the U.S., with up to 50% of those people losing their lives. With prompt diagnosis and treatment, 80% of people could survive.

For more information, go to johnritterfoundation.org.

title: Hollywood Ventures Group, Canada’s Big Picture Cinema Group, and Morocco’s Pink Sheep Team on Casablanca-Set Thriller ‘The Final Bet’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Hollywood Ventures Group (HVG), Canadian film finance and production outfit Big Picture Cinema Group, and Morocco’s Pink Sheep Productions are teaming up to bring bestselling Moroccan crime thriller “The Final Bet” to the big screen.  The acclaimed Casablanca-set thriller by Moroccan author and award-winning screenwriter Abdelilah Hamdouchi was first published in 2001. It is touted as […]
content:
Hollywood Ventures Group (HVG), Canadian film finance and production outfit Big Picture Cinema Group, and Morocco’s Pink Sheep Productions are teaming up to bring bestselling Moroccan crime thriller “The Final Bet” to the big screen.

The acclaimed Casablanca-set thriller by Moroccan author and award-winning screenwriter Abdelilah Hamdouchi was first published in 2001. It is touted as the first Arabic detective novel to be translated into English.

Set in Casablanca, “The Final Bet” is “a high-stakes psychological thriller following a young man framed for the murder of his wealthy wife. As he fights to prove his innocence, he becomes caught in a web of systemic corruption, romance and judicial intrigue,” according to the provided synopsis.

Popular on Variety

“It is a great source of pride to see ‘The Final Bet’ move from the page to the screen,” Hamdouchi said in a statement.

“A novel lives through language and imagination, and cinema gives its characters, tensions and story an entirely new dimension through image, performance and sound,” the Moroccan author added. “To see this Moroccan story take on a new life as a feature film is deeply meaningful to me, both personally and as a writer,” he added.

Hollywood Ventures Group co-founder Glenn Gainor commented: “While this is a work of fiction, it speaks to a period of profound legal and social change in Morocco and to questions of justice that transcend borders. We’re incredibly proud to help bring Abdelilah Hamdouchi’s story to the screen.”

The producers are shopping the project at the Toronto film market and targeting a 2027 start of production date.

Jayce Barreiro, president and head of production at Big Picture Cinema Group, said: “What sold me on ‘The Final Bet’ wasn’t just the plot, it’s that you can feel the heat and pressure of Casablanca on every page. That specificity is rare,” he added. “And it’s exactly what makes a thriller stick with you instead of just moving past you.”

For Pink Sheep Productions’ Seloua El Gouni and Taha Benghalem, bringing ‘The Final Bet’ to the screen “is both a privilege and a responsibility,” they jointly said in the statement. “Abdelilah Hamdouchi is one of Morocco’s great contemporary storytellers,” they went on, “And his novel carries the intelligence, tension and cultural specificity to become a truly international film without losing what makes it distinctly Moroccan.”

Gainor is adapting the novel for the screen with Taha Benghalem, who will also produce alongside Seloua El Gouni for Pink Sheep Productions and Nelly Kim for Hollywood Ventures Group. Jayce Barreiro, Graem Luis and Michael Aleong of Big Picture Cinema Group are co-financing and producing the project. HVG’s Nabeel Laher, Kiran Kaur and Nicholas Wittcoff will executive produce.

title: Nike Unveils Alex Eala T-Shirt Inspired by Tennis Phenom’s Filipino Heritage

content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

Nike is honoring rising tennis star Alexandra Eala with her very own T-shirt, inspired by her Filipino heritage.

Fresh off her maiden WTA 500 title at the Washington Open, and a third-round appearance at the recent U.S. Open, the 21-year-old’s name adorns the back of this unisex tee, surrounded by a sampaguita motif, paying homage to the official national flower of the Philippines.

Eala’s name is written in cursive script above the iconic Nike logo and the brand’s catchphrase, “Just Do It,” in the same font. The front of the T-shirt features a similar sampaguita-inspired crest design.

This is a 100% cotton tee available in sizes small to XXL, though sizes are selling out online so we recommend adding this to cart while it’s still in stock.

This isn’t the first time Nike has collaborated with Eala. The tennis star has been sponsored by Nike since 2019 and the sportswear brand famously designed a custom hair tie in the shape of a white Sampaguita flower for Eala’s Wimbledon debut last year.

Eala made her 2026 U.S. Open debut, meantime, wearing a NikeCourt Slam women’s tennis dress in an “Old Royal” blue colorway. Official photos on the Nike site feature the tennis star modeling the dress, which boasts a basketball jersey-inspired design and stylized mesh panels along the bottom for ventilation.

Nike AS SEEN ON THE COURT NikeCourt Slam Tennis Dress Buy Now AT NIKE $140

As with most things Eala touches these days though, the dress is almost completely sold out online, with just a few sizes remaining.

The Nike website does have Eala’s “Nike One” duffel in stock though. The versatile bag works as well for the court or the gym as it does for travel, with multiple pockets, a separate compartment for shoes (or wet clothes) and an adjustable strap. Nike says the bag is made with at least 65% recycled polyester fibers.

Eala models the duffel in a black and “iron gray” colorway but the Nike site has three other colors available and on sale.

Eala began the 2026 season as the 50th-ranked player in the world but has climbed to a career-high number 18 in the latest WTA rankings. The athlete has also been credited with popularizing tennis back home while bringing out large crowds of Filipino fans to her tournaments abroad.

title: Emmys Sets Reba McEntire For Dolly Parton Tribute; Adds Big ‘Baywatch’ Contingent, McConaughey & Harrelson, LL Cool J & Caan, More As Presenters
summary: More details are coming into light about the 78th Emmy Awards ahead of the September 14 ceremony broadcast live from the Peacock Theater on NBC and Peacock. Jesse Collins confirmed on Thursday that the show will honor Dolly Parton, who died recently at the age of 80. Deadline hears that the tribute will feature Parton’s […]
content:
More details are coming into light about the 78th Emmy Awards ahead of the September 14 ceremony broadcast live from the Peacock Theater on NBC and Peacock.

Jesse Collins confirmed on Thursday that the show will honor Dolly Parton, who died recently at the age of 80. Deadline hears that the tribute will feature Parton’s longtime friend and fellow country music icon Reba McEntire who is also a NBC star, headlining the network’s hit multi-camera comedy Happy’s Place.

As Deadline reported earlier this week, the telecast also will include a tribute to Catherine O’Hara featuring her Home Alone son Macaulay Culkin and her Schitt’s Creek‘s co-stars Dan Levy and Annie Murphy, as well as a 50th anniversary Charlie’s Angels reunion with Kate Jackson, Jaclyn Smith and Cheryl Ladd and a 30th anniversary Buffy the Vampire Slayer reunion with Sarah Michelle Gellar and David Boreanaz.

NBC and the TV Academy have now announced more Emmy presenters for the ceremony hosted by Mariska Hargitay.

Watch on Deadline

The additions include almost the entire influencer-heavy cast of Fox’s upcoming Baywatch reboot: Stephen Amell, Noah Beck, Jessica Belkin, Hassie Harrison, Thaddeus LaGrone and Brooks Nader all will be on hand to give away trophies and promoted their show.

Serving the same double duty will be LL Cool J and Scott Caan, stars of CBS’ new spinoff, NCIS: New York, Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson, leads of the Apple TV comedy Brothers, as well as Julia Garner, star of Netflix’s limited series The Altruists.

Pulling off a triple duty will be Jamie Lee Curtis, a presenter, co-star/executive producer of NBC’s new comedy series Newlyweds and an Emmy nominee this year for The Bear. (She won in 2024.)

Paradise’s Shailene Woodley is the only guest acting winner from last weekend to tapped as a presenter for the main telecast.

Other additions to the Emmy presenter lineup include comedians Awkwafina and John Mulaney as NBC and the TV Academy are looking to amp up the ceremony’s entertainment content as well as House of the Dragon star Emma D’Arcy; Love Story‘s JFK Jr., Paul Anthony Kelly, Furious star Emmy Rossum and NBC’s own America’s Got Talent judge Sofía Vergara.

Previously announced presenters also include Odessa A’zion, Linda Cardellini, Alan Cumming, Sally Field, Jon Hamm, David Harbour, Marcello Hernández, Peter Krause, Julianna Margulies, Niecy Nash-Betts, Keke Palmer, Amanda Peet, Amy Poehler, Florence Pugh, Rachel Sennott and Zendaya.

Also releaved earlier this week — the In Memoriam segment will feature Noah Kahan performing “Bridge Over Troubled Water.”

Collins, Dionne Harmon and Jeannae Rouzan-Clay of Jesse Collins Entertainment and Mariska Hargitay will serve as executive producers.

title: Peacock Unveils Full Trailer & First-Look Photos For ‘Crystal Lake’ Series Starring Linda Cardellini
summary: The full trailer for Peacock’s Friday the 13th prequel series Crystal Lake, which arrives Oct. 15 on the streamer, has been released. From A24 and creator Brad Caleb Kane, Crystal Lake stars Linda Cardellini as Pam Voorhees, a single mother who has been unable to shake her grief after her young, sickly son Jason tragically […]
content:
The full trailer for Peacock’s Friday the 13th prequel series Crystal Lake, which arrives Oct. 15 on the streamer, has been released.

From A24 and creator Brad Caleb Kane, Crystal Lake stars Linda Cardellini as Pam Voorhees, a single mother who has been unable to shake her grief after her young, sickly son Jason tragically drowned in the town lake almost a year before.

“When two strangers arrive at Pam’s door digging into her past, a disturbing chain of events is set into motion, leaving the townspeople of Crystal Lake wondering: just who is Pam Voorhees?” the plot synopsis teases.

The curse on Crystal Lake is traced back to Jason’s previous drowning as a group sits around a campfire in the dark. The legend begins with Cardellini’s Voorhees, as something still lurks in the woods, only knowing how to kill.

Watch on Deadline

“The time has come, so let out a cheer,” a creepy childrens’ chorus chants at the opening of the teaser clip released earlier today. The whole image turns red as a gruesomely shrouded body is wheeled out on a stretcher, dark hair cascading down the side.

All eight episodes of the horror series will premiere the same date in October. Each episode is around an hour long. Alongside Cardellini, series regulars include William Catlett, Devin Kessler, Cameron Scoggins and Gwendolyn Sundstrom. Recurring cast includes Callum Vinson, Nick Cordileone, Joy Suprano, Danielle Kotch, Phoenix Parnevik.

Executive producers include Brad Caleb Kane, Marc Toberoff, Victor Miller, Robert M. Barsamian, Robert P. Barsamian, Stuart Manashil, Tyson Bidner, Michael Lennox and Roy Lee. Michael Lennox directed the first three episodes. Celine Held and Logan George directed episodes 104-106. Quyen Tran directed the penultimate and finale episodes.

summary: EXCLUSIVE: Comedian Dyon “Mojo” Brooks (aka Mojo Brookzz) has announced that his debut special, I Know You Lying, is set to premiere globally on Netflix on October 6. No word on what Brooks discusses in the special. Filmed at Atlanta’s Center Stage Theatre in December 2025, it’s directed by Mike “Homeless Pimp” Lavin and produced by 3 […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Comedian Dyon “Mojo” Brooks (aka Mojo Brookzz) has announced that his debut special, I Know You Lying, is set to premiere globally on Netflix on October 6.

No word on what Brooks discusses in the special. Filmed at Atlanta’s Center Stage Theatre in December 2025, it’s directed by Mike “Homeless Pimp” Lavin and produced by 3 Nuts Studios’ Lavin, Jason Nower and John-J Sheridan. Brooks, Bernie Cahill and Grant Pennel of Activist Artists Management served as exec producers.

Brooks is a comic who’s recently gone stratospheric — climbing from headlining clubs to theaters to arenas in less than two years’ time. I Know You Lying shares its name with Brooks’s sold-out 2025 headline tour, where he sold more than 100,000 tickets across 40 cities. Prior to that, he was on his 2024 Unhand Me Now Tour, which sold more than 65,000 tickets.

Brooks is currently embarking on his biggest headline run yet, the 42-date international Outta Pocket Tour, spanning the U.S., Hawaii and Europe. The sold-out tour includes two homecoming shows at Chicago’s Wintrust Arena as well as two sold-out performances at New York City’s Beacon Theatre as part of the New York Comedy Festival in November.

Watch on Deadline

With millions of followers across social media, Brooks sold out his 2026 appearance at Netflix Is a Joke Fest and stars in Tyler Perry’s series Miss Governor, which spent multiple weeks in Netflix’s Top 10. He can frequently be seen partnering with the Chicago Bears throughout the NFL Season and will next be seen in Holiday Touchdown: A Bears Love Story, from Hallmark, the NFL and Skydance Sports, this December.

Brooks is repped by Bernie Cahill and Grant Pennel at Activist Artists Management, WME, and Todd Rubenstein at Yorn Levin, Barnes.

title: ‘Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother’ Review: Mahershala Ali Is The Glue That Binds A Dour Texas-Set Action Drama – Toronto Film Festival
summary: Everything and nothing seems to happen in this curiously inert action drama, which stars Mahershala Ali as a philosophical Black Muslim hitman trying to raise three children after the death of his wife. The concept itself not without precedent — Forrest Whitaker calmly practised Tai Chi and composed haikus in between Mafia jobs in Jim […]
content:
Everything and nothing seems to happen in this curiously inert action drama, which stars Mahershala Ali as a philosophical Black Muslim hitman trying to raise three children after the death of his wife. The concept itself not without precedent — Forrest Whitaker calmly practised Tai Chi and composed haikus in between Mafia jobs in Jim Jarmusch’s 1999 Ghost Dog; The Way of the Samurai — but the idea of a violent killer who spends his spare time “home-schoolin’, cookin’ meals and cleanin’” is a new one for a fairly straightforward genre movie.

Ali plays Latif, who we first see at work in a bright but grubby restroom, where the hitman dispatches his victim with a sword. As Latif mops up the copious amount for blood, we see the contents of his toolkit, which contains diapers and wet wipes. Latif, it transpires, is a family man who works hard to keep his underworld ties a secret from his children, the teenage Fatiha (Adia), 10-year-old Qadir (Jahleel Kamara), and baby girl Aziza. Latif’s dedication to Aziza, who refuses to feed, is one of the film’s core themes, as he fights his way out of increasingly intense situations, pausing only to find fresh breast milk for her.

Latif may kill for money, but he has standards; he refuses to use a gun and only takes on assignments if the target really deserves it. He is also a dedicated Muslim and a regular at the mosque, which is a sign early on that this isn’t going to be the average shoot-’em-up. Though usually a very smooth operator, Latif has bungled the latest job for his hander Mike (Laith Nakli). As a result, Latif is pulled in, against his wishes, into an escalating feud between Mike and his sleazy porn-impresario nephew Haddy (Abubakr Ali) and the Pastor Hwan Yoon (John Cho), leader of an aggressive Christian Nationalist militia/cult.

Watch on Deadline

The film has two main moods, firstly the dingy, dimly lit, and sometimes hard-to-hear milieu in which Latif juggles his clandestine activities with parenting, and secondly the harsh, saturated world of Pastor Hwan Yoon, a flamboyant figure played by Cho as a kind of line-dancing Asian David Duke (Your Mother… is nothing if not bold in its casting choices). The later tonal shifts from one mood to the other detract from the film’s more naturalistic vibe, and the first half is much more satisfying. The Pastor feels beamed in from a comic-book movie, and it may be no coincidence that Tariq’s film rose from the ashes of an attempt to collaborate with Ali on a remake of Marvel vampire movie Blade.

Thankfully, there many lighter moments, most revolving around a recurring group of Mormons who come to Latif’s aid when he needs them, Your Mother… is a largely dour attempt to inject a little self-reflection to the traditional hitman set-up. Though 180-degrees from his debut, Mogul Mowgli (2020), Tariq’s film shows a similarly inventive depth to its writing, and it’s tempting to wonder what that film’s star, the intense but spiritual Riz Ahmed, could have done with the same material: Ali certainly has a brooding presence, but the studiedly sonorous solemnity of the performance does become a little wearing.

The most curious thing about Your Mother…, though, is that while it purports to celebrate womanhood, and motherhood in particular (the film takes its title from a famous Muslim parable about an encounter with the Prophet), there aren’t too many women to be seen here. Which is especially odd given Latif’s relationship with his daughter, an old head on young shoulders, is the strongest of all.

The film will find an audience for sure, but it will be a hard sell, being far too intelligent for a mindless action movie and not arty enough for those intrigued by its heady promise of violence and theosophy. The latter should check out the work of another Tariq, Tariq Saleh, whose subtle interrogations of religion and politics in a genre context — notably Cairo Conspiracy (2020) — are much more satisfying, accessible and profound.

Title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother

Festival: Toronto (Special Presentations)

Director/screenwriter: Bassam Tariq

Cast: Mahershala Ali, John Cho, Abubakr Ali, Adia, Giancarlo Esposito

Distributor: MGM Amazon Studios

Running time: 1 hr 52 mins

title: Ella Langley’s ‘Dandelion’ Album Returns to No. 1 Spot on Billboard 200 for First Time in Four Months, So ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Won’t Get Lonely at the Top
summary: Ella Langely’s fans are choosing her “Dandelion” album as a complete piece of work, and not just staying entirely trained on her long-running “Choosin’ Texas” smash. “Dandelion” has returned to the No. 1 spot on the Billboard 200 album chart for a third non-consecutive week at the top. Its previous stay at No. 1 was […]
content:
Ella Langely’s fans are choosing her “Dandelion” album as a complete piece of work, and not just staying entirely trained on her long-running “Choosin’ Texas” smash. “Dandelion” has returned to the No. 1 spot on the Billboard 200 album chart for a third non-consecutive week at the top. Its previous stay at No. 1 was contained to the first two weeks it was out, in late April , but the album has rarely been too far from the summit in the intervening four and a half months.

With the re-ascent of “Dandelion” on the album chart, probably no one needs to be told that this means Langley is again topping both of Billboard’s primary charts, as the indomitable “Choosin’ Texas” remained at No. 1 on the most recent Hot 100 singles chart to be released. The next Hot 100 will be made public on Monday, and chances are good that “Texas” will still be on top, which would mark the song’s 22nd week at No. 1. If that turns out to be the case, Langley will have tied Mariah Carey’s all-time record of 22 weeks for “All I Want for Christmas is You” and be one week away from breaking the record.

“Dandelion” benefited from the ongoing hunger for all things Langley, but also from a Labor Day holiday period in which there were no huge albums debuting. It reached the summit with 67,000 equivalent album units. That’s pretty much par for the recent course for Langley’s album; that figure was down just 1% from the previous week for her. But as Billboard pointed out, 67,000 was the lowest number for a No. 1 album in more than a year. (The last time an album was No. 1 with fewer units was in May 2025, when SZA’s “SOS” topped the chart with just 52,000.)

Popular on Variety

The only new album to make the top 10 was Adela‘s first full-length alum, “Prima,” which bowed at No. 4 with 56,000. The numbers for Adela were tilted toward full-album sales, with 31,000; streaming (SEA) units were good for another 25,000 units, on the strength of 25.94 million on-demand streams. The album debuted at No. 1 on the album sales chart and No. 14 on the streaming albums chart.

Beyoncé’s “B’Day” virtually counted as a new album, reentering the chart for the first time in 18 years due to a 20th anniversary deluxe reissue. It reentered at No. 8 with 38,000 units.

Rounding out the top 10: Olivia Rodrigo, still riding high at No. 2 (with 64,000 units, down just 4%), followed by Morgan Wallen at No. 3, Noah Kahan at No. 5, Ariana Grande at No. 6 (up nine spots thanks to a deluxe edition with live tracks coming out), Rod Wave at No. 7 (down six spots and 57% after debuting at No. 1 a week ago), Drake at No. 9 and Olivia Dean at No. 10.

title: ‘On Behalf of My Son’ Review: A Strained Brazilian Drama About a Mother’s Apology Tour
summary: A Brazilian drama with a powerful premise but labored execution, Gabriel Martins’ “On Behalf of My Son” follows the ripple effects of a tragic bus accident through the eyes of the driver’s mother, Vicentina (Rejane Faria). As she pillories herself with an apology tour, family members of the other victims veer in and out of […]
content:
A Brazilian drama with a powerful premise but labored execution, Gabriel Martins’ “On Behalf of My Son” follows the ripple effects of a tragic bus accident through the eyes of the driver’s mother, Vicentina (Rejane Faria). As she pillories herself with an apology tour, family members of the other victims veer in and out of the spotlight, offering more potentially affecting moments which — by structural necessity — quickly fade from view. Instead, the dramatic focus pivots entirely around Faria’s performance, which unfortunately works against the movie, more often than not.

Opening with unassuming portraits of passengers on their commute in the city of Belo Horizonte, “On Behalf of My Son” begins with an enticing visual setup for individual stories that don’t fully materialize. In the moment, however, Martins imbues tremendous intrigue through snippets of the seemingly distracted middle-aged driver, Wesley (Renato Novaes), and eventually, through the crash itself. Its presentation is shocking and harrowing even if you know it’s coming.

Popular on Variety

The film is at its most vigorous here, when its possibilities lie ahead. In the few moments we see Vicentina before she’s told of this tragedy, the aged character hobbles around on her crutch and performs unassuming household tasks with a captivating, disaffected demeanor, as she curtly cuts off an incoming phone call (the dramatic irony of which only the viewer is aware). Something’s clearly on her mind, and we never need to know exactly what in order for her to feel familiar.

Once she’s told of the tragedy by her younger neighbor Joana (Maíra Azevedo), the routine of having to answer questions and identify her son’s remains allows Faria to shift quickly into thorny territory, promising a film that lives within the rankling discomfort of loss. Wesley’s twin brother (also played by Novaes) briefly comes to visit, practically conjuring Wesley’s ghost as he wanders around the house. However, gossipy TV news stories speculate on Wesley’s intent and state of mind, foisting doubt upon the mourning matriarch as an intimate mystery fades into view. Her way of dealing with the ensuing guilt is to track down the families of the other victims and apologize on her son’s behalf, which, on paper, makes for a fascinating approach to grief, but proves rote and repetitive in execution.

Across nearly two-and-a-half hours, the camera follows Vicentina — from an observant distance when she makes arduous journeys between neighborhoods, and then in closeup when she arrives — as she meets with family members one by one. Few of these sit-downs play out with meaningful differences until late into the runtime, during which Faria is shouldered with dramatic heavy lifting that doesn’t quite gel with her approach. She’s clearly adept at summoning despair when required, but behind the character’s rehearsed apology (which we hear spoken ad nauseam) is a near-identical approach to emoting that proves troublesome when repeated back to back. It’s a performance of loud thoughts writ large across her face, reeled in by pursed lips, resulting in the awkward effect of stilted emotions struggling to be expressed, when the film ought to be at its most volatile.

A handful of those she visits offer riveting work in return — like Fábio Leal as a grieving, battered lover who harbors complicated feelings about his fiancé’s death — but Vicentina becomes a mere interloper to these lives, and they seldom affect her own sense of self, or her sense of contrition, in the process. Those who reject or question her motives are pushed far into the movie’s gradual, calculated unspooling, gesturing at thorny complexities which are never allowed to arise.

The recurring appearance of a mysterious friend of Wesley’s, a death-metal frontman with dwarfism named Fred (a heartbreaking Giovanni Venturini), becomes vital to Vicentina understanding that he lived a life of unexpected interests and frustrations. But before these doubts and mysteries can be folded into her worldview, the focus pivots elsewhere, never allowing even dead ends and unanswered questions to emotionally linger, before the film wraps around to questions of how Vicentina is to live and cope going forward.

Martins has a deft eye for place and environment. Many of the victims are poor, and his camera’s tour of Black Brazilian lives hints at a multifaceted cultural portrait not usually contained within the Brazilian cinema that takes hold in North America. (At least, not since “City of God.”) However, the fluidity of his exploration is hardened early on, thanks to a tedious focus on hitting the same beats with little variety or escalation. It is, at best, intriguing from a safe distance, where its detailed, rundown textures can tell you more about its characters’ struggles than up-close depiction of their inner lives ever does.

title: New York Knicks Player Jalen Brunson — Emmys Host Mariska Hargitay’s Buddy — Expected to Open Show (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: As Monday’s 78th Emmys ceremony fast approaches, Variety has learned of two new highlights that viewers should expect to see: New York Knicks point guard Jalen Brunson is expected to appear via a pre-tape at the start of the telecast, while Reba McEntire has been tapped to perform a Dolly Parton song in tribute to […]
content:
As Monday’s 78th Emmys ceremony fast approaches, Variety has learned of two new highlights that viewers should expect to see: New York Knicks point guard Jalen Brunson is expected to appear via a pre-tape at the start of the telecast, while Reba McEntire has been tapped to perform a Dolly Parton song in tribute to the late icon.

They join previously announced special segments including a “Charlie’s Angels” 50th anniversary reunion with stars Jaclyn Smith, Cheryl Ladd and Kate Jackson, as well as a “Buffy, the Vampire Slayer” 30th anniversary tribute with stars Sarah Michelle Gellar and David Boreanaz. Also lined up: Noah Kahan performing “Bridge Over Troubled Water” to accompany this year’s In Memoriam segment, while Julianna Margulies is expected to present the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award to Michael J. Fox.

With New York Knicks superfan Mariska Hargitay as host, there’s been plenty of speculation about how the team might make an appearance during the Emmys — especially regarding pal Brunson. Hargitay herself has hinted in interviews that she hoped the Knicks would have a presence on the Emmys. She also recently told Variety at the HBO Max Emmy Nominee Celebration that Brunson would “definitely” be getting a role in “Law and Order: Special Victims Unit.”

Popular on Variety

“It’s definitely happening,” Hargitay said of an “SVU” guest spot. “He’s kind of magnificent that way. He is just open and ready. I don’t think there is much Jalen can’t do.”

When asked at last Thursday’s Emmys media day about whether Brunson would show up, executive producers Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon and Jeannae Rouzan-Clay were coy: “She’s got a lot of friends,” Collins said. “Her contacts are deep.”

From what Variety has heard, Brunson will appear at the very start of the show as part of a pre-taped number. Hargitay will then continue that performance live on stage, with dancers and other performers. That will then lead to Hargitay’s opening host monologue.

Later in the evening, McEntire’s Parton tribute performance is expected to be introduced by Sally Field, who starred with Parton in 1989’s “Steel Magnolias.” Field will also be on hand as an Emmy nominee on Monday night, in the lead actress in a limited/anthology series or movie category for Netflix’s “Remarkably Bright Creatures.”

McEntire and Parton, of course, were close friends for decades; among their music collabs was 2021’s “Does He Love You,” a reworking of a McEntire hit. McEntire is star of NBC’s “Happy’s Place.”

Other presenters previously announced include “DTF St. Louis” stars Linda Cardellini and David Harbour, who won Emmys last weekend for outstanding limited/anthology actress and actor. Additionally lined up are Odessa A’zion, Macaulay Culkin, Alan Cumming, Sally Field, Jon Hamm, Marcello Hernández, Peter Krause, Dan Levy, Julianna Margulies, Annie Murphy, Niecy Nash-Betts, Keke Palmer, Amanda Peet, Amy Poehler, Florence Pugh, Rachel Sennott and Zendaya.

And then announced on Sunday as presenters were Jamie Lee Curtis, Stephen Amell, Awkwafina, Noah Beck, Jessica Belkin, Scott Caan, Emma D’Arcy, Julia Garner, LL Cool J, Shailene Woodley, Hassie Harrison, Paul Anthony Kelly, Thaddeus LaGrone, John Mulaney, Brooks Nader, Emmy Rossum and Sofía Vergara.

Plus, expect Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson — stars of the upcoming Apple TV series “Brothers” — to appear together and one might assume, further milk the speculation that they might actually be related.

title: ‘Mr. Irrelevant’ Trailer: David Corenswet Plays NFL’s John Tuggle In Underdog Biopic About Late NY Giants Player
summary: Although he’s used to playing a man of steel, David Corenswet’s latest role in Mr. Irrelevant is a classic underdog story. On Sunday, Paramount and Skydance Sports released the trailer for the Jonathan Levine-helmed biopic about the late New York Giants running back, which premieres on Christmas, recounting his final months before his death at […]
content:
Although he’s used to playing a man of steel, David Corenswet‘s latest role in Mr. Irrelevant is a classic underdog story.

On Sunday, Paramount and Skydance Sports released the trailer for the Jonathan Levine-helmed biopic about the late New York Giants running back, which premieres on Christmas, recounting his final months before his death at age 25 of cancer in 1986, three years after he was drafted by the NFL team.

A true underdog, Tuggle was the final draft pick of the final round in 1983. He defied expectations on the field and off for his then first-year head coach, Bill Parcells (Michael Shannon), his newfound love (Isabel May) and his team, proving that remarkable hope and perseverance can transcend even the greatest challenges.

Written by Nick Santora, the film also stars David Krumholtz, Tuwaine Barrett, Thaddeus LaGrone, Alexander England, Spencer House and Tandi Wright.

Watch on Deadline

Producers include David Ellison, Dana Goldberg, Don Granger, Jonathan Levine, Gillian Bohrer and Nick Santora, along with executive producers Jesse Sisgold, Jason T. Reed, Sandino Moya-Smith, Stan Wlodkowski, Pete Chiappetta, Anthony Tittanegro, Andrew Lary, Ross Ketover, Ken Rodgers and Jessica Boddy.

title: Pierce Brosnan Says Next James Bond Could Be “Someone That None Of Us Know About”; Tom Ellis Reveals Brosnan Said He’d “Make A Good Bond”
summary: Many suggestions have circulated about who could be the next 007 agent in the James Bond film franchise, and Pierce Brosnan has a new take on where the studio could go. Auditions for the role in the Denis Villeneuve film are already underway and have taken place over the summer, and Brosnan recently said there […]
content:
Many suggestions have circulated about who could be the next 007 agent in the James Bond film franchise, and Pierce Brosnan has a new take on where the studio could go.

Auditions for the role in the Denis Villeneuve film are already underway and have taken place over the summer, and Brosnan recently said there are “lots of great actors” up for the role, but he thinks they might cast someone unknown.

“I have no desire to see myself in Bond. I’m just a member of the audience now awaiting the next Bond and wishing him well,” Brosnan said in an interview with The Times. “There are lots of good hats in the ring. Lots of great actors. I see it. I follow it. They could probably just go left-field and pick someone that none of us know about.”

When it came to actually saying a name, Brosnan said, “I wouldn’t pick anyone. My wife told me not to say anything and I’ve said too much. Because once I say something, it goes [everywhere] and I get hanged.”

Watch on Deadline

Although Brosnan didn’t drop a name, his Thursday Murder Club co-star Tom Ellis said that the former M16 agent told him he would “make a good Bond.”

“He did tell me he thought I’d make a good Bond, and I was like, ‘Pierce, I think I’m probably too old now. But I’ll take it from you, mate. I’ll take it from you,'” Ellis told Metro UK.

Brosnan began his tenure as the 007 agent in 1995 with GoldenEye, directed by Martin Campbell. The actor would reprise his role in 1997’s Tomorrow Never Dies, 1999’s The World Is Not Enough, and 2002’s Die Another Day. Daniel Craig succeeded Brosnan for 2006’s Casino Royale and ended his tenure with 2021’s No Time to Die.

In March of this year, Deadline reported that Nina Gold had closed a deal to become the casting director for the next James Bond film. Gold’s credits include HBO’s Game of Thrones, the Netflix series The Crown, and five films in the Star Wars franchise.

title: Mattel Studios Boss Says “We All Want To See The ‘Barbie’ Sequel” But Timing Remains Unclear
summary: Barbie producer and Mattel Studios boss Robbie Brenner talked about a follow-up to the hit live-action movie in a session at the Toronto Film Festival. “We all want to see the Barbie sequel,” she told the TIFF crowd. “I want to see it too. I’m sure at some point, one day, there will be one.” […]
content:
Barbie producer and Mattel Studios boss Robbie Brenner talked about a follow-up to the hit live-action movie in a session at the Toronto Film Festival. “We all want to see the Barbie sequel,” she told the TIFF crowd. “I want to see it too. I’m sure at some point, one day, there will be one.”

Timing, however, remains an open question, with other Barbie projects also in the works. “Right now, we’re focused on, and we’re making, an animated Barbie movie with Chris Meledandri. That is super exciting, and yes, we will continue to do other Barbie things as well.”

Brenner, President of Mattel Studios and Chief Content Officer, was speaking at TIFF: The Market, the sales and conference section of the Toronto Film Festival.

Watch on Deadline

She earned an Oscar nom for producing Greta Gerwig’s $1.4BN-grossing live-action Barbie movie, which starred Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling. It was produced in partnership with Robbie and Tom Ackerley of LuckyChap and David Heyman.

Speculation about the sequel reached fever pitch in July when a New York Times article said Warner Bros. has until December to close a deal with Robbie, Gosling and Gerwig, the co-writer and director of the first movie. If a sequel is not put into active development by the end of the year, the rights revert to Mattel. The toymaker then will not be permitted to use any previous iteration of Barbie and will face a full reboot at that point in time.

Brenner did dish some stories about making the first pic. She said she’d heard 40 or 50 pitches before Gerwig raised her hand. “[Gerwig] had a vision of what she wanted to do and said, ‘I love Barbie. I grew up with Barbie; I don’t know what the story is but I know that it’s gonna live in between a high heel and a Birkenstock’… so we went on the journey with her.”

She explained: “When Greta said the thing about the high heel and the Birkenstock… that was the aha moment.”

At a corporate level, “Barbie really put Mattel on the map in terms of content and people knowing that we’re making movies” Brenner said. “That legitimized [Mattel] and it was, ‘Okay, they’re really taking swings and they’re making bold choices.’”

title: Jeff Daniels Leading Comedy ‘The Reception’ About Chaotic Scottish Wedding; Trudie Styler Directing & Beta Launching TIFF Sales
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Two-time Emmy winner and five-time Golden Globe nominee Jeff Daniels has been set to lead comedy The Reception, about a chaotic Scottish wedding. Trudie Styler is directing for her and Celine Rattray’s banner Maven Screen Media and Piers Tempest’s Tempo Productions. Beta Cinema is launching international sales at this week’s TIFF market. CAA Media […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Two-time Emmy winner and five-time Golden Globe nominee Jeff Daniels has been set to lead comedy The Reception, about a chaotic Scottish wedding.

Trudie Styler is directing for her and Celine Rattray’s banner Maven Screen Media and Piers Tempest’s Tempo Productions.

Beta Cinema is launching international sales at this week’s TIFF market. CAA Media Finance is representing North America.

Pre-production is underway, with filming set to begin next month and additional high-end cast being finalized now. The movie will shoot in a castle near the famous Loch Ness, just outside Inverness in Scotland.

The synopsis reads: “Set at a grand Scottish estate, a wedding party proceeds despite the unfortunate absence of the bride and groom. Felix has abandoned Victoria at the altar, leaving their parents, family and friends to navigate a lavish but increasingly chaotic reception. What begins as an attempt to keep up appearances spirals into a day of calamity, hilarity, and unexpected connections, as the in-laws, staff, and guests confront their own relationships amidst the fallout.”

Watch on Deadline

Trudie Styler (Up Against It) directs and produces the feature with Maven Screen Media business partner Celine Rattray (Unicorns) producing alongside Piers Tempest (The Wife). Recent features for Maven include Scarlett Johansson’s directorial debut of Eleanor the Great which premiered at Cannes Film Festival last year.

Screen veteran Daniels, known for hit movies and series including Gettysburg, The Newsroom and Dumb and Dumber, has movies 2034 and Starman upcoming.

The Reception is the fifth directing project from Styler. Her most recent project Up Against it is premiering this week at TIFF. Previous directing projects include The Sweatbox, a documentary commissioned by Disney which she co-directed; her directorial debut Freak Show, which was nominated for three awards at Berlin in 2017 and Posso Entrare? An Ode to Naples, which earned Italy’s Globo d’Oro for best documentary in 2024.

title: Dead Boys Guitarist Cheetah Chrome Dies at 71
summary: Eugene Richard O’Connor, the punk rocker known as Cheetah Chrome and guitarist of the Dead Boys, died Sunday, his bandmates confirmed on Instagram. He was 71. “We are incredibly sad to announce the news of the passing of our beloved friend and bandmate Cheetah Chrome,” the band wrote in the post. “Cheetah was a true original, […]
content:
Eugene Richard O’Connor, the punk rocker known as Cheetah Chrome and guitarist of the Dead Boys, died Sunday, his bandmates confirmed on Instagram. He was 71.

“We are incredibly sad to announce the news of the passing of our beloved friend and bandmate Cheetah Chrome,” the band wrote in the post. “Cheetah was a true original, an architect of the punk rock movement. A one-man hurricane tearing up the musical landscape with his feral guitar riffs and manic energy. Beyond all that Cheetah was also just a really sweet guy that loved rock-roll. We extend our deepest condolences to Cheetah’s family, friends and fans around the world. His music lives on and will continue to inspire others for generations to come. We ask for privacy during this difficult time. Godspeed Cheetah. Tony, Chris, Mark and the entire Dead Boys family.”

Cheetah Chrome was a Cleveland, Ohio-born punk-rock musician based in Nashville. He started as a guitarist in Rocket from the Tombs in 1974 before starting Frankenstein with Dead Boys members Stiv Bators and Johnny Blitz. The band quickly evolved into Dead Boys.

Popular on Variety

The three-piece band released their first album, “Young, Loud and Snotty,” in 1977 and their second, “We Have Come for Your Children,” in 1978 before breaking up a year later. The band reunited for a series of live performances over the years, but never put out another studio album. In honor of its 50th anniversary, the band had plans to tour their debut album in 2027.

O’Connor is survived by his wife, Anna O’Connor, and his 14-year-old son Rogan, who reside in Nashville.

title: Sara Bareilles on ‘Good Grief’ and Finding Joy in the Tough Stuff: ‘Grief Is the Mothership of This Record, but It Carries Release, Hope, Optimism and Connection’
summary: She could have called it “Great Grief,” but that would have been immodest. Sara Bareilles’ “Good Grief,” her first new studio album in seven years, is one of the year’s finest achievements from a singer-songwriter… and its purely musical delights are such that you might feel that way about it even if you haven’t been […]
content:
She could have called it “Great Grief,” but that would have been immodest. Sara Bareilles‘ “Good Grief,” her first new studio album in seven years, is one of the year’s finest achievements from a singer-songwriter… and its purely musical delights are such that you might feel that way about it even if you haven’t been through some shit, as they say.

If you have, all the better to relate to the record and its sometimes somber, sometimes playful meditations on a whole catalog of grief (and grievances): losing best friends to death at too early an age, dealing with fertility struggles, running to and away from the precipice of love, eroding women’s rights, mental health issues, and the challenges of continuing to believe in the promise of America.

Variety had an in-depth conversation with Bareilles about the new album and many of the tough or inspiring issues related to it — along with touching on a recently released documentary film that captures some of the making of the record, “Sara Bareilles: Good Grief,” and her first real tour of the 2020s, which has just gotten underway and includes dates Sept. 18-19 at Radio City Music Hall and Oct. 12-14 at L.A.’s Dolby Theatre. (Scroll down to see a full list of tour dates.)

You’ve gone a pretty long time between solo albums now. Of course you’ve had “Girls5Eva” and composing your next stage musical (“The Interestings”) and plenty of other things occupying yout time. Does it feel any different putting this one out into the world now than in times past?

It does feel different. It’s been a minute since I’ve done this. … But I feel pretty peaceful with the “it takes the time it takes” kind of method around this part of my life. I tend towards a pretty hefty amount of time between records anyway. It takes me a long time to have something else to say. It’s been seven years since my last record, and hopefully it was somewhat worth the wait. I was writing about this this morning; I journal every morning. I found so much catharsis and healing in the making of this record, just going through this period of time with the loss of friends and just the hardships that have happened over the last handful of years in my own personal journey. I felt so grateful to get to put some of those experiences somewhere. So it feels like the timing is right on time, for me personally. I’m hoping it lands for the audience in that way as well.

There are “mature themes” on this record. A lot of your audience has sort of grown up with you and dealt with at least some of these same things you’re writing about. Do you suppose you have to have a certain amount of life experience to relate to an album like this? Or if someone is 20 and hasn’t really lost anybody yet in this life, can they still be impacted by it the same way?

It’s like, yeah, did I make an old person’s record? [Laughs.] In some ways, yeah, I think what I was attuned to when I was much younger, in my late teens and 20s, the stuff that really kept me up at night, it usually had to do with matters of the heart, like a fixation on a romantic love. But I do feel like, as like a global community, the world feels like it has, I would say, wisened. I think I mean we’ve all sort of aged up a little bit together. I feel this in my young nieces and my younger sister and friends that I have that are much younger: There is a kind of awareness about things that I was not as attuned to. I don’t know if it’s about the existential drama of life and death, but I do think that there is a kind of antenna turned towards bigger-picture themes than maybe I was quite aware of when I was that age. I see these young people dealing with the climate crisis and watching what’s happened politically and how divided our world feels. And the way they feel amid the emotionality of the drama of your youth — I do feel like there’s a lot of grief in there. And I don’t think anybody ever called it that for me. But I’m really curious to hear feedback about who relates to this and who doesn’t.

This album is kind of bookended with songs at the beginning and end that deal with grief in a more obvious way, maybe, with death and loss. But you touch on a lot of subjects. Is there a way in which you thought of “Good Grief” as kind of a concept album where even the songs that aren’t so overtly about that are also themed to grief?

There’s a line in the sons called “Ladies in a Line,” and the lyric is “Grief is the blanket, and it covers everything.” I do think that grief is sort of like the mothership of this record. It’s like the home base for all of these experiences… I think that what I’ve learned about grief in my own personal relationship to the experience of it is that it’s not just one thing. It carries joy, it carries release, it carries hope and optimism and connection and a lot of really buoyant themes. So yeah, I think that even a song like “Idiot Heart,” which is about wanting to be led to the edge by a kind of an urgency towards love, there is grief in that too, because what we love, we lose. And so I can kind of find it in everything. But I don’t look at it as a somber experience. I just look at it as a really rich experience.

title: ‘Buddy’ Scaring Up Cash & Tattoos, ‘Runner’ Dashes Out As Indies Crowd Top 10 – Specialty Box Office
summary: Indies including newcomer Runner and holdover Buddy nabbed five of the top 10 spots at the domestic box office this weekend. If I Go Will They Miss Me had a terrific exclusive opening in L.A., and documentary American Doctor passed $400k. Late-summer original horror-comedy hit Buddy from Roadside Attractions and Saban Films grossed $3.5 million in […]
content:
Indies including newcomer Runner and holdover Buddy nabbed five of the top 10 spots at the domestic box office this weekend. If I Go Will They Miss Me had a terrific exclusive opening in L.A., and documentary American Doctor passed $400k.

Late-summer original horror-comedy hit Buddy from Roadside Attractions and Saban Films grossed $3.5 million in week three, landing at no. 6 on 1,719 screens with an estimated $21.2 million cume. The R-rated pic about kids on a ’90s style retro television show who defy their orange unicorn host, voiced by Keegan-Michael Key, fell just 39% for the weekend. It’s Roadside’s fifth highest grossing film and strongest box office performer since Covid. Buddy has over 1 million followers on TikTok and Roadside is hearing anecdotally that moviegoers are coming back three and four times to see it and bringing others. Sepulveda Tattoo in Duarte was mobbed yesterday offering a meet-up with Buddy and a free, exclusive Buddy tattoo designed by Hunter Chao.\

thanks to all my best buddies who made our friendship permanent 🧡 pic.twitter.com/mO0HdGcfu2 — BuddytheUnicorn (@Buddy_The_Uni) September 13, 2026

Among new releases, Angel Studios’ Runner starring Reacher’s Alan Ritchson and Owen Wilson is no. 4 at $6.67 million on 2,568 screens; Neon’s South Korean monster movie Hope at no. 8 in 1,560 theaters on a $3.3 million weekend ($5 million cume since its Wed. debut); and Andrew Garfield-starring The Uprising from Focus Features with $3.2 million at 2,068 locations pulling up at no. 9.

Watch on Deadline

Angel was upbeat about Runner’s A- CinemaScore, calling the release a “significant theatrical milestone” for the company. It had a great summer with Young Washington, which topped out at $47 million.

Coyote vs. Acme from Ketchup Entertainment, at 3,355 locations, is no. 5 this weekend, loping along with a $6.23 million gross and $47.8 million cume.

A24’s holdover Tony continues to serve up strong numbers with $497k on 380 screens in week six for a cume of $14.7 million. Onslaught is at $278k on 1,252 screens in week two for a cume of $3 million.

Prathyangira Cinemas’ Hanuman Ansh debuted to $740k from 200 locations, as per Rentrak.

Limited: If I Go Will They Miss Me starring Danielle Brooks and J Alphonse Nicholson and directed by Walter Thompson-Hernandez, a Rich Spirit release, opened exclusively at AMC’s Century City in Los Angeles to $42.25k with multiple sellouts and additional showtimes added to heep up with demand. This is the second-highest opening of the year for a solo engagement since Maddie’s Secret from Magnolia Pictures with $58k (at the IFC). Expands to 250 theaters next week.

Watermelon Pictures’ American Doctor topped $400k with a $66.2k gross in week five on 65 screens. The documentary follows three U.S. doctors who voluntarily go to Gaza to help save as many lives as possible.

Event cinema: Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger from Disney opened at $1.435 million at 1,225 theaters.

title: Cynthia Erivo’s Riveting ‘Prima Facie’ Performance Earns TIFF Standing Ovation
summary: Cynthia Erivo already earned two best actress Oscar nominations for portraying Harriet Tubman and the green-skinned Elphaba in “Wicked” — not to mention her Tony-winning work in “The Color Purple” — but her latest film, “Prima Facie,” might be her most challenging high-wire act yet. She pulled it off, according to the audience at the […]
content:
Cynthia Erivo already earned two best actress Oscar nominations for portraying Harriet Tubman and the green-skinned Elphaba in “Wicked” — not to mention her Tony-winning work in “The Color Purple” — but her latest film, “Prima Facie,” might be her most challenging high-wire act yet.

She pulled it off, according to the audience at the Toronto International Film Festival on Sunday night. “Prima Facie” held its world premiere at the Roy Thompson Hall, where the crowed rewarded Erivo and her filmmakers with a standing ovation for the harrowing drama.

Erivo plays Tessa, a rising legal star in London who represents defendants of sexual assault. When she’s raped by a colleague, the lawyer finds herself at odds with the patriarchal legal system she so often used to win.

Popular on Variety

White (“Bleak House,” “Jane Eyre,” “Woman Walks Ahead”) directed the adaptation by playwright Suzie Miller from her globally acclaimed one-woman show. The film is one of the hottest sales titles on the block at TIFF. Jodie Comer won the Tony and Olivier awards for the stage version, and Erivo proved equally captivating on the big screen — albeit under a the very racial and socioeconomic context. Erivo’s Tessa is a woman of color from a working class background, navigating a system bolstered by white men dating back to medieval times in the London court.

“We got the chance to meet a lot of Black women barristers. I understood that they sort of work in a different rhythm to everybody else, and the way they approach court is very much making it their own,” Erivo said at a Q&A following the premiere “I wanted that for Tessa, I wanted her to have this outside life that influenced the way she approached [her work].”

Also featured among the supporting cast are Daniel Ings, Elizabeth Dulau and Simon Russell Beale. More to come …

title: Seth Green Says He Was Never Invited Back for the Canceled ‘Buffy the Vampire Slayer’ Reboot
summary: Seth Green revealed in the Sept. 8 episode of “The McBride Rewind” podcast that he was not involved in any discussion of reprising his role as the werewolf guitarist Oz in Hulu’s canceled “Buffy the Vampire Slayer” reboot.  “I was not part of those talks,” he said in the episode.  While he was not involved, […]
content:
Seth Green revealed in the Sept. 8 episode of “The McBride Rewind” podcast that he was not involved in any discussion of reprising his role as the werewolf guitarist Oz in Hulu’s canceled “Buffy the Vampire Slayer” reboot.

“I was not part of those talks,” he said in the episode.

While he was not involved, he would return if asked.

“If they wrote an Oz story, I’d love to see where Oz is right now,” he said.

Popular on Variety

Reps for 20th Century and Hulu did not immediately respond to Variety‘s request for comment.

The original seven-season series followed Sarah Michelle Gellar as Buffy Summers, a young woman who slays vampires, demons and other supernatural creatures with the help of her friends. Inspired by the film of the same title, “Buffy the Vampire Slayer” ran from 1997 to 2003. It was set to be rebooted by Hulu in March 2025 but was cancelled after the pilot.

“I am really sad to have to share this, but I wanted you all to hear it from me. Unfortunately, Hulu has decided not to move forward with ‘Buffy: New Sunnydale,’” Gellar said in a video on Instagram. “I want to thank Chloé Zhao, because I never thought I would find myself back in Buffy’s stylish yet affordable boots. And thanks to Chloé, I was reminded how much I love her and how much she means not only to me but to all of you. And this doesn’t change any of that, and I promise if the apocalypse actually comes, you can still beep me.”

The project, titled “Buffy the Vampire Slayer: New Sunnydale,” would have starred Ryan Kiera Armstrong as the new slayer, with original series star Gellar returning as Buffy. The pilot also starred Faly Rakotohavana as Hugo, Ava Jean as Larkin, Sarah Bock as Gracie, Daniel di Tomasso as Abe and Jack Cutmore-Scott as Mr. Burke.

title: Israel’s Minister of Culture Threatens to Revoke Israeli Citizenships of ‘NAZA’ Filmmakers
summary: Israel’s Minister of Culture Miki Zohar threatened to revoke the Israeli citizenships of “NAZA” co-directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor. He called the documentary “shocking” and accused the filmmakers of “betraying the state.” “The self-loathing that burns in the creators, who are willing to harm their homeland just to get applause from antisemites around the […]
content:
Israel’s Minister of Culture Miki Zohar threatened to revoke the Israeli citizenships of “NAZA” co-directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor. He called the documentary “shocking” and accused the filmmakers of “betraying the state.”

“The self-loathing that burns in the creators, who are willing to harm their homeland just to get applause from antisemites around the world, is inconceivable and constitutes a betrayal of the state,” Zohar wrote. “As Minister of Culture, I will act immediately to revoke the Israeli citizenship of these despicable creators for betraying the state.”

“NAZA” shows “in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza,” according to its official logline. The film recently premiered at the Venice Film Festival, where it received overwhelming acclaim. The standing ovation at the film’s premiere clocked in at 24.5 minutes, the longest in festival history. Abraham and Szor were awarded the special jury prize for their work.

Popular on Variety

After accepting the award, Abraham said, “It’s honestly not very easy to stand here, thinking of all the Israeli politicians and journalists who are now attacking this film and denying it without even seeing it. So much is being done not to look at reality.”

He added, “We believe that the denial of a crime is what helps it persist, and that’s why it’s especially important for us that Israelis watch this film — it’s our country that is doing these crimes — that Europeans watch it, and especially here in Italy because your government and the German government are blocking pressure on Israel that can end this, that Americans watch it because that country is funding much of the killing.”

title: ‘Prima Facie’ Review: Cynthia Erivo Is Lawyer Who Finds Herself The Victim Of Rape, Which Goes On Trial – Toronto Film Festival
summary: In 2022 Jodie Comer took the theatrical world by storm in Suzie Miller’s one-woman play, Prima Facie, which won Olivier Awards for the West End production, including Best Actress for Comer who repeated her triumph on Broadway and won the Tony Award. Now, for whatever reason, Comer did not reprise her role for the film […]
content:
In 2022 Jodie Comer took the theatrical world by storm in Suzie Miller‘s one-woman play, Prima Facie, which won Olivier Awards for the West End production, including Best Actress for Comer who repeated her triumph on Broadway and won the Tony Award.

Now, for whatever reason, Comer did not reprise her role for the film version which has been opened up in a nod to more conventional courtroom dramas. Screenwriter Miller and director Susanna White take it from the spare stage and the inner thoughts voiced by Comer’s English Barrister, and try to keep the same idea through the extensive use of voice over thoughts of the Erivo character, Tessa. It’s a gamble that perhaps doesn’t reproduce the power of the stage production.

Prima Facie signifies a legal claim that has sufficient evidence to proceed to trial or judgment. In this case, that claim comes from a lawyer who finds herself the victim of what she describes as sexual assault, a rape, by a colleague with whom she has a consensual sexual relationship that crosses the line one night. What makes this unique is that Tessa is a dedicated Barrister who often defends men charged with sexual assault, using every trick in the legal book to get them off. The film opens depicting her efforts in the courtroom, as well as in her personal life so we get to know her as the successful professional she is.

Watch on Deadline

Soon though, she starts up a romantic relationship with a longtime colleague, a nice fellow lawyer and seemingly good guy, Julian (Daniel Ings). As he asks for her help one night after hours in the office, it leads to much more. We hear her inner thoughts — “I really want this” — as the two draw closer, leading to their first sexual encounter. It appears this pair of colleagues are the perfect match and on a second date they end up at her place after a nice dinner out, first stopping for a couple of bottles of wine he purchases. She already had poured down a lot of sake, and now is freely drinking wine. They have sex, it goes well, but as the night wears on Julian notices she is not in bed. Instead he finds her on the floor of her bathroom, clearly ill no doubt from all the drinking, and he picks her up and carries her back to bed.

It is here he makes a very bad decision to insist they go for another round of sex, but she is sick and doesn’t want to. Selfishly, he proceeds anyway ignoring her clear lack of desire. Afterward, he rolls over and falls asleep. Disturbed, she quietly gets up and leaves in the pouring rain, first arguing with a cabbie and then just urging him to take her to the nearest police station where she recounts what happened and labels it rape.

The next day at the office Julian can’t understand where she went (it was her apartment after all) or why she is suddenly so cold to him, “What did I do wrong?” he asks. Once he finds out she has filed a rape charge against him, he realizes that his whole life and career could possibly be destroyed. Colleagues wonder why she would do this, and soon she has requested a transfer to another legal office. Some years pass and the case is finally ready for trial. Tessa is about to find out what it is like to be on the other side.

The voiceover device really comes into play here as Tessa knows exactly the drill victims of sexual assault will be put through and thinks to herself she is so aware they will never trap her. She fears, though, losing to the very methods she once employed herself.

The main defense attorney, Hugh Dalton KC (an excellent Simon Russell Beale) even accuses her of setting Julian up so that she could get a job in another jurisdiction, and he also repeatedly points out this affair was consensual, not the usual case we see in violent sexual assault cases (at least those depicted in movies).

Director White, in trying to show there is a broad range to the definition of rape, has presented this one not as black and white but with shades of gray. Julian is never seen as a bad person, but one who genuinely likes and is attracted to Tessa, thus his failure to recognize doing anything wrong that night. For him the worst was he was insensitive to her wishes and pushed way too far, but he is not portrayed as evil or abusive, just a guy who made a very bad call after drinking too much on a night they both drank too much. He also happens to be the son of a top judge who sits in the rafters.

It is all on the victim it appears, and that is clearly Miller’s point (she also has a legal background herself); the startling statistics show the overwhelming number of verdicts in sexual assault cases do not favor the accuser. Tessa’s abrupt change probably has as much to do with what physically happened to her as the psychological pain of the realization she has been on the wrong side of justice too often in these cases in court.

Prima Facie, as it has done on stages around the world, will no doubt spark conversation and arguments afterward, and it will be interesting to see what impact this film version has as the assaulter in this case is not presented as someone who would ever knowingly commit a rape, again at least the way we are used to seeing in Hollywood movies. Shades of gray is what White wants and gets, but perhaps unlike on stage with just Tessa the film, in making this more seem like something out of Billy Wilder’s 1957 classic, Witness For The Prosecution, just doesn’t have the same visceral impact.

Erivo, as she proved in Harriet, is a fine dramatic actor and does what she can with the ambiguity of a role where the legal chairs are suddenly shuffled. The rest of the cast is also fine including Ings who believably demonstrates why Tessa could fall for Julian. The problem is he doesn’t ever come off dark enough to indicate he is hiding some sort of alternate villainous personality capable of intentional sexual assault. Am I missing something? I didn’t see the play. Maybe it was presented differently there. The impact of a one person stage play, versus a fully opened up film version can be a wide chasm.

Another new film this year, Josephine, which also deals with this issue in a courtroom, made me angry that lawyers could argue on behalf of, in that black and white case, a vicious rapist. I was disturbed, whereas with Prima Facie I just have more questions. Maybe that is the point.

The list of reforms to the legal system sparked in part by Miller’s play is impressive, but I can’t help but think in this more literal film version something may have gotten lost in translation. Still if it can help the cause, and the clear injustice for rape victims everywhere, more power to Miller and White in trying to bring this issue to a wider audience.

Producers are Greer Simpkin, Kevin Loader, David Jowsey

Title: Prima Facie

Festival: Toronto – Gala Presentations

Director: Susanna White

Screenplay: Suzie Miller

Cast: Cynthia Erivo, Daniel Ings, Toheeb Jimoh, Noma Dumezweni, Simon Russell Beale, Elliot Levy, Khalid Abdalla.

title: China Box Office: ‘Once Upon a Time in the Middle East’ Stays on Top as ‘The Odyssey’ Crosses $100 Million
summary: Dirty Monkeys’ war comedy-drama “Once Upon a Time in the Middle East” held the number one spot at the mainland China box office for the fifth straight frame, collecting RMB52.9 million ($7.8 million) over the Sept. 11–13 weekend, according to data from Artisan Gateway. Directed by Wen Muye (“Dying to Survive”) and starring Shen Teng, […]
content:
Dirty Monkeys’ war comedy-drama “Once Upon a Time in the Middle East” held the number one spot at the mainland China box office for the fifth straight frame, collecting RMB52.9 million ($7.8 million) over the Sept. 11–13 weekend, according to data from Artisan Gateway.
