title: Doc Talk Podcast: ‘Black Zombie’ Director Maya Annik Bedward On True Origins Of Ghoulish Hollywood Horror Genre
summary: The zombie – slow moving, with sallow complexion, hollow eyes, rotting teeth and a hunger for human flesh – has been lumbering through Hollywood movies for decades now. In fact, the first representation of the undead creatures came in the film White Zombie, released all the way back in 1932. That movie’s sensationalized logline: “A […]
content:
The zombie – slow moving, with sallow complexion, hollow eyes, rotting teeth and a hunger for human flesh – has been lumbering through Hollywood movies for decades now. In fact, the first representation of the undead creatures came in the film White Zombie, released all the way back in 1932. That movie’s sensationalized logline: “A young man turns to a witch doctor to lure the woman he loves away from her fiancé, but instead turns her into a zombie slave.”

The coupling of the terms “zombie” and “slave” points to the racial dimension of the zombie in film history and popular culture, origins few fans think about when they watch World War Z, for example, or going further back, I Walked with a Zombie (1943) or the comedies Zombieland (2009) and Shaun of the Dead (2004), or the TV series The Walking Dead and its spinoffs.

In her new documentary Black Zombie, director Maya Annik Bedward examines Hollywood’s obsession with zombies, and how the horrifying ghouls were appropriated from Haitian culture and the religious practices of vaudou (bastardized in English as “voodoo”). The filmmaker argues Hollywood zombie movies are shot through with racial stereotypes and distortions of vaudou traditions (a zombi in Haitian folklore isn’t a flesh eater but a being deprived of its soul or free will – in that sense, very much the condition of slaves before abolition).

Watch on Deadline

Bedward joins the latest edition of Deadline’s Doc Talk podcast to unpack her findings. She explains how 1968’s Night of the Living Dead became a prototypical “zombie” movie even though the term isn’t used in the film, and she explores how the civil rights movement informed how Black audiences experienced that George Romero classic.

In her documentary, Bedward incorporates scenes she shot in black and white on the island of Hispaniola, which rival anything done by Hollywood in terms of their cinematic beauty. The filmmaker tells us why she had to film those sequences in the Dominican Republic instead of Haiti and why it was important for her to “have fun” with the editing of her documentary.

RELATED: Kino Lorber Acquires Maya Annik Bedward’s Doc ‘Black Zombie’

That’s on the new episode of Doc Talk hosted by Oscar winner John Ridley (12 Years a Slave, Shirley) and Matt Carey, Deadline’s senior documentary editor. The pod is a production of Deadline and Ridley’s Nō Studios.

title: Starz Networks President Alison Hoffman Re-Upped Through End Of 2029
summary: Starz Networks President Alison Hoffman has renewed her contract through the end of 2029. Her new employment agreement took effect August 6 and runs through December 31, 2029, parent Starz Entertainment disclosed Tuesday in an SEC filing. Hoffman will continue to report to CEO Jeff Hirsch, annually receiving a base salary of $1.485 million as […]
content:
Starz Networks President Alison Hoffman has renewed her contract through the end of 2029.

Her new employment agreement took effect August 6 and runs through December 31, 2029, parent Starz Entertainment disclosed Tuesday in an SEC filing.

Hoffman will continue to report to CEO Jeff Hirsch, annually receiving a base salary of $1.485 million as well as bonus and equity awards.

After joining Starz in 2012 from AMC, where she was a VP in the age of Mad Men, Breaking Bad and The Walking Dead, Hoffman eventually earned a promotion to chief marketing officer. In 2020, she was upped to head of domestic networks.

Starz separated from Lionsgate in 2025 after a long strategic review process and started a new chapter as a separate publicly traded company. Now primarily a streaming programmer, the former premium cable network airs shows including the Power franchise, Outlander: Blood of My Blood and new original Fightland. Later this year, it will premiere the third and final season of P-Valley.

Watch on Deadline

RELATED: 2026 Premiere Dates For New & Returning Series On Broadcast, Streaming & Cable

Thus far, Starz has fared well as a stand-alone company, with its shares more than doubling in 2026 to date. When it reported second-quarter financials last month, Starz said it managed to increase subscriber levels despite raising prices, a combination Hirsch called “very rare” in the streaming business.

Hoffman was asked during a conference call with Wall Street analysts about the company’s recent deal with Netflix for the first four series in the Power franchise. She said the global deal “creates an opportunity for us. It’s a way for us to introduce the franchise to new audiences, new viewers. and really reinvigorate it.”

title: So Not A Shocker! Trump Weighs In For David Ellison & Paramount Over $1.88B Bond Battle With States
summary: Surprising no one — except for the timing — Donald Trump’s Department of Justice has weighed in on the $1.88 billion bond battle between David Ellison’s Paramount and a dozen blue states over the $111 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. Disputing the very right of California Attorney General Rob Bonta, New York’s Letitia James […]
content:
Surprising no one — except for the timing — Donald Trump‘s Department of Justice has weighed in on the $1.88 billion bond battle between David Ellison‘s Paramount and a dozen blue states over the $111 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery.

Disputing the very right of California Attorney General Rob Bonta, New York’s Letitia James and others to raise an antitrust stink, the Todd Blanche-run DOJ made its bottom line POV a top line in paperwork filed Tuesday in federal court. “The bond requirement forces parties to have skin in the game, and also provides a measure of protection to defendants who were ultimately found to be wrongly enjoined,” the DOJ asserts, quoting from past Clayton Act cases.

Citing “extraordinary losses” leading up to the March 2027 scheduled trial plus the $7 million a day ticking fee in the WBD contract that kicks in on October 1 (the same day Paramount has threatened to take its corporate HQ to redder pastures), the Melrose-based company wants the plaintiffs to pony up.

Watch on Deadline

The AGs have said if there is any cash to be paid it should be in the realm of $10,000, at most.

Besides this bond tactic being a tried-and-true distraction in a thorny legal fight, even the son of one of the richest men in the world wants to hold onto that nearly $2 billion. With ticking fee equalling more than $635 million a quarter for Para, and at least two quarters before the trial, and the serious money is on the table — even for an Ellison.

“Congress provided for complementary antitrust enforcement by the federal government and private parties — but made clear that it was not a system of equals,” says the 17-page Statement of Interest of the USA to Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín. Drilling down to Section 16 of the antitrust Clayton Act and waving off the lack of an injunction in the case, the feds argue “the plain meaning of the statute and the contemporaneous use of ‘proper bond’ in dictionaries and federal court decisions makes it clear the amount of the bond must be fit, suitable, adapted, and correct to compensate the defendant for ‘damages for an injunction improvidently granted.'”

AKA: Give our “good friend” David the money. We may discover whether or not bond weary Judge Martínez-Olguín agrees when the parties meet in Oakland next week. Today, Bonta’s office did not respond to Deadline’s request for comment on the feds’ escalation of the matter.

They might be busy, and we ain’t talking about the CA AG’s easy path to reelection in November.

With court-orchestrated settlement talks now on again for the end of October, it’s going to be a busy few months heading towards the March 2, 2027 starting trial. There’s September 24 hearing on the bond debate, which the AGs and the WGA have dismissed as more posturing by Para. Then there’s that pricey ticking fee kick-off and a possible SCOTUS intervention in the whole thing.

Rob Bonta and Letitia James Getty Images

Of course, with the close relationship between the Ellisons and Trump administration, which saw the merger approved this spring with too few questions and no condition in the minds of some, the fact that the language in today’s DOJ statement so closely mirrors that of Paramount’s recent filings on the bond is just another non-surprise. Also stating the AGs’ antitrust case is way out of their jurisdiction, a September 11 filing by Paramount calls the whole July 13 lawsuit little more than “a series of attempted shortcuts and assumptions that collapse under scrutiny.”

“Day by day, the weak case against this Merger gets even weaker.”

Again, in the transactional ethos of Trumpland, it’s all about who has real skin in the game

title: ’60 Minutes’ Season Premiere Averages 7.94 Million Viewers, A Falloff From Last Year’s Debut
summary: The season premiere of 60 Minutes averaged 7.94 million viewers on Sunday, off from the more than 10 million who tuned in to last year’s debut. The first episode of the show’s 59th season was highly anticipated — and scrutinized — following the shake up at the newsmagazine last spring, despite its status as one […]
content:
The season premiere of 60 Minutes averaged 7.94 million viewers on Sunday, off from the more than 10 million who tuned in to last year’s debut.

The first episode of the show’s 59th season was highly anticipated — and scrutinized — following the shake up at the newsmagazine last spring, despite its status as one of the network’s top rated programs.

The season premiere was off by 21% compared to the Sept. 28 debut last year, but there are some caveats to the figure, as tends to be the case during football season.

The broadcast was delayed in eastern and central time zones because of the Minnesota Vikings vs. Green Bay Packers game, and that football lead in also was off by 21%, averaging 18.6 million.

Watch on Deadline

CBS’s NFL coverage also faced competition from football on Fox, and the final part of 60 Minutes went up against NBC’s telecast of the Dallas Cowboys vs. the New York Giants. The first quarter hour of 60 Minutes averaged 9.4 million and dropped to 6.7 million in the final quarter hour. Networks also are pointing to changes in Nielsen’s methodology.

In the 25-54 demo, 60 Minutes averaged 1.58 million viewers, down 33% from 2.36 million for last year’s premiere.

CBS News said in a statement, “We are so proud of the exceptional journalism on display in our season premiere and we can’t wait to bring our audience another amazing show this coming Sunday.”

Last spring, CBS News editor in chief Bari Weiss replaced executive producer Tanya Simon with Nick Bilton, and three correspondents, including Sharyn Alfonsi, Cecilia Vega and Scott Pelley, were fired. The season premiere featured some new graphics and the introduction of a new correspondent, Ross Douthat. Stories featured included an exclusive interview with an airman shot down and rescued from Iran, a report on brokers collecting huge sums to secure clients’ pardons from Donald Trump, and a profile of the Los Angeles Rams.

title: Ed Sheeran Tour Openers Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham & Beoga Withdraw After Macklemore Dropped For “Free Palestine” Remarks
summary: Musical acts Finneas, Lukas Graham, Beoga and Aaron Rowe have dropped out as openers for the North American leg of Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour following the dismissal of fellow supporting act Macklemore for his pro-Palestinian remarks at Sheeran’s New Jersey shows September 4 and 5. Finneas, brother to Billie Eilish, posted a short note on […]
content:
Musical acts Finneas, Lukas Graham, Beoga and Aaron Rowe have dropped out as openers for the North American leg of Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour following the dismissal of fellow supporting act Macklemore for his pro-Palestinian remarks at Sheeran’s New Jersey shows September 4 and 5.

Finneas, brother to Billie Eilish, posted a short note on his Instagram that reads: “Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed. I have decided to withdraw from my upcoming tour dates with Ed Sheeran. I stand with Palestine and its people.”

These decisions and statements follow Sheeran’s statement earlier this morning on the matter of Macklemore getting dropped, which he said was the “promoter’s decision.” The “Azizam” singer confirmed that he spoke with Gillette Stadium and New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, who was one of the main influences in the decision to take Macklemore off of the tour.

Watch on Deadline

RELATED: Macklemore Emphasizes “Free Palestine” Pleas Are “In No Way A Criticism” Of Jewish People: “My Message Is For Peace”

“I don’t take the decision lightly,” Rowe wrote in a statement posted to Instagram. “Ed has been a friend to me and has changed my life, I could never thank him enough for this. But as Irish people we know all too well about genocide, forced famine and violent occupation.

“I cannot stand by and allow billionaires to use their position of power to silence the rightful voices of those who speak up against Israeli genocide and who highlight the savage murder of children,” Rowe’s statement continued. “I would lose all respect for myself to carry on as normal. I need to be true to myself and my ancestors who resisted colonization, and fought for a freedom that I enjoy today in Ireland.”

Danish pop band Lukas Graham posted a statement of similar length on Instagram.

“We should be able to speak about war, about civilians being killed, about children who deserve to grow up,” the statement said. “Wherever they live. Whatever flag flies over them. I grew up in Christiania, a small community in Denmark where speaking your mind was part of everyday life. Having more money didn’t make your opinion worth more than anyone else’s.”

Like Rowe, Lukas Graham acknowledged Sheeran and thanked him for the opportunity.

Traditional Irish band Beoga also dropped out, posting a statement to Instagram.

“We have made the decision to depart as Ed Sheeran’s band on the remaining U.S. Loop tour following the silencing of Macklemore by zionist lobbies,” the statement reads. “We are a traditional Irish band who never saw ourselves playing in stadiums of that size and that opportunity is not lost on us. We have been friends with Ed for over 10 years now and will continue to be. We believe in dialogue as a means of progressing the plight of the Palestinian people.

Macklemore, who specified that his “Free Palestine” comments were not a “criticism” of Jewish people, released his own statement once he was dropped from Sheeran’s tour.

RELATED: Macklemore’s “Free Palestine” Onstage Plea Sparks Petition For His Removal From Ed Sheeran Tour

“I didn’t need 10 shows from Ed. I needed 2. Two chances to stand in front of 90,000 people and say the words that somehow became too dangerous to say. Free Palestine,” the “Can’t Hold Us” rapper wrote on Instagram. “But if those words cost me the stage, while turning the conversation back to Palestine, then it was the most successful tour I’ve ever been on.”

He also drew attention to the real victims of the situation, referencing singer P!nk’s involvement in the social media circulation of response to Macklemore’s plea and then protest song performance.

RELATED: Macklemore Cancels Show In Dubai, Citing UAE Role In “Ongoing Genocide And Humanitarian Crisis” In Sudan

“I am not a victim. Ed Sheeran is not a victim. Pink is not a victim,” he said. “We have careers, money, opportunities, safety and audiences around the world. Whatever consequences any of us face for what we say, we get to go home to our families. The victims are the Palestinian people.”

title: Emmys Hit 6.7 Million Viewers, Down 9% From Last Year
summary: NBC’s telecast of the 78th Emmy Awards hit 6.7 million viewers on Monday night, per Nielsen. That total marks a 9% decrease from last year’s ceremony on CBS, which brought in 7.4 million viewers — the award show’s best performance since 2021. It should be noted, though, that the 2025 ceremony took place on a […]
content:
NBC’s telecast of the 78th Emmy Awards hit 6.7 million viewers on Monday night, per Nielsen.

That total marks a 9% decrease from last year’s ceremony on CBS, which brought in 7.4 million viewers — the award show’s best performance since 2021.

It should be noted, though, that the 2025 ceremony took place on a Sunday, making it easier for viewers to sit down for a three-hour telecast. Compared to the most recent Monday night Emmys — televised by Fox in 2024 — NBC accomplished a 41% increase. But since that telecast, which hit only a meager 4.4 million viewers, was the first in Emmys history to air with fierce competition from an NFL playoff game, the most accurate comparison is perhaps to NBC’s own Monday night Emmys in 2022. In those terms, the network’s latest Emmy efforts made a 10% improvement, up from 5.9 million viewers.

Hosted by “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit” star Mariska Hargitay, the Emmys did air against an NFL game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Denver Broncos. Even with that competition, it drew enough viewers to rank as the the most-watched non-sports, non-news Monday telecast of 2026, both overall and among adults age 18-49. Hargitay referenced the football game in a pre-recorded sketch featuring a cameo from Taylor Swift, musing that the pop star wouldn’t be able to attend the show because she’d be supporting her husband, Chiefs player Travis Kelce.

Popular on Variety

According to NBCUniversal, the Emmys generated 133 million social views, counted across Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube. The company touts that that marks a 90% increase from 2025.

It appears that this was the Emmys’ last year on a traditional broadcaster. After 31 years of rotating between NBC, CBS, Fox and ABC, the TV Academy is now in talks with Amazon Prime Video.

title: Judge Sets Date For Settlement Talks In Paramount-WBD Antitrust Case
summary: Paramount and the State Attorneys General suing to block its merger with Warner Bros. Discovery were ordered by a judge to appear for a two-day settlement conference Oct. 14-15 in a San Francisco courtroom. It’s a mandated step for two sides approaching a trial, set in this case for early March, and doesn’t mean there’s […]
content:
Paramount and the State Attorneys General suing to block its merger with Warner Bros. Discovery were ordered by a judge to appear for a two-day settlement conference Oct. 14-15 in a San Francisco courtroom.

It’s a mandated step for two sides approaching a trial, set in this case for early March, and doesn’t mean there’s been any particular behind-the-scenes progress in reaching an agreement. California AG Rob Bonta, who is leading a group of 12 AGs in the antitrust case, canceled a scheduled meeting last month after accusing Paramount of leaking details of a prior discussion. Paramount denied this.

Bonta has insisted publicly on “structural” remedies like asset sales that may include divesting Warner’s cable networks and retaining a degree of separation between the Paramount and Warner Bros. film studios. Paramount CEO David Ellison has made promises about the merged company’s film output (30 a year) and theatrical terms. He has also threatened to relocate the studio out of California if the case drags on.

Watch on Deadline

The company will start racking up a $7 million a day ticking fee on Oct. 1 if the merger hasn’t closed as part of its agreement with WBD. That’s the date, he told senior managers, that he’d start looking seriously at other states.

Magistrate Judge Thomas S. Hixson told the parties in a court filing Monday to send him, and exchange with each other, settlement statements no later than Oct. 7. Those are documents that briefly state claims and defenses, a description of the major issues in dispute, “a candid evaluation of the parties’ likelihood of prevailing” and relief sought. The parties should describe any “discrete issue that, if resolved, would facilitate the resolution of the case” and their positions on settlement, including present demands and offers and a history of past settlement discussions.

Either side can also submit an additional confidential letter to the Court.

The filing said the parties should be prepared to discuss settlement objectives, any perceived impediments to settlement, “and the possibility of a creative resolution of the dispute.”

Reps from the WGA, which is also suing to block the merger, will participate.

The list of attendees is due October 12. The settlement statements are private, as are the meetings. Statements made during the conference are confidential and will not be admissible at trial if the case does not settle.

The sides were told to notify the court if the case settles earlier.

Meanwhile, a separate hearing is set for Sept. 24 where a judge will rule on Paramount’s request that plaintiffs put up a $1.88 billion bond to cover the ticking fee. It will accrue daily even if the company ultimately prevails at trial.

The States argue that nothing beyond a nominal bond is due. The Department of Justice, which approved the Par-WBD merger in June, came out in support of the bond earlier today. “The bond requirement forces parties to have skin in the game, and also provides a measure of protection to defendants who were ultimately found to be wrongly enjoined,” it wrote.

title: ‘NCIS: New York’ Trailer Reveals LL Cool J’s Character Sam Hanna’s Return & His New Team
summary: NCIS: New York has dropped its first trailer (above), and there are so many details packed into the video, setting up the series premiere on October 6. In the pilot, after years of special assignments and covert ops, Special Agent Sam Hanna (LL Cool J) returns to his hometown of New York City for a […]
content:
NCIS: New York has dropped its first trailer (above), and there are so many details packed into the video, setting up the series premiere on October 6.

In the pilot, after years of special assignments and covert ops, Special Agent Sam Hanna (LL Cool J) returns to his hometown of New York City for a brand-new mission. When Sam’s friend and Navy reservist Jack Halloway is found dead, he requests permission from Assistant Special Agent-In-Charge Robyn Wells (Jennifer Beals) to investigate his friend’s death. As the team investigates Jack’s death, they work together to gather key information that can help find the culprits.

The trailer reveals the moment when Robyn introduces Sam and Nick, who will work closely on the cast along with the rest of the team: clean-cut Wyatt Sellers (Shane Harper), bright-eyed Addy Ross (Jacqueline Byers) and hacker-turned-computer guy Sean Sullivan (Devin Druid).

Watch on Deadline

During a recent chat with showrunner and executive producer Byron Belasco (Kingdom, Without a Trace), who developed the series alongside R. Scott Gemmill (The Pitt, NCIS: Los Angeles), shared further details into the crew.

Jennifer Beals as Robyn Wells, Scott Caan as Nick Schaeffer, LL Cool J as Sam Hanna and Devin Druid as Sean Sullivan Michael Greenberg/CBS

On Wyatt: He is just a good old boy from Alaska. You know, a really nice guy. He lived a very sort of – not sheltered life, but just a different life than one in New York City. So when we’re meeting him, he had plans that got t-boned by a breakup, and now he’s trying to figure out. With life not going how he expected, he wonders how life for him would look like in New York. What is the path forward? He’s a great agent. He’s really tough and just a good, solid, loyal guy.

On Addy: She comes from a long line of military officers in the Navy. She’s the youngest of four, with three older brothers. For her, if a pizza was ordered in the house, she had to fight her way to just get a slice. This translated into who she is now, which is very aggressive, very strong, very strong willed, but also, she really cares about the cases and her team. She will do anything for them. She also has her own emotional baggage she’s dealing with in terms of her father and the complicated relationship has with him.

On Sean: He is our wayward boy. He there because he’s working off a little bit of a penalty for a crime he committed. It’s not his first choice to be there. But our team and Robyn in particular are taking it upon themselves to bring Sean into the light to show him that being part of a team and being part of something that matters really makes a difference. Sean’s a little resistant to that, but he’s a human, and I think everybody feels that way. You’ll see him opening up, and he and Robyn have a really special relationship. They kind of relate to each other on a personal level, in a lot of ways.

Pictured: Devin Druid Sean Sullivan, Shane Harper as Wyatt Hill, and Jacqueline Byers as Addison “Addy” Ross in ‘NCIS: New York’ Pilot Episode Michael Greenberg/CBS

Watch the trailer above.

title: Mikayla Matthews Says That “The Only Reason” She’s Leaving Hulu’s ‘Mormon Wives’ Is “Because I Was Told A Certain Person Was Coming Back”
summary: Mikayla Matthews isn’t mincing words, and a day after saying she was leaving The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, she confirmed it was because Taylor Frankie Paul was returning to filming. The Hulu reality series is currently filming Season 6 after Season 5 was truncated due to Paul’s domestic violence claims from her ex, Dakota Mortensen. “The […]
content:
Mikayla Matthews isn’t mincing words, and a day after saying she was leaving The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, she confirmed it was because Taylor Frankie Paul was returning to filming.

The Hulu reality series is currently filming Season 6 after Season 5 was truncated due to Paul’s domestic violence claims from her ex, Dakota Mortensen.

“The ONLY reason I’m leaving the show is because I was told a certain person was coming back,” Matthews shared on Instagram Stories. “I told them before agreeing to do [Season] 6 that I wasn’t going to film if that certain someone came back because it’s UNETHICAL and kids are involved.”

She continued, “And I’m being put in an unfair position because of the things I’ve seen and heard that I don’t agree with. Not just the Barstool video everyone else saw (which mind you I saw this video for the first time in March) and other things with it that obviously made me question the one side I was hearing and unknowingly enabling the whole time. I NEVER knew the dephts of it and I still don’t.”

Watch on Deadline

Matthews said that she filmed Season 6 because Paul was not filming with the rest of MomTok, but as soon as “we were told she was coming back, I said great, then I will not be participating, god bless and goodbye, haven’t filmed a day since.”

The social media influencer said that rewatching Season 5 did not influence her decision to leave the Hulu series, adding, “If you guys thought, ‘Wow this is hard to watch, incredibly triggering and frustrating,’ imagine having it be your reality everyday. Why would you willingly agree to put yourself back in that environment that has cause all that discomfort for every single person on this cast and crew.”

Matthews noted that she did not give an ultimatum, and has no “control” over casting decisions. The reality TV personality said that she would fulfill her “contractual obligations and interviews for what I have filmed and that’s the end of it.”

Taylor Frankie Paul

title: Everything We Know About Season 2 Of HBO’s ‘Harry Potter’ TV Series So Far
summary: A second season of HBO Max’s Harry Potter TV series is in the works, and the cast continues to grow. The streamer has plans for an accelerated production of the series adaptation of J.K. Rowling’s book s, with Season 1 on the way and production looking to start soon for Season 2. Read on for […]
content:
A second season of HBO Max’s Harry Potter TV series is in the works, and the cast continues to grow.

The streamer has plans for an accelerated production of the series adaptation of J.K. Rowling’s book s, with Season 1 on the way and production looking to start soon for Season 2.

Read on for everything we know about Season 2 of HBO’s Harry Potter show:

When will Season 2 of HBO’s Harry Potter TV show come out?

No release date has yet been set for the second season of the series, but production is aiming to start this fall ahead of Season 1’s premiere.

Who will be new in the cast for Season 2 of HBO’s Harry Potter TV Show?

Watch on Deadline

Bonnie Hill will take over the role of Ginny Weasley, Ron’s younger sister and the youngest Weasley sibling, in Season 2 from Gracie Cochrane, who will portray her in Season 1. Cochrane stepped away from the series due to unforeseen circumstances, prompting the recasting of Harry’s eventual love interest as well as a key character in Rowling’s second book, The Chamber of Secrets.

Lenny Rush (Am I Being Unreasonable?) will portray Dobby, the loyal house-elf who serves the Malfoy family. Billy Barratt (Invasion), who holds the record as the youngest International Emmy winner, will portray Tom Riddle, the younger version of Lord Voldemort.

Deadline first broke the news of Nicholas Hoult’s casting as Professor Gilderoy Lockhart, who serves as Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher in Rowling’s book The Chamber of Secrets. We then first reported Kit Harrington stepping up to fill the role after Hoult departed due to scheduling issues. Harrington voices the character in the audiobooks.

RELATED: ‘Black Mirror’ Director Ally Pankiw Roasts ‘Harry Potter’ TV Series, Claiming She Turned Down Gig: “Say No To Funding Transphobia”

The newest round of additions thus far include Molly Hewitt-Richards, who will portray Moaning Myrtle, Rafe Spall as patriarch Arthur Weasley and Jasper Ambrose as Colin Creevey. Rafe Spall is the son of Timothy Spall, who portrayed Peter Pettigrew aka Wormtail from the third Harry Potter film onwards. Deadline first reported that the casting search for Creevey was underway, whose camera comes in handy in Season 2, in June.

Who else is behind Season 2 of HBO’s Harry Potter TV show?

Jon Brown (Succession), who was a writer on the first season, has been elevated to co-showrunner for Season 2 alongside Season 1 showrunner Francesca Gardiner. The elevation lines up with the faster production schedule.

“As we have laid out our plans for the overlapping production schedules to finish Season 1 by Christmas and to return to production for Season 2 this autumn, it has become clear that bringing on a co-showrunner is the key to maintaining our momentum,” Gardiner said. “I’ve loved working with Jon from the very first day we met on Succession through to these recent times together on Harry Potter. Not only do I have huge admiration for his writing, but he’s also a brilliant collaborator and a lovely person. We are lucky to have him.”

Gardiner also executive produces. Mark Mylod serves as executive producer and directed multiple episodes. Rowling, Neil Blair, and Ruth Kenley-Letts of Brontë Film and TV, and David Heyman of Heyday Films also executive produce the series, produced by HBO in association with Brontë Film and TV and Warner Bros. Television. It will air on HBO and be available to stream exclusively on HBO Max.

When does Season 1 of HBO’s Harry Potter series come out?

Season 1 of the series premieres Christmas day 2026.

RELATED: ‘Harry Potter And The Philosopher’s Stone’: See First-Look Photos From Upcoming HBO Series

Will there be more seasons of the Harry Potter show on HBO?

The idea is one season per book, but the show has not yet been renewed for a third season. Chairman and CEO of HBO and Max Content Casey Bloys gave brief updates on the series post-Emmys 2026.

“Each book is a huge event. I’m right now thinking about season by season as far as what it all adds up to. But I can tell you, Christmas Day is going to be a great launch day for Harry Potter,” he said.

He also reinforced the idea of a tight production schedule.

“We’re trying as hard to bring it back as quickly as possible. It’s not going to be two years [between seasons], but we’re trying hard to keep it as compressed as possible,” he said.

RELATED: Casey Bloys Celebrates HBO’s 21 Emmy Wins, Congratulates Apple, Gives Updates On ‘Last Of Us,’ ‘True Detective,’ ‘Gilded Age,’ ‘BLL’, ‘Heated Rivalry’

title: Adam Driver & Anne Hathaway Pic ‘Alone At Dawn’ From Amazon MGM Studios & Imagine To Roll Out At Christmas 2027

Deadline first told you about the project. Oscar winner Anne Hathaway, 2x Oscar nominee Adam […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Amazon MGM Studios and Imagine Entertainment‘s Ron Howard directed true-life film Alone at Dawn will begin a platform release on December 25, 2027, before expanding on January 7 and getting a wide break over the MLK weekend, January 14-17.

Deadline first told you about the project. Oscar winner Anne Hathaway, 2x Oscar nominee Adam Driver and newly minted Emmy winner Betty Gilpin star in the feature take on Dan Schilling and Lori Longfritz’s book about Air Force combat controller John Chapman. Years after he fought to the death to save his fellow soldiers, an intelligence officer strives to prove his valor — leading an investigation that ultimately would secure the Medal of Honor for Chapman.

The year-end holiday corridor historically has been a strong launch window for prestige, adult-skewing action-dramas, including such films as American Sniper, Lone Survivor and 1917. We hear that Alone at Dawn is still being finished, and next Christmas is the prime time.

Watch on Deadline

RELATED: The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office

Michael Russell Gunn adapted Schilling and Longfritz’s 2019 book. Producers are Imagine’s Brian Grazer, Howard, Jeb Brody and Allan Mandelbaum; Hideaway Entertainment’s Jonathan Gray, as well as Matthew Rhodes, Ron West, Kristy Grisham, William M. Connor and Patrick Newall. Thruline Entertainment is producing the action drama feature as well.

Amazon MGM Studios fired up the year with the first tentpole, that being the Ryan Gosling-starring Project Hail Mary, which grossed over $685M WW. It just had two world premieres at TIFF with Peter Farrelly’s I Play Rocky and Basam Tariq’s Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother to respective great reviews at 81% fresh and 100% fresh. I Play Rocky opens on Nov. 6, while Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother begins its platform on Sept. 25.

RELATED: Toronto Film Festival 2026: Read All Of Deadline’s Reviews

Next year’s Christmas Day release schedule isn’t quite full yet. Currently there’s only Warner Bros’ Nancy Meyers-directed feature. The big event pics next year are Disney/Marvel Studio’s Avengers: Secret Wars, New Line’s The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum,and Lionsgate’s The Housemaid’s Secret on December 17, 2027.

Over MLK weekend there’s an untitled Disney movie, Paramount’s Longlegs sequel, and an untitled Universal event feature.

title: Does Stephen Colbert Miss Late Night TV?: ‘Nope!’
summary: Hot off his Emmy win for outstanding variety series, Stephen Colbert went on “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” Tuesday night and revealed if he ever thinks about returning to late night television. “Late night TV. I remember it well. Many fond memories of this,” Colbert said while taking the stage. “Do you ever think about it?” Kimmel […]
content:
Hot off his Emmy win for outstanding variety series, Stephen Colbert went on “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” Tuesday night and revealed if he ever thinks about returning to late night television.

“Late night TV. I remember it well. Many fond memories of this,” Colbert said while taking the stage. “Do you ever think about it?” Kimmel asked, to which Colbert responded: “Nope!”

The Emmy-winner continued to remark about the fact that he no longer has to “think about the news every day,” to which Kimmel pointed out that Colbert seemed “like a different person,” “happier” and “healthier” when he saw the former host at the Emmys Monday night.

“Like I don’t drink a cup of poison every day?” Colbert responded. “A good part of the job is, as I remember it, to be lowered like carbon rods into a radioactive pool every day. And then to be pulled out and put in front of a camera. And to radiate it back at the audience at a nonlethal rad level.”



Speaking with CNN correspondent Elizabeth Wagmeister and Variety co-president and co-editor-in-chief Ramin Setoodeh after the Emmy Awards, Colbert said free speech in is “alive and well” and thinks late-night is still a crucial part of the television ecosystem, despite the genre’s challenges in recent years.

Popular on Variety

“Because if you can’t say something because you go to jail, that is a violation of free speech,” Colbert said. “I think that late night is just as funny and just as vital as it ever has been, and I love watching Jimmy and Jimmy and John and John and Seth and everybody else. And I think I hope it goes on for a long time because you get to work with people like this, and that’s the greatest gift.”

“The Late Show With Stephen Colbert” ended in May after CBS announced the series’ cancellation.

“The Late Show” took home its first outstanding variety series on Monday night for its final season. It competed in the category against “The Daily Show” (Comedy Central), “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” (ABC), “Last Week Tonight With John Oliver” (HBO Max) and “Saturday Night Live” (NBC).

title: Cate Blanchett to Attend Tokyo Festival for Japan Premiere of Displacement Film Fund Shorts
summary: Cate Blanchett will travel to Tokyo for the 39th edition of the Tokyo International Film Festival, where five short films backed by the Displacement Film Fund will receive their Japan premieres. Blanchett co-founded the Displacement Film Fund, which supports displaced filmmakers and those with a demonstrated history of telling authentic stories rooted in the experiences […]
content:
Cate Blanchett will travel to Tokyo for the 39th edition of the Tokyo International Film Festival, where five short films backed by the Displacement Film Fund will receive their Japan premieres.

Blanchett co-founded the Displacement Film Fund, which supports displaced filmmakers and those with a demonstrated history of telling authentic stories rooted in the experiences of displaced people. The fund was announced at the International Film Festival Rotterdam in January 2025 in partnership with IFFR’s Hubert Bals Fund, which serves as managing partner. UNHCR acts as strategic partner, with additional backing from Amahoro Coalition, Master Mind, the Tamer Family Foundation, Uniqlo – a founding partner – and Droom en Daad, a Dutch cultural foundation. The SP Lohia Foundation came aboard as a major partner when the second edition of the fund was confirmed at IFFR 2026.

Blanchett said: “I am privileged to have the opportunity to share the inaugural short films supported through the Displacement Film Fund with audiences at Tokyo International Film Festival. In a world where conflict and persecution are driving displacement and division, cinematic storytelling has a vital role to play in connecting with the experiences of others. Being displaced shouldn’t mean filmmakers abandon their creativity; in fact their stories may feel even more urgent.”

Popular on Variety

Following the screening, Blanchett will participate in a Q&A alongside two of the five directors whose work is included in the program: Mohammad Rasoulof, whose “Sense of Water” centers on an Iranian writer confronting a foreign language in exile, and Shahrbanoo Sadat, director of “Super Afghan Gym,” which is set in a downtown Kabul gym during the one hour each day reserved for women.

The other three films in the selection are “Allies in Exile” (U.K./Syria), directed by Hasan Kattan, which follows two Syrian filmmakers documenting the trauma of waiting for asylum; “Rotation” (Ukraine/Turkey), directed by Maryna Er Gorbach, depicting a therapeutic hypnosis ritual experienced by a young Ukrainian woman who transitioned from civilian life to military service; and “Whispers of a Burning Scent” (Somalia/Austria/Germany), directed by Mo Harawe, in which a quiet wedding musician finds his private life drawn into public view.

Blanchett’s Tokyo visit coincides with a separate honor: she is to receive the Praemium Imperiale Award during the same week. She recently wrapped production on Alice Birch’s “Sweetsick” and is in development with Janicza Bravo on a film about Martha Stewart. Her feature “Father Mother Sister Brother” (2025), which won the Golden Lion at the 82nd Venice Film Festival, is scheduled for Japanese theatrical release on Nov. 20.

The 39th Tokyo International Film Festival is hosted by Unijapan and takes place Oct. 26 to Nov. 4.

title: Drake Unveils Surreal ‘Fear of Missing Out’ Film Featuring New Music Videos, Songs and an Ella Langley Remix
summary: Drake debuted “Fear of Missing Out” on Tuesday night, unveiling an hourlong string of music videos, new songs and scenes featuring a spate of guests including Sexyy Red, Winnie Harlow, Lena the Plug, Don Toliver and his mother, Sandi Graham. The livestream, which Drake had previously described as a “not so short film,” indeed lived […]
content:
Drake debuted “Fear of Missing Out” on Tuesday night, unveiling an hourlong string of music videos, new songs and scenes featuring a spate of guests including Sexyy Red, Winnie Harlow, Lena the Plug, Don Toliver and his mother, Sandi Graham.

The livestream, which Drake had previously described as a “not so short film,” indeed lived up to his promise as he rolled out clips set to songs from his recent albums “Maid of Honour” and “Habibti.” “FOMO” was directed by Theo Skudra, Liam Macrae, Jake Schreier, Zong Li and Glenn Michael, and was presented as a surrealist assortment of visuals that Drake had clearly captured throughout the year in his native Toronto and beyond.

It began with “Cheetah Print” alongside Sexyy Red before Drake hit the beach with Stunna Sandy for “Outside Tweaking,” giving way to an infomercial tutorial on how to make the drink “Panty Dropper.” During the film, Harlow starred in the video for “New Bestie” while Drake’s mom Sandi showed off her new “Icemom” tattoo in the clip for “True Bestie.”

Popular on Variety

Among the videos for previously released songs were “WNBA,” “Road Trips” and “Hoe Phase,” all songs included on his recent records. But he snuck in a few new tracks, namely his highly suspected remix of Ella Langley’s history-making hit “Choosin’ Texas.” Drake’s take on the tune was a slowed-down, underwater rendition that corralled Don Toliver and featured the chorus, “Drinkin’ yak all by myself / She’s from Texas I can tell.”

Drake also unveiled another new song with Toliver as well as one with Yeat. The film came to a conclusion with a full-circle moment as Drake stood in a set piece ripped straight from the video for “Hotline Bling,” and ended with a stagehand bringing out a stepladder for Drake to exit the set. After “FOMO” debuted, the YouTube stream was set to private.

Fans have long speculated if “Fear of Missing Out” would be an album, music video or even a tour. But this past weekend, Drake dropped a teaser on Instagram and described it as a “not so short film directed and scored by the family.”

On Monday, he elaborated on what exactly the project would be, explaining that it’s “self funded surrealism” and “a story about making the absolute most of it all in one summer.”

“Here’s some life advice before you watch,” he wrote in an Instagram post. “Nobody is coming to save you. You must use each day to decipher who you love and trust and march forward with them

I hope this serves as motivation to make that call, take that trip, drop that song, open that shop, see your parents, leave that relationship or stay in it forever, spend the bread, get some more etc.

“They keep saying our genre is dying,” he continued. “Videos don’t matter. Nobody is watching nobody is listening. I still care. As much as I did on the set of Best I Ever Had. So be kind and rewind.”

Drake dropped “Fear of Missing Out” on the back of an already stacked year, which included a trio of albums — “Iceman,” “Maid of Honour” and “Habibti” — that dropped as a surprise in May. The projects had a total of 43 songs and guest appearances from a slew of artists including Future, 21 Savage, Sexyy Red, Central Cee, PartyNextDoor and more.

He had been teasing “Iceman” as early as 2024, and started concretely previewing it in July 2025 with the livestream “Iceman Episode 1” on YouTube. He announced the three albums just after the conclusion of a fourth installment of the “Iceman” livestream series in May.

title: Helicopter Crashes Near Site of Deadly Metro Bus Accident in Chatsworth
summary: NBCLA’s NewsChopper4 helicopter crashed Tuesday night in Chatsworth, just blocks away from an L.A. Metro bus crash that killed two people and sent six others to the hospital. NBC4 Los Angeles reported Tuesday night on the incident and indicated that the crash was in connection with the station. KNBC-TV news anchor Colleen Williams said on […]
content:
NBCLA’s NewsChopper4 helicopter crashed Tuesday night in Chatsworth, just blocks away from an L.A. Metro bus crash that killed two people and sent six others to the hospital.

NBC4 Los Angeles reported Tuesday night on the incident and indicated that the crash was in connection with the station. KNBC-TV news anchor Colleen Williams said on air shortly after the incident, “We know that it is a news helicopter, and we know that we have lost contact” with the station’s helicopter.

Popular on Variety

Authorities with the Los Angeles Fire Department told KTLA that the helicopter went down between two commercial buildings at 9151 N. Mason Avenue just before 7 p.m. PT.

CBS News reports that the helicopter appeared to crash onto two shipping containers, as well as several vehicles that were parked in the vicinity. While it’s unclear how many people were on the helicopter when it went down, the outlet reported that three people were killed in the crash

“We do have one confirmed patient that seemed to be outside of the helicopter when it crashed,” said LAFD Captain Branden Silverman to CBS. “That person was declared deceased on scene. … At this point, we have not confirmed how many victims, or how many people, were inside the helicopter.”

According to the Los Angeles Times, the Metro accident occurred around 5 p.m. PT when an SUV crashed into the bus, which was traveling on Line 166, trapping the passengers inside. Jennifer Middleton, a spokesperson for the Los Angeles Fire Department, told the outlet that the two individuals who were killed were pronounced dead at the scene.

title: ‘Resident Evil’ First Reactions: Zach Cregger’s Zombie Horror Is ‘Gloriously Gory’ and One of ‘The Best Video Game Adaptations’ Ever
summary: “Weapons” and “Barbarian” director Zach Cregger is dabbling in studio IP for the first time with Sony’s “Resident Evil,” but it appears joining a franchise has done nothing to weaken the filmmaker’s knack for outrageously wild scares. Members of the film press are calling Cregger’s “Resident Evil” reboot “a cinematic spectacle” and “easily among the […]
content:
“Weapons” and “Barbarian” director Zach Cregger is dabbling in studio IP for the first time with Sony’s “Resident Evil,” but it appears joining a franchise has done nothing to weaken the filmmaker’s knack for outrageously wild scares. Members of the film press are calling Cregger’s “Resident Evil” reboot “a cinematic spectacle” and “easily among the best video game adaptations.”

Tomatometer critic EJ Moreno shared an enthusiastic review on X, writing that the film is one that “you have to see on the biggest screen with a big crowd! A true horror blockbuster.” He continued: “Zach Cregger goes bigger, scarier, and at his most fun. This is how you make horror into a cinematic spectacle.”

Fellow Tomatometer critic Mark Cassidy wrote that “Resident Evil” taps “into the relentless tension of the games.” “Zach Cregger has actually delivered the most faithful take yet. Very bloody, very funny, and it made me jump at least 3 times (no easy task). The fella sitting in front of me hid behind his jacket for most of the movie. Easily among the best video game adaptations I’ve seen.”

Popular on Variety

Film journalist and editor-in-chief of SplashReport.com Kellvin Chavez shared a glowing review for “Resident Evil” as well. “HOLY SHIT!!! #ResidentEvil has its foot on the gas from the opening scene and NEVER hits the brakes,” he wrote on X. “Zach Cregger delivers relentless suspense, gloriously gory action, and some seriously twisted, Thing-esque creature designs. Pure SURVIVAL HORROR and easily the best ‘Resident Evil’ movie yet. Austin Abrams is terrific. I’ll do a full review tomorrow.”

“It’s just as intense and horrifying as you’d expect a ‘Resident Evil’ movie to be while integrating some great humorous moments throughout,” film critic Tristian Circa ‘89 shared on X. “Austin Abrams plays an everyman in way over his head, but his natural charm makes him a lead worth rooting for.”

Variety‘s Jordan Moreau wrote on X that “Zach Cregger is the fucking man and #ResidentEvil is one of the best video game adaptions ever made, and one of the best horror movies in recent memory. Incredible title drop, Austin Abrams is hilarious to watch stumble around killing zombies, 10/10.”

“Resident Evil” reunites Cregger with his “Weapons” star Austin Abrams, who plays a medical courier who must contend with a zombie outbreak while making a delivery to Raccoon City General Hospital. Cregger wrote the movie’s screenplay with Shay Hatten. The supporting cast includes Zach Cherry, Kali Reis and Paul Walter Hauser.

Notably, Cregger’s new movie does not feature established characters from the “Resident Evil” video game universe such as Leon S. Kennedy or Jill Valentine because Cregger aimed to create a new and original story, which has rubbed a certain section of the fandom the wrong way (Cregger has admitted he was “naive” to think he could create an original story in a pre-existing franchise and get away unscathed from fans).

There have been six previous “Resident Evil” films, beginning with Milla Jovovich and Michelle Rodriguez’s 2002 film. Jovovich went on to lead “Resident Evil: Apocalypse” (2004), “Resident Evil: Extinction” (2007), “Resident Evil: Afterlife” (2010), “Resident Evil: Retribution” (2012) and “Resident Evil: The Final Chapter” (2017). In 2021, filmmaker Johannes Roberts took on the franchise reboot “Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City” as writer and director. The franchise has collectively grossed over $1.2 billion at the global box office.

“Resident Evil” opens in theaters Sept. 18 from Sony Pictures. Check out first reactions in the posts below.

title: NBC L.A. TV News Chopper Crashes, Three Dead
summary: Los Angeles Fire Department has confirmed that a helicopter was downed in Chatsworth, leaving at least three people dead. NBC 4 in Los Angeles later confirmed that it was their chopper that went down. Longtime local news anchor Colleen Williams made the announcement live on NBC 4 just before 9 p.m. “We can now confirm […]
content:
Los Angeles Fire Department has confirmed that a helicopter was downed in Chatsworth, leaving at least three people dead. NBC 4 in Los Angeles later confirmed that it was their chopper that went down.

Longtime local news anchor Colleen Williams made the announcement live on NBC 4 just before 9 p.m.

“We can now confirm that the chopper that went down in Chatsworth tonight two hours ago was, in fact, News Chopper 4,” Williams announced, her voice quavering.

The crash was reported around 7 p.m. (local time), and LAFD confirmed the aircraft went down between two commercial buildings.

“56 firefighters responded to the incident. The fire has been completely extinguished. No exposure to any structures. 4 automobiles and 2 storage containers have been damaged by the fire,” the LAFD reported.

Watch on Deadline

Authorities noted that four patients were assessed, and three of them were “determined deceased on scene.”

“One patient has been transported to a local hospital in unknown condition. NTSB and FAA will be handling the investigation,” read the report.

According to LAFD, one of the people who died was a pedestrian on the ground. It’s undetermined right now where the other two deceased individuals were at the time of the incident.

KNBC noted that several TV news helicopters were in the area covering a crash involving a Metro bus.

title: Fired ‘Shrinking’ Crew Member Accuses Warner Bros TV Of Doing Nothing Over Sexual Harassment By EP; Being Scapegoated After Complaining
summary: Despite 10 nominations, Shrinking came up short at the Emmys on Monday, but the Warner Bros Television produced show may be taking centerstage in court soon. A longtime Key Second Assistant Director on the Jason Segel and Harrison Ford starring series says she was abruptly fired after a long day of shooting on July 10 […]
content:
Despite 10 nominations, Shrinking came up short at the Emmys on Monday, but the Warner Bros Television produced show may be taking centerstage in court soon.

A longtime Key Second Assistant Director on the Jason Segel and Harrison Ford starring series says she was abruptly fired after a long day of shooting on July 10 by Executive Producer Kip Kroeger because of so-called “different needs of production.” In her seven claim compliant filed today in L.A. Superior Court against WBTV, Shrinking EP/director Randall Winston and others, Mindy Tessa McKoin doesn’t buy it.

As the document from attorney Avi Gholian exclaims of the industry vet’s multi-season Shrinking stint: “no performance deficiency, misconduct. or business rationale was identified then or anytime thereafter.”

Watch on Deadline

Filing earlier today with the California Civil Rights Department before going to the LASC docket, McKoin alleges the real reason she was canned was because of reporting an intentional “sexual abuse” by Winston at the June 22, 2024 Shrinking Season 2 wrap party, She says it was because of that and because of her raising a stink about of “inaccurate time records and pay statements.” Production and WBTV problems that Loot and Young Sheldon alum McKoin and her lawyers assert resulted in zero “corrective action” on the former and a lot of her Shrinking bosses not making a “big deal” about the former.

McKoin says the CAA-repped Winston subjected her “to unwelcome, severe harassment because of her sex, including by grabbing and groping her breast without her consent at a work-related function in the presence of a coworker” at the 2024 party. “Such conduct was sufficiently severe to alter the conditions of Plaintiff employment and to create a hostile, intimidating, and offensive working environment.”

An environment made all the worse by WBTV doing nothing about it, according to the plaintiff.

While the sexual harassment and sexual battery claims sit on the top of McKoin’s allegations, it is the pay and timecard tampering of sorts that takes up the bulk of Tuesday’s unspecified damages seeking filing.

In terms of retaliation, McKoin insists she made “bona fide complaints, both orally and in writing, that she was owed unpaid wages and that her time records had been unlawfully altered, and otherwise engaged in conduct protected by the Labor Code, including on or about May 26, May 28, June I0, June 11, June 19, and July I, 2026.” Her filing adds: “Warner Bros. discharged Plaintiff on July 10, 2026 – within 90 days of each of these instances of protected activities.“

“As a direct and proximate result of Warner Bros.’ violation of Labor Code …Plaintiff has suffered and continues to suffer lost wages and work benefits and other actual consequential, and incidental financial losses. as well as emotional distress. humiliation, mental anguish, and anxiety in an amount to be proven at trial.”

WBTV had no comment this evening when contacted by Deadline about the complaint and the allegations McKoin makes. Representatives for the multi-Emmy nominated Winston did no response when Deadline reached out about the claims against their client.

title: ‘Possible Love’ DoP Kim Ji-yong, ‘The Blue Road’ Director Han Jun-hee & WETA FX’s Kimball Thurston Among Speakers For Netflix ‘Creative Asia’ At BIFF
summary: Netflix has announced that speakers including Possible Love DoP Kim Ji-yong, The Blue Road director Han Jun-hee and WETA FX’s CTO Kimball Thurston will join the streamer’s Creative Asia programme at this year’s Busan International Film Festival (BIFF). Ji-yong will deliver a masterclass on how he and Possible Love director Lee Chang-dong shaped the visual […]
content:
Netflix has announced that speakers including Possible Love DoP Kim Ji-yong, The Blue Road director Han Jun-hee and WETA FX’s CTO Kimball Thurston will join the streamer’s Creative Asia programme at this year’s Busan International Film Festival (BIFF).

Ji-yong will deliver a masterclass on how he and Possible Love director Lee Chang-dong shaped the visual world of the film, which just scored the Grand Jury Prize in Venice and is Korea’s official section for the Oscars.

Han Jun-hee, whose credits also include D.P. and Weak Hero Class, is hosting a masterclass entitled “Making Unexpected Stories Resonate” about turning unexpected, even uncomfortable, subjects into stories that capture the world’s attention.

Creative Asia will also feature a masterclass on “Location and Storytelling”, bringing together perspectives from Lauren Cooper of Location Managers Guild International, Perfect Days producer Reiko Kunieda and Sung Q Lee, Senior Director, APAC Production at Netflix.

Watch on Deadline

WETA FX’s chief technology officer Kimball Thurston is one of the speakers on an industry panel about using AI in filmmaking – “AI in Filmmaking: New Tools, New Possibilities” – along with Sung Q Lee and Korean director Kang Yun-sung (Run To The West, The Outlaws).

Another industry panel entitled “New Voices in Filmmaking: What’s Ahead” will examine small- to medium-budget filmmaking and features speakers including Namkoong Sun (Love Untangled) and Wi Eun-kyoung and Son Gwang-min, co-directors of My Aunt.

The programme also includes two workshops: “The Art and Archetypes of Cinematic Storytelling”, led by Netflix’s Director, Content Acquisition, Christopher Mack, is aimed at writers and breaks down what makes a pilot compelling and the structural choices that keep audiences watching.

Led by Netflix’s Director, Creative Strategy, “Understanding the Buyer’s Perspective” looks at what motivates greenlight decisions, how a show gets chosen for financing, and what kind of script or story stays in the imagination after a pitch ends.

Designed to support the region’s next generation of creators, the programme has been devised by Netflix in partnership with BIFF, the Asian Film Commissions Network (AFCNet) and the Motion Picture Association (MPA). It will take place on October 10 at Dongseo University Centum Campus.

BIFF is running October 6-15 at the Busan Cinema Center and locations across Busan, with the Asian Contents & Film Market taking place at BEXCO October 10-13.

title: ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Season 35 Premiere Recap: The Men Take The Lead In First Of Two-Night Kick Off & Someone Goes Home Already
summary: SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from night one of the Season 35 premiere of Dancing with the Stars. Back like they never left! The ballroom at CBS Television City was once again glittering with celebrities on Tuesday night to kick off Season 35 of Dancing with the Stars. There are 16 contestants vying for […]
content:
SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from night one of the Season 35 premiere of Dancing with the Stars.

Back like they never left! The ballroom at CBS Television City was once again glittering with celebrities on Tuesday night to kick off Season 35 of Dancing with the Stars.

There are 16 contestants vying for the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy at the top of the season, and ABC opted for a two-night premiere that split the dances between Tuesday and Wednesday nights. On the first night, only the male celebrities performed. The ladies will take the floor on Wednesday night.

Unfortunately, things did not go over without a hitch. The party was interrupted by some tech issues, with voting going down online in the middle of the show. They threw out the ABC.com votes mid-premiere and relied solely on text votes, which have their own wrinkle this year since there’s two contestants who share the same name. Voters will need to specify Conner L. or Connor W. in their text votes, and they won’t count if they don’t, according to hosts Afonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough. What could go wrong there?

Watch on Deadline

While this week’s results might be questionable, the show must go on. Here’s how things shook out on night one.

Savannah Bananas midfielder Jackson Olson with Emma Slater. The baseball player kicked things off with a cha cha to “Wannabe” by the Spice Girls — and it’s clear that Slater is reveling in being paired with a younger partner this season. In the package before the dance, she said it’s the first time she’s ever worked with a celeb in their 20s, and admits there were less “limitations” working with Olson.The energetic routine was a nice introduction to Olson, and the judges ate it up. “The ballroom is back!” judge Derek Hough said. “Jackson, my man, you are a natural born performer.” BUT! Hough also warned that the judges are going to be pretty tough with their scores this season, and Olson has plenty of room for improvement in the technique department. SCORE: 15 out of 30

Reality star Tyler Cameron with Sharna Burgess. The Bachelor alum was the first of many reality stars to take the dance floor over the next two days, dancing a tango. The former college football player says he did take some dance classes in college, but he’s got some brushing up to do. After a multi-year hiatus from the show, Burgess pleased the judges with her first routine with Cameron. “Tyler, what’s going on here? I have to say, I’m very pleasantly surprised. I mean, look at him. He looks like a tank…you can move, man,” Bruno Tonioli complimented. SCORE: 17 out of 30

Reality star Conner Leavitt with Adele Zaikman. These two stepped onto the ballroom floor with something to prove Tuesday night, what with newcomer Zaikman as the winner of DWTS: The Next Pro and Leavitt married to Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star Whitney Leavitt, who took the ballroom by storm last season and leveraged the exposure to launch a Broadway run on Chicago. They danced a salsa to “Whoomp! (There It Is)” by Tag Team, putting Zaikman in her element as a Latin expert and taking Leavitt straight out of his. Carrie Ann Inaba called the routine “a little chaotic,” but overall, the judges loved the enthusiasm. SCORE: 12 out of 30

Late-night sidekick Guillermo Rodriguez with Witney Carson. Season 34 champ Carson is back on the ballroom floor with a much different contestant this year. She’s guiding Jimmy Kimmel’s right-hand man Rodriguez through the competition, and they started off with a cha cha. Carson, who is impressively competing pregnant this year, tried to disguise her partner’s lack of technique by leaning into Rodriguez’s charm, reminding why he’s spent decades at Kimmel’s side on late night. It only kind of worked. “Listen, was the technique there? No. Was the effort there? Absolutely,” Hough said. “We can’t be having heel leads in the cha cha.” Regardless, the audience clearly responded to Rodriguez’s “spicy” performance, chanting his name when he finished. There were even boos when the judges issued their (probably rightful) rating. SCORE: 10 out of 30

Paralympian Ezra Frech with Daniella Karagach. Julianne Hough kind of botched his introduction, but Frech still made a great impression on his first night as his rehearsal package gave audiences a glimpse of what he’s working through this season as an above-the-knee amputee in the competition. He and Karagach had to make some accommodations to take on the tango, but boy, did they deliver. The judges loved the fiery routine to Kelly Clarkson’s “Since U Been Gone,” and so did the crowd. “What really impressed me, you really looked like a leading man,” Tonioli said. SCORE: 20 out 30

Comedian and podcaster Connor Wood with Rylee Arnold. The second Connor of the night showcased his personality with a cha cha to “I Like It, I Love It” by Tim McGraw. Of the group, Wood has some of the least dance experience, so it appears Arnold may have her work cut out for her this season. But what he lacks in technique, he makes up for in his sincerity. On the bright side, Inaba says he didn’t give her “the ick” when he made a wrong move. A for effort! No comment on the person riding a bedazzled mechanical bull in the background for the entire number. SCORE: 16 out of 30

Musician Taylor Hanson with Britt Stewart. The middle Hanson brother is back on stage after spending years “avoiding dancing.” He says he’s uncomfortable performing without an instrument in tow, but Stewart tells him to think of her as his new “safety blanket.” Having gone from avoiding all dancing to taking on the quickstep night one, Derek Hough assures him he should feel proud, despite the flaws. Tonioli agreed. Now, he needs to work on his frame. “Don’t tighten up,” Tonioli said. SCORE: 16 out of 30

Actor Harry Shum Jr. with Jenna Johnson. The Glee and Grey’s Anatomy actor closed out the night one with yet another cha cha. Johnson took advantage of Shum’s freestyle and hip-hop experience, though, and his prior performance chops on Glee to deliver a performance full of personality and charm. And, well, they absolutely saved the best for last. Those two lit up the ballroom floor with an “emergency disco” that had Tonioli in a fit. “The chemistry between you two is off the charts. Sharp as a scalpel,” he said. SCORE: 21 out of 30 (the highest score of the night!)

So, who goes home?

Sadly, after just one dance, Conner Leavitt and Adele Zaikman are sent packing. Well, they’ll be back in the ballroom at least once more for tomorrow’s ‘live afterparty’ with Season 34 winner Robert Irwin and whomever among the women is voted off on night two.

title: ‘A Talent For Murder’ Review: Helen Mirren Is Mesmerizing As Tortured Genius Crime Writer Patricia Highsmith – Toronto Film Festival
summary: This flawed but very entertaining two-hander belongs in the unique subgenre of literary biographies in which a cult author’s life is investigated through the highly specific prism of their work. Shirley Jackson, for example, was cast into a dark Gothic psychodrama in Josephine Decker’s Shirley; William S. Burroughs became a drug-addicted spy who reports to […]
content:
This flawed but very entertaining two-hander belongs in the unique subgenre of literary biographies in which a cult author’s life is investigated through the highly specific prism of their work. Shirley Jackson, for example, was cast into a dark Gothic psychodrama in Josephine Decker’s Shirley; William S. Burroughs became a drug-addicted spy who reports to a big talking-ass beetle in David Cronenberg’s Naked Lunch; and similarly, as she waits for inspiration to strike, Patricia Highsmith communes with the spirit of her most famous character — suave psychopath Tom Ripley — in Anton Corbijn’s A Talent for Murder.

The framing device recalls classic stage-to-screen thrillers such as Sleuth and, more pertinently, Death Trap, both being one-location cat-and-mouse thrillers in which the power balance constantly changes. Here, the year is 1995 and Highsmith (Helen Mirren) is at death’s door and in exile, smoking like a chimney on the veranda of her home in Zurich. A single piece of paper is parked in her typewriter, entirely blank. Now 74, she is known around the world for “The Ripliad”, a series of five books, starting with The Talented Mr. Ripley in 1955, following the adventures of a vicious but charismatic con man and killer.

Watch on Deadline

The author went on to write four more, the last as recently as 1991, but as the film opens, the writer’s publishing company wants one more. To this end, the boss sends Edward Ridgeway (Alden Ehrenreich), an unassuming junior staffer whom Highsmith instantly mocks for his baby face and awkwardness (“I know a homo when I see one”). A heightened game of wits instantly begins; Highsmith threatens to throw him out then relents, allowing him to stay for a beer. Ridgeway has brought gifts — a few notebooks, several crisp white Brooks Brothers shirts, and six tins of soup — that buy him a little more time with the old lady.

Highsmith — known locally as “The Texas Battleaxe” and the chief suspect when her neighbour’s dog is poisoned — is a piece of work, revealing herself as supremely bigoted and an equal-opportunities racist: “They may be repulsive but they know their stuff,” she says of the French, a begrudging acknowledgment of The Order of Arts and Letters that hangs on her sitting-room wall. But more than foreigners, she hates New Yorkers and especially rich, pretentious upper-class New Yorkers, a minor detail at first but one that will become more significant over time as Highsmith begins to open up about the neuroses that motivate her.

The beginning plays out almost like a horror-comedy — Highsmith’s deliciously mean, spiteful face pops up from time to time in humorously effective jump scares — and the film becomes quite farcical when, over a breakfast of scrambled eggs, she discusses the efficiency of various poisons, knowing that Ridgeway has seen the bottle of arsenic she has strategically placed in her kitchen (“Unoriginal but iconic,” she teases). But Ridgeway pushes on, trying various means — flattery, insults, amateur psychology — to cajole her into delivering a new Ripley book.

Inspiration seems to strike when Highsmith starts freestyling the beginnings of a fresh story, with Ripley in Rome. Ridgeway joins in, thinking back to his recent encounter with a well-to-do American student, Clementine Balfour (Olivia Cooke), that he met on the way, a subtle callback to Highsmith’s 1950 debut, Strangers on a Train. From here, Clementine becomes two distinct characters, both the girl Ridgeway met in real life (and will meet again in the local town) and prey for the ruthless Tom Ripley in Highsmith’s developing fiction.

The blurring of truth and fantasy is fascinating but also exactly that: Blurred. Sometimes it works brilliantly, as the unassuming Ridgeway loses grasp of his better nature, just as Highsmith says he will, somehow becoming infected with her bitterness and cruelty. The parallel story-with-in-the-story, however, in which Ridgeway (as Ripley) marries the other Clementine for her family’s money — entirely confected, by the way — is more problematic, being, to put it mildly, not terribly cinematic, with Highsmith dictating everything we see and hear at the exact same time we’re seeing it and hearing it.

Mirren, playing wildly against type, is a revelation here, perfectly inhabiting the troglodyte genius who seduced the public with their own dark reflections and resented them for the success they gave her. Meanwhile, to put it bluntly, the role of Ridgeway/Ripley would be a stretch for any actor, and Ehrenreich seems a little out of his depth when Corbijn’s film takes off in a meta new direction.

It’s all up in the air for a while but Ehrenreich rallies in time for the film’s enigmatic but strangely satisfying conclusion: This, it transpires, is not a film about Highsmith but about Tom Ripley, her very own “master of seduction”.

Is Ridgeway real or is he a death-dream manifestation of Ripley, the monster she made from her own seething id, an avenging avatar created by a woman who hated life, hated people, hated herself? Is she being taken down by her own creation, playing the same duplicitous, sadistic long game she enjoyed imagining him inflicting on his victims? It’s a fascinating question, and it’s very well posed.

Title: A Talent For Murder

Festival: Toronto (Gala Presentations)

Director: Anton Corbijn

Screenwriter: Joanna Murray-Smith

Cast: Helen Mirren, Alden Ehrenreich, Olivia Cooke

International sales: FilmNation Entertainment

Running time: 1 hr 46 mins

title: Markus Lehmusruusu’s Finnish Oscar Entry ‘The Squirrel’ Earns Aki Kaurismäki’s Stamp of Approval: ‘He Said It’s Like ‘2001: A Space Odyssey,’ but Better Because It’s Full of Humanism’
