He said it was like ‘2001: A Space Odyssey,’ but better because it’s full of humanism. I really loved that,” the director tells Variety. “I hope that […]
content:
Markus Lehmusruusu’s futuristic drama “The Squirrel” has just been selected as the Finnish Oscar submission, and it already has a notable fan.

“Aki Kaurismäki called it a masterpiece. He said it was like ‘2001: A Space Odyssey,’ but better because it’s full of humanism. I really loved that,” the director tells Variety.

“I hope that it can work on two levels. It’s full of humanism, but it also shows that as humans, we shouldn’t always put ourselves first.”

His protagonist, Pasi, needs to understand that as well. In the sterile future, nature and animals no longer exist. At least, that’s how it seems until Pasi, who designs artificial pets, suddenly encounters an actual squirrel – maybe the last one in the world. He brings it home, but it’s not happy there. It belongs in the wild.

Popular on Variety

“The Squirrel” stars Miro Lopperi (“Codename: Annika”), Mimosa Willamo (“Sisu”) and Hannu-Pekka Björkman (upcoming “Red Snow”). Recently shown at Fantastic Fest, the film is sold by REinvent International Sales and produced by Bufo, Pallas Film, Volya Films and Zentropa Sweden.

Being selected as an Oscar submission has been “rewarding,” says Lehmusruusu.

“It’s a big risk to make a film like that, which doesn’t fit within one genre.”

In recent years, Finland has selected several films that don’t fit the typical Oscar mold, from “Euthanizer” to “Family Time” and boozy comedy “100 Liters of Gold.” It has only earned one nomination in the category, for Aki Kaurismäki’s “The Man Without a Past.”

“It’s about telling stories that come from the heart without overthinking where they ‘fit’,” notes Lehmusruusu.

“Now, I’m working on projects that feel almost naturalistic, but I’ve always been interested in films that depict someone’s inner world. Cinema can convey that so easily. It’s like a magic trick.”

For his characters, the situation is clear: animalistic urges are bad. But as the story progresses, they want to give in to them.

“Thanks to technology, we sometimes feel omnipotent. But wouldn’t something be missing if replaced nature with something that doesn’t have its downsides?,” wonders Lehmusruusu.

“This also led to sexuality being a big part of the film because we keep hearing about people not having sex anymore. Young people just aren’t interested, partly because they’re repulsed by bodily fluids. Sexuality is perhaps the most primal force we have left, and we are becoming detached from it.”

Luckily, it only takes one squirrel to open his characters’ eyes and encourage them to venture outside of their comfort zones. Even though they’re so used to controlling their bodies and their surroundings.

The film’s naughty, not-quite-PG side is perfectly exemplified by its titular hero.

“A squirrel is cute, but it’s also a rodent. They destroy things in people’s houses and attack small birds. I wanted to show how we project onto animals. We think we know their emotions. At one point, we wondered if our squirrel should have expressions, but then I went: ‘I don’t want it to do anything it doesn’t actually do.’ It’s one of those animals we take for granted. And when you take something for granted, it’s so painful when it’s gone.”

Instead of choosing obvious villains, Lehmusruusu talks about “the consequences of indifference” in the film.

“I wanted to show people who have good intentions, but they have gone too far. We like to think we’re protecting our families or societies, but what are we willing to sacrifice? It could be nature or another form of life,” he says.

“My idea was to go against this dystopian science fiction where evil is always lurking. In a way, it feels even darker to say that people aren’t bad; they are just making bad choices. As a species, we’re responsible for a lot of shit.”

However, sometimes we are able to clean it up.

“If you look at the bigger picture, the horror of it all slowly sneaks up on you. But I wanted this film to work also if you’re not willing to do that. I want people to find it entertaining, funny and joyful.”

title: Adam Fan Releases Debut English-Language Album ‘Skyfall’
summary: Chinese superstar Adam Fan, also known as Fan Chengcheng, has released his debut full-length English-language album “Skyfall,” expanding his music to international audiences. The release arrived alongside the music video for focus track “Make It Make Sense.” “Skyfall” is produced by international music production company Hits Rhythm and A WW Productions, with an outside-China distribution […]
content:
Chinese superstar Adam Fan, also known as Fan Chengcheng, has released his debut full-length English-language album “Skyfall,” expanding his music to international audiences.

The release arrived alongside the music video for focus track “Make It Make Sense.”

“Skyfall” is produced by international music production company Hits Rhythm and A WW Productions, with an outside-China distribution partnership between Hits Rhythm and Pacific Music Group supporting the album’s global rollout. The album features contributions from Western producers, including Grammy-nominated talents.

Adam Fan first rose to prominence through the Chinese survival show “Idol Producer” before debuting as a member of boy group Nine Percent and launching a solo career. He has since starred in television dramas and variety programs including “The Journey Across the Night” and “Keep Running,” building a combined social media following of more than 100 million across platforms in China and Asia.

Popular on Variety

The album’s title track, “Skyfall,” was cowritten by American artist Lawson, whose writing credits include The Weeknd and Playboi Carti’s “Timeless.”

“Make It Make Sense” was written and produced by Puku, whose credits include the track “Something About You” by Partynextdoor and Drake. Other tracks on the album include “Go Girl,” “TTTM,” “Error,” “Make It Rock,” “Pink” and “Heard of Us.”

Adam Fan said in a statement, “I’m excited to bring Skyfall and its visual world to audiences around the world. This album represents the music I genuinely love and the creative direction I’ve always wanted to explore. I want to keep challenging myself, breaking boundaries and pushing my creativity further, while hopefully inspiring more people to discover new possibilities through music.”

title: John Abraham Starts Shooting Ribhu Dasgupta’s Psychological Thriller ‘Guru’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Principal photography has commenced on “Guru,” a Bollywood psychological thriller starring John Abraham and directed by Ribhu Dasgupta. The film also stars Danish Pandor, Arif Zakaria and Kitu Gidwani. Dasgupta is known for his work in the thriller genre. His credits include the Netflix series “Bard of Blood,” as well as “Girl on the Train” […]
content:
Principal photography has commenced on “Guru,” a Bollywood psychological thriller starring John Abraham and directed by Ribhu Dasgupta.

The film also stars Danish Pandor, Arif Zakaria and Kitu Gidwani.

Dasgupta is known for his work in the thriller genre. His credits include the Netflix series “Bard of Blood,” as well as “Girl on the Train” and “Te3n.” He is also attached to the upcoming “Section 84 IPC.”

Set against a backdrop of unsettling mystery, “Guru” follows a man whose life begins to change when he realizes that something is not right, and that his memory and his reality are two distinct things. As strange events unfold around him, he starts questioning his own perception of reality and wondering whom he can rely on. The story brings together Abraham, Pandor, Zakaria and Gidwani in a plot where memory and reality steadily converge.

Popular on Variety

“The world of ‘Guru’ is unsettling. Anything which has depth in terms of story, treatment and performance, at the same time gives you something to relish, excites and challenges a filmmaker. I have been wanting to collaborate with John for a long time and ‘Guru’ is that script with that destiny,” Dasgupta said.

“‘Guru’ is the kind of story that stays with you long after you’ve read it. What drew me to the film was the uncertainty at its core – when you can’t trust your own memory, reality itself becomes a question. The storyline is layered, unsettling and deeply intriguing, and I’m excited for audiences to experience it,” Abraham added.

The film is produced by Authum Entertainment, Shibasish Sarkar, JA Entertainment and Fusion Flicks.

title: Oscars: Spain Selects ‘La Bola Negra’ for International Features Race
summary: “La Bola Negra,” Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s Cannes Festival sensation, is Spain’s submission for the 2027 international feature film Academy Award. Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s “The Beloved, ”starring Javier Bardem, and Alauda Ruiz de Azua’s Goya and San Sebastián winner “Sundays” also figured in Spain’s international feature shortlist, arguably the strongest in Spanish history. Any other […]
content:
“La Bola Negra,” Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s Cannes Festival sensation, is Spain’s submission for the 2027 international feature film Academy Award.

Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s “The Beloved, ”starring Javier Bardem, and Alauda Ruiz de Azua’s Goya and San Sebastián winner “Sundays” also figured in Spain’s international feature shortlist, arguably the strongest in Spanish history.

Any other Oscar entry choice from Spain than “La Bola Negra,” announced Wednesday by Alejandro Amenábar on behalf of Spain’s Academia de Cine, would have been a shock.

Amenábar, whose “The Sea Inside” won Spain’s most recent international feature Oscar in 2005, opened the envelope and announced “La Bola Negra” at the Academia de Cine’s Madrid headquarters.

Popular on Variety

The choice came after a second-round vote by Academy members, following the Sept. 3 selection of “La Bola Negra,” “The Beloved” and “Sundays” as the country’s three shortlisted titles.

World premiering in Cannes main competition, “La Bola Negra” first caught attention by scoring a 16 minute standing ovation at its world premiere on the Croisette. It caused a further splash winning best director, shared with Paweł Pawlikowski for “Fatherland.”

Picked up by Netflix for the U.S. and later Canada, “La Bola Negra” again moved waves when Netflix announced that it would open the feature theatrically on Oct. 16, setting a 47-day U.S. theatrical window the longest form any movie in the streaming giant’s history, a sure indication that the film will feature strongly among the streamer’s awards priorities for the fall.

Though already regarded as one of the frontrunners in the international feature film category, “La Bola Negra” is already being talked up as a candidate for multiple other categories. “La Bola Negra’ has mucho heat,” Variety has asseverated.

Sweeping, unapologetically passionate and hugely ambitious, “La Bola Negra” braids three connected stories, each shot in a different film style, chronicling the travails and legacy of Spain’s gay experience in 1932, 1937 during the Spanish Civil War, and 2017. It picks up on the first four pages in an unfinished novel by legendary poet-playwright Federico García Lorca, bludgeoned and shot to death by Franco’s troops in 1936 for being a social activist and homosexual, “un maricón” in the Spanish macho slur.

The film features a feisty turn from Penélope Cruz as a cabaret dancer and a cameo from Glenn Close as a modern-day hispanist, accompanying Spanish stars Miguel Bernardeau, Guitarricadelafuente, Milo Quifes and Carlos Gutiérrez in lead roles.

From the get-go, the Javis set out to make “a super production that is auteur-driven but also very queer,” Ambrossi told Variety before the Cannes world premiere.

Heavily researched, “La Bola Negra” reflects not only the ambitions of Los Javis, as its writer-director are known, but also Movistar Plus, the biggest Spanish pay TV/SVOD operator which produced with Los Javis newly launched Suma Content Films. It is co-produced by Pedro and Agustín Almodovar’s El Deseo and France’s Le Pacte, with the participation of Spanish network Atresmedia. Sales agent Goodfellas has practically sold out the world.

After “lighting up” Telluride, Variety has reported, “La Bola Negra,” the film bowed Tuesday in Toronto. It won the Audience Award at Australia Sydney Festival, will open New York’s LGBTQ+ film festival NewFest on Oct. 15. “La Bola Negra” will have is Spanish premiere at the San Sebastián Festival on Saturday, where it has already sparked a feeding fever for tickets.

The shortlist for the 2027 Oscar nominations will be announced by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences on Dec. 15, with the final selection announced on Jan. 21. The 99th Academy Awards ceremony is scheduled to take place on March 14 in Los Angeles.

title: ‘Vivant’ Tops Asia Streaming Chart, First Japanese Drama to Lead, Report Finds
summary: TBS drama “Vivant” outdrew every other streaming title across Asia last month, excluding China and India, becoming the first Japanese show to top ampd Analytics’ regional monthly ranking since the measurement firm began tracking the market. The finding comes from a new ampd Vision report titled “Vivant: A TV Broadcast Hit, Streamed.” “Vivant,” which launched […]
content:
TBS drama “Vivant” outdrew every other streaming title across Asia last month, excluding China and India, becoming the first Japanese show to top ampd Analytics’ regional monthly ranking since the measurement firm began tracking the market.

The finding comes from a new ampd Vision report titled “Vivant: A TV Broadcast Hit, Streamed.”

“Vivant,” which launched its second season in July as part of TBS’s Sunday Theater slot, pulled in 15.6 million unique viewers regionwide in August, with 15.1 million watching in Japan alone. That figure equals a quarter of the 61.4 million viewers ampd tracks across Japanese VOD, according to the report from ampd Analytics, the streaming measurement arm of Media Partners Asia (MPA).

The series follows Yusuke Nogi, a Japanese trading company employee drawn into an international conspiracy tied to a shadowy government intelligence unit known as Beppan. Season 2 picks up immediately after the first season’s cliffhanger and was shot partly on location in Azerbaijan.

Popular on Variety

Much of that reach came through TVer, the free platform operated by Japan’s broadcast networks, which drew 10.2 million of the show’s viewers. Only two other titles have ever pulled 10 million viewers on one platform in a single market within a month, according to ampd: broadcasts of the World Baseball Classic in Japan and the Korean drama “Teach You a Lesson,” both distributed on Netflix. TBS made the new season available on TVer at no cost within an hour of its Sunday broadcast, reserving paid streaming exclusively for U-Next. That arrangement created a second viewing peak each week, on Monday nights, and 92% of viewers who came back for a new episode had already watched the previous one by the time it aired.

The show’s popularity also lifted viewership of its first season elsewhere. Netflix’s audience for “Vivant” grew more than eightfold between May and August, from 300,000 viewers to 2.5 million, while U-Next’s viewership rose over the same period from 100,000 to 2 million. That shift happened even among subscribers who already had access to the show elsewhere: an estimated one in eight Prime Video subscribers and one in 10 Netflix subscribers in Japan chose to watch “Vivant” on TVer rather than on the services they already pay for.

Beyond the streaming platforms, “Vivant” built a substantial following on YouTube, where related content drew 13.2 million viewers, nearly matching its VOD reach. That audience was spread across more than 1,600 videos posted by 450 channels, totaling 8.8 million hours watched at an average of almost 40 minutes per viewer. A companion show TBS produced alongside the drama, “Villains’ Meeting Room,” averaged more than 1.3 million viewers an episode.

“‘Vivant’ is a distribution story as much as a content story,” said Sam Yousif, managing director of ampd Analytics. “A quarter of Japan’s tracked VOD audience watched one drama in a single month, and premium subscribers moved to a free platform to follow it. Japan is the largest VOD market we measure, with the closest relationship between broadcast and streaming anywhere in the region, and measuring a title today means measuring it everywhere it lives, including YouTube, where ‘Vivant’ reached almost as many people as it did on VOD.”

The drama’s success did not extend much beyond Japan’s borders. Some 97% of all “Vivant” viewing came from local audiences, ampd found, a pattern consistent with Japanese dramas’ broader struggles abroad: they land in Netflix’s global top 10 outside Japan just 0.3 times a month on average, well behind Korean dramas at 4.1 times and Japanese anime at 1.4.

title: Wonder Studios: AI Producer Expands LA Office By Hiring CAA Agent & Ex-Westbrook Executive
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Wonder Studios, the UK-based AI production outfit valued at $50 million last year, has expanded its Los Angeles operation with two hires. Inder Gill, a media finance agent at CAA, is joining Wonder as head of studio partnerships and packaging. He helped package and finance films including Monkey Man and If I Had Legs […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Wonder Studios, the UK-based AI production outfit valued at $50 million last year, has expanded its Los Angeles operation with two hires.

Inder Gill, a media finance agent at CAA, is joining Wonder as head of studio partnerships and packaging. He helped package and finance films including Monkey Man and If I Had Legs I’d Kick You.

Ryan Ascencio, co-CEO of Patreon-style company FanFix and formerly EVP of corporate development at Will Smith and Jada Pinkett Smith’s Westbrook, becomes head of growth.

Wonder’s Los Angeles studio will be based at The Lighthouse Campus in Venice Beach, alongside existing teams in London and New York. The company said 90% of its revenue originates from the U.S.

Watch on Deadline

Since launching last year, Wonder has raised $15 million to hit a $50 million valuation, produced re-creation scenes for Campfire’s The Real Wolf of Wall Street, collaborated with Lewis Capaldi on a music video, and made YouTube anthology series Beyond the Loop.

Xavier Collins, co-founder and CEO of Wonder Studios, said: “Wonder has been a global business from day one. While we are proud of our European roots, the U.S. is where the overwhelming majority of our work has come from – winning work with some of the world’s biggest brands and streamers.”

Gill said: “Wonder is redefining what a project costs and how quickly it can come to life, all while empowering filmmakers.”

title: ‘Hunting Gary Glitter’: Netflix Unveils Trailer & Launch Date For Doc About Race To Expose Serial Sex Abuser
summary: Trailer has dropped for Netflix’s Hunting Gary Glitter, the former pop superstar who was exposed as a serial child abuser. Check it out above. Launching October 14, the doc follows the pursuit of journalists alongside the survivors who speak out, charting Glitter’s 1997 conviction, through to his years on the run, and eventual incarceration. This […]
content:
Trailer has dropped for Netflix‘s Hunting Gary Glitter, the former pop superstar who was exposed as a serial child abuser. Check it out above.

Launching October 14, the doc follows the pursuit of journalists alongside the survivors who speak out, charting Glitter’s 1997 conviction, through to his years on the run, and eventual incarceration.

This string of dogged journalists chase the fugitive pop star across the globe — from Cuba to Cambodia to Vietnam — determined to expose the child sexual abuse he concealed behind decades of chart-topping fame.

Real name Paul Francis Gadd, Glitter was a pop sensation in the 1970s and 1980s but was convicted in 1999 of downloading child sexual abuse material and of many more offences over the following years, along with being deported from several countries. He was most recently charged with further historical sex offences.

Watch on Deadline

Netflix’s doc is its latest big UK true crime series and comes from Voltage TV, with Sam Starbuck and Sanjay Singhal producing the three-parter.

Netflix has previously shone a light on serial sex abuser Jimmy Savile via its Jimmy Savile: A British Horror Story doc.

title: Oscars: Spain Selects ‘La Bola Negra’ For International Feature Film Race
summary: Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s breakout Cannes title La Bola Negra has been selected as Spain’s entry for the Best International Feature Film category at the 99th Academy Awards. The Spanish Film Academy confirmed the selection this morning during a press conference. The film explores LGBT heritage and pays tribute to murdered Spanish poet and […]
content:
Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s breakout Cannes title La Bola Negra has been selected as Spain’s entry for the Best International Feature Film category at the 99th Academy Awards.

The Spanish Film Academy confirmed the selection this morning during a press conference.

The film explores LGBT heritage and pays tribute to murdered Spanish poet and playwright Federico García Lorca through the interconnected stories of three men in the three different eras of 1932, 1937 and 2017. The cast features Guitarricadelafuente, Miguel Bernardeau, Carlos González, Milo Quifes, Penélope Cruz, Lola Dueñas and Glenn Close.

World premiering in Competition, the picture took Cannes by storm in May, prompting a 20-minute ovation and then winning Best Director for Calvo and Ambrossi.

Watch on Deadline

In the market, it sparked a bidding war for U.S. rights, with Netflix securing the film for the territory in a record-breaking seven-figure domestic deal brokered by Goodfellas and CAA Media Finance.

In Europe, the film has also sold to Benelux (Cinéart), Switzerland (Filmcoopi), Germany and Austria (Pandora Film), Greece (Rosebud), UK & Ireland (Altitude), Italy (Movies Inspired), Scandinavia (Another World), Portugal (Nitrato Filmes), Bulgaria (Cinelibri), Yugoslavia (MCF), Hungary (Mozinet), Czech Republic (Aero Films), Romania (Independenta), Baltic States (A-One Films) and Poland (Gutek Film).

In the rest of the world, it has been acquired for Israel (New Cinemas), Latin America (Cine Video y TV), Australia and New Zealand (Rialto Distribution), Japan (Transformer), South Korea (Challan), Taiwan (ifilm), Hong Kong (Edko), India (Impact Films), Thailand (Sahamongkol), Singapore (Anticipate Pictures), the Philippines (FDCP) and Airlines (Skeye).

La Bola Negra is an original film by Movistar Plus+ Film and Suma Content Films in co-production with El Deseo and Le Pacte, with the participation of Atresmedia.

Netflix will release the film on October 16.

title: Bill Nighy Playing Socially-Challenged Literary Titan In Richard Curtis’ Debut Audio Sitcom
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Richard Curtis is returning to the sitcom game, this time through audio. The Vicar of Dibley, Blackadder and Mr Bean writer-director is making Greatest Living Writer for BBC Radio 4 starring Bill Nighy, Nicola Walker, Nick Mohammed, Jim Broadbent, Meera Syal and Traitors star Madelyn Smedley. It is Curtis’ first sitcom in nearly 20 […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Richard Curtis is returning to the sitcom game, this time through audio.

The Vicar of Dibley, Blackadder and Mr Bean writer-director is making Greatest Living Writer for BBC Radio 4 starring Bill Nighy, Nicola Walker, Nick Mohammed, Jim Broadbent, Meera Syal and Traitors star Madelyn Smedley. It is Curtis’ first sitcom in nearly 20 years and his first for audio.

Launching on Boxing Day on Radio 4 and as a BBC Sounds box-set two weeks prior, the series centers on John Westlake (Nighy), a literary titan whose towering genius has earned him global reverence, lifelong indulgence, and absolutely no useful social skills. As those around him absorb the blast radius of his genius, the series plays with creativity, legacy, literary celebrity, family, and the uncomfortable truth that being good at writing does not necessarily make you good at being a pleasant person. The character draws comparisons with the iconic Billy Mack, who Nighy played with aplomb in Love Actually.

Curtis is an Oscar-nominated British screen legend whose movie credits include Notting Hill and Four Weddings and a Funeral.

Watch on Deadline

His last TV sitcom was The Vicar of Dibley, which concluded on the BBC in 2007. He has recently turned to animation: writing and producing Netflix’s That Christmas in 2024 and now producing Not Alone for Universal.

Curtis said: “I’m loving working in this tight 15” minute format for the BBC – writing for performers I know and love – and writing something that’s about the creative world I have such direct experience of, as it crashes into family dynamics.”

Script editor Emma Freud added: “Of all his writing, this is the closest Richard has written to his life, his world, his home and his experiences. It’s been a joy to see the scripts flowing out of him – I’ve never seen him write so fast or enjoy the process as much. He isn’t the brute at the centre of this comedy – but that brute is, I think, how he would secretly like to behave if he could. Which he can’t.”

Goldhawk Productions‘ Greatest Living Writer is produced by Emma Hearn, John Scott Dryden and Alex Hollands and script edited by Freud. It comes on a BBC audio slate that includes pilots from Nish Kumar and Jake Bhardwaj, along with stand-up and quiz shows.

title: Jodie Whittaker To Star As Hotshot Media Lawyer In ITV Drama ‘In Contempt’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Jodie Whittaker’s next starring role will be a hotshot media lawyer in ITV drama In Contempt. Ahead of her role in Hulu pilot Chicks and a part in the London-set Only Murders in the Building Season 6, Whittaker will star in the “high-stakes” legal drama as barrister Olivia Savareid. The character’s top-drawer advocacy skills […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Jodie Whittaker‘s next starring role will be a hotshot media lawyer in ITV drama In Contempt.

Ahead of her role in Hulu pilot Chicks and a part in the London-set Only Murders in the Building Season 6, Whittaker will star in the “high-stakes” legal drama as barrister Olivia Savareid.

The character’s top-drawer advocacy skills have built her a career defending people’s reputations and engaging in multi-million pound litigation to prevent their names from being destroyed on social media, but the series will see the tables turned on her.

Sherlock and Dracula maker Hartswood Films is producing in association with its parent, ITV Studios (ITVS), with the show airing in the UK on ITV and STV and on streamers ITVX and STV Player. ITVS has international distribution rights.

Watch on Deadline

Steve Thompson (Sherlock) is the writer, with Sue Vertue and Steven Moffat the executive producers. Ed Bazalgette (The Last Kingdom) is the director and Lawrence Till (Douglas is Cancelled) the producer. ITV’s Director of Drama, Polly Hill, who commissioned the show is also overseeing production for the broadcaster.

In Contempt establishes Olivia’s challenging working relationship with veteran news director Greg Dalman, who edits a London daily newspaper prone to pushing the boundaries of what can be published. With a reputation for taking no prisoners, Greg has the capability of acting recklessly if he believes it’s in the public interest, and and as his legal counsel, Olivia, must summon all her skills and expertise to keep him out of libel court.

She is also the mother of 15-year-old daughter, but when an explosive situation erupts at work, she makes a crucial misjudgement and Olivia’s own reputation is suddenly on the line.

“There’s always been a voracious appetite for what happens behind the scenes before news stories are published,” said ITV’s Hill. “Steve has created a gripping and thought-provoking series and I’m thrilled Jodie Whittaker has agreed to play ‘hotshot’ lawyer Olivia Savereid. I have no doubt In Contempt will captivate our audience, as it’s a really timely story for ITV to be telling.”

Whittaker, known for leading Doctor Who and ITV drama Broadchurch, said of her role as Savareid. “This is an amazing character in a world I haven’t explored before. Steve Thompson’s writing is an absolute joy to work with and I’m so excited to be embarking on this adventure with such a brilliant creative team at Hartswood Films and ITV.”

Vertue said she had been seeking to work with Thompson again since BBC series Sherlock, but that “it was never the right time or the right idea” until now. “Then one day he sat down and said, “In the modern world, if you want to kill someone, you don’t use a gun – you destroy their reputation,’ and so began In Contempt.

“A whirlwind drama of cancellation, online poison and media law, where there’s less than 12 hours to stop a headline that could detonate someone’s life. This is the story of now, and this is the series for today. I’m delighted to be working with ITV again and to bring to screen Steve Thompson’s most explosive and personal drama yet.”

Thompson called the show “a signature piece for me”, adding: “It unpacks the challenging relationship between the media and the law – between the freedom of the press and people’s right to privacy. In a world where all of us are surfing the net, hungry for the latest gossip, this drama takes us behind the curtain and shows us the lawyers who are in the vanguard of that fight.”

In Contempt will begin filming in London in the fall with further casting coming closer to production commencing.

title: Ex-‘Bachelor’ Host Chris Harrison’s Next Dating Show ‘The Vow’ Sets November Premiere on Fox Nation
summary: “Roses fade. True love lasts forever,” says Chris Harrison in a cheeky teaser for “The Vow,” his return to reality television five years after his controversial exit from the “Bachelor” franchise. The new dating show premieres on Fox Nation on Nov. 11, with six episodes rolling out weekly until a series finale on Dec. 9. […]
content:
“Roses fade. True love lasts forever,” says Chris Harrison in a cheeky teaser for “The Vow,” his return to reality television five years after his controversial exit from the “Bachelor” franchise.

The new dating show premieres on Fox Nation on Nov. 11, with six episodes rolling out weekly until a series finale on Dec. 9. “The Vow” follows one eligible bachelor, 30-year-old Jace Cates, as he embarks on a “relationship journey” with 10 women looking for lasting commitment and marriage.

Per the description, the show will explore “whether shared values, faith, communication, and long-term goals can build a relationship designed to last long after the cameras stop rolling. At a time when much of modern dating culture is driven by fleeting connections and social media attention, the series offers a different approach by placing the focus on meaningful relationships, commitment and building a life together.”

Jace Cates, the eligible bachelor of “The Vow” Courtesy of Fox Nation

The teaser for “The Vow” did not hold back on drawing the connection between Harrison and TV’s most iconic dating show. The host even throws a red rose — the symbol of “The Bachelor” — on the ground before threatening to step on it.

And “The Vow” will even feature an appearance from Sean and Catherine Lowe, whose love story unfolded on Season 17 of “The Bachelor” in 2013. The pair has been married since and is one of the most famous examples of a long-lasting relationship to form on reality television.

Other “Bachelor” alumni are on board as well, including executive producer Louis Caris, consulting producer Elan Gale as casting director Lindsay Liles and director Michael Shea. Executive producers also include Harrison’s wife, Lauren Zima, plus Lionsgate Alternative Television executives Nicholas Caprio and Tom Huffman.

Harrison hosted “The Bachelor” and all of its spinoffs from the series’ inception in 2002. He exited the franchise in 2021 after comments he made defending former contestant Rachael Kirkconnell drew sharp backlash and were perceived by some as racially insensitive. Kirkconnell was under fire after photos circulated online of her attending an antebellum plantation-themed party as a college student. Harrison apologized for his comments and stepped away from the “Bachelor” franchise temporarily, but Variety reported at the time that Harrison’s team became outraged with the “dragging-out process” surrounding his return “and was unhappy with the network and studio not publicly supporting Harrison.” So, the host negotiated an exit package and largely disappeared from the small screen in the following years.

“I’m so excited to be back helping people find love, and Fox Nation has been an incredible partner in bringing this vision to life,” Harrison said in a statement. “We were inspired by the faith-driven renaissance happening across America, and as a result, I believe we’ve created the most authentic dating show on television today. At a time when so many people feel dating has become harder than ever, ‘The Vow’ asks a simple but important question: Can genuine, lasting love still be found in the modern world? The stakes couldn’t be higher. I’m incredibly proud and honored to put my name on this show.”

title: ‘Run Hide Fight: Infidels’ Review: Jonathan Majors Scrapes the Barrel in This Islamophobic Drivel
summary: More an epic act of trolling than a sincere creative endeavor, “Run Hide Fight: Infidels” aspires to “own the libs” and antagonize Muslims, but the filmmaking is so shoddy that neither group will likely seek it out, even to assess whether they should be offended. Written and directed by onetime Hollywood hopeful Kyle Rankin (“The […]
content:
More an epic act of trolling than a sincere creative endeavor, “Run Hide Fight: Infidels” aspires to “own the libs” and antagonize Muslims, but the filmmaking is so shoddy that neither group will likely seek it out, even to assess whether they should be offended. Written and directed by onetime Hollywood hopeful Kyle Rankin (“The Battle of Shaker Heights”), this standalone sequel to his 2020 film “Run Hide Fight” actively parrots the views of its distributor, right-wing media platform The Daily Wire, with its story of a military veteran battling jihadists on a college campus. Yet its comically reductive treatment of characters, regardless of their partisanship, ensures that the film’s transgressions are largely artistic instead of political, rendering it (mostly) unworthy of the outrage its Islamophobic promotional campaign has thus far attempted to stoke.

Following in the footsteps of “Citizen Vigilante” star and fellow embattled actor Armie Hammer, Jonathan Majors fights personal financial insolvency as Clay Saunders, a Delta Force captain whose fellow soldier gets killed while the two of them are apprehending Isis mastermind Asad al-Madhi (Alec Rayme). Seven years later, Saunders embarks on a tour for his new book “America Unafraid,” which aims to detail “the ways Islam will conquer the west.” He arrives at Laughton University for a promotional appearance on the same day that campus protestors, fueled by the encouragement of a mysterious group of “elite freedom fighters,” decide to take over the student union. What the protestors don’t know is that the freedom fighters are actually Islamic terrorists led by Ibrahim (Stephen Hailo), al-Madhi’s son.

Popular on Variety

Piggybacking on the scrappy disruption of the protestors, Ibrahim’s well-trained foot soldiers fortify themselves at key positions across campus and begin killing students, faculty and the influx of citizens visiting campus for the school’s fall carnival. Ibrahim’s plan is to establish a new caliphate at Laughton, where he will either convert, “purify” or purge the remainder of the Americans his solders have captured.

Outside the student union, Devlin (JC Kilcoyne), the son of Saunders’ late comrade, decides to take the law into his own hands, albeit primarily to rescue his buddy Kwan (Chris K. Lee), and crush Lizzy (Tyler Aser), who becomes a bargaining chip for Ibrahim after the terrorist discovers that she’s the daughter of a billionaire. Teaming up with Terrence (David Lucas), a quick-witted campus security guard, and his xenophobic roommate P.J. (James Bingham), the heretofore apolitical Devlin attempts both to mount a rescue mission and exact revenge against the school’s violent oppressors, as he begins to learn firsthand about the threats — both existential and violently real — that his late father was fighting to defeat.

Movies have taken aim at “wokeness” at an increasing pace in recent years, but making fun of political correctness is hardly a new concept; “P.C.U.,” which took its namesake when the concept was still freshly being articulated in the mainstream, came out in 1994. Given its nonstop barrage of zeitgeist-pilfering broadsides against progressivism, “Run Hide Fight: Infidels” practically qualifies as the Jason Friedberg and Aaron Seltzer version of such a send-up. (File it alongside “Date Movie” and “Epic Movie” and retitle it “Liberal Movie.”) Every single character arrives on screen with a fully-baked backstory that amplifies their identity with a stereotype — Kwan, a computer whiz; purple-haired campus revolutionary Farrah (Charlotte Delaney Riggs), an “I like everyone” bisexual — and Rankin coaches them to deliver their expository declarations with comically smug entitlement. If only the movie were trying to be funny.

Laughton University (actually South Carolina’s Limestone University, if you were curious what venerated institution would allow this film to be shot on their campus) is paralyzed at every level by self-righteous compassion: George (Jason Gray-Stanford), the school’s dean, is too afraid of appearing discriminatory (much less of endorsing law enforcement) to call in the police, and even local mayor Flores (Shazia Pascal) insists upon efforts to “lower the temperature” at the bloody crime scene rather than making a decisive show of force. When a Black professor suggests that the protesting students are infringing on their classmates’ right to use shared areas, her white counterparts shake their heads in disgust for her refusal to capitulate to progressive groupthink.

Rather than making a satirical point about liberal overreach, the movie argues that all this empathy for other people — including for the Indigenous tribes whose land was seized on behalf of the school, or Palestinians trying to hold onto theirs — is a purely oppressive force. Further, it’s in direct opposition to the uncomplicated, common-sense decisions made by men like Saunders who have faced America’s real enemies.

Unsurprisingly, Rankin’s depiction of Muslims is deeply Islamophobic, although Sue Obeidi, senior vice president for the Muslim Public Affairs Council Hollywood Bureau, has rightly called the film “more ridiculous than it is offensive.” The whole movie is like that — not smart enough to actually explore the viewpoints or value systems of either Muslims or liberals, much less where they come from. Instead, the filmmaker becomes a megaphone for his producer, right-wing commentator Ben Shapiro, whose debate style tends to involve steamrolling his opponent with strawman arguments and acting surprised when they become exasperated.

P.J., one of the film’s lead characters, is a foul-mouthed gamer who lies about his military record to justify calling his Egyptian classmate a “camel jockey,” but after a passing callout by Devlin for “stolen valor,” his aspirations to heroism are validated when he ruefully defies local authorities, gridlocked by legal and ethical restraint, to help save the day.

Majors appears mostly at the beginning and end of the film, giving a thoroughly disengaged performance. (We’re a long way from the awards buzz that his role in “Magazine Dreams” generated at one point.) Then again, the kind of fearmongering peddled here requires a level of conviction that it’s hard to imagine he possesses. The Daily Wire is a perfect platform for “Run Hide Fight: Infidels,” giving it just the right context to set audience expectations. Are you contemptuous of radical leftists who believe that others should be treated with decency, care and respect? If so, this is the film for you. Otherwise, there are dozens of much safer spaces to occupy, whether you’re a bleeding-heart liberal or just a moviegoer with even slightly discriminating tastes.

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Overtakes ‘Star Wars: Force Awakens’ as Highest-Grossing Movie of All Time at Domestic Box Office
summary: All hail Peter Parker. “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” has notched a heroic box office milestone, overtaking 2015’s “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” as the highest-grossing domestic release of all time. “The Force Awakens” had spent more than a decade as the biggest movie ever at the North American box office with $936 million. It has […]
content:
All hail Peter Parker. “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” has notched a heroic box office milestone, overtaking 2015’s “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” as the highest-grossing domestic release of all time.

“The Force Awakens” had spent more than a decade as the biggest movie ever at the North American box office with $936 million. It has officially ceded the crown to Tom Holland’s latest Spidey adventure, which has surpassed that benchmark with $936.773 million in 47 days.

Now the question is whether “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” has the endurance to become the first movie in history to generate $1 billion at the domestic box office — although that might be unlikely at this point without a re-release.

Popular on Variety

After seven weekends in theaters, Sony and Marvel’s epic “Brand New Day” has earned a jaw-dropping $2.4 billion at the global box office. It’s the third-highest grossing movie of all time, trailing just 2009’s “Avatar” ($2.9 billion), “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.7 billion) and ahead of 2022’s “Avatar: The Way of Water” ($2.3 billion) and 1994’s “Titanic” ($2.2 billion).

“Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” Holland’s fourth solo outing as Peter Parker, has been on an epic box office run since late July. The movie launched to a record-breaking $360 million in North America and a staggering $932 million globally in its opening weekend; it then cleared $1 billion after just six days of release. It reached $2 billion after three weekends, becoming the second-fastest film to reach the threshold following 2019’s “Avengers: Endgame,” which got there after 11 days.

Directed by “Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings” filmmaker Destin Daniel Cretton, “Brand New Day” picks up after the events of 2021’s “Spider-Man: No Way Home” — which ended with the entire world forgetting about Peter Parker. Initial demand was stratospheric because audiences were desperate to find out the ramifications of Spider-Man’s fateful choice. (And they wanted to be among the first to find out who Sadie Sink was playing in the movie. Spoiler alert: It’s Jean Grey.) Yet the movie enjoyed unprecedented staying power because of the euphoric word of mouth.

“Brand New Day” marks a needed win for Marvel, which endured a rough 2025 at the box office with commercial misses like “Captain America: Brave New World” and “The Fantastic Four: First Steps.” The comic book empire will build on the success of “Spider-Man 4” with “Avengers: Doomsday,” which reunites just about every superhero you can think of (and reintroduces Robert Downey Jr. not as Iron Man but as the villain Doctor Doom) in December.

title: James Cameron’s Lightstorm Scoops Up AI-Powered 3D Tech Company Outsyders
summary: James Cameron has long loved 3D. Now he’s added an AI-powered 3D tech company to his collection. Cameron’s Lightstorm Vision has purchased Outsyders, a technology company focused on boosting the 3D production and post-production pipeline with the help of AI and machine learning to create “premium stereoscopic content.” Founded in 2024 by Paul Becker, Jared […]
content:
James Cameron has long loved 3D. Now he’s added an AI-powered 3D tech company to his collection.

Cameron’s Lightstorm Vision has purchased Outsyders, a technology company focused on boosting the 3D production and post-production pipeline with the help of AI and machine learning to create “premium stereoscopic content.” Founded in 2024 by Paul Becker, Jared Sandrew and Chris Harvey, Outsyders has worked on films including “Blue Angels,” Disney’s 3D version of “Lilo & Stitch,” Doug Liman’s XR “Asteroid” and more. and Moana, and other films.

As part of the acquisition, Outsyders will work with Lightstorm to help tap into content libraries to produce new 3D versions of films, a measure the companies said could be done “in a fraction of the time and at significantly lower cost than traditional conversion” through Outsyders’ AI models.

Popular on Variety

The terms of the deal weren’t disclosed, though their partnership is not entirely new: Lightstorm and Outsyders worked together on Paramount’s “Billie Eilish – Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour (Live in 3D),” which Cameron co-directed with Eilish.

“At Lightstorm we’ve been working with Paul Becker and his team for almost two years, and really enjoyed the collaboration,” Cameron said in a statement. “As everyone knows, I’ve got a very exacting eye for 3D, and I can confidently say that their work and their AI tools are world class. Together we will provide end-to-end solutions for productions and for studios, as we merge the worlds of conversion and native photographic 3D.”

“We’ve always shared Jim’s vision for stereo,” Becker added. “Our work with Jim confirmed that our combined technologies were the most logical and effective step for the format. We are excited to join and bolster Lightstorm Vision’s mission.”

The acquisition follows Lightstorm’s purchase earlier this year of Stereotec, a 3D camera company, and its 2024 deal with Meta to produce 3D content for its Meta Quest devices.

title: Chris Harrison’s Dating Series ‘The Vow’ Sets Premiere On Fox Nation
summary: Fox Nation is leaning into Bachelor Nation with its new dating reality series hosted by Chris Harrison. Chris Harrison’s The Vow, which Deadline revealed in February, is set to premiere on the streamer on November 11. The six-part series will roll out weekly with the season finale on December 9. The show will see 30-year-old […]
content:
Fox Nation is leaning into Bachelor Nation with its new dating reality series hosted by Chris Harrison.

Chris Harrison’s The Vow, which Deadline revealed in February, is set to premiere on the streamer on November 11. The six-part series will roll out weekly with the season finale on December 9.

The show will see 30-year-old Jace Cates as its first eligible bachelor. He will embark on a relationship journey with ten women, each seeking lasting commitment and marriage. Through curated dates and real-world compatibility challenges, the show explores whether shared values, faith, communication, and long-term goals can build a relationship designed to last long after the cameras stop rolling, per the logline.

In the teaser trailer, Harrison is leaning into the fact that he is best known for hosting The Bachelor and its spinoffs over the last twenty years. “Expecting someone else?,” he says as the camera does a very Bachelor-esque reveal. “Roses fade. True love lasts forever,” he adds with a pointed smile.

Watch on Deadline

It will also feature members of Bachelor Nation; Sean and Catherine Lowe, who fell in love on Season 17 of The Bachelor in 2013, will make an appearance.

It is Harrison’s first new show since he left The Bachelor in 2021 under a slight cloud. In March 2021, he was pushed off The Bachelorette following divisive comments in an interview with former Bachelor and Bachelorette star Rachel Lindsay, where he defended Rachael Kirkconnell after photos of her attending an antebellum plantation-themed fraternity party in 2018 went viral. Harrison apologized for his comments, calling them a “mistake”. But it led to him leaving The Bachelor franchise in June 2021.

Jace Cates (Fox Nation)

Chris Harrison’s The Vow is produced by Lionsgate Alternative Television. Harrison exec produces alongside Lauren Zima, Nicholas Caprio, Tom Huffman and Louis Caric, who serves as showrunner. Elan Gale is a consulting producer.

Harrison said, “I’m so excited to be back helping people find love, and Fox Nation has been an incredible partner in bringing this vision to life. We were inspired by the faith-driven renaissance happening across America, and as a result, I believe we’ve created the most authentic dating show on television today. At a time when so many people feel dating has become harder than ever, The Vow asks a simple but important question: Can genuine, lasting love still be found in the modern world? The stakes couldn’t be higher. I’m incredibly proud and honored to put my name on this show.”

Lauren Petterson, president of Fox Nation, added, “Chris Harrison helped shape one of television’s most recognizable genres, and we’re thrilled to partner with him on a fresh, thoughtful take that returns the focus to what so many people are ultimately searching for: a genuine connection built to last. This series explores the conversations, values and real-life moments that matter long after production ends, and we believe audiences will connect with its authentic and hopeful approach to finding lasting love.”

title: Kapow! ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Beats ‘Star Wars: Force Awakens’ As Highest Grossing Movie Ever At Domestic Box Office With $936.7M
summary: It finally happened: Sony’s highest grossing movie ever, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, is now the highest grossing movie ever at the domestic box office, defeating Star Wars: The Force Awakens which held the record for the last ten years with a final cume of $936.66M. As of yesterday, Spider-Man: Brand New Day counts a running […]
content:
It finally happened: Sony’s highest grossing movie ever, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, is now the highest grossing movie ever at the domestic box office, defeating Star Wars: The Force Awakens which held the record for the last ten years with a final cume of $936.66M.

As of yesterday, Spider-Man: Brand New Day counts a running cume of $936.7M at the domestic box office. Tuesday’s gross was $915k.

Here’s a list of the domestic B.O. milestones for the Destin Daniel Cretton directed, Tom Holland and Zendaya starring movie which opened on July 31:

Biggest domestic opening weekend of all time ($360 million). Also, biggest North American opening ever for Cretton, Zendaya and Holland.

Biggest Thursday previews of all time.

Biggest opening day (Friday) of all time.

Second-biggest Saturday gross of all time.

Biggest Monday of all time.

Biggest Tuesday of all time.

Second film in history to surpass $300 million during its opening weekend.

Highest-grossing opening week in domestic box office history.

Highest 10-day domestic gross in box office history.

Six consecutive weekends at No. 1 domestically.

Fastest film ever to surpass $400 million domestically (4 days).

Fastest film ever to surpass $500 million domestically (7 days).

Fastest film ever to surpass $600 million domestically (9 days).

Fastest film ever to surpass $700 million domestically (13 days).

Fastest film ever to surpass $800 million domestically (19 days).

Fastest film ever to surpass $900 million domestically (36 days).

Only the second film in history to surpass $900 million at the domestic box office.

Highest-grossing domestic release of all time.

Worldwide, the pic stands at $2.45 billion, and will continue to rank third on the all-time list behind 2009’s Avatar ($2.92B) and Avengers: Endgame ($2.799B). The latter pic is getting a re-release later this month and will likely increase its distance ahead of Brand New Day. Holland starred in Endgame, so it’s his highest grossing movie ever. Brand New Day remains Cretton and Zendaya’s highest grossing movie of all-time.

title: Hemingway’s ‘The Sun Also Rises’ Gets Centennial Events In Paris & New York With Michael Shannon & Richard Schiff Among Participants
summary: EXCLUSIVE: A series of events have been set in Paris and New York to celebrate the centenary of the publication of Ernest Hemingway classic The Sun Also Rises. The celebration begins September 21 and 22 at Ritz Paris, with guests including filmmaker Michael Winterbottom, who is set to direct the upcoming A Farewell To Arms […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: A series of events have been set in Paris and New York to celebrate the centenary of the publication of Ernest Hemingway classic The Sun Also Rises.

The celebration begins September 21 and 22 at Ritz Paris, with guests including filmmaker Michael Winterbottom, who is set to direct the upcoming A Farewell To Arms film with Tom Blyth, fashion photographer Ellen von Unwerth, novelist and author Jay McInerney, and British singer-songwriter Westerman among those set to attend.

On October 22, the 100th anniversary of the publication of The Sun Also Rises, Hemingway Ltd. and 92NY (The 92nd Street Y) will present a centennial evening featuring panel discussions, literary figures and readings from Hemingway’s work. Two-time Oscar nominee Michael Shannon and Emmy winner Richard Schiff are among those set to participate, with additional names being finalized.

A further New York celebration is planned at The Morgan Library & Museum, where Hemingway Ltd. will host a centennial dinner.

Watch on Deadline

The global program is being led by Collective 222, Agency of Record for Hemingway Ltd., as it expands the Hemingway brand across film and TV development, publishing, international licensing, hospitality, cultural programming and strategic partnerships.

Additional international events and programming are in the works.

Alongside the centennial, Collective 222 has appointed Jane Owen PR to lead global public relations for the company and its representation of the Hemingway brand.

The appointment brings a fun historical connection: Owen is the great-granddaughter of legendary Scribner editor Maxwell Perkins, whose editorial partnership with Hemingway helped shape The Sun Also Rises (and other works) before its publication in 1926.

First published by Scribner in 1926, The Sun Also Rises follows American journalist Jake Barnes and a circle of expatriates traveling from Paris to Pamplona in the years following the First World War. Widely regarded as the defining novel of the Lost Generation, it remains one of the most influential works of modern literature. The book spawned multiple screen adaptations including a 1957 film with Tyrone Power, Ava Gardner and Errol Flynn, and a 1984 miniseries with Jane Seymour, Robert Carradine, Leonard Nimoy and Hart Bochner.

title: Bonnie Greer Dies: British-American Writer & Cultural Commentator Was 77
summary: The British-American writer and cultural commentator Bonnie Greer has died. She was 77. Greer’s husband, David Hutchins, announced her death in a statement published this afternoon. Hutchins wrote that Greer died on Tuesday evening following a brief illness. Hutchins described Greer as “an acclaimed playwright, author, critic, cultural and political commentator whose intelligence, courage and […]
content:
The British-American writer and cultural commentator Bonnie Greer has died. She was 77.

Greer’s husband, David Hutchins, announced her death in a statement published this afternoon. Hutchins wrote that Greer died on Tuesday evening following a brief illness.

Hutchins described Greer as “an acclaimed playwright, author, critic, cultural and political commentator whose intelligence, courage and distinctive voice made an enduring contribution to British cultural and public life”.

The statement continued: “To me, she was my partner, confidante and inspiration, and I feel profoundly privileged to have shared my life with her. Those closest to Bonnie will remember her warmth, humour, generosity and extraordinary ability to bring people together. At this immensely difficult time, we ask that our family’s privacy be respected. She will be deeply missed.”

Born in Chicago in 1948, Greer moved to the UK in 1986 and became a citizen in 1997.

Watch on Deadline

Her first book, Hanging by Her Teeth, was published in 1994 and told the story of a Black American woman travelling through the US and Europe in search of her father. Greer was also the author of Obama Music, a 2009 memoir about her personal connection to Chicago’s South Side contrasted with that of President Obama’s political rearing in the same community. Greer also published a book-length work on the life of Langston Hughes, titled The Value of Contradiction (2011).

Beyond novels, Greer was also a stage and screen writer. Her playwriting credits include Munda Negra (1993), for which she was awarded the Verity Bargate Award for best play. Greer penned the script for Ngozi Onwurah’s short, White Men Are Cracking Up.

In recent years, Greer became a frequent fixture on British current affairs shows such as Question Time. In 2022, she was made a fellow of the Royal Society of Literature and was awarded an OBE in 2010 for services to the arts.

title: Sam Worthington, Liam Hemsworth & Cara Delevingne Set For Paul Schrader’s Erotic Thriller ‘Non Compos Mentis’ With Filming Lined Up For Next Month
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Sam Worthington (Avatar), Liam Hemsworth (The Hunger Games), and Cara Delevingne (Club Kid) are set to play the lead love triangle in Paul Schrader’s upcoming erotic thriller Non Compos Mentis. Production is due to get underway next month in New York on the movie, which Oscar nominee Schrader has written and will direct. Additional […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Sam Worthington (Avatar), Liam Hemsworth (The Hunger Games), and Cara Delevingne (Club Kid) are set to play the lead love triangle in Paul Schrader‘s upcoming erotic thriller Non Compos Mentis.

Production is due to get underway next month in New York on the movie, which Oscar nominee Schrader has written and will direct. Additional cast is being finalized.

Non Compos Mentis (latin for ‘of unsound mind’) “centers on two privileged brothers confronting their mother’s decline into dementia: one a polished New York defense attorney, the other a hard-edged corporate heir. Their uneasy dynamic fractures when the attorney embarks on a consuming affair with a younger woman, igniting a volatile love triangle that unleashes obsession, betrayal, and a ruthless battle for control of the family fortune”.

We first told you about the project at the start of the year when it had a largely different cast, including Caleb Landry Jones, Sarah Pidgeon and Dianne Wiest.

Watch on Deadline

Pic is being produced by David Gonzales (Master Gardener), Schrader’s manager and producing partner. Executive producer is Nadine de Barros of Fortitude International, which is overseeing international sales.

James M. Vernon of MFM (Hacksaw Ridge) is executive-producing along with Joseph Panebianco and Jina Panebianco of Cardinal North Entertainment. Carissa Knol, Tiffany Boyle, Alex Sagalchik, Stef Dillon, Aimee Schoof, and Isen Robbins also executive-produce.

Fortitude has pre-sold the film to Germany (Weltkino), Italy (Eagle Pictures) and the CIS territory (Capella).

Screen vet Schrader, nominated for an Oscar for A24’s First Reformed and well known for his collaborations with Martin Scorsese on classics like Taxi Driver and Raging Bull, is coming off Venice Competition drama The Basics Of Philosophy. It was another instalment in his “man in a room” movies, also including First Reformed, Focus Features’ The Card Counter and Magnolia’s Master Gardener.

Gonzales and Schrader most recently made Cannes 2024 drama Oh, Canada, starring Richard Gere, Uma Thurman, and Jacob Elordi.

Delevingne is coming off raved about Cannes drama Club Kid, Worthington returned for the blockbuster Avatar franchise and Hemsworth last year had Netflix’s The Witcher.

Hemsworth is represented by Range Media Partners. Worthington is represented by WME and Anonymous Content. Delevingne is represented by UTA and Brillstein Entertainment Partners

title: How to Watch ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Online Without Cable

content:
The ballroom is officially back open.

“Dancing With the Stars” returned this week for its 35th season, kicking off with a two-night premiere on Tuesday, Sept. 15 and Wednesday, Sept. 16 at 8 p.m. ET on ABC and Disney+. After the premiere, new episodes will continue airing live Tuesdays at 8 p.m. ET. Episodes are also available to stream on Hulu the following day.

Another convenient way to stream new episodes live is on DirecTV, whose streaming packages carry local ABC stations in most markets. The service, which offers a five-day free trial, also currently bundles Disney+ and Hulu with ads.

Sling TV, Fubo and Hulu + Live TV also offer ways to watch “Dancing With the Stars” live on ABC without cable. Sling Blue starts at $45.99 per month and includes ABC in select markets, while Fubo carries the network in supported areas through its live TV packages, starting at $73.99 per month. Hulu + Live TV, meanwhile, starts at $89.99 per month and includes ABC alongside more than 100 live channels, plus bundled access to Hulu and Disney+. Local ABC availability can vary by ZIP code across all three services.

Alfonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough are back as co-hosts this season, while Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough return to the judges’ table. This year’s celebrity cast includes “Save the Last Dance” star Julia Stiles, “The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air” alum Tatyana Ali, “Grey’s Anatomy” star Harry Shum Jr., celebrity chef Giada De Laurentiis, “The Bachelorette” alum Tyler Cameron, “Summer House” star Ciara Miller, Olympian Amber Glenn and “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” fixture Guillermo Rodriguez.

Also competing are Paralympian Ezra Frech, Hanson singer Taylor Hanson, “Love Island U.K.” alum Maura Higgins, “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” star Conner Leavitt, Savannah Bananas player Jackson Olson, model Sarah Jane Nader and comedian Connor Wood. Among the returning pros are Mark Ballas, Witney Carson, Jenna Johnson, Val Chmerkovskiy, Emma Slater, Rylee Arnold and Daniella Karagach.

title: How American High Scored Big With ‘Minimum Wage’ Netflix Series While Building a Pipeline for the Next Generation of Comedians (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: It all started with Jeremy Garelick’s simple but ambitious plan for American High: Buy a high school in upstate New York and turn it into the hottest filming spot in town for coming-of-age comedies. Since the full-scale production outfit was founded in 2017 and American High Shorts launched online in 2022, Garelick’s motto for discovering […]
content:
It all started with Jeremy Garelick’s simple but ambitious plan for American High: Buy a high school in upstate New York and turn it into the hottest filming spot in town for coming-of-age comedies.

Since the full-scale production outfit was founded in 2017 and American High Shorts launched online in 2022, Garelick’s motto for discovering talent has been to put the funniest people in a room together and let them prove themselves — whether that be in one of their films that end up streaming on Hulu, or a short-form comedy sketch.

Now, that motto is taking the young talent discovered through American High farther than they ever could have imagined with the 28-episode Netflix order for “Minimum Wage” (as Variety exclusively reported in April). It started out as a web series posted on YouTube back in May 2024 made for under $2,000, but Variety can exclusively reveal that the first 14 episodes of “Minimum Wage” will premiere on Netflix on Oct. 26.

Popular on Variety

“It’s the same philosophy we have with film, but in the digital space. If someone’s doing something cool, we’ll just amplify it without all the gatekeeping,” American High president Will Phelps says. “It’s the model that other people were too afraid to do. And now turn the page, everyone wants to give those creators $10 million to make the next ‘Obsession.’ I think we were probably just there five years earlier.”

“Unlike all the studios and giant companies that like to just be reactive and see what’s working, they don’t want to take chances on first-time directors or actors,” Garelick adds, with a majority of American High’s films being helmed by first-time directors (including Jillian Bell and Jason Orley).

Working with Netflix was a natural fit for Garelick, who directed the 2023 Adam Sandler movie “Murder Mystery 2” and the show “Best Worst Weekend Ever” for the streamer. “This is the biggest opportunity we’ve had at American High in terms of getting our stuff to the broadest audience,” he says.

While Garelick and Phelps served as showrunners on “Minimum Wage,” the ethos of collaboration remained largely the same: Cast members had the opportunity to write and direct many of their own episodes.

When the series was picked up by Netflix, there was, of course, the pressure that came with working with a larger budget and wanting to live up to the original series for a wider audience. But cast member Grace Reiter explains that the show was a natural extension of everything American High has spent years building on its digital platforms.

“What an amazing first experience in a writers’ room and directing your friends. We already built such a language working with each other, it’s like second nature,” Reiter says. “It felt totally comfortable to pitch things in the room and to say not funny things and to get ideas turned down.”

Getting to direct episodes of their own also proved to be a great learning experience for the cast. Reiter says: “It was just maybe coordinating camera movements a little bit more because now we have two cameras. We were more used to, obviously, the vertical frame and cross-shooting, but we tried to carry over all the things that made our digital sketches and web series popular.”

The original “Minimum Wage” series took the model of the classic workplace comedy, following a group of overworked teenagers trying (and often failing!) to run a pizza shop. The cast included Reiter, Aidan Micho, Hyde Healy, Julia Dicesare, Luke Burke, Ryan Micho and Tommy Armstrong, who all returned for the Netflix series.

“It was very scrappy, very homemade,” Reiter says of the original web series.

For Garelick and Phelps, “Minimum Wage” is just one example of how they view all their sketches as possible IP to pitch to streamers. American High has the benefit of its own built-in audience online, with the American High Shorts TikTok account currently holding 2.6 million followers and a collective 248 million likes (and counting) across all videos.

American High’s head of digital, Tristan Hall, who oversees all of the company’s social accounts and marketing efforts for their films, says that the online sketch videos “operate like a Gen Z version of ‘SNL.'” A typical week starts off with a brainstorming session on Monday, a writers’ room on Tuesday, and then production on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday.

“The nice thing about social media is you do get that instant verification,” Hall says. “Within 24 hours, we’ll know if the idea is something we want to revisit.”

American High has focused on organic social media engagement over traditional advertising. After premiering at SXSW in March, “Pizza Movie” — led by “Stranger Things” star Gaten Matarazzo — was released on Hulu in April, and became one of the company’s buzziest titles online.

“Pizza Movie,” starring Gaten Matarazzo Courtesy of American High

“Whatever studio that we’re releasing with will often assist with more traditional marketing, and then we cover the social media side of things,” says Surina Belk-Gupta, American High’s social media manager. “‘Pizza Movie’ was a game changer for us in how we can use our company brand in film marketing.”

Jon Hurwitz worked alongside American High as a producing partner on the 2021 high school comedy “Plan B” after being attracted by the resource facilities of the company’s Syracuse hub.

“What struck me was the youth, which is wonderful,” Hurwitz says of his time on set. “A bunch of young people who were passionate and hardworking, getting experience in the film business.”

The Academy at American High program was established in 2018, giving film students from schools like Syracuse University, Ithaca College and Onondaga Community College the opportunity to intern and work on sets. Now, Garelick estimates that more than 1,500 students apply for internships each semester.

American High likes to keep folks around. Matt Sacca, who started off as Garelick’s first intern, worked his way up to head of development and is now writing a comedy titled “Second First Date” for the company. Phelps started out as Garelick’s assistant back in 2014, and Hall began as a creative intern back in 2022.

Filmmakers and producers who have developed a close relationship with Garelick over the years, from his work on films like “The Hangover” and “The Wedding Ringer,” recognize and trust the next generation of comedians he’s bringing up.

Hurwitz says: “We’re working on the latest ‘Harold and Kumar’ movie and there are going to be some young characters in that. Jeremy’s going to be one of my calls where I’ll have him read the script and say, ‘Hey, are there people in your ecosystem that you think would be great?'”

In addition to the highly anticipated release of “Minimum Wage” later this year, American High is betting big on its first theatrical release, “Rolling Loud,” which stars Owen Wilson and Matt Rife. It was written and written by Garelick and will be released on Oct. 2 from distributor Ketchup Entertainment.

“We’re going to always write and make the funniest movies that we believe deserve a theatrical release. We just did ‘Pizza Movie’ that I am 1000% certain would’ve crushed in the theater just because I’ve sat through several screenings,” Garelick says, referencing American High’s first-look deal with Hulu that limits films to streaming.

“It’s just a matter of when distributors realize that comedies do actually work [in theaters] if they’re funny,” he adds.

“Rolling Loud,” which follows a father and son attending a hip-hop festival in Miami, is also the rare American High production to be shot outside of Syracuse. The only soundstage in the area that would have been big enough to fit a stage the size they needed had been sold off, Garelick says. (They were able to film it in Miami at a Rolling Loud concert.)

While Garelick says that American High is “open” to continue expanding filming outside of Syracuse, he recognizes the opportunity to continue hiring local crew.

“It’s just so easy for us to get things up and running — we know every location,” he says. “We can read a script and be like, ‘We’ll shoot that here, this would cost this much.'”

“Minimum Wage” cast member Burke, who first connected with Garelick after he visited his Syracuse University screenwriting class in 2022 and took a liking to his spec script, was hired as an on-set punch-up writer for “Rolling Loud.”

“Being on a large feature film set was such an insane learning experience,” Burke says. “It felt like I was part of the process.”

Members of American High’s sketch comedies are already expanding their footprint onto other shows; Reiter appeared alongside Tim Robinson in his ambitious HBO comedy “The Chair Company,” but she says the set felt just like a scrappy American High shoot.

“The vibes were similar. As a creative, it’s important to surround yourself with people who you trust. It really was just, ‘They’re friends!'” Reiter says. “In between, they were watching audition tapes and then they’d talk about the [basketball] game, sitting there and making each other laugh. And that’s all I’ve ever wished and hoped for — just to make funny things with my friends.”

As American High gears up for the new school year, a new crop of interns and students interested in working on sets will come across Garelick and Phillips’ desk, becoming part of the ever-growing network.

“We created an accidental ecosystem that has really helped every aspect of our business. It wasn’t like we were doing this on purpose,” Garelick says. “We were just trying to do what was fun for us.”

title: VidCon Is Leaving Anaheim After Creator Convention Combines With LIONS, Parent of Cannes Lions
summary: VidCon’s flagship event for digital creators and their fans is leaving its Anaheim home after 16 years in Southern California. LIONS, the company that produces the Cannes Lions marketing festival, announced that it is merging VidCon with its creator-focused events in North America to create VidCon x LIONS Creators. Both LIONS and VidCon are owned […]
content:
VidCon‘s flagship event for digital creators and their fans is leaving its Anaheim home after 16 years in Southern California.

LIONS, the company that produces the Cannes Lions marketing festival, announced that it is merging VidCon with its creator-focused events in North America to create VidCon x LIONS Creators. Both LIONS and VidCon are owned by U.K.-based Informa PLC, an international events, digital services and academic research firm.

The primary home of VidCon x LIONS Creators will be the Insight to Impact Festival, LIONS’ North American platform. Insight to Impact debuts in Denver in October 2026 before moving to Nashville in 2027, where the first VidCon x LIONS Creators event will be held. VidCon x LIONS Creators will also have a presence at Cannes Lions in June 2027, with further programming details to be announced.

Popular on Variety

VidCon was founded by brothers John and Hank Green in 2010. It was acquired by Viacom in 2018. Paramount Global, Viacom’s successor company, sold VidCon in September 2024 to Informa.

LIONS’ Insight to Impact Festival brings together Informa’s TMRE: The Market Research Event and Content Marketing World (and VidCon starting next year) along with expertise from across LIONS, including WARC, Contagious and Effie. The platform “will connect consumer understanding, marketing effectiveness and creativity for the North American market,” LIONS said in announcing the change.

For the past three years, LIONS has run LIONS Creators, a program dedicated to the intersection of digital influencers and the creative marketing industry. Now, by bringing VidCon into LIONS, “the platform will guide the rapidly growing creator community through its next phase of growth, connecting the ecosystem, and helping brands and creators transform cultural influence into commercial results,” the company said.

LIONS said the move to merge VidCon into its North America business is part of a wider move by the company to evolve its global model across North America, Asia Pacific, and the Middle East and North Africa to be more accessible to the worldwide industry year-round.

“The creator economy has never moved faster or mattered more within the global marketing ecosystem,” LIONS CEO Simon Cook said in a statement. “Creators are increasingly central to how culture is created and how brands connect with audiences. The introduction of VidCon is an exciting next step which will allow us to build out a dedicated global platform for an industry that’s rapidly reshaping the marketing landscape.”

Sarah Tortoreti, VP and business lead at VidCon, said: “For 15 years, VidCon has been the heartbeat of the creator community — the place where emerging and established creators, fans, brands, and industry leaders come together to celebrate digital culture in real life. Joining LIONS allows us to amplify that mission on a global scale. By combining VidCon’s deep-rooted relationships across the creator economy with LIONS’ unparalleled industry authority and global reach, we’re creating unprecedented opportunities for creators to build their careers, for brands to forge authentic partnerships, and for the entire ecosystem to shape what’s next together.”
