content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

If there’s one thing celebrity wedding planner Mindy Weiss knows, it’s how to create a moment.

Now, the woman behind the recent wedding of Selena Gomez and Benny Blanco, plus weddings and parties for Finneas, Justin Bieber and The Kardashians is putting her touch on Ring Pop, the popular candy brand known for its colorful ring-shaped suckers.

While Ring Pop has helped people pop the question since the 80s, Weiss has teamed up with the brand for The Wedding Collection, to unveil Ring Pops that help people say “I Do!”

Amazon NEW RELEASE Ring Pop Wedding Collection Lollipops 50-count pack Buy Now On Amazon $25.50

The new Ring Pop release features the mini lollipops in three romance-inspired flavors: “First Kiss” watermelon; “Main Squeeze” citrus; and “Berry in Love” strawberry. Each Ring Pop is wrapped like a wedding favor, with occasion-appropriate sayings adorning the packaging (think phrases like “Off the Market,” “Ring it On” and “I Said Yes”).

And just so you don’t ruin your first kiss, Ring Pop says The Wedding Collection features “lighter-toned gems” that are designed to not stain your lips or teeth.

Tim Chan

Weiss was tapped as the creative director for the collection, and the event planner helped with everything from the packaging design to the gemstone colors. She says she was excited to offer another way for couples to create a memorable moment on their big day.

“Behind every wedding I’ve planned, there’s a detail that makes guests stop and smile because it’s something unexpected that feels personal,” Weiss says in a release. “Ring Pop already had that magic and couples were finding their own way to use them long before we started this collection. My job was simply to give it the packaging, the polish and the occasions it deserved. This is Ring Pop, all grown up, but still exactly as fun as you remember it.”

“Ring Pop has always been a symbol of celebration, and lately, of love,” adds Joanna Firestone, Marketing Director at Bazooka Brands. “Over the years, we’ve watched Ring Pop organically become part of the wedding journey — engagements, bachelorettes, showers, weddings. With the wedding industry booming and packaging aesthetics mattering more to consumers than ever, it felt like the right moment to make it official. And there was no better partner than celebrity wedding planner Mindy Weiss.”

The Ring Pop Wedding Collection launches exclusively in stores at David’s Bridal and online on Amazon, which has 15-count and 50-count bags of Ring Pops available here.

title: Netanyahu Moves To Get ‘NAZA’ Directors’ Israeli Citizenship Revoked
summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has joined the chorus of Israeli government officials seeking to punish the directors of the Venice Film Festival’s Special Jury Prize-winning documentary NAZA. After decrying what he described as “global antisemitic incitement,” Netanyahu said he will be introducing two bills in his country’s parliament, the Knesset. “We will hit them in […]
content:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has joined the chorus of Israeli government officials seeking to punish the directors of the Venice Film Festival’s Special Jury Prize-winning documentary NAZA.

After decrying what he described as “global antisemitic incitement,” Netanyahu said he will be introducing two bills in his country’s parliament, the Knesset.

“We will hit them in their pockets and also in their citizenship, because their place is not among us,” declared Netanyahu. He also described the bills specifically.

“The first: to revoke the citizenship of anyone who slanders IDF [Israeli Defense Forces] soldiers.

Watch on Deadline

“The second: to hit them in the pocket, raising the defamation damages they can be sued for twentyfold.”

The co-directors of NAZA, Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, are both Israeli.

The prime minister’s comments followed those of his Culture Minister, Miki Zohar, who also threatened to revoke the filmmakers’ citizenship.

On Friday, former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett criticized NAZA and its filmmakers, saying in a statement that that he is “proud” and “deeply grateful” to the Israeli reservists and soldiers “standing between us and that next massacre.” He added, “To portray them as perpetrators of ‘genocide’ is not courageous art. It is a cowardly blood libel.”

NAZA, a late addition to the competition lineup in Venice, received a record 25-minute standing ovation at its premiere there. On Saturday night, it won the festival’s Special Jury Prize. The film is directed by Israeli Jews Abraham and Szor, who were also two of the four directors of the Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land.

In NAZA, Abraham appears on camera, interviewing his subjects on the rooftop; they explain that “NAZA” is a Hebrew acronym used by the Israel Defense Forces to signify collateral damage (נזק אגבי, or Nezek Agavi, per an interview included in press notes), in other words, an acceptable loss of civilian life incurred while trying to kill suspected Hamas militants. The film suggests the number of “NAZA” considered acceptable in each attack was elastic. In some cases, it would be under a dozen, but in others it could be 200 or even 500 people deemed permissible collateral damage, according to Israeli military personnel interviewed in the film.

Matt Carey contributed to this report.

title: Matthew Lillard Is “Embarrassed” About Returning To ‘Scream 7’ After Melissa Barrera Firing: “I Feel Shame About That”
summary: As the Scream franchise continues to serve as a cultural lightning rod in the Israel-Hamas conflict, Matthew Lillard is making his voice heard. The Scream 7 star recently admitted that he’s “embarrassed” to have reprised his role as Stu Macher in this year’s seventh installment in the slasher franchise, explaining that Melissa Barrera was “on […]
content:
As the Scream franchise continues to serve as a cultural lightning rod in the Israel-Hamas conflict, Matthew Lillard is making his voice heard.

The Scream 7 star recently admitted that he’s “embarrassed” to have reprised his role as Stu Macher in this year’s seventh installment in the slasher franchise, explaining that Melissa Barrera was “on the right side of history” when she was fired for speaking up in support of Palestinians in 2023.

“It’s just human, it’s who we are… I don’t know what else to do,” he explained in a video from a recent Q&A. “For me, I have queer kids, if I’m not standing up for queer kids or kids in the trans community, what the fuck am I doing?”

Watch on Deadline

Lillard continued, “But if I’m not standing up about the silencing of Melissa Barrera—listen, I don’t think it’s easy all the time. Melissa Barrera, who’s a beautiful actor, was fired for what she said. It’s really fucking bullshit and really hard, and she’s on the right side of history.”

“And when they start coming after your job, sometimes things are worth it. But I’m just gonna say, what happened to Melissa, the whole world didn’t pipe up. She was like a year early on what the fuck’s going on, but the whole world should have piped up and said, ‘she’s right,’ and they didn’t. And that’s brutal,” he said.

In January 2025, Deadline exclusively revealed that Lillard would reprise his role in Scream 7 as killer Stu Macher, who was believed to have been killed at the end of the first movie.

“And then I went back to do Scream, and I got called out,” said Lillard. “And I was like, ‘Oh fuck, that’s brutal.’ I feel bad about that, I feel shame about that. Because in that moment, I was so excited to got back, I didn’t really think about Melissa and the journey, and I didn’t say ‘no.’ I’m embarrassed, and that’s the truth.”

As the seventh installment of the slasher franchise premiered at Paramount Studios in February, “Free Palestine” protesters lined up outside the entrance to the lot. Back when the first trailer for Scream 7 was released last October, fans quickly began slamming the movie on social media, calling for a boycott.

Spyglass fired Barrera in November 2023 over her social media posts on the Israel-Hamas conflict and the “atrocities being committed against Palestinians,” explaining the company has “zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate in any form, including false references to genocide, ethnic cleansing, Holocaust distortion or anything that flagrantly crosses the line into hate speech.”

Following her ousting, Jenna Ortega also exited the franchise, later noting that the sequel “was all kind of falling apart” without Barrera to play its new “final girl” Sam Carpenter. Director Christopher Landon dropped out of the project as well, citing “highly aggressive and really scary” death threats targeting his children.

Neve Campbell was then brought back to reprise her role as OG “final girl” Sidney Campbell for Scream 7 in March 2024, with original Scream (1996) writer Williamson on board to direct. She previously sat out Scream VI (2023) over the low pay offer.

title: ‘Reacher’s Kathleen Robertson Says Role Is “Certainly Set Up” To Become Powerful Ally In Season 5; Talks Moving ‘Tracker’ To L.A.
summary: SPOILER ALERT: This post contains details about the Reacher Season 4 finale episode “Cut.” As Alan Ritchson’s Reacher brings another far-reaching crime to justice, Kathleen Robertson thinks it could be just the beginning for her politico Elspeth Sampson. The Reacher star recently discussed the Season 4 finale episode “Cut” with Deadline, noting that it’s “certainly […]
content:
SPOILER ALERT: This post contains details about the Reacher Season 4 finale episode “Cut.”

As Alan Ritchson’s Reacher brings another far-reaching crime to justice, Kathleen Robertson thinks it could be just the beginning for her politico Elspeth Sampson.

The Reacher star recently discussed the Season 4 finale episode “Cut” with Deadline, noting that it’s “certainly set up” for her newly widowed character to become a powerful ally for the titular retired soldier in the Prime Video series.

“That’s my hope. Let’s put it out there into the universe,” said Robertson. “Yeah, I mean, I think that she’s certainly set up that way. And it’s been nice to see people’s responses.”

Watch on Deadline

Initially, Elspeth fields Reacher’s request to meet her North Carolina congressman husband John Sampson (Marc Blucas) when the mystery-solving drifter connects the suicide of a Pentagon employee to a photo of the politician during a 1998 military operation in Indonesia.

“The role was fun for me. I love playing obviously very strong, complicated women, and I tend to be sent those roles a lot, which is great,” she explained. “I think they really were sort of looking for somebody that could kind of be believable, going toe-to-toe with Alan Ritchson and not at all having it feel forced, not having it feel like an inherent power imbalance.”

Kathleen Robertson and Marc Blucas in ‘Reacher’

Robertson added, “And I know for [Ritchson], he loved that as well, and it was sort of an interesting color for him to play with.”

Following her husband’s heroic sacrifice in the penultimate episode, when he tackles a chemical bomber into the ocean, Elspeth embraces Reacher as an ally, revealing her intention to take over her husband’s presidential journey.

“It’s always that interesting, funny thing as a woman when you’re married to a man who sort of has the visible power and people just sort of automatically assume at the beginning that she’s just his plus-one and his wife,” Robertson said. “But she’s obviously not, and she’s much more than that.”

Read on about Robertson’s role in Season 4 of Reacher, now available to stream on Prime Video.

DEADLINE: Tell me about joining this ensemble and playing Elspeth, this high-powered politician’s wife.

KATHLEEN ROBERTSON: It was fun. It was really fun. It’s always really great as an actor to work on a show that people actually love and watch. We work on so many projects as actors that never see the light of day, or we love so much and go to film festivals, and then like 250 people see them. So, it’s fun to be a part of something that is so wildly loved and successful, and the role was fun for me. I love playing obviously very strong, complicated women, and I tend to be sent those roles a lot, which is great. I think they really were sort of looking for somebody that could kind of be believable, going toe-to-toe with Alan Ritchson and not at all having it feel forced, not having it feel like an inherent power imbalance. So, I think that that was something that was really fun to kind of play with in a sort of small subtle way, to just kind of trust that the power with this woman is inherent and it’s part of the DNA of who she is as a human being, and so she doesn’t have to necessarily say a lot. It’s just kind of the essence of how she moves through the world, and so that was really fun to play with. With Alan in that regard, with those scenes, it was fun and I didn’t have to do any stunts, which made me very happy. I’m not a stunt person, I hate doing that kind of stuff.

DEADLINE: I also saw you posting photos of your outfit and getting to wear the red bottoms.

ROBERTSON: Yeah, of course. She was fun. She’s very different from me in that regard. I felt very much like a politician’s wife when I would get into wardrobe.

DEADLINE: And you mentioned going toe-to-toe with Alan. I really appreciated that first meeting between the two of you because he has so many physical opponents that he goes head to head with, as far as fighting, but he doesn’t have too many mental opponents.

ROBERTSON: Exactly. I thought that was interesting, and I know for him, he loved that as well, and it was sort of an interesting color for him to play with.

DEADLINE: I also enjoy the dynamic between Elspeth and her husband and the fact that she kind of knows a lot of his secrets, and it seems like she’s pulling a lot of the strings. Tell me about building that dynamic with Marc Blucas and getting to play with that.

ROBERTSON: It was interesting, ‘cause it is such an obviously top secret show in terms of what they want to share or not share in the scripts and whatnot. So, at the beginning, before I signed on to do the role, I had a meeting with [showrunner] Nick Santora and he sort of walked me through it, and it was interesting. He’s great. I’m a huge fan of his, and he thinks about things in terms of backstory. And he really sort of talked me through, this is a woman who was also a politician, and he’s like, “I imagine that there would have been at some point a conversation between her and her husband going like, ‘OK, which one of us is gonna really go for this? Is it gonna be you or is it going to be me? Because it can’t be both of us.'” And so that it became this very sort of practical, strategic — we talked a little bit about the Barack and Michelle thing, of like how Michelle could have equally gone and run for president, but it was that decision of, “You’re a guy, you’re gonna have a much better shot of this happening than me. So, I’m gonna be with you and we’re gonna do this together, but you’re going to be the face of this, and I’m going to be essentially running things behind the scenes.”

So, that was very much kind of how I approached her as a character. It’s always that interesting, funny thing as a woman when you’re married to a man who sort of has the visible power and people just sort of automatically assume at the beginning that she’s just his plus-one and his wife. But she’s obviously not, and she’s much more than that. So yeah, that was interesting too, and I thought the other thing that was interesting about what Nick said from day one to Marc and I, was that these people love each other. They don’t have children, they never had kids, they never did the traditional kind of thing, and they always have been each other’s fiercest advocates. But there isn’t sort of a dark secret where we’re gonna go, “Oh, they don’t really love each other” or “this is all sort of for show,” like some other presidents and wives that we may think, “Are they really in love? Is this real or is this just sort of a facade?””And for them, it very much is not. So that was also something interesting, let’s actually show a couple who moves in this political world that actually is in love, and they do truly love each other. So that was kind of subverting what we sort of expect with political marriages.

DEADLINE: By the end of the season, Elspeth does kind of step into her own political path, and I’m wondering if we could see her again in a future season, because it feels like she could be a powerful ally for Reacher.

ROBERTSON: That’s my hope. Let’s put it out there into the universe. Yeah, I mean, I think that she’s certainly set up that way. And it’s been nice to see people’s responses because I know people have really felt sort of like, “Oh, she’s such an interesting character, and we were so curious to see where it went and what the backstory was.” Of course you only have so many hours of television in a season, so that would be amazing.

DEADLINE: I’m also curious, are you gonna be back for the next season of Tracker.

ROBERTSON: I am, yeah.

DEADLINE: What’s it like playing with those guys?

ROBERTSON: It’s really fun. We actually filmed last season in Vancouver, and then of course I’m sure you saw in the trades, all the excitement over it moving back to L.A. So, it was like a big thing that they really wanted to bring it back to Los Angeles and obviously help create more jobs for L.A. and for the industry there, which has been great. So yeah, this new season’s filming in Los Angeles, and I’ve been back and done a few of those now. The season just started back like a month ago. So yeah, I will be popping up again on that show.

DEADLINE: Anything else you have coming up?

ROBERTSON: I’m in pre-production right now on a new show that I created, that I’m showrunning and I’m starring in it and I’m writing it, and it’s called Blessed Sacrament. We’re gonna start filming in January and we’re doing 10 episodes, shooting it in Toronto. I’m showrunning it, so I’m excited. That’s my main thing I’m really focused on right now, writing and hiring directors and all that kind of stuff.

title: Steven Paul Talks U.S. Production Incentive And “Uplifts” To Sweeten Deal As Draft Legislation Takes Shape
summary: A U.S. tax credit for film and television production is circling four potential uplifts of 5% each: for economically depressed areas; independent films; repatriating films to the U.S.; and shooting in multiple U.S. jurisdictions. “Those are the four being talked about,” says producer Steven Paul, who’s been working with President Donald Trump’s Ambassador to Hollywood […]
content:
A U.S. tax credit for film and television production is circling four potential uplifts of 5% each: for economically depressed areas; independent films; repatriating films to the U.S.; and shooting in multiple U.S. jurisdictions.

“Those are the four being talked about,” says producer Steven Paul, who’s been working with President Donald Trump’s Ambassador to Hollywood Jon Voight and lawmakers and industry groups on the bipartisan legislation aimed at curbing runaway production.

The base tax credit is set at 20% up to a maximum of 30%, so individual productions would be limited to two uplifts, says Paul, who spoke with Deadline after a sweeping alliance called the U.S. Film & TV Production Coalition launched Tuesday with a new study forecasting a major jump in job creation and production spend in the country if the incentive passes.

The legislation is still evolving, and it’s not certain what the final version will include.

Watch on Deadline

Paul says the “independent” designation could apply to films produced by a non-publicly traded entity or an affiliate of a non-publicly traded entity. Major studio parent companies are all publicly traded.

On repatriation, he says, “We don’t know exactly how the mechanics would work … but if you’re a producer or a studio that shot a certain number of films abroad, and you bring a certain number back, you would get a 5% uptick. Also, potentially, a 5% uptick for shooting in multiple jurisdictions within a certain time period, so you don’t just plant yourself in Georgia or New Jersey or Los Angeles and only shoot there.”

“We had recommended a 5% uptick for shooting in a federally declared [FEMA] disaster zone. That may live on or may be replaced with enterprise zones or economically depressed areas,” he says.

Backers had drafted the basics of the bill last year and it informed a study by consultancy Olsberg SPI commissioned by the Motion Picture Association and released yesterday. It calculated the federal incentive would create 143,50 jobs across the country each year on average between the years 2027 and 2035 on $125.3 billion in additional production spending. It forecast the U.S. share of global production would increase to 65% (by 2030 for film and 2032 for TV) instead of continuing to decline.

Paul spoke with Deadline just before lifting off on a Virgin Atlantic flight to London “to film a movie that should be filmed in America, which is why we’re working so hard on this. We’re about to make a movie about a young Richard Nixon, a presidential of the United States, and that movie should be shot here on U.S. soil. But I’m shooting it overseas because I have to, because of tax incentives over there. Otherwise, we wouldn’t be able to make the movie.”

Timing is tight with the U.S. House of Representatives in recess starting today until after the midterms, with the Senate following shortly. Lawmakers can work from afar, however, and Deadline hears draft legislation may be ready this week or next. Backers hope to pass it by the end of the year.

Trump has endorsed the incentive publicly and privately. Earlier today, bipartisan House lawmakers announced the formation of the American Film & TV Production Caucus with founding members Rep. Brian Jack (R-GA), Rep. Laura Friedman (D-CA), Rep. Nathaniel Moran (R-TX), Rep. Linda Sánchez (D-CA), Rep. Nicole Malliotakis (R-NY) and Rep. Tom Suozzi (D-NY).

The Wall Street Journal has slammed the tax credit in an editorial titled “Handouts For Hollywood—Really?”

“Representatives making sure that there’s something that’s beneficial to their constituents, and that it can be paid for, that it’s economically viable, right? I think those are the things you’re going to hear both from the left and the right” as the legislation works its way through Congress, says Paul.

“That’s why we were waiting for this Oldberg report, so we had numbers to back what we already knew. That this benefits all 50 states. That this is something that’s good for all of America.”

title: Jessica Chastain Joins Emilia Jones & Amy Ryan In Netflix Drama Series ‘The Retrievals’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: With her Universal horror film Other Mommy drumming up buzz ahead of its October 9 release, Oscar winner Jessica Chastain has closed a deal to join The Retrievals, Netflix’s new drama series from Sirens and Maid‘s Molly Smith Metzler. Inspired by the Peabody Award-winning New York Times podcast by Susan Burton, The Retrievals follows […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: With her Universal horror film Other Mommy drumming up buzz ahead of its October 9 release, Oscar winner Jessica Chastain has closed a deal to join The Retrievals, Netflix‘s new drama series from Sirens and Maid‘s Molly Smith Metzler.

Inspired by the Peabody Award-winning New York Times podcast by Susan Burton, The Retrievals follows an unlikely community of IVF patients who come together to crusade against Yale University after they are operated on without anesthesia — because a nurse stole their fentanyl. The show is billed as a powerful call to justice and a surprisingly moving story of friendship and perseverance.

RELATED: 2026 Premiere Dates For New & Returning Series On Broadcast, Streaming & Cable

Watch on Deadline

Chastain joins the previously announced Emilia Jones and Amy Ryan. She plays Kaitlyn Langford, a former art historian who has spent the past decade stuck in an endless cycle of failed fertility treatments. When she learns she’s a victim of criminal drug diversion at the Yale Fertility Center — along with Jones’ Gabby Clemente — she faces a devastating personal reckoning and becomes a key plaintiff in a historic lawsuit against Yale.

Ryan plays Carla Russo, a veteran nurse at Yale Fertility Center who pleads guilty to diverting vast amounts of fentanyl and diluting it with saline, forcing many patients to endure egg-retrieval surgery without anesthesia.

RELATED: 2026 TV Series Renewals Photo Gallery

Metzler is showrunner, writer and executive producer for The Retrievals, which is produced by LuckyChap and her Quiet Coyote. Other exec producers include Dani Gorin, Tom Ackerley and Margot Robbie for LuckyChap; Colin McKenna; Caitlin Roper for the New York Times; podcast writer Burton; and Lila Neugebauer, an alum of Maid and Sirens who will direct the pilot. The project reunites Metzler and McKenna with Netflix and LuckyChap following their work on the WGA Award-winning Maid and multiple Emmy-nominated Sirens.

Chastain plays dual roles opposite Jay Duplass and up-and-comer Arabella Olivia Clark in Other Mommy, an adaptation of the Josh Malerman novel Incidents Around the House, directed by Rob Savage. Upcoming, she’ll also be seen in the Netflix thriller Heartland from Shana Fest, out November 13, as well as the Apple series Off Weeks (with Ben Stiller) and The Dealer (with Adam Driver).

She is repped by CAA, Mosaic and Hansen Jacobson Teller.

title: Paul Walter Hauser Explains Mystery Pin He Wore to ‘Resident Evil’ Premiere
summary: Paul Walter Hauser spoke out about the Epstein files with a pin he wore to the “Resident Evil” premiere on Tuesday night in Los Angeles. The numbers on the pin affixed to his black T-shirt were the coordinates of the Zorro Ranch in New Mexico. “It was at one point owned by Jeffrey Epstein,” Hauser […]
content:
Paul Walter Hauser spoke out about the Epstein files with a pin he wore to the “Resident Evil” premiere on Tuesday night in Los Angeles.

The numbers on the pin affixed to his black T-shirt were the coordinates of the Zorro Ranch in New Mexico. “It was at one point owned by Jeffrey Epstein,” Hauser said. “It’s shrouded in mystery, and then a church supposedly bought it, which is even more disconcerting, I think.”

The Oscar-nominated actor said he wants “to bring awareness to evil people who are surreptitious and need to have a little Google search done on them.”

Popular on Variety

"Resident Evil" star Paul Walter Hauser explains his pin's connection to Jeffrey Epstein and why he's always "stirring s–t up." pic.twitter.com/gg8NWSJZ8V — Variety (@Variety) September 17, 2026

In February, Hauser questioned why people in Hollywood weren’t speaking up more for the release of the Epstein files.

“Dear Hollywood Friends, You spoke up for a great myriad of causes, all worthy, though some more dire than others,” he wrote on Instagram alongside a photo of Macaulay Culkin in “Home Alone.” “Right now, the Epstein files that have been released are implicating lawyers, politicians and members of our entertainment media in the worst crimes one can possibly imagine – the enslavement, r*pe, torture…of children and teenagers. With details and allusions that range from ritual killings to c*nnibalism.”

“Where are you now? Where are your voices and your hashtags now? Do you fear job loss? Death?” he continued. “Fear God. And protect children. And grow up. I don’t take my Emmy and Golden Globe with me when I die. The U-Haul truck will not follow the hearse in the funeral motorcade.”

In May, NPR reported that New Mexico officials have launched investigations into the ranch, where accusers allege they were abused by Epstein.

Hauser’s black T-shirt was emblazoned with bright yellow lettering that read, “Kubrick Didn’t Kill Himself.” Hauser told me he was having “fun referencing a little conspiracy theory.”

Famed director Stanley Kubrick died of a heart attack in his sleep in 1999 at age 70. Conspiracy theorists have claimed that his death was under much more nefarious, but unproven, circumstances.

title: Singer Duncan Sheik Hospitalized, in ‘Critical But Stable Condition’
summary: Duncan Sheik, the singer behind hits like the Grammy-nominated “Barely Breathing,” has been hospitalized and is currently receiving medical treatment, per a statement shared on his Instagram page on Wednesday. “We would like to share an update with Duncan’s fans and the public,” the statement read. “Duncan is currently receiving medical care and remains in […]
content:
Duncan Sheik, the singer behind hits like the Grammy-nominated “Barely Breathing,” has been hospitalized and is currently receiving medical treatment, per a statement shared on his Instagram page on Wednesday.

“We would like to share an update with Duncan’s fans and the public,” the statement read. “Duncan is currently receiving medical care and remains in critical but stable condition. Out of respect for Duncan and our family, we will not be sharing any further medical details at this time.”

The statement concluded: “We kindly ask for privacy during this incredibly difficult time and will provide updates when appropriate. Thank you for the continued love and support.”

Popular on Variety

According to Sheik’s social media, he has been in and out of the hospital — earlier this month, the singer shared a post with the caption “Sorry for the selfies. But I’m still bored in hospital.” On Aug. 20, he posted a photo with the caption “I would prefer to be home making music. But a bit of reflection is not too bad … boring hospital stays have their benefits (outside the obvious).”

The news comes ahead of the opening of the new musical “Memoirs of Amorous Gentleman,” an adaptation of Moyoco Anno’s manga graphic novel, for which Sheik penned the score. The first preview is set for September 25, with the opening scheduled for October 15.

Sheik also composed the music for the Broadway show “Spring Awakening,” a revival of which is set to begin previews off-Broadway this fall. The show first debuted in 2006 and ran for 859 performances, featuring a cast including Lea Michele, Jonathan Groff, Skylar Astin, John Gallagher Jr. and more. It won eight Tony Awards, including Best Musical. “Spring Awakening” was last revived in 2015.

title: ‘South Park’ Season 29 Premiere Embraces ‘South America’ Name Change With New Theme Song And a Trump Cameo
summary: “South Park” — or rather “South America” — made its Season 29 debut Wednesday night and wasted no time introducing audiences to the newly named town. The episode, titled “South American Biker Gangs,” kicked off with an updated theme song ringing in the name change — “I’m goin’ down to South America, have myself a […]
content:
“South Park” — or rather “South America” — made its Season 29 debut Wednesday night and wasted no time introducing audiences to the newly named town.

The episode, titled “South American Biker Gangs,” kicked off with an updated theme song ringing in the name change — “I’m goin’ down to South America, have myself a time!” — before showing another new addition: a Donald Trump cameo.

The premiere episode centered around the usual suspects, Cartman, Stan, Kyle and Kenny, and their newfound love of e-bikes. But when the gaggle of kids takes to the streets with their motorized bikes, the parents of South America form their own biker gang in opposition.

Popular on Variety

As per usual, Kenny dies when his e-bike blows up, and his death unites the town to come together, outlaw e-bikes, and begin selling “South America Strong” T-shirts.

Earlier this month, ahead of the Season 29 premiere, creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone announced that the long-running comedy series would furthermore be known as “South America,” a comedic jab at Trump’s recent moves to rename the likes of Lake Ontario as Lake America, New Mexico as New America and the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America.

“Inspired by the bravery and patriotism of Apple and Google, we are changing the name of ‘South Park’ to ‘South America,’” the pair shared in a statement. “We especially want to thank our parent company Paramount — a Skydance Capitulation.”

The show took home the gold for outstanding animated program at the 2026 Creative Arts Emmys, and while celebrating the win, threw another dig at Trump by sharing a graphic of the president with his pants and underwear around his ankles to the official “South Park” X account.

The moves are a continuation of the show’s Season 28 political antics, which included plot points like JD Vance seducing Donald Trump in order to dodge punishment for trying to kill his unborn baby with Satan and Pete Hegseth trying to bust Peter Thiel out of jail.

title: Bran Flakezz on Winning ‘Unwell Summer Games,’ His Future With Reality TV and the Alex Cooper-Alix Earle Drama
summary: Bran Flakezz is anything but “Unwell.” Brandon Edelman, better known as Bran Flakezz online, just emerged as one of four winners of the “Unwell Summer Games” on YouTube, created through Alex Cooper’s “Unwell” network. The four-episode series brought 16 content creators together at a luxury ranch in Canada to compete in a series of challenges […]
content:
Bran Flakezz is anything but “Unwell.”

Brandon Edelman, better known as Bran Flakezz online, just emerged as one of four winners of the “Unwell Summer Games” on YouTube, created through Alex Cooper’s “Unwell” network. The four-episode series brought 16 content creators together at a luxury ranch in Canada to compete in a series of challenges for a chance to win a share of $250,000, with the prize money distributed throughout the four days of the competition.

“There’s just so many exciting things happening that sometimes I do have to remind myself to take a step back,” Edelman tells Variety as he gets ready to speak at a Forbes CMO summit in Aspen, Colo.

Popular on Variety

Unlike a traditional competition series, “Unwell Summer Games” puts a group of established content creators — many of whom already knew each other — in the same house, ensuring there would be no shortage of drama. In the final episode, the contestants split into four teams for a final challenge. Edelman took home $25,000, alongside Jourdan Riane, Blake Gray and Carly Sutherland Lawrence, the last of whom had a less-than-perfect relationship with Bran on the show.

“There is a very funny moment where, after we scream at each other, we end up on the same team for the final challenge, and then we proceed to win the show together,” Edelman says, laughing. “Her and I have a very crazy storyline.”

Edelman got his start posting transparent videos on social media, detailing everything from his life in Philadelphia to the financial realities of being a content creator through his “TikTok Transparency” series. He’s since amassed more than 1 million followers on TikTok and made Forbes’ 30 Under 30 list in Social Media.

After working as a fitting room employee at Forever 21, Edelman went on to compete on Barstool’s “Project Verified” and is now part of Michelle Obama’s Gen Z voter registration intitiative. And after winning the “Unwell Summer Games,” he says he’s just getting started.

Below, Edelman talks to Variety about his time on “Unwell Summer Games,” his future in reality TV and his take on the Alex Cooper and Alix Earle drama.

Will we see you doing more reality TV after this?

Never say never. I think it’s always a case by case situation. As much as I love “Big Brother,” that’s a three-month filming schedule. Three months without posting online for me would be super detrimental, so that would be difficult. I love “Survivor.” No way in hell will you have me on an island like eating rice and sand. I think right now, anything that I want to do in a potential reality TV space is just make something that’s meaningful and real. Something I’ve always noticed when I watch reality TV is that a lot of things feel so overproduced, and that’s not what I want to do. Something that I loved about this show is that none of this drama was manufactured. This truly was how everything played out, and these people’s feelings are very real. That was really refreshing to me.

This isn’t a normal competition show. It’s a house full of content creators. Do you think that having that affected the dynamic and led to some drama?

100%. A lot of us had either been friends, met before or, in some circumstances, were exes. These are all people that have a platform, and you’ve probably seen their content. So your first impression of them is, “Oh, I’ve been watching that guy’s videos for three years. He seems like a D-bag online. I wonder how he’s going to be in real life.” I probably had met over half that cast before we walked in there.

Do you still stay in touch with people from the show?

Yeah, it’s great. We have a big group chat that’s always popping off, especially right now, because the show is actually airing. We’re all like, “Oh my gosh, you said this in your interview,” or, “Oh my gosh, I can’t believe they put this in that sequence, or they cut this part out.”

Are you watching the drama and thinking, “Oh, I didn’t know she said this”?

Definitely. My first reality show [Barstool’s “Project Verified”], I feel like people were talking about me in their interviews, and they probably did talk about me on this show and it just didn’t make the cut. And thank you to the editors for that, because I have a fragile ego. There were definitely some things where I was like, “Oh wow, that person said that about that person. I didn’t realize that.” And even sometimes I will see myself say something and go, “That was kind of mean, Brandon.” But it’s TV, and when you’re in a situation like that, it is a pressure cooker.

You became somewhat of a fan favorite while on “Unwell Summer Games.” People online are saying you were the perfect blend of loving drama but still being an empath.

They did mention that I was the only person out of all 16 of us that was in a relationship, so my strategy going into it was that I’m going to be a matchmaker. I’m going to help the girls go after the guys that they want. I just wanted to be a safe space for everybody, and have fun.

It was interesting, because you were interested in the drama on the show, but you were never directly involved in any.

We all flew out here and we’re working for four days. I didn’t want this to be us all sitting in a circle playing Kumbaya. I definitely wanted there to be realness and honesty. It’s not like I was like, “Everyone needs to fight.” But I was like, ”You want to hook up with that guy? Go for it. This is the time.”

I have to ask about the Blake, Zarah and Carly love triangle. What was it like seeing that unfold in real time?

It was complicated, because I liked all three of them so much. You kind of see in my conversation with Zarah that I just wanted her to be very honest with me about her feelings with Blake, and then act on them. My motto in life is always say what you mean and mean what you say, and that’s where I kind of guided her a little bit. And I was like, “If you said this whole time that you really care about Blake and you want to pursue something with him, or your feelings are still there, then it’s one thing to confront Carly, but you have been telling everybody you don’t want any part of this.” I wanted to be a friend for her in that moment, and be like, “Why don’t you take a step back and really reassess?”

In Zarah’s defense, though, I do think Carly was a little bit scattered. I was really surprised with Carly, because she was also someone who said she wasn’t going to kiss anybody, and then she goes for Blake. She was obsessed with Chad. Then she goes to Tim. I think it’s complicated when you have someone like Blake who is younger and such a genuine guy. But I think he’s there to have fun and doesn’t necessarily want to be in drama either.

In the finale, there’s a moment where you yell at Carly.

Episode 3 ends with me trying to shake Carly and say, “I think a lot of your feelings are valid, but you control how you react to the situation. If you feel like Suede, Zarah and Hallie are excluding you, that’s three out of 16 members of this cast. Maybe you should say, “I’m not vibing with those girls. I’m going to hang out with Brandon, Cassie and Daniela.’” She is playing victim a little bit, and I just wanted her to make the best of this experience and just have fun. This is a silly little show. We leave tomorrow.

One thing they didn’t show me say to her was, “You’re upset that you’re not being picked for anyone’s team, but have you even gone up to any of the captains and say, ‘Hey, I would love to work with you?’ And she’s like, ‘Well, no.’” I said, “You almost expect things to fall on your plate, and when they don’t, you kind of throw your hands up in the air.” It takes two people to communicate. She was just looking at the glass half empty.

What you’ll see in the fourth episode is that pressure-cooker moment of me reaching my breaking point because of how she lashed out a little bit on Chad. When people are hurt, they tend to push away the people that they’re closest to, and I think that day Carly was like, “Oh, Bran’s mad at me.” She was talking to everybody else but me, and I wasn’t mad at her. I was just frustrated with her because I loved her so much. I blew a fuse for sure. And it’s not something that I’m proud of. I definitely never want to yell at anybody, let alone a woman.

How does it feel to win a reality show?

It feels incredible. One of my favorite “Survivor” players of all time is Cirie Fields, and she did a very infamous speech where she was like, “My mother always said, ‘You may not be able to beat them with these [points to his arms], but you can beat them with this [points to his brain]. And I tied that into my experience. I was like, “I might not beat you in a race, but I will beat you in brain power.”

I have to ask you this. You were just on Alex Cooper’s show. We also saw you at Alix Earle’s “Earle Meets World” premiere. Have you been keeping up with the drama?

I will say, I wish we had more fascination with men than we do with women. These are two very successful, powerful women, and everyone just wants to push this narrative of beef and controversy and picking teams. I personally feel like both of them are incredible and super amazing at what they do, and I think one of those elements that both of them have is they’ll never take a business opportunity away from a mutual friend.

This interview has been edited and condensed.

title: Benjamin Netanyahu Calls to ‘Revoke the Citizenship’ of ‘Anyone Who Slanders IDF Soldiers’ Following ‘NAZA’ Documentary Premiere
summary: Following the premiere of “NAZA” at the Venice Film Festival earlier this month, Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is calling for the introduction of a law that would “revoke the citizenship of anyone who slanders IDF [Israeli Defense Forces] soldiers.” “We will hit them in their pockets and also in their citizenship, because their place […]
content:
Following the premiere of “NAZA” at the Venice Film Festival earlier this month, Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is calling for the introduction of a law that would “revoke the citizenship of anyone who slanders IDF [Israeli Defense Forces] soldiers.”

“We will hit them in their pockets and also in their citizenship, because their place is not among us,” he said in a video posted to X on Wednesday. He went on to describe another law that would raise “the defamation damages they can be sued for twentyfold.”

“NAZA,” co-directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, who are both Israeli citizens, shows “in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza,” according to its official logline. The film features interviews with 24 Israeli military intelligence officers and soldiers.

Popular on Variety

The documentary won the special jury prize at the festival, and also received a 24.5-minute standing ovation — the longest in the festival’s history.

Netanyahu’s statement comes following the words of Israel’s Minister of Culture Miki Zohar, who threatened to revoke the Israeli citizenships of Abraham and Szor on Sunday. He called the documentary “shocking” and accused the filmmakers of “betraying the state.”

“The self-loathing that burns in the creators, who are willing to harm their homeland just to get applause from antisemites around the world, is inconceivable and constitutes a betrayal of the state,” Zohar wrote. “As Minister of Culture, I will act immediately to revoke the Israeli citizenship of these despicable creators for betraying the state.”

content:
Chinese director Zhang Yimou has been named as Jury President for the main competition section at this year’s Busan International Film Festival (October 6-15).

Joining him are fellow Chinese filmmaker Bi Gan, whose 2025 film Resurrection played in Busan competition last year; Korean actress Moon Choi, who produced and acted in Bedford Park, which is screening at the festival this year; Japanese director Kei Ishikawa (A Pale View Of Hills); Korean director July Jung (Dora), Vietnamese producer Tran Thi Bich Ngoc (Skin Of Youth) and Kazakh actress Samal Yeslyamova (Ayka).

The jury will be watching the previously announced competition selection of 13 features and presenting prizes across five categories: Best Film, Best Director, Special Jury Prize, Best Actor, and Artistic Contribution, with total cash prize money of $80,000 (KRW110m).

Watch on Deadline

Busan film festival introduced a fully-fledged competition section for the first time last year, with Zhang Lu’s Chinese title Gloaming In Luomu taking the Busan Award for Best Film. Following changes to the Academy Awards’ criteria for Best International Feature, introduced in May this year, films that win Busan’s Best Film Award will be automatically submitted to the Best International Feature category.

The festival has also announced the juries for its Vision – Asia section, with the NETPAC jury comprising Nina Kochelyaeva, Matthew Poon and Lee Dongha; and the FIPRESCI jury including Ma Xingxu, Teresa Vena and Roh Chul-Hwan.

In addition the jury for the BIFF Mecenat Award in the Feature Documentary Competition includes Rintu Thomas, Kim Taeil and Zhou Hao. The Sonje Award Jury comprises Anuparna Roy, Abinash Bikram Shah and Lee Ranhee.

title: Duncan Sheik Hospitalized In “Critical But Stable Condition” Weeks Before Two Major Off Broadway Musicals Set To Begin
summary: Duncan Sheik, the singer and composer whose new musical Memoirs of Amorous Gentlemen is set to begin performances Off Broadway later this month and whose 2006 Broadway musical Spring Awakening is being revived for a major Off Broadway production in November, has been hospitalized and is in “critical but stable condition” for undisclosed reasons. The […]
content:
Duncan Sheik, the singer and composer whose new musical Memoirs of Amorous Gentlemen is set to begin performances Off Broadway later this month and whose 2006 Broadway musical Spring Awakening is being revived for a major Off Broadway production in November, has been hospitalized and is in “critical but stable condition” for undisclosed reasons.

The news comes via Sheik’s official Instagram page, which earlier tonight posted a message, apparently on behalf of the musician’s family: “We would like to share an update with Duncan’s fans and the public. Duncan is currently receiving medical care and remains in critical but stable condition. Out of respect for Duncan and our family, we will not be sharing any further medical details at this time.”

The statement continues, “We kindly ask for privacy during this incredibly difficult time and will provide updates when appropriate. Thank you for the continued love and support.”

Watch on Deadline

In recent weeks, Sheik made several references on the Instagram page about being in a hospital, apparently in New York City. On August 20, he wrote, “I would prefer to be home making music. But a bit of reflection is not too bad … boring hospital stays have their benefits (outside the obvious.)” On September 6 he wrote, “Sorry for the selfies. But I’m still bored in hospital…” and on September 7, the last post before tonight’s message, he wrote, “Out of here in 60 hours.”

See the latest Instagram post below.

Deadline has reached out to representatives for Sheik’s upcoming musical productions for additional information.

Sheik, who rose to fame as an indie singer-songwriter in the 1990s with his hit song “Barely Breathing,” branched out into the world of musical theater with his smash hit Broadway production of Spring Awakening, co-written with Steven Sater. The 2006 musical’s cast featured stars-in-the-making Jonathan Groff, Lea Michele and John Gallagher Jr., and was later revived in 2015 with Deaf West Theatre directed by Michael Arden.

A major new revival of Spring Awakening directed by Danya Taymor (The Outsiders) was recently announced by producers Seaview for an engagement at the Off Broadway venue Studio Seaview set to begin previews on November 27 ahead of an official December 17 opening. Deadline recently revealed the cast consisting largely of young newcomers, with Amalia Yoo, who gained considerable attention and critical acclaim when she made her Broadway debut last year in the Tony-nominated play John Proctor is the Villain, set to play the role of “Ilse.”

Later this month, Sheik’s new musical – an adaptation of the classic Manga graphic novel Memoirs of Amorous Gentlemen, is scheduled to begin performances at the new Off Broadway venue named for a club in the graphic novel — The Night Egg at the Culture Club in Manhattan’s Chelsea neighborhood. The musical, to be directed and choreographed by Rob Ashford, will star Sophia Anne Caruso and begins performances Friday, September 25 with an opening night set for Thursday, October 15.

Deadline will update this post as additional information becomes available.

title: ‘South Park’ Back With Fellatio Shout-Outs Galore, No Trump, Lots Of “Chinese Sh*tty E-Bikes” & ‘South America’ Re-Branding
summary: South Park is back for its 29th season and while Trey Parker and Matt Stone’s satire is now called South America in homage to Donald Trump’s mastery of geography, the Comedy Central show’s bite is still stars-and-stripes sharp — on or off “Chinese sh*tty e-bikes.” Yep, it was the kids’ status symbol of “damn e-bikes” […]
content:
South Park is back for its 29th season and while Trey Parker and Matt Stone‘s satire is now called South America in homage to Donald Trump‘s mastery of geography, the Comedy Central show’s bite is still stars-and-stripes sharp — on or off “Chinese sh*tty e-bikes.”

Yep, it was the kids’ status symbol of “damn e-bikes” that “should be illegal,” according to cycling Dads, and the big change coming in November (aka the long-awaited debut of Grand Theft Auto 6) that dominated the Season 29 premiere Wednesday.

After taking a Satan-impregnating POTUS to task and the animated wood-chipper last year on the Emmy-winning animated series, the newly titled South America tonight avoided any mention of Trump. Instead, the show slammed everyone who got on their knees for the former Apprentice host since Trump’s return to office — with a lot of references to fellatio. Like, a lot of references.

Watch on Deadline

For example: “It’s an outrage! I’ve lived in South America all my life, and I’ve never seen anything like this. These kids almost killed me on the sidewalk, and then told me to s*ck their d*ck. And when you rolled over and sucked a dc*k with the change in the town name, did you feel any outrage? There’s plenty of upset people here, and the question on everyone’s mind is: Is the e-bike change permanent?”

I could say ask Google, Apple and all the rest who are now calling the Gulf of Mexico and Lake Ontario the Gulf of America and Lake America, respectively, since El Presidente took out his Oval Office sharpie …but that would be too pedantic.

As South Park has done for decades, South America also mocked the wide-eye and blue-sky hopes of the left and the anti-MAGA crowd that the midterms will end the current chaos — or just really looked forward to the much-delayed GTA 6 launch in November. Or both.

There was all that, but more so there were over and over the misplaced chaos of the “vicious South American” e-biker gang of Cartman, Stan, Kylie and Kenny. “South America used to be a quiet place, but now you got these kids just going hog wild,” one parent exclaims, before the band of Dads beat up Mr. Kim for selling those previously mentioned cheap “Chinese sh*tty e-bikes” to their kids for pennies.

Comedy Central

And yeah, all those angry Dads in spandex standing in for ICE (kinda) and the kids as hunted illegal aliens — and yes, Kenny dies to unite South America in grief and “South America Strong” tees.

Untangling all this as an exploration of the frayed and divided America of 2026 is a dog’s breakfast at best. Instead, just enjoy the whacking of the pompous, the powerful and parents — that’s what Stone and Parker do. They’ve been doing it since 1997. Tonight they showed exactly just how good they still are at it. In fact, call it South Park or South America, the result was still damn good.

Or, put another way: “Two words that bring a smile to my mouth: America and South. We are South America. We are South America in that northern mountain zone. We’ll always be south. We won’t change for anyone.”

Don’t.

title: Rodney Charters Dies: ‘24,’ ‘Shameless’ Cinematographer Was 80
summary: Rodney Charters, the cinematographer who shot 184 episodes of 24 and helped craft the show’s distinct look, died suddenly in Amsterdam on September 13. The news was announced by the ASC, of which he was a longtime member. He was 80. Charters’ work on the Kiefer Sutherland-starring thriller was structured to capture the energy and […]
content:
Rodney Charters, the cinematographer who shot 184 episodes of 24 and helped craft the show’s distinct look, died suddenly in Amsterdam on September 13. The news was announced by the ASC, of which he was a longtime member. He was 80.

Charters’ work on the Kiefer Sutherland-starring thriller was structured to capture the energy and chaos of Jack Bauer’s 24-hour scramble each season.

“We’ve evolved to the point where we always shoot a scene in its entirety — it’s never broken into setups,” he told American Cinematographer in 2004. “We shoot two directions on every scene. We shoot one direction first, after it’s been blocked and staged by the cast privately, without even me present, which is a little uncommon in television. When we’re brought in, we have an understanding of what the scene is, but sometimes there are pleasant surprises. [Executive producer/director] Stephen [Hopkins] was a great one for saying, ‘Look at the scene and imagine where the camera would never be, and that’s where I want it.’ We’ll film and light in that direction for A camera, and B camera just strays off the axis.”

Charters was Emmy nominated in 2005 and 2006 for Outstanding Cinematography for a Single-Camera Series for his work on the show. He also directed three episodes.

His other work included a long list of high-profile shows, including Nash Bridges, The Commish, The Pretender, Rosewell, Nashville, Shameless, Friday the 13th: The Series, the Dallas, Dynasty and Magnum P.I. reboots as well as The Shannara Chronicles.

In 2013, the ASC honored him with its Career Achievement in Television Award.

title: ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Recap: Season 35 Kick Off Continues With Ladies Night & Another Elimination
summary: SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from the second of ABC’s two-night Dancing with the Stars Season 35 premiere. Why have one night of Dancing with the Stars when you can have two? Fresh off the news that last night’s premiere was the most watched in six years, the kickoff continued Wednesday night with the […]
content:
SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from the second of ABC‘s two-night Dancing with the Stars Season 35 premiere.

Why have one night of Dancing with the Stars when you can have two? Fresh off the news that last night’s premiere was the most watched in six years, the kickoff continued Wednesday night with the women celebrities making their performance debut.

ICYMI, the male celebs performed last night (and were in the audience to dutifully support the ladies on their big night), and Conner Leavitt was the first to go home. There’ll be another contestant sent packing by the end of Wednesday’s show. The results are at the bottom of this post.

You can breathe a sigh of relief, because there’s only one cha cha in this round. Also, online voting was back after it crashed during Tuesday’s live show.

Watch on Deadline

Let’s get into it.

Actress Tatyana Ali with Jan Ravnik. Reuniting with her on-screen brother Alfonso Ribeiro here, Fresh Prince of Bel Air star Ali performed a jive to “Knock on Wood” (her kids’ song choice, she says). Ravnik is one of the newer pros, making his debut last season, and the jive is quite an ambitious dance style for the very first performance. Ali struggled with some timing issues at the start, but they ultimately pulled off a fun first routine. “That was a bit of a rough start,” Carrie Ann Inaba told her. “But what I see in you, that is positive, is that there is a fierce fire burning under you.” SCORE: 12 out of 30 (kind of rough!)

Olympian Amber Glenn with Pasha Pashkov. The gold medalist has some big shoes to fill, considering the show’s lengthy track record of figure skaters who found success on the ballroom floor. She dances the lone cha cha of the night to a Santana song, and while you could tell she was deep in thought the entire time, she rose to the occasion. “OK ice queen! I see you!” Derek Hough told her. “You have such a beautiful awareness of your body…just a little bit more finesse.” SCORE: 18 out of 30

Reality star Ciara Miller with Brandon Armstrong. When she says at the top of her intro package that she’s had a “hell of a year,” she’s pretty much understating it. The Summer House star thinks, at this point, she can take on anything, and she’s ready to express herself through a medium other than words. She and Armstrong come out of the gate with a rocky foxtrot, but listen, it’s the first performance. On a positive note, she nails the “sophistication” of the dance style, Bruno Tonioli tells her. “It’s all there with you to use.” SCORE: 15 out of 30

Celebrity chef Giada De Laurentiis with Alan Bersten. Dancing a tango, this celebrity chef is trying to bring an elegance she says she learned in the kitchen to the ballroom floor. She’s just got to find the right recipe! Looks like she’s sniffing it out, because the judges were truly surprised at her performance despite her zero dance experience, but Derek says he wished it was a little less safe. “With that said, I love seeing the joy in this dance,” he adds. Prepare yourselves for a lot of cooking puns this season. The judges were really packing them in there. SCORE: 16 out of 30

Actress Julia Stiles with Ezra Sosa. While she might’ve starred as a Julliard student in Save the Last Dance, Stiles really doesn’t have much dance experience. If you didn’t know, the movie was doubled, she tells viewers in her intro package. (“I’m well aware,” Sosa sweetly replies when she tells him). These two brought a quickstep to “9 to 5” by the late Dolly Parton to the show on Wednesday, and there may be room for growth, but this DWTS superfan totally disproved Andy Cohen’s previous remarks that Stiles can’t dance! Yes, they did bring that up. “Andy Cohen, you can eat it!” Derek said to the camera when the performance was finished. SCORE: 18 out of 30

Reality star Maura Higgins with Mark Ballas. These former Traitors co-stars reunited for a foxtrot on their first night in the ballroom. She’s been on several reality series at this point, and yet she’s never prevailed in the end, so she’s got her eyes on that mirrorball trophy. Too bad dance does not come naturally to her. Yet, Ballas still had her out there looking like a pro herself strutting across that floor to “Black Velvet.” A blessing and a curse to deliver like that the first week, because she’s now set the bar high. “You foxy traitor! So seductive, so enticing, smooth as silk and ready for the kill,” Tonioli said. “The movement, I’ve never seen something like that on week one.” SCORE: 21 out of 30 (highest of the night)

Reality star Sarah Jane Nader with Hailey Bills. Sarah Jayne is no stranger to the ballroom, since her sister Brooks previously competed. She took the stage for one or two counts on Season 33, but now she’s ready to take the stage for herself. This is the second time that DWTS has had a same-sex female couple, and last time it was Bills’ aunt and longtime pro Jenna Johnson paired with JoJo Siwa. So, they both have a lot to prove with their jive to “Sk8er Boi,” and it seems they did decent. “Can I just say what we’re all thinking? That was super hot!” exclaimed Inaba before delivering a hard truth: “You were out of sync.” Room for improvement! SCORE: 14 out of 30

Actress Jenna Dewan with Val Chmerkovskiy. The Rookie and Step Up star Dewan closed out the show with a tango. After starting her career as a backup dancer, she’s been focusing on purely acting for a long enough time now that she’s not sure if she can meet the expectations that she assumes people have for her run on DWTS. Chmerkovskiy is ready to push her, though, and he got a lot out of her on night one. “You put the ‘go’ in ‘tango,’” Derek says. He called it “a little frantic in places” but it certainly sets the standard for her performances to come. SCORE: 19 out of 30

So, who goes home?

After just one performance, Sarah Jayne Nader is the first female celebrity to be eliminated from the competition. The 14 remaining contestants will take on Week 2 to some viral hits next Tuesday at 8 p.m. ET/PT on ABC and Disney+.

title: Pingyao Festival Sets 10th Edition Lineup With Fei Mu Restoration, Films From Cristian Mungiu, James Gray
summary: The Pingyao International Film Festival has unveiled the full lineup for its 10th edition, with a 4K restoration of Fei Mu’s 1948 classic “Spring in a Small Town” opening the anniversary program and Hong Kong dramedy “Good Trip” set to close it. The festival, founded by Jia Zhangke in Shanxi province, will run Sept. 24-30. […]
content:
The Pingyao International Film Festival has unveiled the full lineup for its 10th edition, with a 4K restoration of Fei Mu’s 1948 classic “Spring in a Small Town” opening the anniversary program and Hong Kong dramedy “Good Trip” set to close it.

The festival, founded by Jia Zhangke in Shanxi province, will run Sept. 24-30. “Good Trip,” directed by Norris Wong Yee Lam and Hoi Wong, will have its mainland China premiere as the closing film.

Jia’s own short “Torino Shadow,” an Italy-China co-production, will screen as part of a Fenjiu Night presentation and mark an Asian premiere. The Cinephile strand will feature Keane T.K. Wong’s Hong Kong title “Afterpiece.”

Popular on Variety

The Hidden Dragons competition includes three world premieres: Malaysian director Kethsvin Chee’s “Dead Tide,” Chengjie Cai’s “Suzhou Quartet” and Niu Niu’s “Final Payment.” The section also features Dongnan Chen’s documentary “Whispers in May,” a Netherlands-Sweden-South Korea-Hong Kong co-production, and Zou Jing’s France-China co-production “A Girl Unknown.”

The Crouching Tigers section spans a wide geographic range, with entries including Colombia-Portugal co-production “Gemstones” from Simón Vélez, Russian director Anastasia Kuzina’s “Bo Bo” and Philippines-Singapore-France-Netherlands-U.K. co-production “Filipiñana” from Rafael Manuel on which Jia is an executive producer. The lineup also features Rwanda-Gabon-France-Norway co-production “Ben’Imana,” from Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo, and multi-country production “Yesterday the Eye Didn’t Sleep,” directed by Rakan Mayasi.

The Galas section brings together established auteurs, including Cristian Mungiu’s Cannes-winning Norway-Romania-Sweden-Finland-Denmark-France co-production “Fjord,” James Gray’s U.S. title “Paper Tiger” and Marie Kreutzer’s Austria-France-Germany-Sweden co-production “Gentle Monster.” South Korean director Na Hong-Jin’s “Hope” and Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s “The Beloved” will both have mainland China premieres, while Fernando Eimbcke’s “Flies” and Kent Jones’ “Late Fame” mark China premieres.

Special Presentations will showcase Liu Wenpu’s world premiere “A Better Jianghu” alongside a 4K restoration of Allen Fong’s 1986 film “Just Like Weather.” A restoration of festival juror Ann Hui’s (Hui On Wah Ann) 1981 film “The Story of Woo Viet” anchors the East-West Contribution strand.

Marking the festival’s 10-year milestone, PYIFF has built out several retrospective sections. The Pingyao 10 Years·Tributes strand pairs the “Spring in a Small Town” restoration with Pan Yilin’s new documentary “Echoes of Fei Mu,” alongside Roberto Rossellini’s 1959 film “Generale Della Rovere” and Alessandro Rossellini’s 2020 documentary “The Rossellinis.” A memorial program will screen restorations of “Phony Phoenixes,” which includes a video introduction recorded by the late Tony Rayns, and “Aces Go Places,” dedicated to the memory of Nansun Shi, the driving force behind the film, alongside Apichatpong Weerasethakul’s “Memoria,” dedicated to the memory of producer Simon Field.

A separate Pingyao 10 Years·Start From Pingyao Corner strand traces the trajectories of filmmakers first spotted in the festival’s short-film program, pairing early shorts with the directors’ subsequent Hidden Dragons features, including Wei Shujun’s “Only the River Flows” and Kong Dashan’s “Journey to the West.”
