title: ‘Belzebubs’ Created by JP Ahonen Is a Relatable Story About Liberal Values Where ‘The Addams’ Family Meets ‘Modern Family’ – and Satanism (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Finnish artist JP Ahonen is ready to unleash the animated series “Belzebubs” onto the unsuspecting world. Based on his successful webcomic, it will premiere at Helsinki Intl. Film Festival – Love & Anarchy. Banijay Kids & Family is handling distribution. Terhi Väänänen is producing for Pyjama Films, Samppa Kukkonen directs and Lassi Vierikko is responsible […]
content:
Finnish artist JP Ahonen is ready to unleash the animated series “Belzebubs” onto the unsuspecting world.

Based on his successful webcomic, it will premiere at Helsinki Intl. Film Festival – Love & Anarchy. Banijay Kids & Family is handling distribution. Terhi Väänänen is producing for Pyjama Films, Samppa Kukkonen directs and Lassi Vierikko is responsible for the script.

The series debuts first-look stills with Variety.

Popular on Variety

“It started as a self-therapy project over 10 years ago. I was burnt out and going through depression,” Ahonen tells Variety.

“My wife and I had just had our first kid after experiencing several miscarriages. I wanted to be at home with our child, but I also needed to work. It got to the point where I thought: ‘I need to pack up my pencils and change professions.’”

The Inktober challenge, which encourages artists to create one ink drawing for each day in October, changed everything.

“The first thing I came up with were two black metal dudes. I started thinking about this stay-at-home dad, Sløth, who wants to be a good husband and role model for his kids, but he also tries to fulfill his dream of making a living through music. It’s funny because in the black metal scene, it’s basically impossible to make it big. If you do, they tear you down and call you a poser. So either way, Sløth is fucked,” he laughs.

JP Ahonen

Ahonen ended up juxtaposing black metal and satanic imagery with family dynamic. Sløth is married to Lucyfer, and they’re raising Lilith and Leviathan.

“They do weird things, but they stick together. It’s one of those don’t-judge-a-book-by-its-cover stories. On the one hand, you have God, abstinence and conservatism, and then you have Satanism, which is all about indulging in life,” he says.

“One fan said it’s like ‘The Addams Family’ meets ‘Modern Family.’ That’s it in a nutshell.”

It’s also a call for tolerance.

“I strongly believe in creating relatable stories, and this one is about liberal values. There’s a lot of prejudice toward these characters, but they’re open to whatever you’re into,” he notes.

“You have the grandma who’s an old-school Satanist, and the kids who are more liberal. They don’t mind dressing up as an angel for a school play. But at the end of the day, they all support each other.”

In the upcoming episodes, he gets to “really dive into their individual stories.”

“Even if you’re familiar with the comics, there’s so much more going on.”

JP Ahonen

The show also allows him to return to his music videos, as Belzebubs is also a functioning band.

“We made our first album in 2019, and it charted in Finland. The second one is ready,” he says.

“A musician friend and I were juggling some ideas that’d include animation and music, and then the comic suddenly went viral. We needed proper music videos, and that’s when Pyjama Films got involved. Things snowballed from there, much like in our “Cathedrals of Mourning” music video, and we started plotting an animated series adaptation.”

He’s already developing the second season of the show.

“I hope we get to do several. It’s evident there’s so much more we can do with these characters. The comic is still the beating core of this story, but the series pulls everything together.”

He hopes it will go global – after all, his fandom already has.

“This fandom isn’t limited to Finland. If I look at the numbers, I think it’s the U.S. first, then Canada, Mexico, Brazil and Italy. Finland actually comes in fifth.”

He’s still surprised that something that started out as a very personal project resonated with so many people.

“They know my history with depression and suicidal thoughts – all this really bleak stuff. It’s wonderful that now I can be there for them through my art.”

title: King Charles Denies Bombshell Book Claim That He Said World Would ‘Forget’ Princess Diana
summary: King Charles III has issued a rare statement regarding a new book about his ex-wife, the late Princess Diana. Written by Diana’s brother, Charles Spencer, the book claims (according to reports) that after Diana’s sudden death in a car crash in 1997, Spencer got into a heated argument with Charles, then still heir to the […]
content:
King Charles III has issued a rare statement regarding a new book about his ex-wife, the late Princess Diana.

Written by Diana’s brother, Charles Spencer, the book claims (according to reports) that after Diana’s sudden death in a car crash in 1997, Spencer got into a heated argument with Charles, then still heir to the throne. During the argument, Charles allegedly “hissed” at Spencer: “Rest assured, we’ll forget her soon enough!”

In a statement issued to the BBC, Buckingham Palace dismissed the claim, saying: “While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss.”

Popular on Variety

Spencer’s memoir, “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister,” is not set to be published until next week. However, the Daily Mail reported that on Monday a truck carrying copies was travelling between a printing plant and a warehouse in the Netherlands when it was intercepted while parked in a lay-by, with four copies of the book mysteriously stolen.

Revelations about its contents leaked soon afterwards, including the claim about the argument between Spencer and Charles, which reportedly took place by telephone not long after Diana’s death.

The Royal Family, whose relations with Spencer have long been strained, are said to fear the book could contain numerous bombshells about Charles and Diana’s relationship, which was infamously plagued by adultery and acrimony.

The claims would deal yet another blow to the King, who is still battling cancer. An equally loquacious memoir by his son, Prince Harry, was published in 2022, creating headlines around the world and leading to a fall-out with his family.

title: Lasse Hallström, Lena Olin, Trine Dyrholm, Fares Fares, Ólafur Darri Ólafsson Among Awardees at The Freyas
summary: The Freyas, also known as the Nordic Film and TV Awards, has revealed its first honorees and award-winners. They are Lasse Hallström, Lena Olin, Trine Dyrholm, Ólafur Darri Ólafsson, Fares Fares, Thea Sofie Loch Næss, Laura Birn and Ebba Katrín Finnsdóttir. The first-ever edition will be held in Helsinki on Sept. 22, bringing together leading […]
content:
The Freyas, also known as the Nordic Film and TV Awards, has revealed its first honorees and award-winners. They are Lasse Hallström, Lena Olin, Trine Dyrholm, Ólafur Darri Ólafsson, Fares Fares, Thea Sofie Loch Næss, Laura Birn and Ebba Katrín Finnsdóttir.

The first-ever edition will be held in Helsinki on Sept. 22, bringing together leading creative talents and industry professionals from Finland, Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Iceland.

“The Nordic countries may represent relatively small individual markets, but together they have created an audiovisual culture with a remarkable global footprint,” Kirpi Uimonen, one of The Freyas founders, said. “The Freyas are about celebrating that collective achievement – and the people who have been bold enough to take Nordic stories to the world.”

Popular on Variety

Honorees will include Swedish director Lasse Hallström, who represents “one of the pioneering Nordic filmmakers who have established successful careers on both sides of the Atlantic,” the awards organizers said.

His international breakthrough came with “My Life as a Dog” in 1985, which earned him two Oscar nominations. He subsequently built an extensive international career, including audience and critics pleasers such as “What’s Eating Gilbert Grape,” “Chocolat,” “An Unfinished Life” and “The Hundred-Foot Journey.”

Another honoree will be Swedish actress Lena Olin, who “embodies the international reach of Nordic acting talent.” From Bergman’s “Fanny and Alexander” and “After the Rehearsal,” and of her international breakthrough performance in Philip Kaufman’s “The Unbearable Lightness of Being,” to “Enemies,” “A Love Story” and “Chocolat,” Olin built a distinguished international career spanning European and American cinema and television.

Denmark’s Trine Dyrholm will be awarded at The Freyas with Outstanding Nordic Actor (in a Series) for her role as the formidable Ditte Jensen in Benedikt Erlingsson’s series “The Danish Woman,” a co-production between Iceland, Denmark and France.

Her past performances include Thomas Vinterberg’s “The Celebration,” Susanne Bier’s “In a Better World” and “Love Is All You Need,” Nikolaj Arcel’s “A Royal Affair,” Vinterberg’s “The Commune,” for which she won the Silver Bear for best actress at the Berlinale, and May el-Toukhy’s “Queen of Hearts.”

Recently, she has starred in “Margrete: Queen of the North,” “The Girl With the Needle” and “Beginnings.”

Ólafur Darri Ólafsson, one of Iceland’s most internationally recognized actors, will be accepting an Outstanding Nordic Actor (in a Series) Freya Award for the lead role in the Icelandic-Finnish series “Reykjavik Fusion,” which he also executive produced through his company Act4.

He is perhaps best known internationally for his leading role in the acclaimed Nordic noir series “Trapped,” alongside appearances in “True Detective,” “The Secret Life of Walter Mitty,” “The Big Friendly Giant,” “Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald,” “The Tourist” and “Severance.”

Swedish-Lebanese actor and filmmaker Fares Fares is awarded with a Freya Award for Outstanding Nordic Actor (in a Film) for “Arkipelag,” directed by Alex Schulman.

He first rose to prominence with “Jalla! Jalla!” and went on to appear in films including “Easy Money,” “Zero Dark Thirty,” “Rogue One: A Star Wars Story” and “The Contractor,” as well as the series “Westworld,” “Chernobyl” and “The Wheel of Time.”

Icelandic actress Ebba Katrín Finnsdóttir will also be honored. She won Iceland’s Gríman Award for Actress of the Year in 2020 and has recently starred in the series “Húsó,” “Vigdis,” “Reykjavik 112,” “The Danish Woman” and “Hildur.”

The Freyas also recognizes a new generation of Nordic artists working at the highest international level.

Finnish actress Laura Birn is being honored, recognizing a Finnish professional whose international breakthrough has “helped put Nordic talent in front of a global audience.” Birn has become internationally known for her acclaimed portrayal of Demerzel in Apple TV+’s epic science-fiction series “Foundation,” a role she has carried across the series’ first three seasons. She also recently appeared alongside Javier Bardem in “Beloved” (El Ser Querido), which got its world premiere at the Cannes Film Festival in May.

Thea Sofie Loch Næss is one of Norway’s internationally recognized young acting talents. She gained local fans in the “Olsenbanden” movies and international attention as Skade in Netflix’s “The Last Kingdom” and has since built an impressive body of work across Norwegian and international film and television, including “Wisting,” “Christmas Storm,” “So Long Marianne,” “La Palma” and as Cinderella in recent festival darling “The Ugly Stepsister.”

title: Sonia Rovai Appointed Disney Italy VP of Original Production (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Sonia Rovai, one of Italy’s most respected TV and film production executives, has been appointed VP of original production at the Italian unit of The Walt Disney Company. Rovai, who since 2024 served as CEO of Fremantle-owned Wildside — the Rome-based company behind “My Brilliant Friend” and, more recently, Netflix’s hit series “The Monster of […]
content:
Sonia Rovai, one of Italy‘s most respected TV and film production executives, has been appointed VP of original production at the Italian unit of The Walt Disney Company.

Rovai, who since 2024 served as CEO of Fremantle-owned Wildside — the Rome-based company behind “My Brilliant Friend” and, more recently, Netflix’s hit series “The Monster of Florence” — will report to Angela Jain, head of content, Disney+ EMEA.

In her new role, Rovai will lead Disney+’s Italian team and be “responsible for scripted and unscripted local original productions, including production management and business affairs,” according to a Disney statement.

Popular on Variety

Prior to heading Wildside, Rovai led Comcast-owned pay-TV serice Sky Italia’s original series department from 2016 to 2024. During her stint, she shepherded over 80 Sky Original productions including international standouts like “Gomorrah,” “The Young Pope” and “ZeroZeroZero.”

“Sonia joins us at a pivotal moment of growth as we scale our originals across the world,” Jain said in a statement. “Italy is a key market for us, and following the greenlight of ‘Murder on Lake Garda’, our goal is to champion local content that enriches and complements our global line-up with true cultural authenticity and local specificity. Sonia brings an incredible wealth of experience to the team and can’t wait to work with the very best of the Italian creative industry.”

The “Murder of Lake Garda” series, which is based on Tom Hindle’s eponymous Sunday Times bestseller, is being directed by Laura Bispuri (“Sworn Virgin,” “Daughter of Mine”) with cast details still under wraps.

The announcement of Rovai’s appointment, which will give Disney+ Italy’s footprint a boost, follows Disney CEO Josh D’Amero’s statement in a recent shareholder letter, following the company’s Q3 earnings report, in which he vowed that “Across the next three years we plan to roughly triple the number of local original series on Disney+ to drive new international users to the platform and reduce churn.”

title: ‘Happily Ever After’: First Look Footage Of K-Pop Star Shuhua In Movie Debut — Toronto Film Festival
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Here’s your first-look footage of K-pop star Shuhua in her movie debut, Happily Ever After, which is debuting this week at the Toronto Film Festival. The Korea-based Taiwanese singer, a member of the girl group I-dle, stars alongside Xuan Chen (I, Myself) in the second feature from Taiwanese writer-director Feng-i Fiona Roan. Taiwanese outfit […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Here’s your first-look footage of K-pop star Shuhua in her movie debut, Happily Ever After, which is debuting this week at the Toronto Film Festival.

The Korea-based Taiwanese singer, a member of the girl group I-dle, stars alongside Xuan Chen (I, Myself) in the second feature from Taiwanese writer-director Feng-i Fiona Roan. Taiwanese outfit Splash Pictures produces.

The story follows two sisters with vastly different personalities and a stray cat that unexpectedly enters their lives. Hong Kong-based sales outfit Moebius Entertainment is handling international sales rights (excluding Taiwan).

The full synopsis reads: “Twenty-nine-year-old Kitty Lin’s life is upended when her devoted boyfriend, Ledo, unexpectedly proposes. To Kitty, marriage offers love, stability, and the promise that she is finally moving toward the life she has always imagined.

Watch on Deadline

“Her older sister, Claire, is an independent writer who has rejected many conventional expectations, yet still lives with their parents while keeping her longtime relationship with her girlfriend hidden from their conservative mother. Unconvinced by Kitty’s sudden engagement, Claire questions the future her sister is choosing.

“As Kitty takes in an abandoned orange cat and wedding preparations gather momentum, the distance between the sisters widens. While Kitty struggles to meet the expectations of Ledo’s traditional family, Claire grows increasingly frustrated by what she sees as compromise. Kitty, in turn, resents Claire’s judgment and the contradictions behind her hard-won independence.”

title: STV Studios Ups Stake In ‘Patrick Melrose’ & ‘Army Of Shadows’ Producer Two Cities Once Again
summary: EXCLUSIVE: STV Studios has once again upped its stake in Patrick Melrose and Blue Lights producer Two Cities Television. The Scottish production giant has shifted its ownership from 51% to 75%, according to a recent Companies House filing. STV, which owns Criminal Record maker STV Studios, confirmed the move. “As was the plan from the […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: STV Studios has once again upped its stake in Patrick Melrose and Blue Lights producer Two Cities Television.

The Scottish production giant has shifted its ownership from 51% to 75%, according to a recent Companies House filing.

STV, which owns Criminal Record maker STV Studios, confirmed the move. “As was the plan from the point we moved to a majority holding of Two Cities Television in early 2024, our intention has been to continue to increase our stake as the label grows,” said a spokeswoman. “The company continues to go from strength to strength and, accordingly our stake has increased to 75%.”

STV first took a minority stake in Two Cities in 2020 before increasing this to 51% in 2024.

Watch on Deadline

The latest adjustment solidifies STV’s backing for Two Cities.

Run by Michael Jackson and Stephen Wright, Two Cities, which is based out of London and New York, has been on something of a roll of late delivering regular seasons of police procedural Blue Lights for the BBC along with limited series like Sky’s Amadeus. Upcoming it has Channel 4 and Canal+’s Army of Shadows from Day of the Jackal showrunner Ronan Bennett, along with an RTÉ series starring Star Trek icon Kate Mulgrew.

Speaking to Deadline several weeks back, Jackson said the indie’s strategy is to keep the plates spinning with one or two returners while simultaneously seeking interesting IP for limited series. “One helps keep the operation going and gives you the run room to develop the other,” said Jackson, a former BBC One and Channel 4 boss.

STV Studios has stakes in drama indies including Frank Spotnitz’s Man in the High Castle producer Big Light and Criminal Record maker Tod Productions. It recently struck a deal with Grey’s Anatomy star Kevin McKidd and his Ferryman Films.

title: Princess Diana Documentary Featuring Unheard Tapes Set For International Launch At MIPCOM
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Diana Unheard, a new documentary series featuring previously unheard audio recordings of the Princess candidly discussing her life, loves and the royal family, is getting an international launch. Cineflix has landed the rights and the show will be a big launch at MIPCOM in Cannes. The three-part doc was made by Love Monday TV, […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Diana Unheard, a new documentary series featuring previously unheard audio recordings of the Princess candidly discussing her life, loves and the royal family, is getting an international launch.

Cineflix has landed the rights and the show will be a big launch at MIPCOM in Cannes. The three-part doc was made by Love Monday TV, the UK indie behind shows about the British monarchy including Her Majesty The Queen: Behind Closed Doors for ITV and William and Harry: Love and Betrayal for Channel 5.

There is always keen interest in Diana and the British royal family. This week the Palace and Diana’s brother, Earl Spencer, have become embroiled in a war of words over ‘Swan Song: Diana, My Sister’, his memoir about her life and death.

The producers of Diana Unheard secured access to the secretly taped conversations Diana had with her friend James Colthurst in 1991. These formed the foundation of Andrew Morton’s explosive book ‘Diana: Her True Story’. Love Monday worked with Morton and Colthurst to secure access to several hours of tapes and both appear in the factual series.

Watch on Deadline

The Princess is in revealing form in the audio tapes. She talks candidly about Prince Charles and Camilla (now King Charles III and Queen Camilla), as well as the then Prince Andrew, who has since been stripped of his royal titles following scrutiny of his ties to Jeffrey Epstein.

The producers said the doc moves away from framing Diana’s story through a lens of vulnerability.

“In making Diana Unheard, we wanted to challenge the narrative that has too often portrayed Diana, Princess of Wales simply as a victim of her circumstances,” said Kerene Barefield, Creative Director, Love Monday TV.

“This is Diana not as a passive victim of events, but as a woman taking control of her own narrative and risking everything to make her voice heard. Diana Unheard restores authorship of one of the most scrutinized lives in modern history to the woman at its center.”

It will be one of the big factual launches at MIPCOM, with Cineflix Rights handling worldwide sales.

“What really sets Diana Unheard apart is the unique opportunity to hear several hours of intimate recordings of the Princess; her own story in her own voice at a pivotal point in her life,” said Richard Life, SVP Acquisitions and Co-productions, Cineflix Rights.

“Thirty years on, Diana remains a global icon and source of endless fascination for viewers. We are thrilled to be representing this premium limited series from Love Monday TV, and look forward to launching it to our international buyers at MIPCOM.”

title: Audiences Flocking To Anime On Netflix At 10 Times The Rate Of Other Genres, Report Reveals
summary: Viewing to anime on Netflix has rocketed at almost 10 times the rate of the streamer’s total viewing numbers over the past three years. A Media Partners Asia (MPA) report into anime shone a spotlight on audiences’ love for the genre on the U.S. streaming behemoth, which has anime hits like Blue Eye Samurai, Cyberpunk: […]
content:
Viewing to anime on Netflix has rocketed at almost 10 times the rate of the streamer’s total viewing numbers over the past three years.

A Media Partners Asia (MPA) report into anime shone a spotlight on audiences’ love for the genre on the U.S. streaming behemoth, which has anime hits like Blue Eye Samurai, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners and the upcoming Bass X Machina, along with its live action adaptation of One Piece.

According to MPA’s The Anime Economy report, views to Japanese anime rose from 3.33 billion hours in the first half of 2023 to 4.64 billion during the first half of this year, up 39% against 4.5% for total viewing, and from 3.6% to 4.75% of all Netflix hours. These figures were taken from Netflix’s bi-annual What We Watched reports.

When it comes to anime in Asia, MPA said Netflix now carries half the region’s anime across eight markets. And zooming in on the home of anime, Japan, the landscape is now a “two-horse race” between Netflix and Prime Video, which both have more than 40% of overall anime.

Watch on Deadline

The genre has flown into the mainstream in recent years via the big streaming platforms and was one of the major talking points at this year’s Annecy International Animation Film Festival.

MPA’s Anime Economy found the genre to be in rude health, claiming it hits the highest monthly reach of any genre on Asian streaming, with 31–47% of premium VoD users across eight markets watching anime in any given month compared to a 26-34% average for the seven other main genres.

With YouTube also big into anime – it reaches 70 million monthly viewers in Japan, according to today’s report – the MPA now expects global anime spend to rise by around 10% per year to 2030 led by Asia (excluding Japan) and North America, “with growth concentrating among a handful of franchise owners, studio groups and platforms.”

“The next 24 months will determine how the financing of new anime is shared between global platforms and Japanese IP groups,” it added, pointing to main players like Aniplex, Sony, TOHO and Toei Animation. Sony, the report said, has built the only “end-to-end anime stack” across Crunchyroll, Aniplex, Sony Pictures and Sony Music.

“Anime’s scale is established; the question is where the next growth comes from and who captures it,” said MPA CEO Vivek Couto. “The catalysts are streaming pushing deeper into new markets globally, theatrical events on the scale of Infinity Castle becoming repeatable, and games and merchandise carrying franchises well beyond the screen. The direction is toward ownership: platforms financing production directly, Japanese IP groups buying studios, and the two learning to work together.”

title: CJ ENM Sells ‘Hotel Del Luna’, ‘Signal’ & Other Hit K-Dramas To CME Slovakia & Czech Channels
summary: Korean studio CJ ENM has signed partnerships with TV Markíza in Slovakia and TV Nova in the Czech Republic, both owned by European media giant Central European Media Enterprises (CME), as part of an expansion of its K-Content distribution efforts in Central and Eastern Europe. The deals cover a total of 10 scripted titles including […]
content:
Korean studio CJ ENM has signed partnerships with TV Markíza in Slovakia and TV Nova in the Czech Republic, both owned by European media giant Central European Media Enterprises (CME), as part of an expansion of its K-Content distribution efforts in Central and Eastern Europe.

The deals cover a total of 10 scripted titles including major K-drama hits such as Signal, Encounter, Her Private Life, Hotel Del Luna and True Beauty. Other popular CJ ENM titles covered by the deal include The Witch’s Diner, Doom At Your Service, Twinkling Watermelon, Lovely Runner and Guardian: The Lonely And Great God.

The two deals greatly expand the range of Korean content available for viewers in Central and Eastern Europe. “CEE is a market where we see strong potential for further growth,” said Sebastian Kim, Head of Content Distribution Business at CJ ENM. “We will continue to strengthen our partnerships with local broadcasters and platforms, while expanding our content offerings and creating more opportunities for audiences to discover and enjoy K-content.”

Watch on Deadline

CJ ENM has also signed a memorandum of understanding with the Korea Creative Content Agency (KOCCA) and the Korean Cultural Center in Poland with the aim of strengthening local collaboration. The MoU was signed during the 2026 Poland-Korea Brand Week, hosted by KOCCA, which also featured B2C activities for fans, including interactive booths for recent shows Lovely Runner and The Legend Of The Kitchen Soldier.

A special screening of The Legend Of The Kitchen Soldier was also held, followed by a panel with Kim Tae-hoon, CJ ENM Chief Producer, who talked fans through the story behind the series and its production.

title: India-Canada Screen Industry Corridor Takes Shape as NFDC, SASC Sign Pact at Toronto Market
summary: India’s National Film Development Corporation and the South Asian Screen Council of Canada put their names to a Letter of Intent at the Toronto Film Festival market, launching a plan to connect Indian and South Asian filmmakers with fresh openings across Canada’s screen business. The signing was witnessed by the Consul General of India in […]
content:
India’s National Film Development Corporation and the South Asian Screen Council of Canada put their names to a Letter of Intent at the Toronto Film Festival market, launching a plan to connect Indian and South Asian filmmakers with fresh openings across Canada’s screen business.

The signing was witnessed by the Consul General of India in Toronto, alongside representatives of NFDC, SASC Canada and TIFF. Under the pact, projects that come out of NFDC will be plugged into SASC Canada’s platforms for finding new content, building international programming slates, forging industry ties and breaking into the Canadian market.

“This collaboration is about building a practical two-way bridge between Canada and India,” said Sunny Gill, president of SASC Canada. “It creates stronger pathways for Indian filmmakers and stories to be discovered and engaged within Canada, while opening new connections to India’s industry and market for Canadian storytellers. For us, the opportunity is to build a more connected screen ecosystem where talent, projects and industry relationships can move in both directions.”

Popular on Variety

SASC Canada bills itself as Canada’s biggest South Asian screen ecosystem, an umbrella group whose initiatives take in IFFSA Toronto and the South Asian Screen Office of Canada. Its work touches professional and talent development, project development, market access, international engagement and exhibition.

“NFDC has always been about creating meaningful opportunities for Indian stories and filmmakers to connect with the global industry,” said Prakash Magdum, managing director of NFDC. “This collaboration with SASC Canada creates a focused pathway into the Canadian market, giving filmmakers greater access to festivals, industry partners and audiences while expanding the international reach of their work.”

NFDC serves as India’s national body for growing and promoting the country’s cinema, with a hand in production and co-production deals, developing projects and talent, and building the country’s presence in markets and international engagement circles.

The Letter of Intent aims to open a direct pipeline between the Indian and Canadian screen industries, moving films and filmmakers beyond festival discovery and into deeper market and industry engagement in Canada.

title: ‘SNL’ Season 52 Cast: Who Left, Who Joined and Who Stayed
summary: Live from New York, it’s Season 52! The summer of “Saturday Night Live” casting announcements has come to a close, with the ensemble for this year’s season finally solidified (less than two weeks before the Sept. 26 premiere). This year’s cast has remained largely intact compared to last year’s shakeup. Bowen Yang left midway through […]
content:
Live from New York, it’s Season 52!

The summer of “Saturday Night Live” casting announcements has come to a close, with the ensemble for this year’s season finally solidified (less than two weeks before the Sept. 26 premiere).

This year’s cast has remained largely intact compared to last year’s shakeup. Bowen Yang left midway through Season 51, and Chloe Fineman announced her departure in July. Martin Herlihy, a member of sketch trio Please Don’t Destroy who was then moved to the writing staff for one season, is also not returning.

But the rest of the Season 51 cast is on board for at least another year, with all five freshmen — Ben Marshall, Jeremy Culhane, Kam Patterson, Tommy Brennan and Veronika Slowikowska — coming back. Veterans like Kenan Thompson, Colin Jost, Michael Che and Mikey Day are also returning, as well as a handful of other fan favorites like Sarah Sherman, Ashley Padilla, James Austin Johnson, Marcello Hernández, Andrew Dismukes and Jane Wickline.

New to the cast are Grace Reiter and Saidah Belo-Osagie, who auditioned this summer alongside tons of other hopefuls in Los Angeles, New York and Chicago. Reiter is a Wisconsin-born comedian who stars in Tim Robinson’s “The Chair Company” and the upcoming series “Minimum Wage.” Belo-Osagie is a filmmaker and comedian from New York who created the solo show “Saidah Gets Closure.”

Below, read about all the cast members who have left, joined and stayed on “SNL” ahead of Season 52, which premieres on Sept. 26 with host Jalen Brunson.

title: ‘People Are Still Terrified of Me’: Sharon Stone on Thriving for 46 Years in Hollywood and Why ‘My Lane Was Never Going to Be Sex Psychos’
summary: Sharon Stone has every reason to be tough. It’s not just that her father hung the carcasses of the animals he shot on the clothesline during her childhood in rural Pennsylvania and her mother once pulled a huge nail out of Stone’s foot that had gone straight through, wrapped it up and then sent her […]
content:
Sharon Stone has every reason to be tough. It’s not just that her father hung the carcasses of the animals he shot on the clothesline during her childhood in rural Pennsylvania and her mother once pulled a huge nail out of Stone’s foot that had gone straight through, wrapped it up and then sent her back outside to play. Stone, now 68, was a self-described “weirdo” growing up, bringing a live bat to school for show-and-tell and chasing kids with snakes rather than “playing bride.” Extremely smart, she started second grade at age 5 and took college classes at 15 (she got into Howard, she says, but her father was afraid to send her — “I imagine I would for sure have just a bundle of beautiful little biracial children right now. I’d be so happy”). The reason she moved to New York at 19 to be an Eileen Ford model was that her older brother had been busted for having several kilos of cocaine and sent to Attica, and the threats against her family from people who thought he might rat them out made it too risky for her to stay.

Ramona Rosales for Variety

But Stone wasn’t afraid. “I grew up with boys. My older brother is seven years older, and if I didn’t want to die, I had to be physical to not get the shit beat out of me.” Back then, she rode horses naked, shot guns and arrows and swung happily from vines over a ravine.

Stone had good luck in the city. At 20, she got an audition to be an extra in Woody Allen’s 1980 “Stardust Memories.” She roller-skated there with her big black modeling portfolio under her arm — “Clomp, clomp, clomp,” she says — and sat silently beside Allen at a bus stop while he took a few minutes to look it over. A couple days later, when an actress with a bigger role dropped out, Allen chose Stone to take her place.

But Stone also has had some seriously bad luck: In 2001, nine years after she played the part of the panty-less serial killer Catherine Tramell in Paul Verhoeven’s 1992 “Basic Instinct,” which had catapulted her to superstardom, she had a vertebral artery rupture, a nine-day brain bleed and a stroke that took her seven years to come back from. During that time, she lost custody of her adopted son, Roan, now 26. (She has since adopted two more boys on her own, Laird, 21, and Quinn, 20.) “And I lost my place in the business,” she says, “and had to start from the bottom all over again.”

When asked how she got her career back, she says simply, “I didn’t.” But in fact, Stone has made more than 40 movies, including Martin Scorsese’s 1995 “Casino,” opposite Robert De Niro, for which she won a Golden Globe and was nominated for a best actress Oscar. She’s also appeared on TV, including recently as a Sherry Lansing-style Hollywood executive opposite Sydney Sweeney in Season 3 of “Euphoria.” At the moment, Stone has three films in the can, including “In Memoriam” with Marc Maron, which premiered at the Tribeca Festival in June.

Bringing a live bat to show-and-tell and chasing kids around with snakes — were you kind of a dark kid?

I wouldn’t say so much that I was dark as I’ve always been full. I’m as fascinated by the dark as I am by the light; I’m not afraid of it. I was always in trouble for my naivete, mostly about why everybody was scared — scared of me bringing the bat to school, scared of me picking up snakes in the garden. People were scared when I wasn’t scared.

The “Basic Instinct” interrogation scene — were people afraid of you after that movie?

Yes. And what they would do is they would show the film to the press and then bring them in to interview me. They were terrified, and they would sit down opposite me and panic. That hasn’t changed; people are still terrified of me in one way or another. I think that the basic construct of a woman declaring herself as separate and indomitable was, and remains, a terrifying construct.

Ramona Rosales for Variety

How do you feel about that when people say they’re afraid of you?

I’m starting to learn that there are just places and things I can’t do by myself; I need an icebreaker. I also really understand how I need to say, “Hi, I’m Sharon. What’s your name?” But it’s not me, right? It’s very hard for people to understand that I’m a fragile, physically little, delicate, shy, private, loner, gentle, very empathetic artist. Not at all like that character, nothing to do with that character.

I guess we need more comedy.

Right? Because I was in “Irreconcilable Differences” — that was my lane, right? My lane was never going to be sex psychos.

Can we talk about “Euphoria,” where you played an executive opposite Sydney Sweeney’s sex worker?

In “Euphoria,” I tried to get Sydney Sweeney’s character to stop being a cam girl and to come and work for me on the series I was producing called “L.A. Nights.” And she agreed to stop being a cam girl — which she didn’t do. As you can see from Sydney’s new lingerie line, it didn’t take.

Did you always want to act?

No. I wanted to direct. But I do have that troubling vagina issue that got in the way of being allowed to have jobs or be paid fairly for them or be considered to have an intelligent point of view.

Now you can do some directing?

Now I have the troubling postmenopausal problem that makes me feel too tired to put up with people’s bullshit in order to take a directing position. I would prefer if they just kept their opinions about that to themselves while I live a happy life.

Did you choose the ACLU for your Power of Women charity because of what Trump is doing to the country?

I’m not going to make a political statement. But the majority of my global humanitarian work focuses on the things that are most needed, and right now it feels like American civil liberties is something that is up for grabs. And though most of the online chatter — the really negative stuff — is done by about 3% of the people, it makes up 300% of the bad news that we see on our devices. So it’s really important that those of us who want to be loving, concerned and protective of each other’s civil liberties need to be vocal about it.

Ramona Rosales for Variety

Have you ever had the opportunity to talk to some of the tech people who seem to be in control of those algorithms? Mark Zuckerberg?

No. And I say this from a loving heart, because I’m a mom and I’m a little bit on the spectrum: A lot of these tech people who are making up a lot of these choices and algorithms and ideas about how we should do things are people who are on the spectrum. They’re people who are highly intellectual but whose emotional intelligence may not be on par with that. And the balance might not be a healthy way to be guiding us into the future. And so to allow people who are out of balance to be guiding us forward is probably why we all have diarrhea right now. And I think it’s really important to notice if you’re shitting yourself, maybe you’re not making the smartest moves for us as a nation.

Is it true that Ryan Murphy told you he had written the lead role in his TV series “Ratched” with you in mind? What kind of discussions did you have with him?

Ryan Murphy took me out to lunch and he said, “I wrote you a part.” And I said, “OK.” And he said, “Well, you don’t seem to be very excited.” I said, “Well, I don’t know what it is yet.” He was not very happy with me that I wasn’t just excited that he did it. And I didn’t want to tell him that people write parts for me with a bit of regularity, and I don’t take all of them. Clearly, they’re not as special as Mr. Murphy.



But then he said that he wanted me to have a monkey on my shoulder for the entire part. The monkey came over to my house and, no offense to all of the amazing gentlemen who have been my co-stars on the many, many years I’ve been in this business, but I have to say, the monkey was the most fun, the most present, the most hilarious and a little bit mean-humored in a way that was absolutely riotously hilarious.

And Mohammed Ali. You said you met him when you were a teenager in Pennsylvania participating in a beauty pageant?

Muhammad Ali had been in Hershey with his body man and had walked into the pageant —probably because they were dogs — and they’d seen me. And Ali called my dad. He said he wanted to put me in the movie “The Greatest.” And Dad said, [in a low voice] “Mr. Ali, Sharon will be staying in college. She has a very high IQ. I’m not sure you’re aware of that. She’s going to be an architectural engineer. She’s been tested. We have plans for her. She won’t be being in the film business, Mr. Ali. Thank you for your call.” And Ali said, “You could put that girl under a bushel basket, Mr. Stone. That girl’s going to be a movie star no matter what you think.”

Everyone still talks about your costumes in “Casino.” Did you keep anything?

I put my costumes in my contract in the ’80s, and everyone made fun of me. “What are you, some kind of hoarder?” But women didn’t get paid in the business. And I was on an episodic TV show, and one day I walked out and my underwear and bras were all for sale on a folding plastic table outside. And I was so embarrassed, and I was like, “This is just so degrading to me as a woman.” I just went to my manager and I was like, “Chuck, I want my costumes in my contract.” He goes, “That is the weirdest thing I’ve ever heard.” I’m like, “I just don’t want them auctioning off my underwear anymore. If I keep them, great. If I burn them, great. If I give them to Goodwill, great. But this? Not anymore.”

Carrie Fisher taught me how to write my contract, thank God, a hundred years ago because [her mother, Debbie Reynolds] taught her. And then the studios still want to give me a hard time. “You can’t have that in your contract.” “Well, guess what? Carrie did, and so did Debbie, and so do I.” And that is the power of women, right there, ladies. Read your contract, because the agents that work at your agency, they work for the studios, not for you. God love them, but that’s the reality.

This interview was edited and condensed from two conversations.

Courtesy of A Better Chance

Charity Spotlight: American Civil Liberties Union

Most of Sharon Stone’s global humanitarian endeavors have been around issues of health, and she’s been recognized for it: In 2013, she won the Nobel Peace Summit Award for her work in HIV/AIDS (she stepped in for Elizabeth Taylor in 1995 to host the annual Cinema Against AIDS gala in Cannes, later taking over leadership of the campaign). In 2023, she was named Global Citizen of the Year by the United Nations Correspondents Association for her efforts supporting children’s charities, disaster relief and homelessness. “The work that I do outside of the Hollywood community is probably more time-consuming than the work I’ve done within the Hollywood community,” she says.

For her Power of Women charity, Stone is taking a detour to highlight the importance of the American Civil Liberties Union, the nonprofit founded in 1920 to defend and preserve individual rights and liberties guaranteed by the Constitution — free speech, voting rights, reproductive rights, LGBTQ rights and freedom from government abuse.

“At a time where it becomes a controversial statement to raise a flag in your own yard, I think it’s an important thing to be able to feel proud of your own country and protective of your own neighbors,” she says.

It’s not a light subject, but looking back, Stone smiles. “When I was a young person, you actually got a little cardboard card that you carried in your wallet,” she says. “And I, for decades, was a card-carrying member of the ACLU.”

title: ‘The Boulet Brothers’ Dragula’ Season 7 Sets October Release Date on Shudder (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Emmy-nominated “The Boulet Brothers’ Dragula” returns for its seventh season Oct. 27 on Shudder and AMC+. The series was renewed in April as part of drag stars Dracmorda and Swanthula Boulet’s multi-project deal with Shudder. The show is the platform’s highest-performing unscripted original franchise and one of its most popular series. The seventh season marks […]
content:
Emmy-nominated “The Boulet Brothers’ Dragula” returns for its seventh season Oct. 27 on Shudder and AMC+.

The series was renewed in April as part of drag stars Dracmorda and Swanthula Boulet’s multi-project deal with Shudder. The show is the platform’s highest-performing unscripted original franchise and one of its most popular series.

The seventh season marks the tenth anniversary of the original season, which debuted on Oct. 31, 2016, and will pay homage to 1980s and ‘90s VHS horror.

Popular on Variety

“Ten years ago, we opened the gates to our world without a roadmap, a television network or any idea of how far this strange underground experiment would take us. Today, ‘Dragula’ has become an internationally recognized and Emmy-nominated franchise, but its heartbeat remains the same: fearless artists, disruptive ideas and a refusal to play it safe,” the Boulet Brothers said in a joint statement. “For season 7, we wanted to celebrate everything that has always made ‘Dragula’ dangerous and different while pushing the series into its next era. We cast raw, hungry artists who were completely unprepared for what was waiting for them, creating a season that feels unpredictable, cinematic and alive in a way that takes us back to the beginning.”

Guest judges include Rose McGowan, Doug Jones, David Dastmalchian, Harvey Guillén, Rachel True, Darren Stein, Lloyd Kaufman, Brandon Rogers, James A. Janisse, Chelsea Rebecca, Yvie Oddly, Lauren LaVera, Bailey Sarian, Howard Berger and previous “The Boulet Brothers’ Dragula” winners Landon Cider, Dahli and Asia Consent.

Shudder has also renewed all-star spinoff “The Boulet Brothers’ Dragula: Titans” for a second season and greenlit a new holiday special, “The Boulet Brothers’ Holiday of Horrors.”

title: ‘War’ Trailer: Sienna Miller and Dominic West Endure a Bitter Divorce Battle in HBO and Sky’s Legal Drama
summary: Sienna Miller and Dominic West are at the center of an intense divorce trial in the trailer for HBO and Sky’s upcoming series “War.” Hailing from “Lupin” and “Hijack” creator George Kay, “War” is a “high-stakes, legal drama following the lives of London’s most powerful lawyers as firms Cathcarts & Sons and Taylor & Byrne […]
content:
Sienna Miller and Dominic West are at the center of an intense divorce trial in the trailer for HBO and Sky’s upcoming series “War.”

Hailing from “Lupin” and “Hijack” creator George Kay, “War” is a “high-stakes, legal drama following the lives of London’s most powerful lawyers as firms Cathcarts & Sons and Taylor & Byrne clash over a headline-grabbing legal battle,” the official synopsis reads.

The anthology series’ first season — it has already been renewed for Season 2, which will focus on an explosive defamation case — follows the “divorce of British tech entrepreneur Morgan Henderson (West) and international film star Carla Duval (Miller), as Cathcarts & Sons and Taylor & Byrne stop at nothing to secure victory for their clients,” the description continues.

Popular on Variety

Alongside Miller and West, the “War” Season 1 stars Phoebe Fox as Serena Byrne and James McArdle as Nicholas Taylor, partners in life and business at Taylor & Byrne; Archie Renaux as Jonathan “Johnny” Warren; as well asNina Sosanya as Beatrice “Queen Bea” Ubosi and Pip Torrens as St John Smallwood, their counterparts and fierce rivals at Cathcarts & Sons. Other cast members include Celia Imrie, Nick Mohammed, Emma Laird, Aran Murphy, Archie Panjabi, Adrian Scarborough, Shaheen Jafargholi, Akiya Henry, Honor Swinton Byrne, Miles Jupp, Kartanya Maynard, Alexandra Mardell, Dylan Edwards, Mark Quartley and Steve Furst.

“War” is co-produced by New Pictures (a Banijay company) and Observatory Pictures, in association with Sky and HBO. It’s set to premiere Oct. 1 at 9 p.m. ET/PT on HBO and will stream the next day on HBO Max. In the U.K., it will premiere Oct. 2 on Sky and streaming service NOW.

Watch the trailer for “War” below.

UPDATE 08.00 a.m. PT: HBO and Sky legal War has now released full trailer.

As the two transatlantic players build buzz in time for October launch, the full-length featuring Dominic West, Sienna Miller and an ensemble cast can now be watched above.

PREVIOUS: “You are the wronged party here.” That’s the message ringing in the ears of both Dominic West and Sienna Miller as they prepare to do battle in HBO and Sky’s new series War.

HBO has released a trailer and first look photos for the divorce drama, which stars West and Miller as tech entrepreneur Morgan Henderson and film star Carla Duval in the grips of an acrimonious split.

Sitting in their corners are Cathcarts & Sons and Taylor & Byrne, two of London’s most powerful law firms. The divorce draws young lawyer Jonathan “Johnny” Warren (Archie Renaux) into a ruthless world where ambition is currency, betrayal is strategy, and winning is everything.

Watch on Deadline

Produced by Banijay-owned New Pictures and Observatory Pictures, the eight-part series premieres on October 1 on HBO and October 2 on Sky. War will stream on HBO Max in the U.S., Australia, Southeast Asia, Latin America, France, and Belgium.

Other cast includes Phoebe Fox as Serena Byrne and James McArdle as Nicholas Taylor; Nina Sosanya as Beatrice “Queen Bea” Ubosi and Pip Torrens as St John Smallwood; Celia Imrie, Nick Mohammed, Emma Laird, Aran Murphy, Archie Panjabi, Adrian Scarborough, Shaheen Jafargholi, Akiya Henry, Honor Swinton Byrne, Miles Jupp, Kartanya Maynard, Alexandra Mardell, Dylan Murphy, Mark Quartley, and Steve Furst.

The series is created, written, and executive-produced by George Kay, alongside executive producers Willow Grylls and Matt Sandford for New Pictures, and Susan Breen, Ben Taylor, Andrea Dewsbury, and Megan Spanjian for Sky. The lead director is Ben Taylor, and the series producer is Laurie Borg.

Season 2 has already been greenlit and is in production. Marisa Tomei, Kelly Macdonald, and David Harewood will star in the next legal battle, as their lawyers become embroiled in an explosive defamation case.

title: ‘Kikuyu Land’ Trailer: A Man Fights To Reclaim Stolen Ancestral Land Worth Billions Of Dollars
summary: EXCLUSIVE: The award-winning nonfiction feature Kikuyu Land documents a case of cultural erasure and land theft on a massive scale. The documentary directed by Andrew H. Brown and Bea Wangondu unfolds in the tea highlands of Kenya, fertile lands that were seized from local people by the British during their colonial rule over the country. […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: The award-winning nonfiction feature Kikuyu Land documents a case of cultural erasure and land theft on a massive scale.

The documentary directed by Andrew H. Brown and Bea Wangondu unfolds in the tea highlands of Kenya, fertile lands that were seized from local people by the British during their colonial rule over the country. Mr. Mungai, a descendant of those original landowners, is doing everything he can to reclaim his family’s possessions and to see justice done for others like him.

“The colonials stole my ancestors’ land,” he says in the new trailer for Kikuyu Land. “Today, it’s worth billions.”

A worker on a tea plantation in ‘Kikuyu Land.’ Courtesy of Trifilm Studios/Photo by Andrew H. Brown

Kikuyu Land, which premiered in World Cinema Documentary Competition at Sundance, is set to open in UK cinemas on October 2, and in Los Angeles on October 9 at the Monica Film Center. A theatrical run at DCTV Firehouse Cinema in New York City begins November 13. Additional theatrical engagements will be announced in the coming weeks.

Watch on Deadline

Watch the trailer for Kikuyu Land below.

The film won Best Documentary Feature at Mountainfilm Festival in Telluride, CO in May and has screened at more than 40 festivals in the U.S. and internationally.

Stephen in ‘Kikuyu Land.’ Courtesy of Trifilm Studios/Photo by Andrew H. Brown

In the film, Mr. Mungai “pursues justice for land taken from his family, bringing him into conflict with a powerful multinational corporation still operating on contested ground,” according to a synopsis. “His case draws Bea [co-director Bea Wangondu], a local news producer, into an investigation that becomes deeply personal as she uncovers long-silenced truths about her own family history. Running alongside their stories is Stephen, the son of a tea worker whose childhood unfolds within the plantations at the center of the dispute.”

The synopsis continues, “Moving between legal struggle and lived memory, Kikuyu Land explores the central role of land in identity, inheritance and resistance, while revealing how the structures created under colonial rule continue to shape lives in Kenya today.”

Directors Andrew H. Brown and Bea Wangondu speak at a reception at the Sundance Film Festival on January 25, 2026 in Park City, Utah. Matthew Carey

In a statement, filmmakers Andrew H. Brown and Bea Wangondu said, “Kikuyu Land is deeply personal for both of us. We wanted to center the voices of people living with the consequences of colonial land policies and create space for these stories to be told on their own terms. The film is ultimately about survival, generational inheritance and the question of what accountability looks like when the past refuses to stay buried. We hope it sparks conversations about who owns the land, who owns its stories, and what it means to reclaim both.”

Kikuyu Land is produced by Oscar nominee Moses Bwayo, Bea Wangondu, Andrew H. Brown, Mike Morrisroe for Trifilm Studios and Joseph Njenga. Executive producers include Tracy Rector, Amanda Brown, Mia Vyzis, and Barbara Terzieff. Cinematography is by Andrew H. Brown; Brown also edited the film. The original score is by Nyokabi Kariũki and Keir Vine.

“From the very start, our goal was to center the people whose stories we were telling and to highlight their experiences with honesty and empathy,” Wangondu commented in an interview. “We also had to work quietly. The issues at the core of this film are politically charged, and sharing too much about the project within Kenya could have put community members at risk or drawn unwanted attention before it was safe. So, we kept the circle small, focusing on relationships built on trust and mutual understanding.”

Brown noted, “We did our best throughout the shoot to balance visual beauty with ethical storytelling. The film needed to feel cinematic and immersive without compromising the people whose lives we were documenting. Every shot was chosen to represent the community, the land, and their stories, highlighting the richness and resilience of daily life without sensationalizing it.”

title: Prime Video’s ‘Rose Hill’ Adds 5 To Cast
summary: Prime Video’s Rose Hill series has added 5 to its cast, including Siobhan McGroarty, Sophia Reid-Gantzert, West Mulholland, Gigi Zumbado, and Curtis Hamilton. Rose Hill, based on the best-selling book series from Elsie Silver, follows best friends and neighbors West Belmont (Jake Weary), a rancher with commitment issues, and brooding record label owner Ford Grant […]
content:
Prime Video‘s Rose Hill series has added 5 to its cast, including Siobhan McGroarty, Sophia Reid-Gantzert, West Mulholland, Gigi Zumbado, and Curtis Hamilton.

Rose Hill, based on the best-selling book series from Elsie Silver, follows best friends and neighbors West Belmont (Jake Weary), a rancher with commitment issues, and brooding record label owner Ford Grant (Sean O’Pry), aka Forbes’ “World’s Hottest Billionaire,” who’s long carried a torch for West’s sister, Rose (Hannah Galway). And when country-pop star Skylar Stone (Sadie Dickerson) breezes into their rugged mountain town, the heat gets turned way up in this romantic family drama.

In series regular roles, McGroarty will play Cora, Reid-Gantzert will play Emmy Belmont, and Mulholland will play Oliver Belmont. In recurring guest roles, Zumbado will play Tabitha and Hamilton as Bash Rousseau.

Watch on Deadline

Heidi Cole McAdams serves as writer, showrunner, and executive producer. Marc Webb will direct the pilot and second episode and executive produce. Silver also serves as executive producer alongside Wyck Godfrey, Marty Bowen, and James Seidman for Temple Hill. Temple Hill’s Annika Patton will also serve as a co-executive producer.

McGroarty has made guest appearances in Law & Order and VHS: Kidprint. She is repped by Rebel Creative Group and Vainshtein Law.

Reid-Gantzert most recently recurred in Netflix’s Free Bert, with additional TV credits in Hulu’s Death and Other Details, as well as two additional Netflix titles: Scaredy Cats and The Babysitters Club. In film, she was the lead in Popular Theory. She is repped by Innovative Artists, Skrzyniarz & Mallean, and Trademark Talent.

Mulholland recurred on TNT’s Animal Kingdom and made guest appearances on FX’s Legion, Hulu’s Little Fires Everywhere, and ABC’s Fresh Off the Boat. His big-screen credits include Steven Soderbergh’s Presence, Angelo Pizzo’s Bloomington, and Xavier Tera’s The Color of Sun. He is repped by Seven Summits Management, Osbrink Agency, and Jackoway Austen Tyerman.

Zumbado most recently starred in the CBS comedy DMV, with additional TV credits on Netflix’s The Lincoln Lawyer, Apple’s She’s Fine, Starz’s Hightown, and a series regular on Epix’s Bridge and Tunnel. She is repped by Innovative, Artists First, and GGSSC.

Hamilton made his lead debut in the Sony and Lifetime feature biopic Surviving Compton, then went on to be a series regular on OWN Network’s The Kings of Napa, and recurred on the final season of Insecure on HBO. He is repped by Realm Talent and Luber Roklin.

title: Heather McMahan Sets Hulu Launch For Third Stand-Up Special ‘By A Thread’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Comedian Heather McMahan has announced that her third special, By a Thread, will premiere on Hulu on October 16. In the new hour, filmed across two sold-out nights at The Bijou Theatre in Knoxville, TN, the Southern comic leaves no stone unturned, from being canceled by golf and the MAGA-sphere attempting to claim her […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Comedian Heather McMahan has announced that her third special, By a Thread, will premiere on Hulu on October 16.

In the new hour, filmed across two sold-out nights at The Bijou Theatre in Knoxville, TN, the Southern comic leaves no stone unturned, from being canceled by golf and the MAGA-sphere attempting to claim her as one of their own, to husband Jeff’s kidney stones and getting her neck done — twice.

McMahan unveils the hour following her recent national tour, The Bamboozled Tour. She wrote, performed and self-produced it via her Absolutely Not Productions. The special is directed by Jen Zaborowski and exec produced by Maggie Haskins and Christina Tompkins alongside McMahan and Zaborowski.

Born and raised in Atlanta, McMahan is known for material on relationships, family, aging, and the everyday chaos of trying to hold it all together. The rare comic to release each of her first three specials to premium streamers, her last hour, Breadwinner, premiered on Hulu in October 2024. Prior to that, she put out the Netflix special Son I Never Had, which debuted at #4 in October 2023 and held a top-10 position for seven days.

Watch on Deadline

Outside of stand-up, McMahan has been seen on Is It Cake? and The Great American Baking Show — Celeb Edition as well as on Celebrity Jeopardy, winning her first-round match-up vs. Cynthia Nixon & Cedric the Entertainer. She’s co-hosted E!’s Live from the Red Carpet for the Emmys, Grammys and Oscars, is a frequent guest and co-host on the fourth hour of The Today Show, alongside Jenna Bush Hager, and starred opposite Nina Dobrev and Jimmy O. Yang in Netflix’s Christmas movie, Love Hard.

Next May, McMahan is set to take off on her sophomore comedy cruise, Absolutely Knot!, taking place on the Norwegian Jewel. The comedian is repped by UTA, Artists First, and Ziffren Brittenham.

title: Sony TV Chief Keith Le Goy on Why PlayStation 5 FAST Channels Are Set Up for Success: 40-50 Million People ‘Incredibly Engaged With That Platform’
summary: Sony struck synergy gold last month with the introduction of “Live TV on PS5,” an offering of more than 100 free ad-supported video channels available via the PlayStation 5 video game console. Backed by Sony Pictures Television, the venture is a chance to get the IP available to Sony TV (and the ads that can […]
content:
Sony struck synergy gold last month with the introduction of “Live TV on PS5,” an offering of more than 100 free ad-supported video channels available via the PlayStation 5 video game console.

Backed by Sony Pictures Television, the venture is a chance to get the IP available to Sony TV (and the ads that can be tied to it) in front of a massive audience that is usually spending their time on gaming consoles, well, gaming.

“The intent is that you have 40-50 million people on PlayStation 5 who are incredibly engaged with that platform, who are spending hours and hours and hours on their favorite games, but who also love to watch entertainment,” chairman Keith Le Goy said Thursday during a panel conversation with Variety co-editor-in-chief Cynthia Littleton at the Variety Entertainment & Technology Summit presented by EY. “And therefore, if you can do two things, one is to curate the entertainment offering in a way that is pertinent to them, but also make it a very seamless transition from their gaming engagement to their entertainment engagement, then you have a real chance to engage an audience which traditionally has been a hard-to-reach audience for linear channels, a very hard-to-reach audience and a very attractive audience for advertisers.”

Popular on Variety

Goy added: “So if we can give that audience something that they’re going to like in an environment that they are comfortable with, give our channel partners an audience that they are going to be going after and give their advertisers an audience that’s valuable for them. That is one plus one equaling a lot more than two.”

The PlayStation 5 FAST channel offering launched last month in the U.S. and Goy says the intention is to roll it out across “other countries in the coming months.” Goy sees the option as one unique to Sony, which distinguishes itself from many other players in Hollywood by having film, TV, music and gaming divisions all under one roof.

“In many ways, people talk about the incursion of the tech companies into Hollywood, we were the first and I think we’ve learned a lot along the way,” You mentioned the relationship with PlayStation. “That’s the other thing that Sony has, that frankly a lot of other companies would love to have, is a gaming business and the level of engagement with gamers and gaming fans. That is what PlayStation has.”

Goy says another area where Sony has “an unfair advantage, a particular right to win” is the anime industry through Crunchyroll and Aniplex.

“Obviously, Crunchyroll has been an incredibly successful venture for us and has really allowed us to create this kind of anime ecosystem with Aniplex and Crunchyroll where we are able to super serve fans in a way that very few other companies, in fact, really no other company could do,” Goy says.

title: Fan Bingbing, Pedro Pascal, John Malkovich, Javier Bardem Films Lead Tokyo Festival’s Gala Selection
summary: The Tokyo International Film Festival has named its 15-title Gala selection, headlined by Fan Bingbing in Wayne Wang’s “Diary of a Mad Old Man,” Pedro Pascal in Tony Gilroy’s “Behemoth!,” John Malkovich in Martin McDonagh’s “Wild Horse Nine” and Javier Bardem in Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s “The Beloved.” Wang’s film adapts Tanizaki Junichiro’s novel of the same […]
content:
The Tokyo International Film Festival has named its 15-title Gala selection, headlined by Fan Bingbing in Wayne Wang’s “Diary of a Mad Old Man,” Pedro Pascal in Tony Gilroy’s “Behemoth!,” John Malkovich in Martin McDonagh’s “Wild Horse Nine” and Javier Bardem in Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s “The Beloved.”

Wang’s film adapts Tanizaki Junichiro’s novel of the same name, relocating the story to present-day Tokyo, with Fan starring opposite Lily Franky and Kudoh Youki. Gilroy’s “Behemoth!” casts Pascal as a cellist alongside Olivia Wilde and Eva Victor.

McDonagh’s “Wild Horse Nine,” also starring Sam Rockwell and Steve Buscemi, follows two CIA agents sent to Easter Island; Malkovich won the Venice Film Festival’s best actor award for the role. Bardem stars opposite Victoria Luengo in “The Beloved,” about an estranged father and daughter confronting old wounds during a new film project.

Popular on Variety

Cristian Mungiu’s “Fjord,” winner of the Palme d’Or at the Cannes Film Festival, stars Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve as members of a family relocating from Romania to Norway. Sode Yukiko’s “All the Lovers in the Night,” adapted from Kawakami Mieko’s novel, played in Un Certain Regard at Cannes ahead of its Tokyo bow.

The festival’s opening film is “Sukiyaki,” with “Godzilla Minus Zero” screening as the centerpiece selection and “Colony” as the closing film.

TIFF also unveiled a 12-title Animation Section, which includes three Japanese titles selected under the theme “Women Directors: Diverse Visions”: Nagaoka Chika’s “Detective Conan: The Fist of Blue Sapphire,” Watanabe Kotono’s “Gold Kingdom and Water Kingdom” and Yoshimura Ai’s “The Rose of Versailles.”

The 39th Tokyo International Film Festival runs Oct. 26-Nov. 4, hosted by Unijapan. Market TIFFCOM runs alongside it from Oct. 28-30.

FULL GALA SELECTION

“All the Lovers in the Night” (Japan) – Directed by Sode Yukiko. Starring Kishii Yukino, Asano Tadanobu, Morita Misato.

“Arrested Memory” (Taiwan/Japan) – Directed by SABU. Starring Ethan Juan, Hsieh Ying Xuan, Tsutsumi Shinichi.

“Behemoth!” (U.S.) – Directed by Tony Gilroy. Starring Pedro Pascal, Olivia Wilde, Eva Victor.

“The Beloved” (Spain) – Directed by Rodrigo Sorogoyen. Starring Javier Bardem, Victoria Luengo, Marina Foïs.

“A Bouquet of Light for You” (working title, Japan) – Directed by Ando Hiroshi. Starring Hara Nanoka, Sakuma Ryuto, Mashima Hidekazu.

“Bye Bye Love: Detective Is in the Bar” (Japan) – Directed by Shiraishi Kazuya. Starring Oizumi Yo, Matsuda Ryuhei, Suzuki Kyoka.

“Diary of a Mad Old Man” (U.S.) – Directed by Wayne Wang. Starring Lily Franky, Fan Bingbing, Kudoh Youki.

Displacement Film Fund screenings (U.K./Syria/Ukraine/Turkey/Iran/Germany/Somalia/Austria) – Directed by Hasan Kattan, Maryna Er Gorbach, Mohammad Rasoulof, Shahrbanoo Sadat and Mo Harawe.

“Fjord” (Romania/France/Norway/Sweden/Denmark/Finland) – Directed by Cristian Mungiu. Starring Sebastian Stan, Renate Reinsve.

“Sunshine Women’s Choir” (Taiwan) – Directed by Gavin Lin. Starring Ivy Chen, Judy Ongg, Sun Shumei.

“Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma” (U.S./Canada) – Directed by Jane Schoenbrun. Starring Hannah Einbinder, Gillian Anderson.

“The Tiger and Her Wings the Movie” (Japan) – Directed by Nagikawa Yoshiro. Starring Ito Sairi, Okada Masaki, Matsumoto Koshiro.

“Verity” (U.S.) – Directed by Michael Showalter. Starring Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson, Josh Hartnett.

“Wild Horse Nine” (U.K./U.S./Chile) – Directed by Martin McDonagh. Starring John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell, Steve Buscemi.

“Your Story – Kimi No Hanashi” (Japan) – Directed by Nakagawa Ryutaro. Starring Kitamura Takumi, Deguchi Natsuki.

FULL ANIMATION SECTION

“Amadeo and the Hypothetical New World” (Brazil) – Directed by Brenda Lígia and Edu Felistoque. Starring Sérgio Menezes, Naruna Costa, Edmilson Filho.

“Cherry and Virgin” (Japan) – Directed by Kawajiri Masanao. Starring Okado Takashi, Kiyose Yaeko.

“Forgotten Island” (U.S.) – Directed by Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado. Starring the voices of H.E.R., Liza Soberano, Dave Franco.

“Ghost – End of Night” (Japan) – Directed by Natsume Shingo. Starring the voices of Hotta Mayu, Takahashi Issey.

“Grotesqqque” (Japan) – Directed by Nishigori Atsushi. Starring the voices of Ichinose Kana, Minami Sara, Inoue Nagi, Hoshino Gen.

“Iron Boy” (France) – Directed by Louis Clichy. Starring Gary Clichy, Rod Paradot, Dimitri Colas.

“Son of a Bitch” (Brazil) – Directed by Érica Maradona, Otto Guerra, Tania Anaya and Sávio Leite. Starring Gabriel Martins, Matheus Nachtergaele, Zora Santos.

“Walking with Animators” (France) – Directed by Alexandre Poncet and Gilles Penso. Starring Lucie Arnissolle, Will Becher, Doug Chiang.

“We Are Aliens” (Japan) – Directed by Kadowaki Kohei. Starring Bando Ryota, Okayama Amane.

“Detective Conan: The Fist of Blue Sapphire” (Japan) – Directed by Nagaoka Chika. Starring Takayama Minami, Yamazaki Wakana, Yamaguchi Kappei.

“Gold Kingdom and Water Kingdom” (Japan) – Directed by Watanabe Kotono. Starring Kaku Kento, Hamabe Minami.
