title: Dr. Orna Guralnik Gives Ciara Miller, Dylan Efron and Carl Schmidt a ‘Couples Therapy’ Session in New Samsung Galaxy Spot
summary: Samsung is taking its latest Galaxy campaign to therapy. The tech giant has tapped “Couples Therapy” star Dr. Orna Guralnik to lead “Switchers,” a new campaign that centers a counseling session on the anxieties around ditching a longtime smartphone. The branded spots pair Guralnik with pairs of contrived couples such as “Summer House” star Ciara […]
content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

Samsung is taking its latest Galaxy campaign to therapy.

The tech giant has tapped “Couples Therapy” star Dr. Orna Guralnik to lead “Switchers,” a new campaign that centers a counseling session on the anxieties around ditching a longtime smartphone.

The branded spots pair Guralnik with pairs of contrived couples such as “Summer House” star Ciara Miller and Dylan Efron, reality TV personalities Carl Schmidt and Aniya Harvey and former NFL players Nick Foles and Clay Matthews, who work through tech-centered issues such as “brand loyalty,” “group-chat fears” and the “perceived hassle of transferring data between devices.”

“My profession is all about change,” Guralnik, a clinical psychologist who stars in Showtime’s “Couples Therapy,” tells Variety. “People come to analysis when they’ve reached a certain point where they’re just repeating the same old patterns and having a hard time letting go or changing.”

“The fact that Samsung decided to go toward this kind of psychological, even psychoanalytic language — even using language like, ‘What’s your defense?’ — it just tickled me a lot,” Guralnik continues. “What a great way to bring psychoanalytic and psychological language into mass culture, which is really what I’m doing with the show anyhow.”

The commercial is the latest example of Samsung leaning on talent to market its Galaxy lineup. Earlier this year, the company added singer and rapper Audrey Nuna, model and influencer Haley Baylee and 11 other creators across music, gaming, fashion and culture to its #TeamGalaxy roster around the Galaxy S26 launch. Samsung also enlisting K-pop talent including Eric Nam for its Galaxy Experience in February.

Samsung’s latest Galaxy Z lineup now spans three foldable models: the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Z Fold8 and Z Flip8. The company says 30% of Galaxy Z Flip8 buyers since launch have switched from a competing smartphone brand, while the Fold8 and Fold8 Ultra are also bringing in a higher proportion of competitive switchers than the previous Fold7 generation.

That makes convincing longtime iPhone and other smartphone users to defect a central part of Samsung’s sales pitch. The campaign highlights Smart Switch, which transfers contacts, photos, videos, messages, apps and settings from iOS or Android devices, alongside cross-platform RCS messaging and Samsung’s broader suite of Galaxy AI features.

Guralnik even tested that proposition closer to home with her teenage son, whom she describes as highly resistant to changing phones. “He was constantly worried about how easy it would be to switch,” she says. “Would he lose all his contacts? Would he lose all his chains of messages with his friends? His photos? All of that.”

Once he made the jump, she says, his concerns largely mirrored the barriers Samsung had built the campaign around.

“They really dug deep into people’s anxieties and addressed them,” Guralnik says. “So, touché to Samsung.”

title: Greta Gerwig Says ‘Narnia’ Is Inspired by David Bowie, Confirms Meryl Streep Is Voicing Aslan: ‘I Wanted Someone Profound but Not Pretentious’
summary: Greta Gerwig is reuniting with her “Little Women” star Meryl Streep on “Narnia,” the director’s adaptation of the C.S. Lewis fantasy series. Streep is voicing Aslan, the mythical lion who creates the mystical world of Narnia. “I wanted someone who was profound but not pretentious, who had gravitas but not morose self-seriousness. Someone who could […]
content:
Greta Gerwig is reuniting with her “Little Women” star Meryl Streep on “Narnia,” the director’s adaptation of the C.S. Lewis fantasy series. Streep is voicing Aslan, the mythical lion who creates the mystical world of Narnia.

“I wanted someone who was profound but not pretentious, who had gravitas but not morose self-seriousness. Someone who could communicate depth and pathos as well as joy and delight,” Gerwig told Empire in a cover story about the upcoming film. “I wanted someone who was older than 70, so there was a wisdom of experience, but who also had the capacity of fresh wonder, like a child. And also to be one of the greatest actors to ever do it. That list is not a long one.”

David Bowie was a source of inspiration, both for the look of Aslan (who has multicolored eyes and a red-striped face in this version) as well as the essence of the movie, according to Gerwig. She described wanting the movie to be “big and transporting” and feel like a “rock opera.”

Popular on Variety

“David Bowie saved my life. Paul McCartney saved my life. David Gilmour saved my life. Pete Townshend saved my life. Jimmy Page, Robert Plant,” Gerwig told Empire. “When I heard their music, I had this deep sense of [thinking], ‘You’re gonna be OK.’”

As it relates to the fantasy adventure, she says, “Narnia is literally a world made out of music. It is a world sung to life by Aslan, and rock ’n’ roll to me felt like a world made out of music.”

“The Magician’s Nephew” is Gerwig’s much-anticipated follow-up to “Barbie,” her Oscar-winning box office sensation starring Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling. “The Magician’s Nephew” serves as a prequel to “The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe” and follows two children, Digory and Polly, who are the first to discover the “Wood between the Worlds,” aka Narnia, after their uncle (Daniel Craig) gives them a magical ring. David McKenna, Beatrice Campbell, Emma Mackey, Carey Mulligan and Ciarán Hinds round out the cast.

Previously slated for Thanksgiving 2026, “Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew” will open in theaters on Feb. 12, 2027, before landing on Netflix on April 2.

title: ‘The Simpsons’ Casting Director Scott Muller to Recruit Voices for Animated Film ‘The Most Serious Fart’
summary: “The Simpsons” casting director Scott Muller will oversee voice casting for “The Most Serious Fart,” Utopai’s animated feature based on Mike Bender’s bestselling children’s book, which wafts into theaters in 2027. “The Most Serious Fart” follows Siegfried, an uptight fart who is ashamed of who he is and determined to change farts into something respectable. […]
content:
“The Simpsons” casting director Scott Muller will oversee voice casting for “The Most Serious Fart,” Utopai‘s animated feature based on Mike Bender’s bestselling children’s book, which wafts into theaters in 2027.

“The Most Serious Fart” follows Siegfried, an uptight fart who is ashamed of who he is and determined to change farts into something respectable. Siegfried sets out on a journey that ultimately teaches him to accept himself, find friendship and discover fun along the way.

“Voice casting will define how audiences first connect with Siegfried and the world around him,” Muller said in a statement. “Mike has created characters that invite bold comedy but also have a genuine emotional point of view. I am excited to find the voices that can make the humor land while giving the story the warmth and humanity at its center.”

Popular on Variety

Muller has also worked as the casting director on “Futurama,” “King of the Hill” and the animated “Napoleon Dynamite” series. He is joined by “Coyote vs. Acme” story artist Andy Brooks as key story artist, Bender as writer, director and producer. Russell Hollander will also produce.

Human animators and illustrators will lead the creative process and originate the film’s artwork. AI will be used selectively as a production tool to support iteration under their direction, Utopai said in a statement.

“From the beginning, our goal has been to make a film that feels as distinctive as the book,” Bender said. “Scott understands how much performance shapes an animated world. Andy brings a remarkable ability to tell stories through character, expression and movement. Together with the rest of our creative team, they will help make Siegfried’s world feel completely original while keeping its heart intact.”

title: ‘The Kardashians’ Sets Season 8 Release Date; Unveils Trailer Which Reveals Kim In A Hospital Bed & More
summary: We’re getting the first extended look at Season 8 of The Kardashians ahead of its fall return. The new season premieres Thursday, October 8 on Hulu, Hulu+ for bundle subscribers in the U.S. and Disney+ internationally. The official trailer opens with a question posed to Kris. “How are your daughters getting along this season?”, to […]
content:
We’re getting the first extended look at Season 8 of The Kardashians ahead of its fall return. The new season premieres Thursday, October 8 on Hulu, Hulu+ for bundle subscribers in the U.S. and Disney+ internationally.

The official trailer opens with a question posed to Kris. “How are your daughters getting along this season?”, to which a hesitant Kris replies “Well….it’s been a week.”

And what a week it was.

Of course, the conversation turns to dating. “Have you dated anyone privately?”, Kim is asked. “Let me just say this. I can’t control myself.” We also see Khloe in a playful exchange with Scott Dissick, asking if they’re having a baby together.

Footage later jumps to Kim in a hospital bed as she reveals she has esophagitis.

Watch on Deadline

Per the official description, a new chapter begins this season for the Kardashian-Jenners. “This season is all about love, reinvention, and what comes next. Kris, Kourtney, Kim, Khloé, Kendall, and Kylie balance empire-building with something far more personal, from unexpected sparks and new relationships, to healing old wounds and embracing independence. As the family steps into this new era, they’ll discover that love, whether it’s self-love, family, or something new, might be the most powerful journey of all.”

Cast includes Kris Jenner, Kourtney Kardashian Barker, Kim Kardashian, Khloé Kardashian, Kendall Jenner, and Kylie Jenner.

Fulwell Entertainment partner Ben Winston executive produces alongside Danielle King, Emma Conway, Elizabeth Jones, and Erin Foye. Kris Jenner, Kourtney Kardashian Barker, Kim Kardashian, Khloé Kardashian, Kendall Jenner and Kylie Jenner also serve as executive producers.

title: ‘The JLO Show: Live in Las Vegas’ Teaser: Jennifer Lopez’s Vegas Residency Concert Film Debuting Thanksgiving On CBS, Paramount+
summary: Jennifer Lopez is spending this Thanksgiving in fans’ living rooms, with the release of her Las Vegas residency concert film. On Thursday, CBS and Paramount+ released the teaser for The JLO Show: Live in Las Vegas, premiering Thursday, Nov. 26 at 8pm ET/PT with an extended version exclusively available on the streaming platform, featuring the […]
content:
Jennifer Lopez is spending this Thanksgiving in fans’ living rooms, with the release of her Las Vegas residency concert film.

On Thursday, CBS and Paramount+ released the teaser for The JLO Show: Live in Las Vegas, premiering Thursday, Nov. 26 at 8pm ET/PT with an extended version exclusively available on the streaming platform, featuring the final performance 2x Grammy nominee’s sold-out, 12-show residency that opened earlier this year at The Colosseum at Caesars Palace.

Tracing her journey from the Bronx to global icon, Lopez blends her most iconic hits with personal storytelling, featuring the artists and songs that influenced her, and backed by a full orchestra, vocal ensemble and 16 dancers.

Told in four acts, “Act I: I’ll See You in My Dreams”, “Act II: Tales from Manhattan”, “Act III: Kiss Kiss, Kill Kill” and “Act IV: Shall We Dance,” The JLO Show celebrates Lopez’s more than 20 years of music, with new renditions of “Waiting for Tonight”, “Jenny from the Block”, “Love Don’t Cost a Thing”, “Get Right”, “On the Floor” and “Let’s Get Loud”.

Watch on Deadline

The Thanksgiving premiere date is a nod to Lopez’s family tradition of watching movie musicals with family over the holiday.

title: Meghann Fahy Set For Limited Series ‘Smokeshow’ From SK Global, David E. Kelley
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Meghann Fahy, the two-time Emmy-nominated star of Sirens and The White Lotus, has inked a deal to star in Smokeshow, a new limited series based on the upcoming novel by Catriona Stewart, which has landed with SK Global and David E. Kelley Productions following a highly competitive bidding war. The package is set to […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Meghann Fahy, the two-time Emmy-nominated star of Sirens and The White Lotus, has inked a deal to star in Smokeshow, a new limited series based on the upcoming novel by Catriona Stewart, which has landed with SK Global and David E. Kelley Productions following a highly competitive bidding war.

The package is set to hit the market in the coming weeks, with a select round of pitches being scheduled with buyers.

Part thriller, part dark romantic comedy, Smokeshow centers on a covert operative, Rory (Fahy), who becomes entangled with her target, the charming and devastatingly earnest Nolan. Rory must then choose between the life she’s known and the chance to break free.

The novel marks the first stateside release from Stewart, who as a communications strategist based in San Francisco, has spent over a decade advising some of the most prominent figures in California politics.

Watch on Deadline

Sweetpea‘s Kirstie Swain is adapting from Stewart’s novel, which will be published by Random House next summer.

Fahy is producing alongside Kelley, Matthew Tinker and Shelby Leshine for David E. Kelley Productions. SK Global’s Head of Television, Chloe Dan, and Trish Esselen are overseeing for the studio.

Smokeshow marks the second limited series starring Fahy that we’ve scooped in recent months, following The Trial of Louise Woodward at HBO. Her upcoming slate includes Peacock series The Good Daughter, where she stars opposite Rose Byrne and Amazon MGM’s rom-com You Deserve Each Other, which she leads with Penn Badgley. She is repped by WME, Anonymous Content, and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern.

Swain is the BAFTA nominee who created, writes and exec produces Sweetpea, the dark comedy based on CJ Skuse’s novel, which is set to air its second season with Sky and Starz in early 2027. She also wrote the dramas Pure, Run and Clique, and is repped by UTA and Lark.

SK Global’s recent projects include The Season, Thai Cave Rescue, Delhi Crime, and the documentary Catching Fire: The Story of Anita Pallenberg.

Hit-makerDavid E. Kelley Productions is coming off of Margo’s Got Money Troubles, the Elle Fanning-led young motherhood dramedy that recently scored eight Emmy nominations, including Outstanding Comedy Series, with three wins. Other new series to come include Myron Bolitar for Netflix and Not a Sound, starring Ellen Pompeo, for Hulu. Kelley is repped by CAA and Gendler, Kelly and Cunningham.

Author Stewart is repped by CAA.

title: ‘The Mafia Nanny’ Series Based On Webtoon Action Romance In Works At Hulu; Charlize Theron To EP
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Hulu is developing The Mafia Nanny, a drama series based on Webtoon’s popular action romance title. It comes from executive producer Charlize Theron and 20th Television. This is believed to be the first English-language live-action series adaptation of Webtoon IP, which has been popular source material in Korean and Japanese television. (Webtoon and sibling […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Hulu is developing The Mafia Nanny, a drama series based on Webtoon‘s popular action romance title. It comes from executive producer Charlize Theron and 20th Television.

This is believed to be the first English-language live-action series adaptation of Webtoon IP, which has been popular source material in Korean and Japanese television. (Webtoon and sibling Wattpad are owned by South Korea’s tech giant Naver.) One such adaptation, K-Drama The Remarried Empress, premieres on Hulu Nov. 4.

Written for TV by Max Gill, The Mafia Nanny centers on Davina who serves as an elite nanny to high-net-worth families. Her job should be straightforward: protect the charge, obey the client, and avoid becoming emotionally attached. But when Davina receives her first mission in the form of young Mikey Angelini, his imposing – and alluring – father threatens to drag her back into the world of organized crime she had tried to leave behind.

Gill executive produces with Theron, Beth Kono, AJ Dix and Matt Maher for Secret Menu, David Madden and Sera Tabb for Webtoon Productions and Dawn Olmstead for Steady Collective.

Watch on Deadline

Created by Violet Matter and illustrated by sh00, Roususu and Drawniels, The Mafia Nanny webcomic has amassed 420 million global views. Theron’s Secret Menu optioned the property while Olmstead was running it; she has since launched her own company.

The Mafia Nanny brings Madden back into the 20th Television fold. Years ago, he was president of Fox Television Studios which was subsequently folded into Fox21 and ultimately into 20th TV.

Gill is developing shows with Netflix, Fifth Season, Chernin, and A24 and will soon be joining the writers room for Lena Dunham’s new Netflix series Covers. He is repped by WME, Entertainment 360, and Ziffren Brittenham.

David Madden, Dawn Olmsted and Sera Tabb Michael Smiy/Joshua De La Garza/Michael Smiy

On the TV side, Secret Menu, whose film credits include Apex, Atomic Blonde, The Old Guard franchise and Bombshell, has upcoming projects for HBO, Hulu, Netflix and AMC. The company also produced documentaries Last Call for HBO and Into the Fire for Netflix, as well as the competition series Hyperdrive for Netflix.

Olmstead, executive producer of Girlfriends’ Guide to Divorce and the original Prison Break series, is currently shooting the Prison Break reboot for Hulu and is producing Black List film Mommy’s Home, for Lionsgate. She has projects set up at Hulu, FX, HBO, Netflix, and Peacock.

Webtoon Productions’ recent and upcoming projects include Prime Video’s Lore Olympus, the Sidelined trilogy and Kissing is the Easy Part with Tubi; Wattpad adaptation Chasing Red, Prime Video’s Love Me Love Me and upcoming Love Me Love Me 2, among others. Recent and upcoming webcomic-based titles include Bloodhounds, My Daughter is a Zombie, Chicken Nugget and The Remarried Empress for Disney+/Hulu.

With the film grossing more than $350 million worldwide, the duo recently completed the script for a sequel. A native Uruguayan, Sayagues […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Brillstein has signed writer-director Rodo Sayagues for management in all areas.

Sayagues most recently co-wrote Alien: Romulus alongside frequent collaborator Fede Álvarez for 20th Century Studios and Ridley Scott’s Scott Free Productions. With the film grossing more than $350 million worldwide, the duo recently completed the script for a sequel.

A native Uruguayan, Sayagues first gained recognition through his short films before co-writing Álvarez’s 2012 take on Evil Dead. He followed that up by writing and producing Álvarez’s Sony horror film Don’t Breathe, which was both a critical and commercial success at a worldwide gross of $158 million.

Sayagues made his directorial debut with Don’t Breathe 2, which he also wrote for Sony Pictures. He then produced and wrote the story for Netflix’s Texas Chainsaw Massacre, continuing his work across some of horror’s most iconic franchises, and is currently writing a film for Andy Muschietti and Warner Bros., while developing his next directorial feature to be produced by Michael Schaefer and Álvarez.

Watch on Deadline

Sayagues continues to be represented by WME and attorney Karl Austen.

title: ‘Evil Genius’ Review: Courteney Cox Fashions the Pizza Bomber Case Into a Broad, Shrilly Played Farce
summary: If you were glued to “Evil Genius,” Netflix’s 2018 documentary series about the bizarre “pizza bomber” killing of 2003, but wished its true-crime study rang just a little less true, then Courteney Cox’s new film of the same title has you covered. Dramatizing that sad, sordid story of weaponized criminal incompetence into a heightened comedy […]
content:
If you were glued to “Evil Genius,” Netflix’s 2018 documentary series about the bizarre “pizza bomber” killing of 2003, but wished its true-crime study rang just a little less true, then Courteney Cox’s new film of the same title has you covered. Dramatizing that sad, sordid story of weaponized criminal incompetence into a heightened comedy of errors, the film has little to reveal that we don’t already know, so settles for raking over the stranger-than-fiction facts of the case with lurid, mocking glee. Viewers’ mileage will largely depend on their patience for Patricia Arquette’s unmodulated, to-the-rafters performance as the scheme’s criminal not-so-mastermind Marjorie Diehl-Armstrong, which is scarcely tempered by David Harbour’s more quietly shambling work as her co-conspirator and sometime lover Bill Rothstein.

Assembled with little formal style or finesse by Cox — in her first feature-length directorial effort since 2014’s Seann William Scott comedy “Just Before I Go” — this very broad affair likely has a built-in audience of rubberneckers, given the level of public fascination that this case has maintained in the U.S. for over 20 years. But it’s doubtful that many would venture out to a theater to see a rehash of a story they they previously binged on from the comfort of their couch. This iteration of “Evil Genius,” like its nonfiction predecessor, would make most sense as streaming fodder, with potential Emmy catnip in Arquette’s offputting but undeniably attention-grabbing characterization. As a gala Toronto premiere, however, the film felt a little small for the room.

Popular on Variety

The core details of the case are presented much as they were in the doc series and copious headlines before it. On August 28, 2003, middle-aged pizza deliverer Brian Wells (played by actor-filmmaker Tom McCarthy as a hopeless patsy) robbed a branch of PNC Bank outside Erie, Pennsylvania, claiming to be a hostage, with an explosive device collared to his neck that he said would be detonated if his demands were not met. Demanding $250,000 but making off with a four-figure sum, he was apprehended shortly afterwards by police, whereupon the bomb did indeed go off, killing him, and cuing a tortuous, years-long FBI investigation.

Structurally, at least, this calamity serves as the climax of the frenetically pinballing script by Courtenay Miles (a writer on Netflix’s hit crime drama “Mindhunter”), but it’s also nearly incidental to all the other narrative chaos at play, beginning with an entirely different murder at the outset of proceedings — as Rothstein calls the police to report the dead body of Diehl-Armstrong’s boyfriend in her freezer. Where the series worked backwards from the bomb to uncover the botched grand plan behind it, the film loopily joins the dots from an apparent crime of passion to a far more famous crime of greed.

There’s an awful lot of incident here to cram into 97 minutes — the series had more than twice as much time to unfold this saga, and the difference is felt — but Cox’s film distinguishes itself with a greater focus on the toxic, on-off amour fou between Diehl-Armstrong, presented here as an embittered harridan convinced the world owes her a break, and Rothstein, the hapless milquetoast in her thrall. Flashbacks to the characters’ youth (with Arquette’s own daughter Harlow Jane playing her younger self) identify Diehl-Rothstein as an intelligent, ingenuous young woman who just needs a little help to make something of herself. But neither the script nor Arquette’s showy but curdled, stridently one-note performance of terminal misanthropy persuasively draw a line between past and present, and it’s increasingly hard to feel for a character missing this much connective tissue.

Not that feeling is really the point of “Evil Genius,” which mostly dwells on the shouty, combative dysfunction of the relationship between the two principals, and punches down on their plain incapability as criminals: The title is strictly, snidely ironic, as “Evil Genius” flags and foreshadows their every miscalculation with a knowing, get-a-load-of-this smirk. Their accomplices — played by Garret Dillahunt and Danielle Macdonald, among others — are mostly figures of fun, granted limited personality and motivation, as the film increasingly stages their doomed venture as ragged farce.

Tonally, it all feels a bit over-egged: The absurdities of the case would, if anything, register even more startlingly in a more humane, character-oriented study of how it played out. But “Evil Genius” insists on casting a pretty ugly story in the ugliest possible light — quite literally so in the case of Eigil Bryld’s intentionally harsh, roughly framed lensing. The film’s pitiless gray images compete with the abrasive sound design (frequently submerging the dialogue in loud, blunt needle drops that run the rock gamut from Blue Oyster Cult to Radiohead) for maximum unloveliness in a story that, yes, offers precious little scope for grace or beauty. But a little empathy wouldn’t go amiss.

title: Rei Ami on Her New Pop Girl Era, and How Feeling Confident Inspired Her New Single ‘2 Loud’: ‘It’s a Clapback’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Rei Ami is loving life, and she’s also learned to love herself. But it wasn’t an easy journey getting to this stage. Before breaking out as one-third of Huntr/x in Netflix’s smash “KPop Demon Hunters,” Ami largely released rap songs like “Snow Cone” and “Body Bag,” which she says came from a place of anger […]
content:
Rei Ami is loving life, and she’s also learned to love herself. But it wasn’t an easy journey getting to this stage.

Before breaking out as one-third of Huntr/x in Netflix’s smash “KPop Demon Hunters,” Ami largely released rap songs like “Snow Cone” and “Body Bag,” which she says came from a place of anger and resentment. But following the release of “Hunters,” which won her both an Oscar and a Grammy, the 31-year-old found a new path forward.

“I think the ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ campaign healed something in me,” Ami tells Variety. “It shifted and changed a lot for me.” After the film introduced the singer-songwriter to a new generation of fans and propelled her to another stratosphere of stardom, it also unlocked a new era of confidence and self-acceptance, something reflected in her latest single “2 Loud,” a brassy pop anthem for the dance floor-sounding song releasing this Friday.

Popular on Variety

“2 Loud” signals a shift in her music, influenced by Ami’s inner pop girl. Here, Ami speaks with Variety about this new chapter and sound, and what to expect from her in the near future.

This is a new era for you, and there’s so much confidence in this song. You can hear it in the lyrics. Where did that shift happen?

We’ve chatted so many times. You saw me and the girls throughout the campaign, and it was crazy. I’ve never been thrust into that level of visibility in my life. I’ve never had people online comment about just me existing. And I had to process so many things all at once. I’ve had to develop new habits, like not reading the comments and putting a pause on the doomscrolling.

At one point, I read a comment about one of our performances, and it said, “She’s doing too much.” I thought, “How am I doing too much?” I am in a position where millions of people are watching me. I have an opportunity of a lifetime. You want me to not do my job, right? What are you even talking about?

And it made me think: These people don’t actually know me. Sometimes, you just have to let it be. You don’t have to understand why they would comment such a bizarre thing, but they do, and that’s not my problem.

It made me realize that me being “too much” has opened so many opportunities for me. It has given me the ability to change my life and change my parents’ lives. So I channeled this feeling that’s been weighing on my heart for so long into a song, and that became “2 Loud.”

I am just so unapologetically me. I love myself, and I accept myself—flaws and all—for what and who I am, because it has brought me this far. I am human. I’m imperfect. But so are you.

I love how you’re embracing that. “2 Loud” is definitely a statement, but also a different vibe. It’s fully you embracing your pop girl side. Talk about this new sound.

I’ve been raised by the pop girls — Rihanna, Britney Spears, you name it. I’ve always been a pop girl to the core.

When I was releasing “Snow Cone” and “Body Bag,” I was in a very dark place in my life. I was still figuring it out. I was angry, resentful, and bitter about so many things in my career and personal life. I think that’s normal and human, and it’s only natural as an artist that I poured it into my work.

With “2 Loud,” I’m no longer angry. I’ve let go of a lot. I want to dance. I want to celebrate life. I want to live life. I want to express myself. That’s what I am prioritizing in my life: happiness, joy, and being able to live this blessing of a life to the fullest, as my most authentic, truest self.

And that’s what “2 Loud” is about. That’s what I want to usher into this new era of music — this freedom to be human. I think that’s what everyone wants. They want to feel human, to feel heard and connected. And I think that’s what the world needs right now.

It’s a very fun pop tune. I heard that you were inspired to go into the studio after the 20th anniversary of “Hannah Montana.” Is that true?

It’s so funny because we’re actually releasing on the same day as Miley’s album, which is, again, synchronistic. My co-writers, producers, and executive producer were already setting up shop at the studio because that week I was going to start writing camp. But there was something in me that said, “Let’s stop by the studio.”

So I went there, and they had already started building out “2 Loud.” My co-writer, Maia Kelly, was already writing the verse, and she had tracked it. We were talking about it because, at the time, I really was feeling it. I was like, “Oh my God, am I too much?”

I’ve been really in my head, asking: “Am I losing myself? Am I becoming something I’m not?” But I also have a new audience now—children — and I have to be considerate. I’m part of something bigger than me. All these thoughts kept me overanalyzing and second-guessing everything. I was losing my mind. Maia and I were talking, and she said, “Too loud, too much — let’s just fucking talk about it.”

The next day, I wrote the second verse. I went in because I was pissed. I thought, “I’m not safe for your work. My old shit? Definitely not safe for your kids. It’s not even PG-13. It’s rated R for Rei Ami.” So we tracked it, and as I was listening to it, I thought, “This is everything I’ve wanted to say for a minute now.” It’s a clapback. It’s essentially saying, “Y’all don’t actually fucking know me. You don’t know what ‘too loud’ is. You haven’t seen loud.” If this is too loud for you, ooh, I can’t fucking wait for you to see what’s coming next. If you don’t like it, turn it off.

This is you being your authentic self. How much of a creative explosion has this been for you?

This album is my story as an artist. There’s nothing really profound or philosophical about it. It’s very honest and human. It’s every high and low that I’ve experienced, and it’s just me talking about the things that matter to me and have affected me. I think many people are going to relate to that. It’s told through the lens of my life and my human experience, but it’s a very universal album.

How has writing these songs, especially “2 Loud,” healed you?

It’s made me more confident and self-assured in who I am and in my gut intuition. When you’re confident and you know what you want, the vision becomes a little clearer. I urge people to find confidence wherever they can because it can heal so many parts of you. A lot of the things we shame ourselves for are the things that could really change our lives and our futures. For me, being loud or extra—I dimmed that part of myself heavily. Growing up in a religious environment, there was a lot of suppression. It was disgusting and evil. But the moment I let her out, people found it charming. And especially in this kind of career, it really helped.

This interview has been edited and condensed.

title: ‘Far Cry’ FX Series Casts Brendan Gleeson, Jennifer Jason Leigh, Hamish Linklater, Sam Spruell, Jamie Demetriou
summary: The “Far Cry” TV series at FX is continuing to build out an all-star cast. Variety has learned that Brendan Gleeson (“The Banshees of Inisherin,” “In Bruges”), Jennifer Jason Leigh (“The Hateful Eight,” FX’s “Fargo”), Hamish Linklater (“Widow’s Bay,” “Midnight Mass”), Sam Spruell (“A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms,” FX’s “Alien: Earth”), and Jamie Demetriou […]
content:
The “Far Cry” TV series at FX is continuing to build out an all-star cast.

Variety has learned that Brendan Gleeson (“The Banshees of Inisherin,” “In Bruges”), Jennifer Jason Leigh (“The Hateful Eight,” FX’s “Fargo”), Hamish Linklater (“Widow’s Bay,” “Midnight Mass”), Sam Spruell (“A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms,” FX’s “Alien: Earth”), and Jamie Demetriou (“Stath Lets Flats,” “The Afterparty”) are all set to appear in the first season of the series, which is based on the video game franchise of the same name.

The five new additions join previously announced lead and co-creator Rob Mac and fellow cast members Lizzy Caplan and Steve Buscemi.

Popular on Variety

The series was first reported to be set up at FX in November 2025 from creators Noah Hawley and Mac. Exact plot and character details remain under wraps, but the series will follow an anthology format like the “Far Cry” games and feature a different cast and setting each season.

“Far Cry” will air on FX, Hulu, and Disney+ internationally. Mac will executive produce under his More Better Productions banner, while Hawley will executive produce under his overall deal with FX and Disney Entertainment Television via 26 Keys. Simon Emanuel will also executive produce along with Emilia Serrano for 26 Keys, Nick Frenkel for 3 Arts, Monica Macer, Peter Calloway, John Campisi, and Gerard Guillemot, Margaret Boykin and Austin Dill for Ubisoft Film & Television. The series will be produced by FX Productions.

Gleeson is repped by CAA and Principal Entertainment. Leigh is repped by by CAA and Untitled Entertainment. Linklater is repped by Untitled Entertainment, Gersh and Johnson Shapiro Slewett & Kole. Spruell is repped by Lou Coulson Associates and Luber Roklin Entertainment. Demetriou is repped by United Agents, CAA, and Multitude Media.

title: ‘Lizzie Borden’ Cast on Treating the Story as a Comedy, the Joy of Playing a Sadistic Character and Finding Empathy for a Bloody Monster: ‘I Understand This Person’
summary: “Don’t you worry: I look after my axes,” Charlie Hunnam says proudly with an impish grin. At the moment, he’s not in character but rather marveling at a hobby he picked up before filming “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story.” In it, he plays Lizzie’s father, an undertaker who is fine chopping a client’s legs off […]
content:
“Don’t you worry: I look after my axes,” Charlie Hunnam says proudly with an impish grin.

At the moment, he’s not in character but rather marveling at a hobby he picked up before filming “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story.” In it, he plays Lizzie’s father, an undertaker who is fine chopping a client’s legs off if they are too tall for the coffin.

Hunnam himself says that in the months leading up to filming, he’d been noticing felled trees on the side of the road while driving through Los Angeles. He took to chopping them up and throwing them into the back of his pickup truck.

“I ended up with probably about 10 tons of wood and bought some great axes and started becoming quite the axeman,” he says. “I’ve been really, really wanting these beautiful Scandinavian axes. When I got this, because Andrew Borden’s an ax collector, I said, ‘Well, it’s for the work. I’ve got to have these axes.’”

Popular on Variety

Charlie Hunnam as Andrew Borden in “Monster” Courtesy of Netflix

The conversation mirrors the surprising, irreverent tone of this season of “Monster.” A complete turn from the darkness of “The Ed Gein Story,” in which Hunnam starred as the titular killer, there is a lightness, beauty and levity to Lizzie’s story — even when she grabs an ax and takes some whacks.

This fourth season stars Ella Beatty as the naive, curious title character, whose world brightens when a new housemaid, Bridget Sullivan (Vicky Krieps), arrives and introduces Lizzie to daring literature and kinky sex. Yet her awakening is dampened by her depressed father and cruel stepmother Abby (Rebecca Hall).

Despite Lizzie committing such a legendary crime, Beatty was able to find a kindred spirit in the character, a very complicated young woman.

“I felt very connected to the character immediately,” she says. “I remember making the audition tape and thinking, ‘I understand this person.’ When I found out that I had gotten the part, I was over the moon and also really scared. I felt a huge responsibility to the part, to the anthology, to the real person. I think immediately I just wanted to start working on it. How does she move? How does she dream? How does she think? How does she speak? How does she blink?”

Rebecca Hall as Abby Borden and Ella Beatty as Lizzie Borden Courtesy of Netflix

Hall, whose character says some jaw-droppingly mean things to her stepdaughter, was thrilled to unwrap a deliciously cruel antagonist.

“I’ve never played a true out-and-out villain,” she says. “I just loved on the page how funny she was. It just felt like such an opportunity to be both funny and scary at the same time, which is an interesting tonal challenge. I loved [writer] Ian Brennan’s take on this character, which felt like it was a creation of Ian Brennan and [executive producer] Ryan Murphy and had nothing to do with history really, as much as it gave me license to create this unique character.”

Despite Abby’s savagery, Hall saw a unique reflection of the character and the title killers in the series.

“Nothing in this ‘Monster’ world is straightforward,” she says. “The exercise of the show is really about how monsters aren’t born, they’re created. So even Abby Borden has that as well. There’s reason behind it. She’s also in a pressure cooker, and she’s become an alcoholic over time. I sort of loved the character. There’s a lot of fun to be had, and there’s something very interesting about playing someone who’s keeping up appearances, who wants to appear posh and together and is just a complete and utter mess — and a sadistic one to boot.”

This season is a star-making moment for Beatty, whose parents, Annette Bening and Warren Beatty, are legends in their own right. Yet she’s found her way to “Monster” through plenty of time on stage as well as smaller parts in movies such as “If I Had Legs I’d Kick You” and the 2024 Murphy-verse series “Feud: Capote vs. the Swans.”

As the central figure on the show, Beatty says she definitely had nerves but was fascinated to get on the series’ unique wavelength.

“I knew that they were interested in exploring an almost farcical tone,” she says. “We all just continued to discover it together. It felt a lot more available on set than you might initially think. I was constantly surprised by the ability of comedy and really intense sadness or drama to be in the show. I felt like we discovered it together the whole time.”

Despite its 19th-century trappings, there is a universality to the story and its outrageousness that Hunnam is excited for audiences to engage with.

“It felt like there was much more license for a bonkers absurdity that felt like it was on the page and that I was surprised by and really excited about,” he says. “I thought there was a complexity and a tragedy and a nastiness and a vulnerability and all of the things that you look for that are true of all of us.”

Watch a trailer for “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story” below.

title: Miley Cyrus Describes Last Conversation With Dolly Parton, Prompted by Sending Over Her New Album: ‘Though We Were So Different, That’s What Made Us Perfect for Each Other’
summary: Miley Cyrus, now being professionally known as just Miley, spoke about her last conversation with her godmother, Dolly Parton — stemming from Cyrus sending Parton an advance copy of her new album, “Bass Persuades” — in a fresh interview with Zane Lowe. “Dolly has been the first person that when I get a vinyl printed,” […]
content:
Miley Cyrus, now being professionally known as just Miley, spoke about her last conversation with her godmother, Dolly Parton — stemming from Cyrus sending Parton an advance copy of her new album, “Bass Persuades” — in a fresh interview with Zane Lowe.

“Dolly has been the first person that when I get a vinyl printed,” Parton told the Apple Music podcast host. “That’s the first person I send it to since I’ve been making vinyls, and this time around I was going to send her a vinyl because I always do. I’m just trying to keep myself together, but the time that we talked, which was the last time we would talk, it was actually me telling her about this record because even though we are so different, that’s what made us so perfect for each other, It’s that — and she knew this, and I know this — she is known for the fake, the hair, the makeup, and the show of it. But there’s a part of her that I think is what everyone gravitates towards… how real she is and how authentic she is.

“And there was a time in my life — we hit on it with Hannah (Montana) — so much of my life was about persona. And I think a way that I could look at that as you can have a persona and still be who you are is because I had Dolly. Sometimes I call what I do drag because the way that I present myself is just someone that is so different from the person that feeds the tortoise every morning. But again, that person’s inside of me. I just kind of have her off. One of the things we talked about was, in my performances, I always cry; I can’t help it. (SInging) ‘End of the World,’ I start crying and she watched me on Letterman and was like, ‘What are you crying about?’ That song’s about the world ending and me never seeing my mom again.”

Popular on Variety

Lowe suggested that maybe what Parton was trying to tell her was: You need to be more professional.

“That’s pretty much what she said,” responded Cyrus. “She was like, ‘Music is escapism. Let them cry. You need to get through it.’ And I was like, ‘I know, but this is who I am.’ And she loved me for it,” despite their different takes on how emotional to get in public.



Cyrus discussed having a keen sense of how the role models she has had in her life will eventually disappear from it, as Parton has.

“I cried singing ‘I Will Always Love You’ with her,” she said, “but I think she knew at that time that the reason I was crying is the reason that I cry now, which is because so many of my really stabilizing peers that I have in my life [come from] generations before me. And they’ve laid down, brick by brick, the road that I travel now. And they aren’t always going to be here for me to call them and say, ‘What do I do now?,’ which I always did with Dolly. And she was always right. It’s like how your mom’s like always right, and when you’re a kid, you’re like, what does she know? And then as you get older, you’re like, ‘How? Where did this come from? You’re just a normal person. Why do you know everything?’ Dolly was just always right about stuff.”

Cyrus’ new album comes out at midnight Thursday night. She described how producer Max Martin convinced her to go for a certain upbeat and propulsive sound on the album, which she resisted, at least for songs that were conceived as ballads.

Of a track called “Aftermath,” Cyrus said, “A funny story about that song: one of the lyrics actually says ‘the Titan sinks,’ so it was actually about a submarine, and I wrote it as a very sad ballad. I was playing a bunch of the songs that I had written, because I wrote them a little differently this record, and I was playing the record as it was with Max and I said, ‘Is there anything? Like, be brutal, tell me what you don’t like.’ He was like, ‘God, that “Aftermath” song is boring. I’m just going to be honest with you.’ He’s like, ‘So boring.’ So [I say] ‘What would you do with it?’ And then boom, boom, boom, boom and I was like, that is better. I was going for the Thom Yorke-like vibe, but he’s like, ‘No, boring.’ So he made that song so much better.”







”

title: ‘Dark Winds’ Zahn McClarnon Receiving Santa Fe Film Festival’s Visionary Award
summary: The Santa Fe International Film Festival will present its Visionary Award to Dark Winds actor Zahn McClarnon on October 16 at the Lensic Performing Arts Center in Santa Fe, NM. McClarnon plays Lt. Joe Leaphorn in the AMC series Dark Winds executive produced by George R.R. Martin and the late Robert Redford. McClarnon also serves […]
content:
The Santa Fe International Film Festival will present its Visionary Award to Dark Winds actor Zahn McClarnon on October 16 at the Lensic Performing Arts Center in Santa Fe, NM.

McClarnon plays Lt. Joe Leaphorn in the AMC series Dark Winds executive produced by George R.R. Martin and the late Robert Redford. McClarnon also serves as an EP and director (Season 4, episode 2) for the series, which just wrapped its fifth season.

Based on Tony Hillerman’s Leaphorn & Chee novels, Dark Winds follows two Navajo police officers in the 1970s as they investigate numerous seemingly unrelated crimes in the American Southwest. The series is shot in Santa Fe.

McClarnon also played Officer Big in the FX series Reservation Dogs, earning him a Film Independent Spirit Award for Best Ensemble Cast in a New Scripted Series.

Watch on Deadline

Other standout roles include Officer Mathias in Longmire, Akecheta in HBO’s second season of Westworld, and Hanzee Dent in the second season of FX’s Fargo. McClarnon was a series regular on National Geographic’s Barkskins, opposite Marcia Gay Harden and David Thewlis. He also starred on AMC’s The Son. His film credits include The Silencing, with Nikolaj Coster-Waldau, and Mike Flanagan’s adaptation of Stephen King’s Doctor Sleep. On television, he has recurred on Disney+ and Marvel Studio’s Hawkeye and Echo.

Additional credits include Hulu’s History of the World, Part II, the Jennifer Lawrence comedy No Hard Feelings, and Tony Tost’s Americana. He also voiced Olrox in Netflix’s animated series Castlevania: Nocturne.

“Zahn McClarnon brings authenticity and excitement to each of his roles. His entrée into directing makes him an exemplary person to receive the Visionary Award,” said Santa Fe Film Festival executive director Liesette Bailey.

Previous recipients of the festival’s Visionary Award include Giancarlo Esposito, Sterlin Harjo, Wes Studi and Catherine Hardwicke.

title: Johnny Depp’s First Sculpture To Be Unveiled At Art Fair
summary: Johnny Depp’s first sculpture, a two-metre white bronze called ‘The Bunnyman’, will be unveiled at Turkish art fair Contemporary Istanbul, which runs 22–27 September. The artwork will be presented outdoors at Tersane Istanbul, the historic Ottoman shipyard on the Golden Horn, as one of the fair’s special projects. The sculpture is described as a “half-human, […]
content:
Johnny Depp’s first sculpture, a two-metre white bronze called ‘The Bunnyman’, will be unveiled at Turkish art fair Contemporary Istanbul, which runs 22–27 September.

The artwork will be presented outdoors at Tersane Istanbul, the historic Ottoman shipyard on the Golden Horn, as one of the fair’s special projects.



The sculpture is described as a “half-human, half-rabbit guardian carrying a ‘sword of truth’”. The work began with a drawing by Depp’s son Jack, aged around five, which reminded Depp of his own recurring childhood dream. The figure has since appeared across Depp’s sketches, paintings, and prints.

The sculpture came about through a collaboration between the Sigg Art Foundation, Pantheon Art, and Fonderia Artistica Battaglia in Milan.

Watch on Deadline

The unveiling coincides with Depp’s exhibition, A Bunch of Stuff, at the Modern Art Museum Shanghai, which features more than 200 of his art works.

Depp, who is in post on movies Ebenezer and Day Drinker, said: “When people see the painting I did — The Bunnyman — they always ask the same question: where did it come from? Some character that Jack had scribbled, beautiful scribbles into that shape, that image, reminded me of a kind of recurrent dream that I had as a child, probably around Jack’s age, five, six…”

title: Chelsea Handler Denies Firing Tour Opener Over “Free Palestine” Support: “I Would Never”
summary: Amid the fallout from Ed Sheeran removing Macklemore from his tour, Chelsea Handler is denying that she fired an opener over her “Free Palestine” support. Following comic Salma Hindy’s claim that the Grammy nominee tried “to get rid of me” for speaking up about Palestinians, Handler denied the accusation on social media, insisting she “never […]
content:
Amid the fallout from Ed Sheeran removing Macklemore from his tour, Chelsea Handler is denying that she fired an opener over her “Free Palestine” support.

Following comic Salma Hindy‘s claim that the Grammy nominee tried “to get rid of me” for speaking up about Palestinians, Handler denied the accusation on social media, insisting she “never fired” Hindy.

“Ah, that’s actually not what happened,” commented on Hindy’s Instagram video. “You quit opening for me, and I have the emails from your agents. Your agent is full of it. I would never fire someone for disagreeing with me politically on this issue.”

Handler added, “And I never fired her. Period. Not on this issue.”

Watch on Deadline

Additionally, Handler shared screenshots of her communications with Hindy, which appear to show her dropping out of a show that she claimed to have been canceled without her knowledge. It also shows Handler approving her reimbursement for travel that Hindy claimed her team refused to pay.

On Wednesday, Hindy posted the video claiming, “I lost my position as Chelsea Handler’s opener after I spoke to her about Palestine.”

The Canadian-Egyptian standup comedian said she opened for Handler on two tours since 2022, and they “generally had a very loving, warm sisterly relationship.” But when Hindy asked “if she wanted to speak about the Palestine-Isreal thing” in the wake of her friends Sarah Silverman and Amy Schumer’s “disgustingly racist, dehumanizing” posts about Palestinians, she claimed Handler ignored her and removed her from three shows.

Hindy said that Handler later canceled two shows last minute due to severe weather, without notifying her. And although she said Handler’s team bought her a plane ticket back to New York City, she claimed they refused to reimburse her.

The comedian alleged that her manager told her, “Chelsea Handler is trying to get rid of [Hindy] because of the Palestine thing, but she doesn’t want to say it so that she doesn’t incriminate herself.”

Handler’s response comes after Ed Sheeran dropped Macklemore from his tour, amid pressure from Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft and other venues over the “Hind’s Hall” singer’s “Free Palestine” peach at recent shows on Sheeran’s Loop Tour.

title: Eric Schrier Stepping Down As President Of DTC International Originals, Segues To Producing Deal With Disney Entertainment Television
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Eric Schrier is departing his post as Disney’s President of Direct-to-Consumer International Originals, Strategic Programming, and Emerging Media — but not the company. The 26-year FX/Disney veteran is launching a production company, which will be based at Disney Entertainment Television. Disney Entertainment Television chairman Debra OConnell revealed Schrier’s change of status in an internal […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Eric Schrier is departing his post as Disney‘s President of Direct-to-Consumer International Originals, Strategic Programming, and Emerging Media — but not the company. The 26-year FX/Disney veteran is launching a production company, which will be based at Disney Entertainment Television.

Disney Entertainment Television chairman Debra OConnell revealed Schrier’s change of status in an internal memo, which followed the announcement of Adam Smith’s elevation to Chairman, Direct-to-Consumer for Disney Entertainment and Joe Earley’s move to DET as President, Disney Entertainment Television Franchise and Content Strategy.

“As Eric and I have been talking about the future, he shared with me his desire to return to his creative roots,” OConnell wrote. “After an extraordinary 26 years at Disney, including as one of the early architects of FX, Eric has decided this is the right moment to pursue that next chapter. I’m so pleased that we’ll continue working together through a new producing partnership with DET. Eric plans to share more about what’s ahead soon, and we’re excited about what we’re going to create together.”

Watch on Deadline

Details of Schrier’s producing arrangement are still being hammered out but he is expected to work across divisions, which include FX, where he had spent most of his career to date, rising to Entertainment President; FX Productions, which he launched with FX chairman John Landgraf; Hulu/Disney+, which he supplied with international originals; and 20th Television, which he oversaw for two years as President of Disney Entertainment Studios, until the March restructuring following Dana Walden’s elevation to President and Chief Creative Officer of The Walt Disney Company.

It saw Schrier move to Direct-to-Consumer under Earley as President of DTC International Originals, Strategic Programming, and Emerging Media.

Building Disney+ international streaming originals’ infrastructure and slate has been a focus for Schrier over the past couple of years. He has expanded the streamer’s global content lineup to 65 shows across 16 international markets and has appointed new EMEA and LATAM heads as well as new country managers. He also has been charting Disney+ path in emerging content space while also maintaining his existing responsibilities overseeing all BA, labor relations and creative development and inclusion across DET.

The role came with a heavy travel load, taking Schrier away from his young family for 1-2 weeks every month and making him miss important events and anniversaries.

It also came with a large focus on administrative duties, pulling Schrier away from the creative process, which was at the center of his tenure at FX. He missed working with writers, directors and talent, as well as being entrepreneurial, which he did at FX where he helped establish a new production model and launch a viable cable studio in FX Productions.

The two factors, as well as him being confined within the Disney walls for the past two years, led to Schrier’s decision to take on a new chapter as a producer. The timing of the decision is likely tied to the latest Disney restructuring that has Earley move to DET under OConnell, which would’ve involved Schrier moving back with him. (OConnell is expected to reorganize her unit too in the coming months.)

Schrier’s exit from the executive ranks comes just a couple of weeks after another key FX architect, Chuck Saftler, also announced his departure.

At age 50, Schrier has plenty of runway ahead of him as he puts an end to a 25-year executive career spent entirely at FX/Disney. He joined FX in late 2000 as an assistant to then-President of Entertainment Kevin Reilly. Just months later, in July 2021, Schrier was promoted to Manager of Current Series and rose steadily through the ranks to Entertainment President. Some of the series that he was closely involved in include The Shield, Sons of Anarchy, The Americans, Atlanta and The Bear.

Since leaving FX to become President of Disney Television Studios in 2022, Schrier oversaw such Disney+ international originals as Rivals, Alice and Steve and Perfect Crown and the upcoming The Remarried Princess. He spearheaded major Disney TV Studios deals with networks and talen,t including the blockbuster four-season pickup of four 20th Animation series by Fox: The Simpsons, Family Guy, Bob’s Burgers as well as American Dad! in its return to the network after an 11-year run on TBS.

Additionally, he helped Walden manage the DTC business and its turnaround to profitability and create the combined Disney Entertainment division.
