The writers worked closely with DC’s Jim Lee to develop the versions of the comic characters that appear in Thursday’s episode. Lee teased the partnership over the summer at San Diego Comic-Con, assuring the audience in Hall H that the DC IP would be in good hands with the Stuart team.

“Some of the DC characters they have in it, I think are some of the best versions I’ve seen of those characters, and so I’m super excited for you guys,” Lee said at the time.

Penn, who had previously collaborated with Lee and the DC team on Ready Player One, remembered the Stuart reteam fondly: “They were great. They basically said, ‘How can we help? Other than we won’t give you Green Lantern.'”

The series has already been renewed for a second season ahead of next week’s Season 1 finale. Penn tells Deadline he “would be shocked” if the writers didn’t once again mine from the DC universe in future episodes, but Season 2 is still in early stages.

“The writers’ room hasn’t started yet. Next week, we’re going to get back together and start talking about this,” he said.

title: Tom Cruise Says Taylor Swift Was ‘Schooling Me on Football’ at Chiefs Game, Calls Her a ‘Brilliant Musician and Director’
summary: Tom Cruise and Taylor Swift made headlines on Monday when they sat next to each other at the Kansas City Chiefs’ first game of the season. But what were the two megastars talking about? “She was schooling me on football. For real,” Cruise revealed to Jimmy Fallon during an appearance on “The Tonight Show” on […]
content:
Tom Cruise and Taylor Swift made headlines on Monday when they sat next to each other at the Kansas City Chiefs’ first game of the season. But what were the two megastars talking about?

“She was schooling me on football. For real,” Cruise revealed to Jimmy Fallon during an appearance on “The Tonight Show” on Thursday. But that wasn’t the first time Cruise and Swift have had a meeting of the minds — he was spotted at her Eras Tour in London in 2024, and when the pop star married Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce in July, Cruise was in attendance.

“First of all, she’s a genius. I’ve been following her since she was a kid,” Cruise said of Swift. “Everybody there, all their friends — they’re a beautiful couple and magical in their own right.”

Popular on Variety

And Swift has real ball knowledge. “Oh, she knows her stuff,” Cruise continued, adding that the singer “knew nothing about football when she met Travis.”

Other than Swift coaching him through the game, Cruise said they “talked about music and movies.”

“She’s funny, she’s got such a great sense of humor,” he said. “A brilliant writer also, by the way. A brilliant musician and director — very skilled.”

Swift has directed many of her own music videos over the years, and delved further into filmmaking with 2021’s “All Too Well: The Short Film,” starring Sadie Sink and Dylan O’Brien. In late 2022, it was announced that she would be making her feature directorial debut for Searchlight Pictures, though her record-breaking Eras Tour that began the next year (and extended through December 2024) seems to have delayed this.

Elsewhere in his interview with Fallon, Cruise was asked about rumors that his new film “Digger,” directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu, was actually a musical.

“No, but I think it’s a very good idea,” he laughed. “I think we should do ‘Digger’ the musical. Digger down!” Cruise and Fallon then broke out into song and dance in their seats.

Cruise’s press tour for “Digger” will also include an appearance on Travis and Jason Kelce’s “New Heights” podcast, releasing on Friday.

Watch Cruise’s full interview with Fallon below.

title: ‘Best of the Best’ Director Lena Khan on Making a Bollywood Fusion Dance Movie for Netflix, Working With Hasan Minhaj and Telling Maitreyi Ramakrishnan to Bring ‘Channing Tatum Energy’
summary: Competitive Bollywood fusion dance has thrived on American college campuses for decades, but it has rarely been the subject of a scripted feature film. Lena Khan’s “Best of the Best,” premiering Friday on Netflix, follows childhood best friends Maya and Anjali as they join UCLA’s competitive dance team, only to discover that the road to […]
content:
Competitive Bollywood fusion dance has thrived on American college campuses for decades, but it has rarely been the subject of a scripted feature film.

Lena Khan‘s “Best of the Best,” premiering Friday on Netflix, follows childhood best friends Maya and Anjali as they join UCLA’s competitive dance team, only to discover that the road to the U.S. Championship is far more raucous and cutthroat than they imagined.

Written by Hasan Minhaj and Prashanth Venkataramanujam, who each competed in similar circuits growing up, the script drew Khan in even though she was not initially sure she would take on the project. Early on, she recalls mentioning it to a childhood friend, who was dismissive. “Bollywood competitions, really?” the friend said, and made it seem like it was not that cool, according to Khan, who says the reaction reflects something broader. “I think South Asians, especially in the diaspora, are so used to not even having our own self-respect.”

Popular on Variety

That realization shaped how she approached the film’s tone. “We have so much respect for the skill sets of other cultures. We’re looking at kung fu, we’re looking at these different arts. But when we look at our own, we’re used to seeing ourselves as Apu or as the funny nerdy side characters,” Khan says. She wanted the movie to carry a different posture entirely. “We can be proud of things that we do as South Asians,” she says.

Minhaj and Venkataramanujam drew on their own backgrounds for the script. Minhaj’s wife danced competitively, and Venkataramanujam performed with an a cappella team called Chai Town, giving him firsthand knowledge of how consuming the competition circuit can become. Khan spent time with UCLA’s own dance team and traveled to North Carolina to observe competitions in preparation.

Khan’s earlier work directing episodes of Netflix’s “Never Have I Ever” fed into how she thinks about representation. “When you have more than one of a minority character, then there’s suddenly become real characters,” she says, describing the shift that happens once side characters are allowed the same depth as anyone else. “You get to focus on the humanity between them, the things that become relatable to everybody else.”

Casting required actors who could carry both comedy and depth, and several, including Maitreyi Ramakrishnan, had never danced competitively before landing their roles. Khan recalls pushing Ramakrishnan toward a specific physical transformation during casting. “I need you to give me some Channing Tatum energy. And then I was like, no, actually, I need you to do a Christian Bale on me. I need a complete athletic transformation,” she says. Ramakrishnan went on to complete months of intensive dance training ahead of the shoot.

Khan built the dance sequences with choreographers Phillip Chbeeb and Makenzie Dustman, with Joya Kazi credited as co-choreographer. Each number was approached with a single guiding question, she says: “What is the essence we are trying to bring out in this particular moment?” Where a typical Bollywood dance sequence gets five days to shoot, the production often had just one. The choreography also draws on multiple regional styles, including Kuthu, Bharatanatyam and Pakistani-influenced dance, reflecting the mix of identities on the fictional team.

Priyanka Kedia, Lena Khan and Maitreyi Ramakrishnan on the sets of “Best of the Best” Netflix

Khan, whose credits include the independent feature “The Tiger Hunter,” says the industry’s relationship to South Asian stories has shifted since that film came out in 2016, even as some structural limits remain. “We still don’t have that many romances or romantic comedies with South Asians,” she says, pointing out that South Asian men are often not given the chance to play the lead. The film flips that dynamic elsewhere in its own casting, she notes: “The nerdy minority character is actually a white guy. Like we have a token white guy.” She also credits a wave of South Asian musicians and actors, including Joy Crookes, whose song she fought to include in the soundtrack, with making the film possible. “And now we’re like, well, we’ve really made it when we make a movie that’s just good,” she says.

That philosophy extended to how much cultural context the film explains for a global Netflix audience. Khan says she resisted pressure to over-explain South Asian references, trusting shows like “Never Have I Ever” to have already proven audiences do not need everything spelled out. “At some point this country and the world is just full of people in different cultures,” she says.

Working with Minhaj and Venkataramanujam, both first-time feature writers, meant frequent creative disagreements, Khan says, but never without purpose. “There would be such a thoughtful reason that we were always fighting over why we’re doing a certain thing, but it was never for a vapid reason,” she says. “And they’re also just the most gracious people.”

Hasan Minhaj – “Best of the Best” Netflix

Looking ahead, Khan says she is drawn to projects centered on overlooked people or subjects, alongside a personal passion project already underway. “I’m always on the hunt for that,” she says, describing a search for stories she wishes already existed and a way to make them for a wide audience.

“Best of the Best” also stars Lilly Singh, Nihar Duvvuri, Nico Greetham, Amryn Khurana, Tanishq Joshi, Saara Chaudry and Sasha Bhasin. It is streaming now on Netflix.

title: Alfonso Cuaron to Make First Korea Visit at Busan as Festival Also Spotlights European Women+ Filmmakers
summary: The 31st Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) has announced the first-ever Korea visit by Alfonso Cuarón, alongside a dedicated spotlight on nine films from European women and genderqueer filmmakers. Cuarón, who has won the Academy Award for best director twice, for “Gravity” (2013) and “Roma” (2018), also holds the Venice Film Festival’s best screenplay prize […]
content:
The 31st Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) has announced the first-ever Korea visit by Alfonso Cuarón, alongside a dedicated spotlight on nine films from European women and genderqueer filmmakers.

Cuarón, who has won the Academy Award for best director twice, for “Gravity” (2013) and “Roma” (2018), also holds the Venice Film Festival’s best screenplay prize for “Y Tu Mamá También” (2001) and a Golden Lion for “Roma.” He first caught Hollywood’s attention with “Y Tu Mamá También,” a portrait of youth and desire, before taking “Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban” (2004) in a moodier, more personal visual direction than the series had gone before, and later used extended long takes in “Children of Men” (2007) to pull audiences directly into a world at war. He is expected to appear at BIFF’s opening ceremony and will sit down for an extended conversation with festivalgoers about the camera language and instincts behind his films. An Imax screening of “Gravity,” co-written with his son, filmmaker Jonás Cuarón, will also be at the festival.

Jonás Cuarón’s latest feature, “Campeón Gabacho,” will have its Asian premiere in the World Cinema section, followed by a post-screening Q&A. Since writing on “Gravity,” the younger Cuarón has built his own filmography with “Desierto” (2015) and “Chupa” (2023). “Campeón Gabacho,” starring Juan Daniel García Treviño, Leslie Grace, Rubén Blades, Eddie Marsan, Rosario Dawson and Cheech Marin, follows a Mexican immigrant building a life in the United States, and was produced by Jonás Cuarón alongside his father and Gabriela Rodriguez under their Esperanto Filmoj banner, with Nicolás Celis also producing.

Popular on Variety

Elsewhere at the festival, BIFF is showcasing “Europe! Voices of Women+ in Film,” a program run with the European Film Promotion (EFP), spotlighting nine officially selected films through targeted promotion and industry networking. The lineup spans period drama, documentary and contemporary narrative work built around questions of freedom, memory and family, with four of the nine as feature debuts. May el-Toukhy‘s “Woman Unknown,” winner of the Golden Lion at Venice, anchors the group; el-Toukhy became the first Danish woman filmmaker to take that prize, while Mathilde Arcel won the Volpi Cup for best actress in the same film. Also included are Marine Atlan’s debut “La Gradiva,” Pegah Ahangarani’s “Rehearsals for a Revolution,” Sandra Wollner’s “Everytime,” winner of the Un Certain Regard Prize at Cannes, Margherita Ferrari’s debut “Föa – Once Upon a Future,” Isabelle Stever’s “I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming,” Marie Kreutzer’s “Gentle Monster,” Shahrbanoo Sadat’s “No Good Men” and Sarah Arnold’s debut “Too Many Beasts.” Judith Godrèche’s “A Girl’s Story,” part of this year’s gala presentations, joins Angela Schanelec’s “My Wife Cries,” Janay Boulos and Abd Alkader Habak’s “Birds of War,” Jacqueline Lentzou’s “A Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra,” winner of the Horizons Award for Best Director at Venice, and Konstantina Kotzamani’s “Titanic Ocean” among the additional selections.

Five directors from the program, el-Toukhy, Godrèche, Ferrari, Lentzou and Kotzamani, will travel to Busan to present their films. Godrèche will also take part in a Cine Class session, “Women, Rewriting the Screen,” and BIFF and EFP will co-host a Talk-to-Talk panel, “Women Directors: Taking the Scene,” bringing together Ferrari, el-Toukhy and Lentzou alongside Iranian director Marjan Khosravi (“Dreams of the Wild Oaks”), Chinese director Michelle Zhou (“Big Little Things”) and Afghan director Zainab Entezar (“771 Days”).

BIFF programmer Seo Seunghee said that in reviewing films for this year’s festival, she noticed European women directors becoming more prominent among the strongest titles under consideration, in both volume and quality. “Moreover, the fact that four of the nine invited films are feature debuts is also an indicator of the generational shift taking place in European cinema,” Seo said. “Our ongoing collaboration with EFP has become a reliable channel for discovering and validating outstanding films and filmmakers, and the results are fully reflected in this year’s lineup.”

EFP managing director Irina Ignatiew-Lemke said the “Europe! Voices of Women+ in Film” initiative lets EFP and its member organizations “join forces to give distinctive European voices greater international visibility.” She added, “Busan is an important platform for bringing these filmmakers and their works into dialogue with audiences and industry professionals in Asia. By combining the festival’s selection with EFP’s targeted promotion and networking, we are proud to support underrepresented voices and create opportunities for the next generation of women+ filmmakers.”

The program runs in collaboration with BIFF, the Sydney Film Festival and Festival do Rio, with support from the Creative Europe – MEDIA Programme of the European Union. This year’s participating national film promotion organizations are Austrian Films, Cinecittà, the Czech Film Center, the Danish Film Institute, German Films and Unifrance, with Cineuropa serving as media partner.

The 31st Busan International Film Festival will run Oct. 6-15 at the Busan Cinema Center and venues throughout Busan, with the 21st Asian Contents & Film Market held Oct. 10-13.

title: ‘Tenzing’ Actor Tenzin Dalha Unveiled as Male Lead in Bengali Thriller ‘Chheledhora’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Tenzin Dalha, at the Toronto Film Festival with Jennifer Peedom’s Apple original Film “Tenzing,” has been revealed as the male lead in Bengali-language thriller “Chheledhora,” opposite Swastika Mukherjee. His casting had been withheld when the Indo-American production was first announced earlier this year, with producers naming only Mukherjee at that point. “Tenzing,” a gala presentation […]
content:
Tenzin Dalha, at the Toronto Film Festival with Jennifer Peedom’s Apple original Film “Tenzing,” has been revealed as the male lead in Bengali-language thriller “Chheledhora,” opposite Swastika Mukherjee.

His casting had been withheld when the Indo-American production was first announced earlier this year, with producers naming only Mukherjee at that point.

“Tenzing,” a gala presentation at TIFF, features Genden Phuntsok as legendary mountaineer Tenzing Norgay, with Tom Hiddleston, Willem Dafoe and Caitríona Balfe also in the cast. A limited theatrical run begins Oct. 9, with global streaming on Apple TV following Oct. 16.

Popular on Variety

In “Chheledhora,” written and directed by Shieladitya Moulik – whose credits include “Sweater” and “Surjo” – Dalha and Mukherjee anchor a story set off by an act of parental defiance. Mukherjee plays Brishti, a divorced mother who “steals” her own daughter for a birthday outing, only for the child to be genuinely abducted. The discovery then draws a group of deeply flawed adults and their children into an erratic journey through Northeast India, where the youngest characters gradually emerge as the moral compass for the adults around them. Filmed extensively in Arunachal Pradesh’s Ziro Valley, the production combines family drama, thriller elements and dark humor with the cultural texture of India’s Northeast. It is currently in post-production.

“We made a very conscious decision not to announce Tenzin when we first revealed ‘Chheledhora,'” said Ann Mukherjee, founder of Indo-American production company Sita22 Films. “We knew he had this extraordinary international moment ahead of him with ‘Tenzing,’ and TIFF felt like exactly the right time for audiences to discover another side of him. Tenzin possesses a quiet emotional intelligence and restraint that makes him a fascinating counterpoint to Swastika’s tremendous emotional force. Their chemistry is central to the film.”

Mukherjee described “Chheledhora” as a film that makes both a physical and emotional journey into India’s Northeast. “We want to tell stories that are deeply rooted in India but aren’t constrained by conventional ideas of language, geography or identity,” she said.

Dalha said it felt “particularly special” to be discussing one project while at the festival for another. “They are completely different films, yet rooted in human grit, empathy, the lengths to which humans are capable of going for people they love,” he said. “What drew me to ‘Chheledhora’ was Shieladitya’s writing. His understanding of humans as imperfect complex beings and looking at life beyond the dichotomy of individuals as good or bad. He wrote these beautiful broken young adult characters making questionable choices for their loved ones.”

The actor described Mukherjee as “a force of nature in frame and a force of joy on set,” adding that the Arunachal landscape shaped the film’s atmosphere from the outset. “Shooting in Ziro and Arunachal Pradesh provided the perfect backdrop for a thriller, and the weather set the tone right for the ambience,” he said.

The film is produced by Ann Mukherjee for Sita22 Films, with Jitin Hingorani as co-producer and creative producer, Dhanraj Sawant as executive producer and Priyangi Borthakur as supervising producer. Italian cinematographer Vincenzo Condorelli shot the film.

“The idea was never to make a Bengali film that simply happens to travel to the Northeast,” said Hingorani, who also heads content and development at Sita22 Films. “The journey changes these characters, and the Northeast becomes part of the film’s emotional language. Pairing Swastika and Tenzin gives us two performers coming from very different cinematic and cultural energies, and that tension is part of what makes the film so exciting. At Sita22, our mandate is to find stories that can be hyper-local and super-global at the same time, and ‘Chheledhora’ embodies that philosophy beautifully.”

title: San Sebastián 2026: ‘Les Mis,’ Los Javis, Brad Pitt, Penélope Cruz and Much More
summary: Ten takes on this year’s San Sebastián Film Festival, which runs Sept. 18-26 at the picturesque Basque Country resort: Brad Pitt, Penelope Cruz, Naomi Watts and More Last in San Sebastián way back then with “Inglourious Basterds,” Brad Pitt returns for “Heart of the Beast.” Busiest star of the festival? Penelope Cruz, fresh off a […]
content:
Ten takes on this year’s San Sebastián Film Festival, which runs Sept. 18-26 at the picturesque Basque Country resort:

Brad Pitt, Penelope Cruz, Naomi Watts and More

Last in San Sebastián way back then with “Inglourious Basterds,” Brad Pitt returns for “Heart of the Beast.” Busiest star of the festival? Penelope Cruz, fresh off a TIFF Special Tribute Award, at San Sebastián with “The Invite” and “La Bola Negra,” both moreover Oscar contenders, as Awards season conversation spills over into San Sebastián. Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s admired “The Beloved” should attract Javier Bardem. Watts receives a prestigious Donostia Award Sept. 19, New German Cinema leading light Werner Herzog picks up his at San Sebastián’s Sept. 18 opening ceremony.

James Belmont (Brad Pitt) and Odin in ‘Heart of the Beast’ from Paramount Pictures. Scott Garfield

San Sebastián-CAA Media Finance Creative Investors Conference

Popular on Variety

From 2022, speakers like Roeg Sutherland, Patrick Wachsberger, Vincent Maraval and Neon’s Sarah Colvin have laid it on the line on how to confront challenges in the U.S. (cost, contracting budgets, unreliable tax breaks) and Europe (most recently, the need to scale), plus more promisingly, an evolution in U.S. theatrical audiences. Speakers this year take in execs from Acme AI & FX, Black Bear International, Media Capital Technologies, Mubi, Neon, Studiocanal and Sumerian Pictures, the Larraín brothers and Rodrigo Teixeira. Topics include the New U.S. Landscape, Europe’s Current Challenges & Opportunities and Vincent Maraval’s Insights from Goodfellas.

Spain Has Never Had It Better

In 2024, the last year for which figures are available, global streamers poured €2.0 billion ($2.3 billion) into Spain, €0.8 billion ($0.9 billion) into France, €0.7 million ($0.8 billion) into Germany, according to the European Audiovisual Observatory. Spain made 423 features last year, France 228: Cannes Marché du Film Focus report estimates. In TV, Netflix Spain has just shepherded the Mallorca shoot, much in the Mallorquín local language, of “Rafa,” the first non-English language series to score a Primetime Emmy nomination. “Spanish Cinema has never been more powerful, with so many international titles,” says San Sebastián Festival Director José Luis Rebordinos. That power plays out across the whole festival.

‘La Bola Negra,’ San Sebastian’s Biggest Movie

One case in point: It’s a mark of synergies struck between festivals that the biggest title at San Sebastián, at least for local audiences, already played at Cannes: the French Festival’s biggest Oscar contender, “La Bola Negra,” a Movistar Plus Original. “We’re being flooded with requests for tickets and we haven’t even announced its screening date, let alone opened sales,” Rebordinos told Variety late August. Launching its first movie slate, SVOD-pay TV Movistar Plus talked about backing event auteur films. In “La Bola Negra,” from Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, it has its biggest yet.

Spain’s Finest Hour at San Sebastián

And another: San Sebastián’s Made in Spain, its recent Spanish standouts strand, framed an average 11 films over 2018-22. In 2026, it will showcase 24 including Pedro Almodovar’s “Bitter Christmas” and Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s “The Beloved” (though the both have opened in Spain). Playing out of competition are “After Society,” J.A. Bayona’s follow up to “Society of the Snow,” and Oscar winner Fernando Trueba’s country-hopping “Bajañí.” “Flamenco Sketches,” from double San Sebastián Golden Shell winner Isaki Lacuesta, bows in Zabaltegi.

Buzz Titles & Discoveries

There’s big expectation for the world premiere of “Les Miserables,” an epic, but more realistic thriller take on the classic from Fred Cavayé and Studiocanal. Michaël R. Roskam’s fest closer “Le Faux Soir” and series “El Castillo” count among buzz titles. As for new directors, there’s good word on titles from Japan’s Maha Harada (“In My Father’s Room”) in competition and in New Directors pics from Norway’s Marlene Emile Lyngstad (“Cute”), Brit Billy Lumby (Florid”), Kazakh Anna Nurdinova (“Mugalim) and Mexico’s Rodrigo García Saiz (“Morro”). Anybody who hasn’t caught Clara Simón’s sensational “Flamenco” has a chance to do so on Monday, with the director in attendance.

Pablo Larráin, Benjamín Naishat

“I’m convinced that in 10 years time Rodrigo Sorogoyen and Los Javis will be among the most important directors in the world,” says Rebordinos. Another Spanish-language filmmaker, Chile’s Pablo Larraín, has arguably already made the grade. The director of “Jackie,” “Spencer” and “Maria” has at San Sebastián the world premiere of “My Sad Dead,” a movie format presentation of the Netflix TV series and one of the buzziest of competition contenders. Naishtat segues from Toronto with “Glaxo,” packing a scene-stealing turn by Lali Espósito. “She reminds me of the stars of classic Hollywood studios cinema,” says Rebordinos.

Lali Espósito in ‘Glaxo’ Courtesy of RT Features, Rei Pictures

One of San Sebastián’s Big Questions

This July, Movistar Plus, behind “The New Years,” “La Mesías” and “Querer,” announced it will double Spanish original series production from 8 to 16 a year, co-producing or acquiring 10 more. “Movistar Plus is still the foremost home for Spanish creativity. We aim to build even more on that sense of local ambition, but looking for titles with international relevance,” Movistar Plus Contents Director Juan Andrés García Ropero “Bropi” tells Variety. In films, Movistar Plus also co-produced ““Sirāt,” “The Beloved” and “La bola negra.” The industry will be looking for hints at San Sebastián as to Movistar Plus’ movie production roadmap.

Basque Cinema’s Newest Generation

There’s no Basque film in main competition this year, which is quite unusual, down from three titles in 2025. That’s not to say that there aren’t notable Basque films. Historical serial killer thriller “The Harvester,” from the rated David Pérez Sañudo (“Ane is Missing”), weighs in as one of the biggest Basque films ever made. Igor Legarreta’s “Blind Ants” is another calling card for Basque Country production standards. There’s good word on “The Last Goodbye,” Koldo Almandoz (“Mouths of Sand”), one of the most distinctive of Basque auteurs, plus Javier Giner’s “This Solitude” in New Directors and Nitya López Saitua’s “Family Drill” in Zinemira, first features from a newer generation of Basque directors whose ranks are fast swelling.

José Luis Rebordinos’s Swan Song

When Rebordinos appeared on stage this July at Madrid’s Academia de Cine to present San Sebastian’s Spanish titles, the industry-press audience got to its feet to a man and woman to deliver him a standing ovation. Few festival directors have proved so popular. Among his achievements since 2010: Stability, sponsors, a battling candor on hot-button issues, an industry build and the vision to frame and help drive Spain’s emergence as one of Europe’s key film-TV powers. Rebordinos’ Madrid tribute will not be his last. With Maileen Beloki, his successor from Jan. 2027, a member of Rebordinos’ team from 2016, expect evolution not revolution: You don’t tear down one of the loveliest festivals in the world.

José Luis Rebordinos

title: ZDF Boards BBC Drama ‘Shy & Lola’ Featuring ‘Harry Potter’ & ‘Night Manager’ Stars
summary: EXCLUSIVE: German network ZDF has boarded the BBC’s upcoming drama Shy & Lola starring Harry Potter’s Bel Powley and The Night Manager’s Hayley Squires. ZDFneo is now aboard in association with the series from Baby Reindeer maker Clerkenwell Films and Amanda Coe, which stars Squires and Powley as the titular characters. They are two very […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: German network ZDF has boarded the BBC’s upcoming drama Shy & Lola starring Harry Potter’s Bel Powley and The Night Manager’s Hayley Squires.

ZDFneo is now aboard in association with the series from Baby Reindeer maker Clerkenwell Films and Amanda Coe, which stars Squires and Powley as the titular characters. They are two very different women who are forced to become allies when a murder entangles them in the criminal underworld operating in Shy’s small coastal town in the North of England. Beginning as exploited novices, the unlikely duo turn out to have a talent for crime.

Squires plays a cleaner scraping by and dreaming of a new life in Portugal while Powley is an ex-model-turned-grifter who arrives in town with trouble at her heels. I, Daniel Blake star Squires plays Sally Price-Jones in The Night Manager for the BBC and Prime Video, which will air Season 3 soon, while Powley can soon be seen playing Aunt Petunia in HBO’s Harry Potter.

Watch on Deadline

Shy & Lola is the latest show to involve both the BBC and ZDF as the pair solidify a partnership. They have a high-end drama pact together already, which has produced the likes of Killing Eve origin story Honey, although we understand Shy & Lola is not part of this official pact. A Good Girl’s Guide to Murder is another show the pair have worked on together, along with the upcoming The Reluctant Vampire.

BBC Studios also has a long-term partnership with ZDF and will be selling Shy & Lola along with Channel 4’s Break Clause, which is also being co-produced with ZDF.

Shy & Lola will be one of BBC Studios’ key shows at MIPCOM next month. It was revealed to Deadline on a hefty slate by BBC drama boss Lindsay Salt several months back, who has previously said Coe’s “superb scripts will surprise and amuse viewers in equal measure.”

title: A+E Global Media Backs Lifetime Korea Series ‘Oh! My Guard’ Starring K-Pop Performer Jung Yong-hwa & Hong Seung-hee
summary: EXCLUSIVE: A+E Global Media is backing Lifetime Korea series Oh! My Guard starring K-pop performer Jung Yong-hwa and rising star Hong Seung-hee. With A+E prioritizing Korea, the studio is investing in and globally distributing Oh! My Guard, which has been licensed for release in 83 countries including to Asian streamer Viu. Launching next month on […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: A+E Global Media is backing Lifetime Korea series Oh! My Guard starring K-pop performer Jung Yong-hwa and rising star Hong Seung-hee.

With A+E prioritizing Korea, the studio is investing in and globally distributing Oh! My Guard, which has been licensed for release in 83 countries including to Asian streamer Viu.

Launching next month on Lifetime Korea, Oh! My Guard follows Um Tae-bong, a melodramatic star with a devastating secret, and a woman who, after an accident, comes to believe she is the heroine of his drama, setting the stage for an unpredictable romance.

A+E said it “recognized the series’ potential to bring together the nuanced emotional storytelling associated with Korean dramas, the buoyant pace of romantic comedy and the international fandom surrounding Korean actors and K-pop stars.”

Watch on Deadline

Jung Yong-hwa has amassed a big following as a member of K-pop band CNBLUE, while Hong Seung-hee has appeared in the likes of Just Dance, Navillera and Move to Heaven.

Produced by Syn & Studio and People Story Company, Oh! My Guard is penned by Byun Sang-soon and directed by Yoon Jong-ho and Lee Seung-hoon. Yoon Jong-ho recently made hit K-drama Lovely Runner.

A+E Korea MD Youngsun Soh said: “We are thrilled to bring Oh! My Guard to audiences around the world. From the outset, we were drawn to its inventive premise, the fresh pairing of Jung Yong-hwa and Hong Seung-hee, and director Yoon Jong-ho’s sophisticated direction.”

A+E will be selling the show at MIPCOM Cannes. Last year it rebranded from A+E Networks.

title: ‘Resident Evil’ Scaring Up Franchise Best Previews With $8M-$9M & Rotten Tomatoes 91% Audience Score
summary: Buckle up your 4DX seat because it’s gonna be a fun weekend as out of the gate, Zach Cregger’s take on Resident Evil is already posting the best previews ever for the franchise with tonight north of $8M and maybe even north of $9M. The outlook going into the weekend was $40M-$50M. Those who are […]
content:
Buckle up your 4DX seat because it’s gonna be a fun weekend as out of the gate, Zach Cregger‘s take on Resident Evil is already posting the best previews ever for the franchise with tonight north of $8M and maybe even north of $9M.

The outlook going into the weekend was $40M-$50M. Those who are smart, inside the industry and study ticket sales believe the movie has a shot to go over $50M.

Similar to how this Resident Evil is posting the series best critical score on Rotten Tomatoes (now at 96% certified fresh), so is it posting the best audience score as well at 91%. On Rotten Tomatoes, the previous best audience score belonged to the original 2002 film at 67%.

Previews for the Sony/Constantin R-rated feature adaptation of the Capcom video game began at 2PM stateside.

Watch on Deadline

Tonight’s estimated take easily decimates the franchise’s previous high (which wasn’t much), 2016’s Resident Evil: Final Chapter at $1M. That was the first time a Resident Evil movie posted seven digits in its previews.

But get a load of this: Resident Evil‘s previews even on the low-end of $8M scorch Cregger’s Weapons ($5.75M previews, $43.5M opening), Scream 7 (yes, $7.8M, $63.6M opening, but put a pin in that one), Mortal Kombat 2 ($5.2M, $38.5M, a Midway video game adapted into an R-rated franchise), Sonic the Hedgehog 3 ($6.5M, $60.1M; yes, we know that’s a family film, but it’s based on a video game. Calm down).

Here’s the thing, the Friday/preview-to-Saturday holds for some previous Resident Evil movies are pretty good with The Final Chapter +1.4% between those two days, the original 2002 movie +1%, and Resident Evil: Afterlife -9%, that pic holding the series previous domestic opening record at $26.6M). The point is, because it’s horror, and because it’s a different iteration of Resident Evil from the previous Milla Jovovich films, the wait-and-see is just how front loaded this movie is. Scream 7 was a completely different animal in the return of Neve Campbell to the franchise and tracking sources tonight advise not to comp Resident Evil to that horror pic (at least not yet). It was Cregger’s vision here to make a more authentic adaptation of the games which he has avidly played.

The net $75M Constantin/Sony production of Resident Evil is playing in PLFs and Imax, with the latter format’s 70MM still on a crusade with The Odyssey (about 35 auditoriums).

Tonight’s figures come from distribution sources, not the studio, so take everything with a grain of salt.

title: Werner Herzog and Orlando Bloom on ‘Bucking Fastard’ and That Threesome Scene With the Mara Sisters: ‘It Has Such Charm and Depth’
summary: While speaking at the San Sebastián Film Festival, where they are presenting “Bucking Fastard,” renowned German director Werner Herzog and the film’s star Orlando Bloom spoke about a threesome scene between the “Pirates of the Caribbean” actor and Rooney and Kate Mara, who lead Herzog’s latest as two deeply intertwined sisters. Asked about the scene, […]
content:
While speaking at the San Sebastián Film Festival, where they are presenting “Bucking Fastard,” renowned German director Werner Herzog and the film’s star Orlando Bloom spoke about a threesome scene between the “Pirates of the Caribbean” actor and Rooney and Kate Mara, who lead Herzog’s latest as two deeply intertwined sisters.

Asked about the scene, Bloom said there is “such simplicity to the characters and [their] carnal desires, but also an innocence to the sisters.” “My character, the Bucking Fastard, is sensitive too. And he’s quite quickly out of his depth in some ways. It was a very sincere sort of moment that was created.”

“There are moments when a director has to step back,” Herzog jumped in to say. “In the love scene, I said to Orlando: ‘You are in bed, and you have two women in your arms. How you deal with it, I cannot give instructions.’ It is beautiful because it has such charm and depth.”

Popular on Variety

Despite having world-premiered his latest less than two weeks ago, prolific director Werner Herzog, who is also a recipient of this year’s Donostia Awards at San Sebastián, is only days away from wrapping his next project. “Three days, and I’ll have my next film finished,” he said. “On Monday, I am back to work.”

Herzog did not go into further details about the next project, but one could speculate he is referring to “The Twilight World,” an animated adaptation of his eponymous book that tells the story of a Japanese intelligence officer who defended a small Filipino island for 29 years after the end of World War II. The director also noted he is currently writing two books and continues to work on scripts for future projects.

Courtesy of Gateway to Orkney, Venice Film Festival

The director also spoke about the dangers of the rise of AI and new technologies. “We have to defend our souls against encroachment from outside,” he said. “This is why I would be very clear with very young people around their cellphones all the time. Do not live a life that is dictated by algorithms to keep your attention. Why don’t you dig a hole in the ground? Why don’t you build a little house on a tree? The moment the world starts to occupy our souls, you have to be very vigilant. Now with AI, it’s coming big time at us.”

Herzog’s name was intertwined in debates around artificial intelligence given the release of Piotr Winiewicz’s “About a Hero,” an experimental film that saw the Polish director feed Herzog’s sprawling body of work into an AI bot and then shoot the resulting script. The film also created an AI-generated version of Herzog’s characteristic voice. The German director recently called the film “phenomenally, abysmally stupid.”

Back to “Bucking Fastard,” the director cut off a journalist who referred to the film’s long gestation as an “obsession.” “I do not like the word obsession,” he said firmly. “Do you see an obsessed man here? I’m totally relaxed. If you have an obsessive director, actors will run away, producers will run away. You have to run away from yourself if you’re obsessive, and I’m not, period.”

“I have many a good story in me,” he added when speaking about what keeps him going as a filmmaker. Offering a metaphor of stories as burglars invading his house, the director said he usually tackles the intruder that poses the most serious threat. “Whatever comes with real vehemence at me, that’s what I’m dealing with. And I’m never afraid, whatever it might be.”

Herzog gushed about Bloom. The actor plays the titular character in a way: a charming sweet talker who becomes romantically involved with the Maras’ Holbrooke sisters. The director noted how Bloom “left behind what he is famous for: the heartthrob for the teenies.”

“You have to step into a new arena, play different parts,” he recalled telling the actor once they met. To emphasize this breakthrough, Herzog asked Bloom to grow a beard and make his character more “manly.” “It had to be distinct, a new terrain. It is a very interesting transition, and I will keep an eye on what [Bloom is] doing in the future.”

“When I look at Orlando’s career, he’s famous everywhere in the world, but a part of how he’s now navigating what is coming at him, I have the feeling that time is on his side, so wait for what’s coming,” he continued. “I am very, very curious. There will be beautiful stuff coming from him. I am totally convinced.”

Bloom was also praiseful, calling working with Herzog a “bucket list item.” “What I love about ‘Bucking Fastard’ is that it refuses to judge its characters and offer any kind of easy answers. That is something that Werner focused on. It was wonderful to work with Kate and Rooney; I’ve been a long admirer of both of them. We had a lot of fun in Dublin. It was a great experience and certainly a bucket-list opportunity to work with someone like Werner and such a phenomenal cast.”

title: ’Dungeon Crawler Carl’ Sets Limited Edition, Free CGC Comic Book Drop for New York Comic Con (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Attention, Crawlers! Collectibles grading company CGC is teaming up with “Dungeon Crawler Carl” author Matt Dinniman for the release of a free exclusive variant cover of his comic book series at New York Comic Con next month. From Oct. 8-11, CGC will offer a limited-edition Dungeon Crawler Carl #0 variant featuring new commissioned artwork by […]
content:
Attention, Crawlers! Collectibles grading company CGC is teaming up with “Dungeon Crawler Carl” author Matt Dinniman for the release of a free exclusive variant cover of his comic book series at New York Comic Con next month.

From Oct. 8-11, CGC will offer a limited-edition Dungeon Crawler Carl #0 variant featuring new commissioned artwork by “The Mask” and “Aliens” artist Doug Mahnke at its NYCC booth.

Adapted from Dinniman’s bestselling litRPG novel series of the same name and published as a webcomic and in print through Vault Comics, the “Dungeon Crawler Carl” comic book is a post-apocalyptic story that follows Carl and his ex-girlfriend’s cat, Princess Donut, as they’re thrust into a deadly, game-show-style dungeon where survival depends on wit, grit and leveling up fast.

Popular on Variety

“Comics are still new to me, and it’s surreal to see all these awesome artists coming together to make badass art in the DCC universe,” Dinniman said. “Doug’s cover stands out, and I’m forever grateful an artist like that wants to work on something I created.”

CGC and JSA return to NYCC this year as the convention’s official grading and authentication services. Per CGC, fans submitting eligible collectibles to CGC for grading at the brand’s NYCC booth (CGC Booth #2805, CGC Signature Series & JSA Booth #HB906) will be able to receive the exclusive “Carl” variant for free, limited to one per person while supplies lasts.

“We’re giving this variant away because we want the fans who’ve followed Dungeon Crawler Carl from the beginning to be the ones who get it first,” CGC’s vice president of comic book grading Shawn Caffrey said. “That’s always been the idea behind our program — put incredible art directly into collectors’ hands, free, and let them be part of the moment a series like this breaks wide open.”

Con-goers will be able to pick one of three options between the “Carl” comic book and two new variants of “Absolute Batman” #24 featuring original artwork. Written by Scott Snyder with art by Nick Dragotta, “Absolute Batman” reimagines Bruce Wayne as a younger Dark Knight without the Wayne fortune, forcing Batman to rely on ingenuity, determination, and sheer physicality.

Additionally, CGC is also introducing a new “Dungeon Crawler Carl” custom label that will be available beginning Sept. 22 for “Dungeon Crawler Carl” comic book submissions.

News of the CGC-“Dungeon Crawler Carl” collab comes amid intense popularity for the book series, which is now in the works as a TV show at Peacock.

“It’s awesome to see people collecting stuff based on my world,” Dinniman said. It’s humbling to know people are actually interested in collecting them and keeping them to display.”

See below for Variety‘s Q&A with CGC’s Caffrey about the collaboration.

How did the partnership come about?

Caffrey: CGC has spent the last couple of years building a tradition of giving away exclusive, free variant covers to fans at San Diego Comic-Con and New York Comic Con, including a Superman #680 variant from Dan Mora and an Avengers #31 variant from Peach Momoko, among several other fan-favorite artists.

For New York Comic Con, artist representative Jon Jespersen approached CGC about working with acclaimed artist Doug Mahnke on a variant cover. With the incredible buzz surrounding “Dungeon Crawler Carl,” we saw an opportunity to do something especially fun for fans of the series. Jon shared an initial concept art-directed by his wife, Sarah, a longtime “Dungeon Crawler Carl” fan, and with Doug’s artwork and colors by David Baron, we knew we had something special.

We’re thrilled to bring the “Dungeon Crawler Carl” variant to New York Comic Con and to have both Doug Mahnke and David Baron signing for free at the CGC booth during the show.

What was the process like working with Matt Dinniman on the art? Fans know these characters so well already that remaining text accurate while also having artistic license could be difficult.

Doug approached the cover with a real respect for Matt’s world – the characters, the tone, and all of those details “Dungeon Crawler Carl” fans know so well. That gave him the foundation to bring his own distinctive artistic style to the cover while still making it feel unmistakably DCC. David Baron’s colors really bring the finished piece to life, and we think fans are going to love what they created together.

“Dungeon Crawler Carl” #0 has already been released, but this will be the first opportunity for fans to get a Doug Mahnke “DCC” variant. That makes being able to debut it at New York Comic Con especially exciting.

What made NYCC the right time for this collaboration, and are there plans for more?

Issue #0 launched right alongside a huge wave of momentum for “Dungeon Crawler Carl,” and issue #1 comes out right after the show, so NYCC felt like the perfect moment to put this variant directly into fans’ hands. It also fits the model we’ve built with artists like Peach Momoko and Dan Mora: giving devoted collectors free access to premium variant art rather than charging for it. At the end of the day, a lot of us on this side of the business are the same fans we’re serving — we read the novels, we love this world, and we collect what we love, so of course we want to be part of the moment it becomes a comic. Our booths are always popular at fan fests like Comic Con and we expect this year at New York to be no different. If you look at all the trending novels for Audible and all the best books of the year, “DCC” is right there topping the charts with numerous books fighting for the top spot. And we’re also excited to see “DCC” as a live-action series on Peacock.

We are looking forward to potentially more collaborations with the “DCC” franchise and the creator himself. There are no plans locked in yet, but Doug and David will be signing at our booth during the show, and we see this as a great first step. We’d love for this relationship with the “Dungeon Crawler Carl” world to keep growing.

title: Fan Bingbing on Toronto and Busan Selection ‘Diary of a Mad Old Man’ and Her International Ambitions: ‘Cinema Should Be Able to Cross Borders’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Chinese superstar Fan Bingbing’s latest role puts her at the center of an unusual dynamic: a Chinese caregiver drawn into the fixation of an aging, stroke-paralyzed Japanese widower. “Diary of a Mad Old Man,” Wayne Wang’s adaptation of Tanizaki Jun’ichirō’s 1961 novel, is having its world premiere at the Toronto Film Festival in the gala […]
content:
Chinese superstar Fan Bingbing‘s latest role puts her at the center of an unusual dynamic: a Chinese caregiver drawn into the fixation of an aging, stroke-paralyzed Japanese widower.

“Diary of a Mad Old Man,” Wayne Wang‘s adaptation of Tanizaki Jun’ichirō’s 1961 novel, is having its world premiere at the Toronto Film Festival in the gala presentations section. The film is also a selection at the Busan International Film Festival.

Over a four-decade career, Wang’s credits include “Chan Is Missing” (1982), “The Joy Luck Club” (1993) and “Smoke,” which won the Silver Bear Grand Jury Prize at the 1995 Berlinale.

Popular on Variety

Fan plays Susu, daughter-in-law and sole caregiver to Utsugi (Lily Franky). She describes Susu’s position as complicated — someone with real influence over Utsugi, but also vulnerable and dependent on the family around her.

The actor resists framing her character as either predator or victim. “I don’t think Susu is someone who is simply trying to control Utsugi,” she says. “She understands the influence she has over him, but in many ways, she is also vulnerable and dependent on the family.” For Fan, the power at stake is less about domination than survival: a woman working with whatever leverage her circumstances allow her. Rather than settling the question of who is using whom, Fan says she was more drawn to the emotional exchange between two people who both need something from each other.

That refusal to settle on a single reading extends to how Fan and Franky calibrated the relationship’s tone on set. Working closely with Wang to find the right register, the two actors treated the bond as something built on desire and imagination rather than conventional physical intimacy, letting Susu’s willingness to draw close or pull away shift scene to scene so no single interpretation of the relationship ever hardens into place. “There is tenderness, desire, dependency and also discomfort,” Fan says. “All of these things can exist together.”

Tanizaki’s original Susu is a deliberately provocative figure, and Fan says she wanted to hold onto that boldness and mystery while giving the character more visible wounds. “I wanted the audience to see that behind her provocative side, there is also loneliness and vulnerability,” she says. “She is not simply one thing.”

Lily Franky, Fan Bingbing – “Diary of a Mad Old Man” Toronto Film Festival

Susu’s identity as a Chinese woman inside a Japanese family, itself a departure from Tanizaki’s original text, became one of the production’s more pointed choices. Fan says the character’s outsider status shaped how she approached nearly every scene, drawing a direct line between Susu’s position and her own experience working across borders. “When you enter another culture, you are always observing: how people communicate, what they don’t say, the relationships, etc.,” she says. “Sometimes being an outsider makes you more sensitive to these things.”

Wang, who has built much of his career around characters moving between cultures, never pushed Fan to play Susu as Japanese, she says. Instead, he encouraged her to draw on her own instincts, having spent years navigating multiple cultures himself and understanding the particular feeling of being inside a culture while still observing it from the outside.

Fan says a woman like Susu today occupies a different social position, with more awareness of her own choices, than a woman would have had in the early 1960s. “So I didn’t want to approach her sexuality as something that automatically makes her immoral or provocative,” she says. “She understands her body, her attractiveness and the effect she has on Utsugi, and I think she has the right to have that awareness.”

At the same time, she says, being a modern woman doesn’t mean being completely free. “Financial dependence, family expectations, loneliness and unequal relationships still exist today,” Fan says. That contradiction is what interested her most: Susu has agency, but she also has limitations.

Fan says she deliberately avoided deciding, even for herself, how Susu truly feels about Utsugi at any given moment. She didn’t want to resolve for audiences whether Susu loves him, pities him, uses him or feels some combination of all three at once. “Human emotions are rarely completely pure or simple,” she says. “I hope everyone can have their own interpretation of her.”

The part marks a sharp departure from the large-scale Chinese productions and star-driven roles that have long defined Fan’s public image. At this stage of her career, she says she’s more concerned with whether a character moves her than whether it fits any particular image of her, adding that she still wants to discover parts of herself she hasn’t shown before. She says she enjoys roles that let audiences forget they’re watching Fan Bingbing and simply see the character.

The role continues a run of international collaborations Fan has built since 2023, when “Green Night,” directed by Han Shuai, premiered in the Panorama section of the Berlin Film Festival. In 2025, she starred as a shamanistic healer in Chong Keat Aun’s Malaysian period drama “Mother Bhumi,” which premiered in the main competition of the Tokyo International Film Festival, picked up eight nominations at the Golden Horse Awards and won her best leading actress. “For me it is not about choosing international cinema over Chinese cinema,” she says. “I simply want to work with good filmmakers and good stories, wherever they come from.”

On what she is looking for next, Fan says the scale of a production matters less to her than the strength of a filmmaker’s voice and whether a character offers her something she hasn’t played before. “For me, cinema should be able to cross borders,” she says. “If there is a filmmaker with a unique vision and a story that truly moves me, wherever they come from, I would love to work with them.”

“Diary of a Mad Old Man” also stars Saito Takumi and Kudoh Youki.

title: ‘Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift’ Ride Opens to Thrill Fans at Universal Studios Hollywood
summary: Fans yearning to drive like Dominic Toretto or Letty can finally strap into a Dodge Charger or a Toyota Supra at Universal Studios Hollywood, as the long-awaited “Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift” ride officially opened Sept. 16 at the park. The much-anticipated outdoor roller coaster features four iconic cars from the $7 billion franchise — […]
content:
Fans yearning to drive like Dominic Toretto or Letty can finally strap into a Dodge Charger or a Toyota Supra at Universal Studios Hollywood, as the long-awaited “Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift” ride officially opened Sept. 16 at the park.

The much-anticipated outdoor roller coaster features four iconic cars from the $7 billion franchise — the Dodge Charger, Mazda RX-7, Nissan Skyline GT-R and the Toyota Supra — that propel riders on a “unique dual-launching, split-ride track,” according to Universal Studios Hollywood. The cars spiral over and under portions of the park’s multilevel escalator, and include four launches, an inverted dive loop, twisted pretzel loop, an inverted stall and other thrills, reaching speed of 72 mph. Riders experience force of up to 3.6 Gs along 4,100 feet of aerial track constructed with sound-reduction technology while drifting at 360-degrees in their individual ride vehicles, according to Universal Studios Hollywood.

“Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift’ is officially open, and we are so excited to be able to put guests in the driver’s seat of one of the most celebrated film franchises in history,” said Scott Strobl, executive VP and general manager, Universal Studios Hollywood. “The debut of this first-of-it-kind roller coaster is a literal game changer for Universal Studios Hollywood, and we look forward to sharing this thrilling experience with fans of the ‘Fast’ saga and our guests visiting from around the world.”

Popular on Variety

The ride is anchored by an original mural created by artist Tristan Eaton, which depicts the finale street racing action scene in 2001’s “The Fast and the Furious,” the film that kicked off the franchise, which is celebrating its 25th anniversary this year.

title: Japan’s Top Broadcasters Unite for First Joint Delegation to MipCancun (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Ten major Japanese broadcasters are joining forces for the first time to send a joint delegation to MipCancun, marking the country’s first coordinated television market presence outside Asia. The “All-Japan” initiative is organized under the Japan Commercial Broadcasters Association (JBA) in collaboration with Japan’s Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) and the Broadcast Program […]
content:
Ten major Japanese broadcasters are joining forces for the first time to send a joint delegation to MipCancun, marking the country’s first coordinated television market presence outside Asia.

The “All-Japan” initiative is organized under the Japan Commercial Broadcasters Association (JBA) in collaboration with Japan’s Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) and the Broadcast Program Export Association of Japan (BEAJ). JBA represents commercial broadcasters operating television and/or radio services across the country, and the initiative is designed to promote Japanese IP and expand business opportunities across the Latin American content market. MIP Cancun is marking its 13th edition this year.

The delegation includes Tokyo-based key stations TBS Television, Nippon TV, TV Asahi, Fuji Television Network, Inc. and TV Tokyo, along with Wowow Inc., BS Asahi, Tokai TV, MBS, Inc. and Yomiuri Telecasting Corp. A dedicated Japan Pavilion will be set up within the market’s matchmaking zone, giving each company its own table for meetings with Latin American buyers.

Popular on Variety

While Japan remains best known internationally for anime, the delegation will emphasize live-action content, particularly television drama, a category the Japanese government is now specifically targeting for overseas growth.

“As IP development and co-productions become increasingly vital in the entertainment market, the industry is reaching a major turning point,” said Maria Perez Bellière, director of MipCancun. “We have high expectations for this initiative to introduce the appeal of Japan’s new content and firmly establish the ‘Japan brand’ in Latin American countries, with whom Japan shares a long history. We are deeply honored that Japan has united to leverage the unique Latin American market opportunities that MipCancun has spent 13 years building here in Cancun.”

A “Japan Content Showcase” screening event will run Nov. 18 in the Cancun Theater Room, spotlighting programming from the participating broadcasters with a focus on Japanese drama for Latin American industry professionals. A networking cocktail reception will follow, giving the visiting companies and local buyers additional time to talk business.

The push into Latin America comes as the Japanese government has named the content industry one of the country’s core growth sectors. Tokyo has set a target of expanding the overseas market for Japanese-origin content from JPY5.8 trillion ($37 billion) in 2023 to JPY20 trillion ($129 billion) by 2033, with a specific target of JPY0.5 trillion ($3.2 billion) for live-action content overseas by 2033.

Latin America brings its own long history of serialized television drama, rooted in telenovelas that have been produced across the region since the 1950s and have traveled widely across borders. The continued growth of streaming in the region is also opening new pathways for international scripted content to reach audiences.

Organizers frame the delegation as a way for Japanese networks to strike deals with Latin American buyers, distributors and producers when the market runs in November.

MipCancun is a content market and conference serving Latin American and U.S. Hispanic television, bringing together acquisition, distribution and production companies to close content deals in the region’s growing TV markets.

title: Fatih Akin On How A Period Of Professional Crisis Inspired His Paranormal Love Story ‘Ghost Song’ — San Sebastian
summary: This evening, Spain’s San Sebastian Film Festival opens with Ghost Song, the latest feature from German filmmaker Fatih Akin. The screening marks Akin’s first appearance at the festival in his decades-long career, a surprising fact considering his strong presence on the festival circuit: Akin is among the rare group of directors to win major competitive […]
content:
This evening, Spain’s San Sebastian Film Festival opens with Ghost Song, the latest feature from German filmmaker Fatih Akin. The screening marks Akin’s first appearance at the festival in his decades-long career, a surprising fact considering his strong presence on the festival circuit: Akin is among the rare group of directors to win major competitive prizes at Berlin, Cannes, and Venice.

“They previously passed on a film of mine,” Akin says, with a smile, about his long absence from the Spanish festival during an interview with Deadline ahead of this evening’s screening.

Directed from a screenplay he co-wrote with Ruth Toma, Ghost Song tells the story of Farasha and Faris, two young teens, who meet at a graduation party and fall in love at first sight. When Farasha suddenly dies that same night, a paranormal love story unfolds as Farasha discovers that, for 40 nights, she can meet Faris in his dreams. Their love continues to grow until the very last night.

Watch on Deadline

Presented on a bold black-and-white print, Ghost Song is an earnest and spiritually rich film that Akin says was born out of a period of crisis in his career.

“Around 10 years ago, I made a film. It was very ambitious and expensive. I worked on it for many years. I really strongly believed in what I was doing, but sometimes it doesn’t go the way you wish, and I crashed hard,” Akin says.

The filmmaker politely declined to name the feature that pushed him into his period of crisis, but it is a safe bet to assume it was 2014’s The Cut, which won an award at Venice but was divisive among critics and struggled at the box office.

“That was the first time that I had such a crash. And when you experience that, you doubt everything: your talent, lifestyle, everything,” he says. “You almost have to reinvent yourself.”

Akin explains that this is when his son pitched him an idea about a story featuring two young adults. Akin took the idea to Toma, and the pair hashed out a story that would become Ghost Song.

The film is led by Eren M. Güvercin, a German-born actor with credits on titles across German television, and the fantastic Mariam Dawoud, a Syrian-born refugee currently living in Austria, who makes her screen debut in the title.

Akin explains that Dawoud was discovered following an open call on social media, which surprisingly didn’t garner many applicants.

“They made an announcement on social media looking for native Arab speaking girls for a love story. And because of religion, and our current conservative world, not so many popped up,” he says. “We saw many fewer than we hoped or expected, maybe only 20, but Mariam immediately nailed the scene.”

Akin describes Ghost Song as a “very tough” shoot and his most complex production to date. The film features a large open water scene. It was also originally shot in color and was flipped to black-and-white in post-production after Akin was unhappy with the color grading in an early cut.

“I was so frustrated. Everything was so pale. Nothing worked conceptually,” Akin says. “My DP said, ‘Have patience.’ But that’s one thing I’m not. I’m not patient. I don’t have that talent.”

Akin and his DP, Frank Griebe, proceeded to produce both color and black-and-white cuts of the film.

“I was so much over budget,” Akin jokes, adding that both copies of the film will be distributed.

Moving forward, however, the veteran filmmaker says that he plans to move away from work that requires him to build elaborate productions.

“I know this industry is about money, but what comes after? Just more money and higher budgets? There must be another way,” Akin says.

“I’m 53 now. I don’t want to make it more complex. I don’t want to make it more expensive. There must be another way, like how John Cassavetes used to work. I want to find a more humble way to work, because I’m searching for the truth, and that doesn’t come with a higher budget. That is all just a distraction.”

Ghost Song will be distributed by Warner Bros. under Akin’s first-look deal with the studio. The pact was first announced in 2022, and Akin says the two parties remain in business. He is not particularly concerned by the chaos of David Ellison’s messy Warnermount merger.

“They are great partners. They have made some of the most important films in cinema history: Casablanca, Dog Day Afternoon, Mean Streets. And the two best American films of last year, Sinners and One Battle After Another,” Akin says of Warners.

“When I first signed with them, it was Time Warner, and then AT&T, and then Discovery. I’ve survived all of these different companies, and they still let me do what I want, so all I can do is take the chance.”

Akin continues: “Let’s see what happens and if I feel happy and comfortable.”

In previous interviews, Akin has joked that his hometown of Hamburg is the perfect base for a filmmaker because it is boring and allows him to focus on his work. As such, the filmmaker is already working on his next project. He was tight-lipped about what the project will be, but he confirmed what the project won’t include.

“I’m not shooting it in Hamburg. And it won’t be in the German or English language,” he says.

Ghost Song debuts this evening in San Sebastian.

Check out the film’s official trailer above.

title: ‘Musk’: Was Universal Getting Cold Feet Over Releasing Alex Gibney Doc?
summary: A couple days ago a THR report claimed that Universal was getting cold feet over releasing Alex Gibney’s Musk documentary in international territories. Despite the film opening theatrically in the U.S. in a few weeks (via Bleecker Street), no international dates had been revealed. The filmmakers were surprised and a little concerned, according to the […]
content:
A couple days ago a THR report claimed that Universal was getting cold feet over releasing Alex Gibney’s Musk documentary in international territories.

Despite the film opening theatrically in the U.S. in a few weeks (via Bleecker Street), no international dates had been revealed. The filmmakers were surprised and a little concerned, according to the report.

Last night, a spokesperson for Universal told us and others that the studio has no plans to ditch the film. We’ve now had it confirmed this morning, following Puck’s initial report, that Universal is lining up a Q1, 2027 release.

What to make of the cold feet suggestion? These type of reports don’t usually come out of thin air. I was reminded of our recent exclusive about Venice cancelling its jury press conference, then rowing back on those plans after our story triggered backlash. So, we did some digging.

Watch on Deadline

For reasons I’ll get into, the filmmakers probably had cause to at least question Universal’s commitment. It’s somewhat unusual these days for a high-profile film with an imminent U.S. release not to have any international dates on the calendar.

The reality seems to be that nothing had been firmly decided one way or another. Sources indicated to us yesterday that Universal had been carrying out an internal legal review of the film after getting the final copy of the movie just shortly before its Venice Film Festival world premiere. The studio didn’t deny a legal review to us when we put it to them yesterday.

This review, which is seemingly now complete, probably felt more essential after Musk’s lawyers reportedly sent a legal complaint about the film to Gibney’s production company Jigsaw. Supposedly, the film’s distributors were mentioned in the letter, which was seemingly leaked to the New York Post.

There was also surprise in some quarters that Universal’s logo hadn’t appeared on screen before the film’s launch in Venice. And that the studio had taken an unusually light-touch approach to the film’s international engagements, including press on the Lido. But Uni hadn’t blocked the Venice launch or its announced screening at the London Film Festival. Rather than ditching the movie, the studio was seemingly going through a process to determine whether it faced a legal challenge it didn’t want to grapple with.

The context is also important here and probably speaks to potential filmmaker fears over their politically spicy project being jettisoned. Amazon, which ploughed millions into a fawning Melania Trump movie, recently ditched its Sam Altman biopic, Artificial, about the birth of OpenAI, with whom it has a hugely lucrative AI contract. Trump biopic The Apprentice was avoided by the major studios and then faced significant challenges before release. Even at the arthouse level, lauded films with strong political stances have been shied away from. No Other Land, The Voice Of Hind Rajab, and now NAZA? A chill has descended on Hollywood since Trump came to power with studios and indies increasingly anxious about tackling political and anti-establishment fare. We heard a long time back that at least one significant Hollywood financier detached themselves from Musk when it became clear it wouldn’t be a flattering portrait of its subject.

So, kudos to Bleecker for sticking with the film theatrically stateside. And to Universal for seemingly sticking with the film, which has been reviewed well by critics and comes from one of the great American documentarians. Let’s hope it’s not buried by the studio overseas and it gets its due.

The next and most obvious question is what happens with the film’s U.S. TV and streaming release via HBO. Will Musk-Trump-Ellison politics and connections get in the way of that release? Paramount owner David Ellison is of course in the throes of acquiring Warner Bros and has already proven to be more than amenable to Trump and allies. Puck’s report this morning noted that HBO is also lining up for a Q1 2027 stateside release. We’ve reached out to WBD for confirmation of that.

The home ent plans will be just as telling as the theatrical ones. This project became a home ent play in many ways with HBO initially acquiring it in a splashy U.S. deal and it’s a Universal Pictures Content Group acquisition, rather than big Universal, so home ent was always key. Will it get good play on a TV service like Sky in the UK, for example? We’ll see.

title: Chloë Sevigny Joins HBO’s True-Crime Limited Series ‘The Trial Of Louise Woodward’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Chloë Sevigny (Monsters: The Lyle and Erik Menendez Story) is the newest addition to HBO’s new true-crime limited series, The Trial of Louise Woodward. She joins a cast featuring Catriona Chandler in the title role, which also so far includes Joanne Froggatt, Meghann Fahy and Sagar Radia. Created by Matthew Barry, who serves as […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Chloë Sevigny (Monsters: The Lyle and Erik Menendez Story) is the newest addition to HBO‘s new true-crime limited series, The Trial of Louise Woodward.

She joins a cast featuring Catriona Chandler in the title role, which also so far includes Joanne Froggatt, Meghann Fahy and Sagar Radia.

Created by Matthew Barry, who serves as showrunner, writer and exec producer, The Trial of Louise Woodward tells the shocking true story of how, in 1997, an 18-year-old British au pair (Chandler) was accused of shaking to death a baby left in her care by her American host family, setting off an international media firestorm as the trial unfolds in full view of both the British and American public.

Sevigny is set to play Louise’s defense attorney, Elaine Whitfield Sharp. Froggatt plays Louise’s mother, Susan, with Fahy and Radia as Deborah and Sunil Eappen — parents of the victim, Matthew Eappen.

Watch on Deadline

Other exec producers on The Trial include Susanne Bier, who directs all episodes, as well as Frank Spotnitz, Emily Feller, Tobi de Graaff, and Antoine Douaihy. Big Light Productions and Anton TV are the production companies.

Sevigny can currently be seen starring in Peacock’s drama series The Five-Star Weekend, which quickly secured the streamer’s biggest scripted series launch of all time before being renewed for a second season. Last year, she earned her first Emmy nomination for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Limited Series or Movie for her role of Kitty Menendez in Ryan Murphy’s Monsters: The Lyle and Erik Menendez Story. She is represented by WME and Circle Management + Production.

title: Everything We Know About Prime Video’s ‘Rose Hill’ Series Adaptation So Far
summary: One of Prime Video’s next big book adaptation bets is that on Elsie Silver’s Rose Hill series. The streamer is adapting the contemporary small-town romance into a TV show, which sounds like its in the vein of Netflix’s My Life With the Walter Boys and Ransom Canyon. The cast is currently being assembled with many […]
content:
One of Prime Video’s next big book adaptation bets is that on Elsie Silver’s Rose Hill series. The streamer is adapting the contemporary small-town romance into a TV show, which sounds like its in the vein of Netflix’s My Life With the Walter Boys and Ransom Canyon.

The cast is currently being assembled with many lead roles already established.

Read on for everything we know about Prime Video’s Rose Hill series adaptation so far:

When will Prime Video’s Rose Hill TV series adaptation come out?

A release date has not yet been set for the series’ arrival because it is in early stages of development with casting.

Watch on Deadline

Has Prime Video’s Rose Hill TV series started production?

Not yet, but as stated above, a cast is being assembled.

Who will be in the cast of Prime Video’s Rose Hill adaptation?

Jake Weary (The Waterfront, Animal Kingdom), Sean O’Pry, Hannah Galway (Under the Banner of Heaven) and Sadie Dickerson (Just In Time) have been cast as West Belmont, Ford Grant, Rose and Skylar Stone.

Jake Weary, Sean O’Pry, Hannah Galway and Sadie Dickerson Courtesy/Kate Kondratieva/Calyssa Lorraine/Arden Dickson

American model O’Pry is well known for appearing in the music video for Taylor Swift’s single “Blank Space” off of her 1989 album.

Siobhan McGroarty, Sophia Reid-Gantzert, West Mulholland, Gigi Zumbado, and Curtis Hamilton also recently joined the cast. McGroarty will play Cora, Reid-Gantzert will play Emmy Belmont, and Mulholland will play Oliver Belmont. In recurring guest roles, Zumbado will play Tabitha and Hamilton will portray Bash Rousseau.

Siobhan McGroarty, Sophia Reid-Gantzert, West Mulholland, Gigi Zumbado and Curtis Hamilton

Who else is behind the Rose Hill adaptation at Prime Video? Is Elsie Silver involved in the creation of the series?

Heidi Cole McAdams will serve as showrunner, which was revealed when Amazon announced the news of the adaptation at its upfront presentation in May 2026. Marc Webb will direct the pilot and second episode, and Temple Hill is producing.

Silver also serves as executive producer alongside Wyck Godfrey, Marty Bowen, and James Seidman for Temple Hill. Temple Hill’s Annika Patton will also serve as a co-executive producer.

How many books are in Elsie Silver’s Rose Hill series?

The series consists of four books — Wild Love, Wild Eyes, Wild Side, and Wild Card.

What is Elsie Silver’s Rose Hill book series about?

The story centers rancher with commitment issues West Belmont and brooding record label owner Ford Grant, who are best friends and neighbors. Grant, known as Forbes’ “World’s Hottest Billionaire” has long carried a torch for West’s sister, Rose. Country-pop star Skylar Stone’s entry into the rugged mountain town setting causes ripples in the romantic family drama.
