title: Ukraine War Doc ‘A Simple Soldier’ Getting U.S. & International Release Via Jolt & Propagate
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Jolt is partnering with Propagate Content to support the North America, UK, Australia, Latin America, and Asia release of Ukraine war documentary A Simple Soldier. The partnership will include theatrical screenings, an impact campaign, a Jolt.film TVOD window, and digital aggregation. The film follows Ukrainian filmmaker and cinematographer Artem Ryzhykov “as he trades life […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Jolt is partnering with Propagate Content to support the North America, UK, Australia, Latin America, and Asia release of Ukraine war documentary A Simple Soldier.

The partnership will include theatrical screenings, an impact campaign, a Jolt.film TVOD window, and digital aggregation.

The film follows Ukrainian filmmaker and cinematographer Artem Ryzhykov “as he trades life behind the camera for life on the frontlines after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Filmed over three and a half years, the documentary offers a deeply personal, ground-level view of war, duty, love, loss and the moral complexities of documenting conflict from within.”

Directed by Ryzhykov and Juan Camilo Cruz, the film is produced by Ryzhykov and Cruz as well as Propagate’s Howard T. Owens and Ben Silverman.

Watch on Deadline

The documentary is executive-produced by James Packer, John Battsek, Marcel Mettelsiefen, Andrew D. Corkin, Catalina Ramirez, and Jonathan Schaerf.

The film’s North American release is due to include community screenings led by Ukrainian-American diaspora organizations.

“An extraordinary and deeply personal documentary, A Simple Soldier brings an entirely different perspective to the experience of war,” said Howard T. Owens, co-founder and co-CEO of Propagate Content.

“A Simple Soldier is exactly the kind of urgent, human and artistically powerful documentary that deserves a thoughtful path to audiences,” added Tara Hein-Phillips, CEO and Co-founder of Jolt, which specializes in data and audience demand-led releases. “This is a film that asks viewers to look closely at the human cost of war, but also at the courage, responsibility and resilience of those living through it. We are proud to partner with Propagate on a release strategy that brings together theatrical, impact and digital in one data-driven campaign.”

title: Brad Pitt Returning for ‘World War Z’ Sequel at Paramount With Edward Berger to Direct
summary: Brad Pitt will return to star in Paramount’s forthcoming sequel to “World War Z.” Edward Berger, who recently directed Pitt in “The Riders” for A24, has signed on to direct from a script by Dennis Kelly. Plot details for the long-awaited sequel are being kept under wraps. The original “World War Z,” based on Max […]
content:
Brad Pitt will return to star in Paramount’s forthcoming sequel to “World War Z.”

Edward Berger, who recently directed Pitt in “The Riders” for A24, has signed on to direct from a script by Dennis Kelly. Plot details for the long-awaited sequel are being kept under wraps.

The original “World War Z,” based on Max Brooks’ bestselling 2006 novel, “World War Z: An Oral History of the Zombie War,” made more than $540 million at the global box office. Pitt will produce the sequel alongside Dede Gardner and Jeremy Kleiner on behalf of Plan B, with Berger on board as executive producer.

The news comes as Pitt is on a press tour for his latest Paramount movie, “Heart of the Beast,” directed by David Ayer and in theaters next Friday. He will next star in “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” for Netflix later this year. Pitt and Berger filmed “The Riders” earlier this year; the movie is currently in post-production.

Popular on Variety

Pitt is represented by CAA and Brillstein Entertainment Partners; Berger is represented by CAA, Range, Casarotto Ramsay & Associates, and Hanson Jacobson and Kelly is represented by UTA and Davis Law Group.

Deadline first reported the update on the sequel’s development.

More to come…

title: Getting to Know Juan Andrés García Ropero ‘Bropi,’ the New Director of Content of Movistar Plus
summary: Juan Andrés García Ropero, “Bropi,” Movistar Plus’ new director of content from May 2026, re-adjusts himself in his seat on a Zoom call. “I’ll sit with my best side showing, this profile,” he jokes. For an executive in one of the most pressured jobs in Spain, whom its film and TV industry desperately hope it […]
content:
Juan Andrés García Ropero, “Bropi,” Movistar Plus’ new director of content from May 2026, re-adjusts himself in his seat on a Zoom call.

“I’ll sit with my best side showing, this profile,” he jokes. For an executive in one of the most pressured jobs in Spain, whom its film and TV industry desperately hope it will continue to invest in movies and shows with an ambition which has yielded “Querer,” “The New Years” and “The Anatomy of a Moment” in TV and “Sirat,” “The Beloved” and “La Bola Negra” in movies, García Ropero seems remarkably relaxed.

He does, however, have good reason. When Variety interviewed García Ropero in late July, he already had on his hands not so much a feature as a movie phenomenon.

Popular on Variety

Recipient of a 16-minute standing ovation and a shared best director award at Cannes, queer epic “La Bola Negra” reflects the extraordinary aspirations of not only writer-director-producers Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi but also producer Movistar Plus, the biggest Spanish pay TV/SVOD operator.

Those ambitions even two months ago were scaling globally. Netflix had set a 47-day U.S. theatrical window for “La Bola Negra” the longest for any movie in the streaming giant’s history, as the film also appears to feature among the streamer’s awards priorities for the fall.

That breakout success is part of larger traction. In a bigger picture, over 2025-26, apart from France, no country in the world apart, not even the U.S., has had more Cannes main competition contenders than Spain.

Three of the five movies are Movistar Plus originals: Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s “The Beloved,” starring Javier Bardem, “La Bola Negra” and 2025’s “Sirāt,” a two-time Oscar nominee and Cannes Jury Prize winner. A fourth, Pedro Almodovar’s “Bitter Christmas,” was the subject of a muscular Movistar Plus pre-buy.

A significant part of the conversation at the 74th edition of Spain’s San Sebastián Film Festival, running Sept. 18-26, looks set to be driven by Movistar Plus does next, the Spanish premiere of “La Bola Negra,” a screening of “The Beloved,” and world premieres of Movistar Plus series “El castillo” and new movie “5 More Minutes.”

With all three movies screening on Sept. 19, this converts that day into a kind of Movistar Plus Super Saturday.

‘La Bola Negra’

Unveiling its first movie slate in January 2024, Movistar Plus talked about creating “event auteur movies.” No Movistar Plus film fits better that description to date than “La Bola Negra.”

Boasting big stars – Penelope Cruz is an extended cameo performance as a cabaret star rousing and arousing the troops, and Glenn Close as a modern-day Hispanist academic – “La Bola Negra” braids three inter-connected stories of gay identity, desire, repression and legacy set in 1932, 1937 and 2017, shot in 35 mm, each story mixing different film registers. It has big Spanish stars, such as Miguel Bernardeau (“Elite,” “Querer”), an enormous Spanish ensemble, and “the idea of a super production that is auteur-driven but also very queer,” as Ambrossi told Variety.

“Given its production standards, how it’s shot and told, ‘La Bola Negra’ becomes a great event. It will make a lot of noise in San Sebastian and I’m convinced it will mark a milestone in Spanish cinema, a great success for Movistar Plus and and Los Javis, taking them into another dimension,” says García Ropero.

Sold out worldwide by Goodfellas, “La bola negra” will see Elastica Films launch its nationwide theatrical release on Sept. 25. On Wednesday, the film was announced as Spain’s Oscar race entry for International Feature.

‘The Beloved’

“The Beloved” (“El ser querido”) also features as a 2026 standout Spanish feature. Framing a monumental performance by Javier Bardem as an Oscar-winning director seeking reconciliation with his daughter (Victoria Luengo) casting her in his latest movie, “The Beloved,”a story about the story people tell, even to deceive themselves, drew excellent reviews at Cannes: “Bardem is “a formidable presence, Luengo “exudes a fascinating quality of pensive engagement” in the film’s memorable opening scene.” The Beloved has also grossed €3.0 million ($3.45 million) in Spain from an Aug. 28 bow.

Movistar Plus Strategy Going Forward

The two films’ roll-out comes just months after the second management shakeup in just over a year at Movistar Plus+ with Daniel Domenjó replaced as CEO by Alfonso Gómez Palacio, to to date head of operations of Movistar Plus+ parent Telefónica in Latin America, outside Brazil. Gómez Palacio has won fame for balancing the books and improving margins. Given that, Spain TV and film industry feared that his appointment woild signal a pull back from production.

So early July news took the industry by storm: Movistar Plus announced that over the next three years it will double original Spanish series annual output from eight to 16 titles, while adding another 10 titles via co-production and licensing deals.

In early May, Movistar Plus launched a cut-price Free Plan: Series-Cinema subscription offer at just €4.99 ($5.78) a month

“We are suddenly seeing promise in (and putting money behind) scaled local streaming services to ‘take on’ the U.S. giants. Arguably Sky/ITV are angling for the same,” says Guy Bisson. “We are at a point in the industry where legacy players (and legacy usually goes hand in hand with geographic footprint limitations) see that they have to scale or die and that is now being reflected in content strategy.”

“Movistar Plus is still the foremost home for Spanish creativity. We aim to build on that sensation even more with a sense of local ambition, but looking for titles which can have international relevance,” García Ropero tells Variety.

Justifying the production hike, Movistar Plus noted that “Originals attract more clients and generate more engagement.”

García Ropero cites the case of YouTube-podcast Victoria Martín’s debut “Many People Need to Die,” a withering take on Millennial angst which has proved to be the most watched series of the year on Movistar Plus. “It’s been an audience and new subscriber driver,” says García Romero, noting that Movistar Plus has already ordered a Season 2.

Financial website El Confidencial claims that Movistar Plus will now double content investment to €200 million ($232 million) a year. Garcia Ropero declined to comment on exact figures but recognized that the pay TV/streamer will be upping not only content volume but investment. The increased TV show hike indeed guarantees that.

One major key to Netflix and HBO Max growth in international has been their bundling in international markets through partnerships with local distributors, such as HBO Max’s alliance in Germany with RTL+.

Having insisted on not partnering with rivals in Spain, Movistar Plus has now tapped “Ella maldita alma,” a young Spanish priest romantic melodrama, from Plano a Plano and Mediaset España, “33 days” from Atresmedia; and live audience sitcom “La Casa Nostra,” a hot on Catalan public broadcaster 3Cat, made available on Movistar Plus in either its original Catalan or dubbed into Castilian Spanish.

“In the final analysis, we’re aiming for clients to find on Movistar Plus what they need,” said García Ropero, noting that buying “33 Days” is a “very natural step,” given that it is a fiction recreation from Carles Porta, already a true crime fixture on Movistar Plus.

The Spanish streamer’s plans for film production have still to be announced. Their strategy, however, may not differ from series, since Movistar Plus seeks the same effect: Subscribers and fidelity for its pay TV and streaming service.

“Above all, what we’re trying to do is to bet on the best talent,” not on genres or formats but creators with their own voices,” says García Ropero. “That’s been the policy in recent years and we want to continue.”

‘El Castillo’

That can be seen in both “El Castillo” and “5 Minutes More.”

San Sebastián has become a privileged launchpad for series which go on to glean international renown: 2024 hosted world premieres of “Querer” and “Celeste,” both Movistar Plus+ Original Series, which went on to win the two biggest prizes at 2025’s Series Mania, Europe’s most important TV festival.

In 2020, one of the received titles, films included, was Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s “Riot Police,” written with Isabel Peña, his career-long co-scribe, and producer-writer Eduardo Villanueva, a partner at Sorogoyen’s label El Caballo Films.

“[San Sebastián Festival director] Jose Luis Rebordinos is a fan of our series and all of the work over these years to bring cinema talent to elevate our original Spanish fiction series,” says García Ropero.

Bearing out a creator-driven approach, as in “La Bola Negra,” with “El Castillo” and Movistar Plus+ is looking to take talent to the next level. A six-part series, “El Castillo” marks Peña first series without Sorogoyen, catching Spain’s sex trade as it transforms from small road-side establishments to organized crime.

Told from a triple point of view, part procedural, part personal odyssey of a victim, Colombian Claudia, part the rise – and one suspects fall – of a prostitution kingpin, “El Castillo” looks high on two factors many viewers now look for in a series: Authenticity and relevance.

“Again, I think “El Castillo” will make a lot noise, prove a conversation driver at San Sebastián,” says Garcia Ropero.

‘5 More Minutes’

A top Spanish stand-up comic, “5 More Minutes” writer-actor Berto Romero has risen the ranks at Movistar Plus from with star turns on late nights shows “Buenafuente” and “Leit Motiv,” to a first fiction series, “Look What You’ve Done,” a parenting comedy and then “The Other Side,” a comedic-horror-thriller. “5 More Minutes” delivers another genre mashup, a comedic sci-fi survival thriller as an on-the-rocks couple are caught in time loop at a rural getaway.

“The Other World,” Season 2 of “The Other Side,” will bow later this year with Romero co-directing for the first time.

“It’s not easy to blend comedy, horror and parapsychology,” says Romero. “Berto likes this mix of different genres and ‘5 More Minutes’ is a magnificent example.”

title: Drunk Shakespeare Theater Producer Sues Amazon, Alleging Prime Video’s ‘Off Campus’ Violated Its Trademarks
summary: Double, double toil and trouble! The company that produces the Drunk Shakespeare-branded theatrical shows sued Amazon, claiming an episode of Prime Video’s YA ice hockey romantic-drama “Off Campus” used its trademarks without permission. Brass Jar, the New York-based company behind Drunk Shakespeare, did not specify the amount of monetary damages it is seeking but said […]
content:
Double, double toil and trouble!

The company that produces the Drunk Shakespeare-branded theatrical shows sued Amazon, claiming an episode of Prime Video’s YA ice hockey romantic-drama “Off Campus” used its trademarks without permission.

Brass Jar, the New York-based company behind Drunk Shakespeare, did not specify the amount of monetary damages it is seeking but said in the complaint, “As a result of such counterfeiting by Defendants, Brass Jar is also entitled to recover attorneys’ fees, treble damages, and/or statutory damages of up to $2 million per counterfeit mark per type of services sold, and pursuant to each type of good sold, if any, pursuant to 15 U.S.C. § 1117,” citing the section of U.S. law addressing monetary recovery for violation of marks.

Amazon declined to comment.

Popular on Variety

“Off Campus,” which is based on a series of novels by Elle Kennedy, premiered all eight episodes on Prime Video on May 13, 2026.

In Episode 4 of Season 1, titled “The Breakup,” there’s “an extended sequence set at a fictional college ‘Drunk Shakespeare’ production, together with multiple lines of dialogue referencing ‘Drunk Shakespeare,’ without Plaintiff’s authorization or consent,” the lawsuit states.

Amazon’s alleged unauthorized use of the Drunk Shakespeare and Drunk trademarks, according to Brass Jar’s lawsuit, “has caused and is likely to continue to cause confusion – including reverse-confusion — mistake, and deception among consumers as to the source, sponsorship, or affiliation of Defendants’ Off Campus series and Plaintiff’s Brass Jar Productions.”

Brass Jar says its live theatrical productions of Drunk Shakespeare combine “Shakespearean performance with alcohol consumption in an intimate, sophisticated, upmarket, professionally staged setting.” The company currently produces shows in New York, Chicago, Washington, D.C., Phoenix, Los Angeles and Houston, and offers additional Drunk-branded productions (including Drunk Romeo & Juliet, Drunk Dracula, Drunk Pirates and Drunk Christmas Carol).

Brass Jar said its attorney notified Amazon in a June 3 letter of Brass Jar’s “rights in the Asserted Marks and requested that the parties discuss a resolution of Plaintiff’s concerns regarding Off Campus’s unauthorized use of Plaintiff’s marks and Trade Dress.” According to the lawsuit, counsel for Amazon “responded in a letter that included an extensive discussion of why Defendants’ program did not infringe on Plaintiff’s copyright, despite Plaintiff making no allegation in the June 3 Letter that Off Campus was infringing on Plaintiff’s copyright.”

Brass Jar filed the lawsuit against Amazon on Thursday (Sept. 17) in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida, Miami Division. A copy of the complaint is available at this link.

According to Drunk Shakespeare’s description of the show, it goes like this: “Five professional actors gather as members of The Drunk Shakespeare Society, and one of them downs five shots of whiskey before attempting a leading role in a Shakespearean classic. What follows is 90 minutes of comedy, chaos and quick-thinking improvisation while the four sober actors fight to keep the script on track. No two performances are ever the same. It all comes down to who’s drinking and what they’re drinking.”

title: Jesse Eisenberg’s ‘The Debut’ Named as Opening Night Film at Middleburg Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Jesse Eisenberg’s “The Debut” will open the Middleburg Film Festival. A Q&A will follow with the film’s star Julianne Moore. “The Debut” follows Moore as Mona Friedman, a housewife who lands a small role in a community theater production and transforms into a zealous method actor willing to do anything to protect the artistic integrity […]
content:
Jesse Eisenberg‘s “The Debut” will open the Middleburg Film Festival. A Q&A will follow with the film’s star Julianne Moore.

“The Debut” follows Moore as Mona Friedman, a housewife who lands a small role in a community theater production and transforms into a zealous method actor willing to do anything to protect the artistic integrity of her part.

The centerpiece film of the festival is “I Play Rocky,” directed by Peter Farrelly. Inspired by the true story behind the making of the 1976 film “Rocky,” Farrelly’s take stars Anthony Ippolito as Sylvester Stallone as he struggles to get his screenplay made while refusing to let go of his dream of playing the role himself.

Léa Seydoux, Jordan Firstman, Daniel Pemberton, Jack O’Connell, Nadia Stacey are among the festival’s honorees.

Popular on Variety

Seydoux will receive the Outstanding Achievement in Acting Award for her performance in “Gentle Monster.” Jordan Firstman will be recognized with the Breakthrough Filmmaker Award for his feature directorial debut “Club Kid,” which he wrote, directed and stars in. Composer Daniel Pemberton will receive the Distinguished Composer Award recognizing his work on “Project Hail Mary” and “Ink.” Jack O’Connell will receive the Spotlight Actor Award for his performance in “Ink.”

Olivia Colman will attend the festival representing both “Elsinore” and “Wicker.” The Oscar-winning actress will participate in Q&As for both films. “Elsinore’s” makeup and hair designer Nadia Stacey will be presented with the festival’s Distinguished Makeup & Hair Design Award.

As previously announced, “The Odyssey” artisans — costume designer Ellen Mirojnick, production designer Ruth de Jong and editor Jennifer Lame — are set to receive the Variety Creative Collaborators award.

The conversation will be moderated by Variety’s senior artisans editor, Jazz Tangcay, on Oct. 16. The talk will look at their collaboration and serve as a career retrospective.

The festival is set to run Oct. 15-18.

At the festival, Tangcay and Variety’s chief awards editor, Clayton Davis will also host their annual Coffee and Contenders conversation on the state of the awards race.

title: Lily Collins Says Goodbye to ‘Emily in Paris’ as Filming Wraps on Series Finale: ‘This Has Forever Changed Me’
summary: Lily Collins has officially bid adieu to Emily Cooper. The actress recently spent her last day on set playing the title role in the Netflix hit “Emily in Paris” and shared an emotional post on Instagram about the experience. “I’m speechless. It’s impossible to find the words for what this journey has meant to me,” […]
content:
Lily Collins has officially bid adieu to Emily Cooper.

The actress recently spent her last day on set playing the title role in the Netflix hit “Emily in Paris” and shared an emotional post on Instagram about the experience.

“I’m speechless. It’s impossible to find the words for what this journey has meant to me,” she wrote. “For so many years, Emily has been a part of my life, and through every season, she’s continued to surprise me, inspire me, and challenge me.”



“Thank you, Darren Star, for dreaming up this endlessly optimistic American girl in Paris who finds herself constantly outside of her comfort zone, learning to trust herself while leaning on others as she navigates her new life,” Collins continued. “I’m so grateful you trusted me to bring her to life. Thank you to our unparalleled crew, our writers, our directors, and of course our incredible cast who is now family and who I cannot imagine this without. You have made Emily, Emily. You made this world feel like home. And merci to all of you who have been supporting us over these past 7 years and 6 seasons, keeping us inspired to dream bigger along our epic adventure.”



The post concluded: “I will carry this chapter with me forever. Saying goodbye feels completely surreal and bittersweet, but mostly, I feel so incredibly proud and grateful that I got to be her. And be part of something so joyful. This has forever changed me. Au revoir, Emily Cooper…”

“Emily in Paris” premiered in 2020 and is wrapping up with its sixth season on Dec. 24. Along with Collins, the cast includes Philippine Leroy-Beaulieu, Ashley Park, Lucas Bravo, Samuel Arnold, Bruno Gouery, William Abadie, Lucien Laviscount, Minnie Driver and Paul Forman.

title: Brad Pitt Reunites With His ‘Riders’ Director Edward Berger On Paramount’s ‘World War Z’ Sequel
summary: EXCLUSIVE: The long-awaited and highly-anticipated sequel to the hit zombie epic World War Z is gaining some serious momentum as Paramount has not only closed a deal with Brad Pitt to return but has also tapped Edward Berger to direct the pic. World War Z is based on Max Brooks bestselling 2006 novel, World War […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: The long-awaited and highly-anticipated sequel to the hit zombie epic World War Z is gaining some serious momentum as Paramount has not only closed a deal with Brad Pitt to return but has also tapped Edward Berger to direct the pic.

World War Z is based on Max Brooks bestselling 2006 novel, World War Z: An Oral History of the Zombie War. Pitt, Dede Gardner and Jeremy Kleiner will produce on behalf of Plan B Entertainment. Berger will executive produce.

Dennis Kelly will write the script. The film marks Pitt’s return to World War Z following the 2013 film, which earned more than $540 million at the worldwide box office. Plot details are being kept under wraps.

Pitt has wanted to do this sequel for more then a decade going back to when he began wooing his long-time friend and collaborator David Fincher to potentially direct. That plan nearly came together but when budgetary issues arose, Fincher left the film and the project was put on hold but Pitt still hoped to make the sequel some day.

Watch on Deadline

Fast Forward to last summer, new life was breathed into the project after Josh Greenstein and Dana Goldberg were tapped as Co-Chairs of Paramount Pictures. The two saw this as a high-priority project, confirming their desire to get this film made at the recent Cinemacon event in Vegas. Skydance played a big part in getting the first film off the ground and Skydance founder David Ellison shared Pitt’s desire in moving forward with a sequel.

As for Berger, him and Pitt recently wrapped production on the A24 and Scott Free pic The Riders and sources say the shoot went very well with Pitt and Berger eager to figure out what that new project would be. Insiders add that early on in the shoot, Pitt began pitching Berger on World War Z 2 and how perfect he would be for the project. By end of production, Berger was on board and in recent weeks the studio was able to close the deal with both talents to board the project.

With Pitt, the film continues a strong bond between Paramount and the Oscar winner with his upcoming survival thriller Heart of the Beast bowing next weekend. The pic reunites Pitt with his Fury director David Ayer. Pitt can also be seen later this year in the Netflix pic The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.

Pitt is repped by CAA and Brillstein Partners and Berger is repped by CAA and Range. Kelly is repped by UTA.

title: Nateland Promotes Adrian Kulp To EVP, Sets Fall/Winter Comedy Slate
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Nate Bargatze’s Nateland has promoted Adrian Kulp to EVP of Digital, Production, Content + Special Live Events. With Nateland for a little under two and a half years, Kulp was previously SVP of Digital + Production. As EVP, he will continue to spearhead Nateland’s incubator, or farm system, for the elevation of the next […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Nate Bargatze’s Nateland has promoted Adrian Kulp to EVP of Digital, Production, Content + Special Live Events.

With Nateland for a little under two and a half years, Kulp was previously SVP of Digital + Production. As EVP, he will continue to spearhead Nateland’s incubator, or farm system, for the elevation of the next generation of clean-comedy talent.

Bargatze has formalized the steps comics go through as part of his incubator as follows— they go from stand-out performance at his weekly Nashville residency show Nateland Live, to tapings for his series The Showcase, to half-hour and full-hour specials under his Nateland Presents banner, to further opportunities.

In a statement to Deadline, Kulp underscored that Nateland’s farm system for comics has become “a big part of how we think about the future.”

Watch on Deadline

He explained, “We want talented people to have multiple ways into Nateland and multiple opportunities once they’re here — whether that’s Nateland Live, The Showcase, a half-hour or hour special, a podcast or eventually an original series. As we build relationships with more comedians, writers and creators, the opportunity is to create a real home for clean comedy where talent can develop, audiences can discover them and we can build new things together.”

You can read more about each core facet of the Nateland universe’s talent pipeline below.

In his new role at Nateland, Kulp will also continue to expand Nateland’s library of specials, series, live recordings and original IP, original digital series and repeatable comedy formats. He will work to expand the company’s relationships with clean-comedy writers, creators, hosts and emerging talent, in the stand-up world and beyond, while growing its slate of podcasts.

The next stage of the expansion has already been conceived, with a slate of comedy specials releasing on the Nateland YouTube Channel through end of year that we can announce exclusively. This includes a half-hour from Mike Goodwin (premiering today), an hour from Brad Upton (October 9) a half-hour from Alex Velluto (October TBD), another half-hour from John Heffron (November TBD), and a full hour from Graham Kay (December TBD).

New Nateland EVP Kulp has worked for nearly three decades across comedy, television, publishing and digital entertainment. He began his career booking comedy for CBS’ The Late Late Show before moving into development with Adam Sandler’s Happy Madison Productions and Chelsea Handler’s Borderline Amazing Productions. Subsequently, he founded a comedy-driven fatherhood brand, produced A&E’s Modern Dads, and authored six parenting books that have sold more than a million copies worldwide. After relocating to Nashville, he expanded into live radio, streaming and podcasts, executive producing projects with Cumulus Media and Apple Music.

Since joining Nateland in 2024, Kulp has helped expand the company from its flagship podcast into a growing multi-platform comedy and entertainment ecosystem. He oversees digital and production initiatives spanning the Nateland Podcast Network, Nateland Live, Nateland Presents: The Showcase, half-hour and hour-long stand-up specials and premium-platform projects, while building an interconnected pipeline that moves comedy talent across live performance, podcasts, digital programming, specials and larger development opportunities.

Speaking to Kulp’s promotion, Bargatze said, “Adrian has been a huge part of building Nateland into what it is today. We’ve proven what we can do. Now, we’re being even more intentional about how we grow and level up for what comes next.”

While continuing to scale his family-friendly production banner Nateland Entertainment, Bargatze recently announced plans to expand in another direction simultaneously with the launch of No Pictures, a label producing film and television that will delve into edgier genres and stories more suited for older audiences. We were first to the story.

NATELAND ECOSYSTEM

LIVE EVENTS, FORMATS + SPECIALS



Nateland Live – Weekly Nashville Residency Show

Since 2024, Nateland has hosted Nateland Live, a Monday night residency show at The Lab at Zanies Comedy Club in Nashville; a 90-minute live event that features clean comics from across the country.

Nateland Presents: The Showcase

A stand-up comedy series; currently premiering Season 5 with comedian Collin Chamberlin (Thursday, 9/17), with Season 6 filming in Spring 2027. Current library includes sets from 75+ rising and veteran comedians.

Nateland Presents: Half-Hour Specials

An ongoing series of 1/2 hour specials filmed at the historic Woolworth Theatre in Nashville beginning this week with the premiere of Nateland Presents: Mike Goodwin (9/18).

Bio: Mike is a stand-up comedian, speaker, and leader native to Camden, South Carolina who holds a master’s degree in Education from the University of South Carolina. He’s a veteran of the U.S. Army, as well as a former primary and secondary education professional who infuses his varied life experiences into his act, making him relatable to audiences from all walks of life. He’s appeared on America’s Got Talent, Dry Bar Comedy, Lifetime, BET, Amazon Prime, TBN, Daystar, USA, the Word Network and Circle TV, and been featured on SiriusXM, the That Sounds Fun Podcast Tour with Annie F. Downs and USO Europe Comedy Tour.

Special Description: In his latest special, Mike Goodwin brings his warm, unmistakably Southern perspective to Nashville for a half hour about getting older, raising kids, staying married, growing up in the church, and trying to make sense of a world that feels a little different than the one he came up in. From sending his oldest daughter off to college and navigating life after 50, to teenage sons, old-school teachers, Southern expressions, weddings, fatherhood and his own time in the Army, Mike turns everyday observations into stories that are both deeply relatable and uniquely his own. It’s clean, personal comedy delivered with the kind of charm, storytelling and playful exasperation that makes you feel like you’ve been sitting on the porch laughing with him the whole time.

Nateland Presents: Hour Specials + Netflix

Nateland continues expanding the clean comedy library with hour specials including the upcoming premiere of Nateland Presents: Brad Upton ‘Code Blue’ (10/9); filmed at The Franklin Theatre in Tennessee.

Brad has the most-viewed Nateland Showcase set of all-time with over a half-million views.

Bio: With a career spanning over 37 years, comedy veteran Brad Upton is just getting started. The former fourth grade teacher and part-time track coach is seeing a resurgence unlike anyone else. His 2019 Dry Bar comedy special, Boomer Triggers Gen-Z Snowflakes, boasts 16.1 million views on YouTube. The album hit No. 1 on the iTunes Charts and drove his ensuing special I’m Not Done Yet to new heights. Collectively, the clips and full specials have garnered well over 200 million views across all platforms and continue to build momentum from newfound fans all across the country. Over his career, Brad has appeared with acts like Jeff Foxworthy, Neal McCoy, Kenny Rogers, Lewis Black, Dolly Parton, George Jones and even now continues to tour with music icon Johnny Mathis. In 2019, he drew the attention of the Grand Ole Opry where he’s had the honor to step into the circle multiple times becoming a regular guest.

Special Description: Brad Upton has spent decades finding the funny in getting older. In Code Blue, he may have more material than ever. From pill caddies and bad drivers to marriage, kids, generational differences and the indignities that come with aging, Brad brings his sharp, boomer perspective to an hour of comedy about a life well lived — and a body that occasionally has other plans.

After Upton, the hour production pipeline includes: Graham Kay Hour (December premiere).

Previous special releases include:

Aaron Weber’s Signature Dish

Mike Vecchione’s The Attractives & Low Income White

Greg Warren’s The Salesman and The Champ

Stephen Bargatze’s Out in a Minute

Graham Kay’s Pete n’ Me

With Bargatze, Kulp and Nateland also produced Derrick Stroupe’s Nostalgic (No. 6 Netflix Top 10) and Ryan Hamilton’s This Just Hit Me (No. 7 Netflix Top 10) for Netflix.

Nateland at Sea + Live

During Super Bowl Week 2026, Nateland presented Nateland at Sea on Norwegian, a 5-day cruise experience for superfans; daily programming that included 25 comedians, live podcasts, and a surprise sneak-preview live episode of Nate’s Greatest Average American before its premiere on ABC.

Archive, Library + Distribution

Creating a long-term library of owned/controlled programming and reusable IP. To date, between the podcast network and archive, stand-up specials, BTS content from Nate’s tours, digital series and more on the way — Nateland is a clean comedy destination with over 1,000 hours of programming.

NATELAND PODCASTING

The Nateland Podcast Network is built around original formats developed within Nateland and established shows brought into the network that align with the Nateland audience and brand:

title: Wil Traval Joins ‘General Hospital’ As Jude
