Per the show’s official logline, “‘Ride or Die’ follows best friends Debbie Claybourne (Spencer) and Judith Burton (Waddingham) who thought they knew everything about each other, except Judith turns out to be an international assassin. When a mysterious figure emerges from Judith’s past and a hit goes horribly wrong, both of their worlds are turned upside down as they’re forced to go on the run together. It’s a race against time and a road trip across Europe, with law enforcement, highly trained assassins, and some very dangerous criminals at their heels.”

Popular on Variety

In her review of Season 1, Variety’s Aramide Tinubu wrote that “‘Ride or Die’ works best when it fully leans into the ‘Thelma & Louise’ aspects of the central storyline… Spencer and Waddingham have a robust and genuine chemistry — a companionship that will undoubtedly resonate with countless viewers. Moreover, watching Waddingham as a full-fledged action star is something everyone should be witnessing on a daily basis.”

Other cast members included Ed Skrein, Calam Lynch, Savannah Steyn, Jamie Parker, and Jacky Ido, with Sylvia Hoeks and Bill Nighy.

Tessa Coates created the series and serves as executive producer and showrunner along with Matt Miller and director Peyton Reed. The show is produced by Paramount Television Studios, Amazon MGM Studios as well as Andy and Barbara Muschietti’s Double Dream and Octavia Spencer’s Orit Entertainment. Coates, Miller, and Reed executive produce alongside Spencer for Orit Entertainment; Waddingham; Andy Muschietti, Barbara Muschietti, and Irene Yeung for Double Dream; Brian Clisham; and Stephanie Kluft.

title: Ed Sheeran Addresses Macklemore Controversy While on Stage at First Concert Since Rapper Dropped From Tour: ‘What Is Happening in Gaza Is Catastrophic and Unjustifiable’
summary: Ed Sheeran addressed the controversy surrounding Macklemore’s removal from his Loop Tour on Saturday night, speaking from the stage at Philadelphia’s Lincoln Financial Field during his first concert since the rapper was dropped from the trek. “Before I play some songs tonight, I hope it’s okay if I say a few words about this last […]
content:
Ed Sheeran addressed the controversy surrounding Macklemore’s removal from his Loop Tour on Saturday night, speaking from the stage at Philadelphia’s Lincoln Financial Field during his first concert since the rapper was dropped from the trek.

“Before I play some songs tonight, I hope it’s okay if I say a few words about this last week,” Sheeran said at the top of Saturday’s show. “I’m used to my music being criticized, and I’m always happy to take that because I’m lucky. A lot of you like my stuff, and to be honest, I’m surprised. I’m not surprised that I’ve even done it. You know, it’s normal. But this week, the criticism was about something much more important, and I’ve had to take and make difficult decisions, and I am making mistakes, and I’m so, so sorry.”

Sheeran continued: “I don’t want to disappoint fans, and I’ve never wanted to be an activist musician, but this has put me in the middle of an important and passionate argument about freedom of speech and the most complex political issue on the planet. My concerts have always been a safe space for everyone, and that matters hugely to me. Honoring my commitment to my fans is also completely essential to who I am, and that is why I’m here tonight on my own and continuing my current tour.”

Popular on Variety

Saturday’s concert marked Sheeran’s first performance since a tumultuous week for the U.S. leg of his Loop Tour, which saw Macklemore removed from the remaining dates following the rapper’s onstage remarks in support of Palestinians during Sheeran’s Sept. 4 and 5 shows at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

During his MetLife performances, Macklemore spoke about the war in Gaza and the West Bank and told the stadium crowd, “Free Palestine.” His set also included “Hind’s Hall,” his 2024 protest song supporting Palestinians. The remarks drew criticism from some Jewish and pro-Israel organizations, including the Israeli-American Council, which called for Macklemore to be removed from the tour.

Messina Touring Group, the promoter behind the U.S. leg of the Loop Tour, subsequently announced that Macklemore would no longer appear on the remaining dates. The company said venues had informed the promoter that they would not allow concerts featuring Macklemore to proceed, a situation it said could have resulted in cancellations affecting hundreds of thousands of ticket holders.

While Sheeran addressed the decision in a statement earlier this week, stressing that Macklemore’s removal was made by the promoter and venues rather than by him, he again acknowledged that he is “deeply worried about the idea that venues pre-approve content for performance.” “This happens in so many places that I perform around the world, but it should never happen in the free world,” he said.

At the time of his initial statement, Sheeran said he was “appalled by the conflict between Israel and Palestine,” describing the suffering caused by the war as a “human tragedy,” while explaining that he has generally sought to keep his concerts focused on “unity, joy, escapism, love” rather than his own political views. On Saturday, he restated these feelings, though also speaking more explicitly about where he stands on the Israel-Palestine conflict.

“I have tried in my career not to be a political commentator of any kind, because I want my music and shows to be about unity, not division,” he said. “But this is a humanitarian issue, and I cannot hide how I feel about it anymore. What happened in Israel and at the Nome Museum Festival on Oct. 7 was horrific and compounded centuries of Jewish pain. What is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable, and disproportionate. Our hearts can be broken by the scale of devastation and loss of civilians’ lives, children’s lives and the systemic injustice we’re seeing unfold in the West Bank cannot be overlooked.”

He continued, “I am already speaking to people across the spectrum to work out how to make a contribution that helps victims of these terrible times, and listening and learning because I do not know enough.”

After Macklemore was dropped, he responded to his removal in a statement, saying that he and Sheeran had held “difficult conversations” in the aftermath of the MetLife shows. While expressing respect for Sheeran personally, the rapper challenged the singer’s preference for remaining publicly neutral and said he did not regret using the tour stage to speak in support of Palestinians. Macklemore has since said he will donate $1 million to Palestinian relief organizations.

The fallout quickly spread beyond Macklemore. Singer-songwriter Aaron Rowe and Danish band Lukas Graham, who had been expected to support Sheeran on upcoming North American dates, both withdrew from the tour. Finneas, who was scheduled to join Sheeran for a run of South American dates later this year, also pulled out, while Irish folk group Beoga — longtime collaborators who had been performing as part of Sheeran’s live show — exited as well. All four cited Macklemore’s removal in announcing their decisions.

The Philadelphia date nevertheless proceeded as scheduled Saturday at Lincoln Financial Field, kicking off the next stretch of Sheeran’s U.S. stadium run.

title: Ed Sheeran Admits To “Making Mistakes” With Macklemore, Calls Out “Systemic Injustice” In Gaza: “I’m So, So Sorry”
summary: As Ed Sheeran returns to the stage amid the fallout from dropping Macklemore as his tour opener, he’s addressing the controversy head-on. On Saturday, while beginning his Loop Tour stop at Philadelphia’s Lincoln Financial Field, the 4x Grammy winner apologized for “making mistakes” in his handling of the situation after pressure from Gillette Stadium owner […]
content:
As Ed Sheeran returns to the stage amid the fallout from dropping Macklemore as his tour opener, he’s addressing the controversy head-on.

On Saturday, while beginning his Loop Tour stop at Philadelphia’s Lincoln Financial Field, the 4x Grammy winner apologized for “making mistakes” in his handling of the situation after pressure from Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft and other venues to drop Macklemore over his pro-Palestine onstage remarks.

Meanwhile, protesters gathered outside the Philly stop to call out Sheeran for dropping Macklemore, over which fellow tour openers Finneas, Aaron Rowe and Lukas Graham also exited the tour, along with Sheeran’s backing band Beoga.

Watch on Deadline

Read Sheeran’s full statement below:

“Before I play some songs tonight, I hope it’s okay if I say a few words about this last week. I’m used to my music being criticized, and I’m always happy to take that because I’m lucky. A lot of you like my stuff, and to be honest, I’m not surprised that other people don’t. You know, it’s normal. But this week, the criticism was about something much more important, and I’ve had to take and make difficult decisions, and I am making mistakes, and I’m so so sorry.

“I don’t want to disappoint fans, and I’ve never wanted to be an activist musician, but this has put me in the middle of an important and passionate argument about freedom of speech and the most complex political issue on the planet.

“My concerts have always been a safe space for everyone, and that matters hugely to me. Honoring my commitment to my fans is also completely essential to who I am, and that is why I’m here tonight on my own and continuing my current tour.

“But I am deeply worried about the idea that venues should pre-approve content of a performance. This happens in so many places that I perform around the world, but it should never happen in the free world.

“Now, I want to address the question of where I stand on the situation in Israel and Palestine, and whether my doing this concert here tonight implies where I stand. I have tried in my career to not be a political commentator at any time, because I want my shows to be about unity, not division, and humanity, not politics. But this is a humanitarian issue, and I can’t hide how I feel about it anymore.

“What happened in Israel at Nova Music Festival on Oct. 7 was horrific and compounded centuries of Jewish pain. What is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate. Our hearts have been broken by the scale and devastation and loss of civilian’s lives, of children’s lives. And the systemic injustice we’re seeing unfold in the West Bank cannot be overlooked.

“I’m already speaking to people across the spectrum to work out how to make a contribution that helps victims of these terrible times, and listening and learning, because I do not know enough.

“I honestly am so grateful that you are here tonight with me. This concert is still a place where everyone is welcome, and everyone here can stand beside people that have opposing views, and everyone here can stand by people they don’t agree with on everything. But they can all agree on singing these songs, and these songs are about love, hope and unity.

title: Mark Ruffalo Urges AG Bonta “Do Not Cave” On Paramount Deal, Suggests Protest Outside Oakland Office: “The People Don’t Want It!”
summary: As attorneys general meet with Paramount this weekend over a potential deal in the Warner Bros. Discovery merger, Mark Ruffalo is continuing to apply pressure. On Saturday, the 4x Oscar nominee called on Rob Bonta to “reject the deal” that he and other AGs are currently negotiating with the Ellison-run Paramount ahead of a scheduled […]
content:
As attorneys general meet with Paramount this weekend over a potential deal in the Warner Bros. Discovery merger, Mark Ruffalo is continuing to apply pressure.

On Saturday, the 4x Oscar nominee called on Rob Bonta to “reject the deal” that he and other AGs are currently negotiating with the Ellison-run Paramount ahead of a scheduled March 2, 2027 federal antitrust trial.

“Don’t you dare @AGRobBonta, do not cave. 5670 film makers put their necks on the line for you to fight this merger. Another 75,000+ and counting have signed to tell you not to concede in just 3 weeks,” he wrote on X. “You work for the people — the very people who will be hurt if you let this lousy deal filled with empty promises go forward.”

Sharing Block the Merger‘s petition to stop the settlement, Ruffalo added, “Please sign to send a message to the AGs and Paramount. Reject the deal. The people don’t want it!”

Watch on Deadline

Ruffalo went a step further, telling his followers that Bonta “is about to cave,” urging his Bay Area supporters, “We can’t let him do that. Can you show up outside his AG office in Oakland tomorrow at 5pm to reject this backroom deal?”

Don’t you dare @AGRobBonta, do not cave. 5670 film makers put their necks on the line for you to fight this merger. Another 75,000+ and counting have signed to tell you not to concede in just 3 weeks. You work for the people — the very people who will be hurt if you let this… — Mark Ruffalo (@MarkRuffalo) September 19, 2026

To my friends in the Bay Area: I'm hearing Rob Bonta is about to cave and hand Warner Bros over to the Ellisons. We can't let him do that. Can you show up outside his AG office in Oakland tomorrow at 5pm to reject this backroom deal? Reject the deal. The people don’t want it!… — Mark Ruffalo (@MarkRuffalo) September 19, 2026

Block the Merger, with support from Ruffalo, Bryan Cranston, Hannah Einbinder, Jane Fonda, Noah Wyle, Denis Villeneuve, Sofia Coppola and more, previously released a statement on the settlement talks.

“Thousands of industry leaders took a risk when they spoke out publicly about the harm the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger would cause,” they said, claiming that more than 75,000 people have joined them to tell the state AGs to stand strong, including national leaders like Elizabeth Warren.

“We know a bad deal when we see one,” they added. “AG Bonta and his fellow state AGs should reject this deal, stand strong, and fully block the merger with no concessions.”

As leaks of talks between the AGs, led by California’s politically ambitious Bonta, and Paramount flooded the media late Friday, AG Bonta’s office did not respond to Deadline’s request for comment.

title: ‘Sweet Magnolias’ Creator Bids Farewell To Serenity, S.C. After Netflix Show Ends: “Keep Pouring It Out!”
summary: As Sweet Magnolias comes to an end on Netflix, Sheryl J. Anderson is bidding farewell to Serenity, South Carolina. On Saturday, the series creator thanked fans for their “passion for our characters” in a statement after Netflix canceled the romantic drama based on Sherryl Woods’ books after five seasons. “Living in Serenity for five seasons […]
content:
As Sweet Magnolias comes to an end on Netflix, Sheryl J. Anderson is bidding farewell to Serenity, South Carolina.

On Saturday, the series creator thanked fans for their “passion for our characters” in a statement after Netflix canceled the romantic drama based on Sherryl Woods’ books after five seasons.

“Living in Serenity for five seasons has been a privilege and a blessing,” she wrote on Instagram. “The people I’ve met and worked with — our incredible writers, cast, crew, executives, and producers — have touched my heart and changed my life.”

Anderson continued, “And our fans have been amazing in their passion for our characters. Thank you all. Though our journey has sadly come to an end, I hope Serenity will always have a place in your heart. Keep pouring it out!”

Watch on Deadline

The post comes after Deadline exclusively announced on Friday that Netflix has canceled the series after five seasons. Meanwhile, the streamer has greenlighted a new series from Sweet Magnolias EP/showrunner Anderson and star JoAnna Garcia Swisher.

Loosely based on Lauren Edmondson’s novel Ladies of the House, the new series also centers on a trio of women. Swisher is attached as an EP, and she’s being eyed to star.

In Ladies of the House, when the charismatic owner of a winery dies unexpectedly, his wife and two adult daughters must battle through their issues with each other in order to confront challenges with the business, their extended family, and the men in their lives. Good friends and good wine will aid in the journey to hang on to the winery, but what matters most is that they find a way to hang on to each other.

title: Ed Sheeran Met With Pro-Palestine Protest Outside Philadelphia Concert: “F*ck Your Concert, F*ck Your Fans. Palestine Is Our Demand!”
summary: Ed Sheeran’s return to the Loop Tour drew protesters to the City of Brotherly Love amid ongoing fallout. After the 4x Grammy winner dropped Macklemore from his tour over pressure around the “Hind’s Hall” artist’s Palestinian onstage remarks, Sheeran’s Saturday stop at Philadelphia’s Lincoln Financial Field was met with pro-Palestine protesters. “The fact of the […]
content:
Ed Sheeran‘s return to the Loop Tour drew protesters to the City of Brotherly Love amid ongoing fallout.

After the 4x Grammy winner dropped Macklemore from his tour over pressure around the “Hind’s Hall” artist’s Palestinian onstage remarks, Sheeran’s Saturday stop at Philadelphia’s Lincoln Financial Field was met with pro-Palestine protesters.

“The fact of the matter is, now Palestine is associated with his concert, whether he wants it to be or not. He thinks that he is apolitical,” one protester told Freedom News. “Whether Ed Sheeran believes his music is apolitical, that decision is no longer in his hands.”

The protester continued, “Palestine is now associated with his concert, so he has to make a decision. Will he support the women, children, men and innocent people of Gaza who have been bombarded and killed by Israel?”

Watch on Deadline

Outside the venue, protesters chanted, “Globalize the intifada. Fuck your concert, fuck your fans. Palestine is our demand. Free Palestine!”

NOW: "Fuck your concern Fuck your fans" and "Globalize the Intifada" chants outside Ed Sheeran concert in Philadelphia pic.twitter.com/VNmb7WpTM0 — Oliya Scootercaster 🛴 (@ScooterCasterNY) September 19, 2026

NOW: Protester explains why they are protesting Ed Sheeran concert in Philadelphia https://t.co/NvxHMnTMyG pic.twitter.com/BQnFVawRfp — Oliya Scootercaster 🛴 (@ScooterCasterNY) September 19, 2026

On Monday, Sheeran dropped Macklemore from his tour amid an outcry around his “Free Palestine” onstage remarks. Opting to remain publicly neutral on the issue, Sheeran subsequently released a statement saying it was the “promoter’s decision” after Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft assembled several of the tour venues to give him an ultimatum.

Following the statement, fellow tour openers Finneas, Aaron Rowe and Lukas Graham dropped out of the tour, along with Sheeran’s backing band Beoga.

title: Ready, SETT, Go: SETT Execs Drill Down on the Spanish Sovereign Venture Capital Fund That Will Drive Industry Conversation at San Sebastián
summary: One of the major industry narratives at this year’s San Sebastián Festival, running Sept. 18-26, will be the presentation of SETT, the venture capital fund of Spain’s Ministry for Digital Transformation.SETT director general Javier Ponce and its audiovisual director María Coronado deliver a practical guide to Spain’s governmental investment drive powering up companies in Spain: […]
content:
One of the major industry narratives at this year’s San Sebastián Festival, running Sept. 18-26, will be the presentation of SETT, the venture capital fund of Spain’s Ministry for Digital Transformation.

SETT director general Javier Ponce and its audiovisual director María Coronado deliver a practical guide to Spain’s governmental investment drive powering up companies in Spain: What it’s doing, why, and where it could go in the future. The companies it s investing in – with more to be revealed – are likely to be among the most dynamic in Spain.

What, explained very briefly, are the objectives of SETT’s Spain Audiovisual Hub strategy?

Javier Ponce: SETT is a public investment entity that manages investments in strategic, transformative sectors, including the audiovisual industry. It serves as a public catalyst for growth, employment, innovation and talent—all core elements of the audiovisual sector. SETT has managed the Spain Audiovisual Hub Fund, an instrument established under Spain’s Recovery Plan and financed through the European Union’s Next Generation funds.

Through the Spain Audiovisual Hub Plan, SETT provides financing and equity or quasi-equity investments, either directly to companies in the sector or through financial intermediaries active in the audiovisual industry. The objective has been to attract private investment and improve access to finance for projects related to films, television, animation, multimedia and interactive content, among others. Priority has been given to high-impact projects focused on creating audiovisual content and intellectual property rights while ensuring that those rights remain with the production companies.

And the rationale of a sovereign venture capital fund’s co-investment model?

Ponce: It is based on public-private collaboration to launch transformative initiatives that, because of their innovative nature, involve additional risks that make it difficult to attract purely private funding. Only highly liquid, large-scale markets with a long-established audiovisual industry are able to mobilize sufficient capital to finance major new productions or transformative industry initiatives.

SETT’s Spain AVS Hub fund could draw down up to €1.5 billion ($1.75 billion) from NextGeneration E.U. funding. According to María Gonzalez Veracruz, investments made are just under €250 million. Her explanation is that you simply ran out of time. Could you comment?

Ponce: Indeed, European funds have been fundamental for Spain, and the Recovery Plan has played a key role in driving major structural reforms and stimulating economic growth. However, it is also true that these funds came with specific requirements, including strict implementation deadlines, which made optimal execution more challenging.

For the audiovisual sector, the possibility of co-investing alongside a public entity represented a major innovation. Time therefore became a critical factor, as market participants first needed to understand the role and implications of partnering with a public investor that shared both risks and returns.

The next challenge is to ensure that these investments continue to thrive, identify new opportunities, and maintain confidence in the talent and ambition of Spanish audiovisual companies, which now benefit from SETT’s backing.

SETT, however, is not over, I believe. Obviously it has to exercise governance over investment accords now struck. I believe as well that there are plans to launch a new program España Crece, with a €13.3 billion ($15.6 billion) budget, held by ICO, but whose investments will be handled in part by SETT, if I understand correctly. Could you comment?

Ponce: The audiovisual sector will remain one of SETT’s strategic areas of activity and will continue under new fund “España Crece”. We have begun discussions with ICO to define the procedures and framework for collaboration between the two institutions, ensuring the continuation of co-investment in strategic technologies and sectors.

SETT has represented a significant shift in the way public investment in strategic industries is conceived. Through SETT, the State acts as a catalyst and partner in the most innovative areas of the economy, with the objective of positioning Spain at the forefront of transformative industries. That is why we invested in the audiovisual sector and why we will continue to do so.

Its ability to generate industrial activity, employment and broad economic impact makes it a strategic sector that will continue to enjoy our support.

Could you illustrate the rationale of SETT’s co-investment model in one or two of the investments made and the obvious benefits it could bring to the companies Spain’s film-TV industry.

Coronado: The SETT model has been built on three pillars. First, it adopts an industry-wide approach, rather than a project-based one, addressing the entire audiovisual business ecosystem. Second, its investment facilities are directed at the equity capital of companies or regulated investment vehicles. Third, it promotes public-private partnership instruments on a medium-long term.

Under this model, promoters must convince a genuinely private investor that their company represents a worthwhile investment opportunity. SETT co-invests alongside the private investor on a pari passu basis: public investment is intended to support companies, but always under the same terms and conditions as private capital.

This approach strengthens both domestic and international private investment in companies based in Spain, while also attracting foreign businesses that see Spain as an attractive location to establish their operations. Clear examples include the South African transactions involving The Refinery and Moonlighting, with a combined investment of €25 million, as well as Amuse Labs and Milo, two leading examples of Spain’s animation industry, which have mobilised €13 million and €19 million respectively.

My sense is that SETT investors can indeed help companies scale, create more such expertise and build infrastructure. But would you agree?

Coronado: In my view, the main challenge for the coming years is to consolidate the model we have been promoting and supporting. It is essential to continue strengthening and diversifying support policies so that Spain can establish itself as a global hub for the audiovisual industry over the long term. This means supporting every segment of the industry according to its specific needs.

Scale is undoubtedly part of the challenge, as is ensuring the availability of the infrastructure needed to accommodate medium- and large-scale productions, strengthening technical training, and fostering talent across the industry. It will also be important to continue enhancing the tax framework and the legal and regulatory environment to maintain Spain’s competitiveness, while further developing public-private investment instruments.

In addition, it will be essential to understand the cash-flow financing needs of projects to address the full range of companies’ financing requirements. Finally, the industry’s ability to adapt and diversify will remain critical, both in terms of technology and creativity, as well as business models and corporate structures.

In your view, does the introduction of sovereign venture capital in the Spanish film and TV industry encourage a change of mindset in the industry?

Coronado: Yes, absolutely. It creates new opportunities. It is essential to think in terms of medium- and long-term business strategy, rather than focusing only on immediate projects. It enables companies to strengthen their capital base, making them more ambitious, better able to protect their intellectual property, diversify, expand internationally, and bring their products to market more effectively.

What have you learnt in the two years of the Spain AVS Hub Phase II which you would like to apply in future investments by SETT under España Crece?

Coronado: The main learning here is the confirmation that SETT has a clear and necessary purpose for the industry, both in attracting private investment and foreign companies, and in creating opportunities for the local industry. It is important to allow more time for business plans to mature and for companies to secure private investment.

Can you outline very briefly what the SETT event at San Sebastián Festival will consist of?

Coronado: As you would expect, we will have a strong presence at the festival, with a wide range of activities. On Sept. 20, the Secretary of State for Digitalisation and Artificial Intelligence, through the Ministry for Digital Transformation and the Civil Service, which is leading the Government’s Spain Audiovisual Hub Plan, will host an event in which SETT will present the huge progress we have made in financing the audiovisual sector and new ongoing projects. Additionally, on 22 September, I will take part in a panel discussion at the conference organised by the CAA as part of Spanish Screenings Investment & Tech. That same day, we will also host an exclusive roundtable with investment funds and banks specialising in the audiovisual sector, bringing together both international and Spanish participants. We also have a few more surprises in store, which we will unveil throughout this very important festival for the industry.

title: Princess Di Returns To ‘SNL UK’ As “Deeply Intelligent, Autonomous, Neurokinetic Android” In Cold Open Skewering King Charles, Ed Sheeran & AI
summary: Princess Diana made a royal return to SNL UK – only this time as a “Deeply Intelligent, Autonomous, Neurokinetic Android.” Jack Shep’s celebrated impression of the late royal was back in episode two of the Sky show last night, in a cold open that skewered her former husband, King Charles III, Ed Sheeran and artificial […]
content:
Princess Diana made a royal return to SNL UK – only this time as a “Deeply Intelligent, Autonomous, Neurokinetic Android.”

Jack Shep’s celebrated impression of the late royal was back in episode two of the Sky show last night, in a cold open that skewered her former husband, King Charles III, Ed Sheeran and artificial intelligence.

The ep opened with Charles, played by Larry Dean, having a private chat with a pair of tech billionaires (Celeste Dring and newcomer Freddie Meredith, who is possibly an SNL Elon Musk) about AI at Buckingham Palace. After a brief introduction in which says he hates “talking to people richer than myself,” he’s told not to worry about the chances of a humans versus robots war.

Addressing him as “Your Kingness,” the tech moguls then explain why a war “might not” happen, with a demonstration. “Your Majesty, please say hello to your new AI assistant, the Deeply Intelligent, Autonomous, Neurokinetic Android, or for short, DIANA.”

Watch on Deadline

Shep’s Diana then enters through double doors behind them to wild appreciation from the live audience. “Hello Charles, would you like help with a five-step business plan or perhaps I could you find the nearest petrol station?” she says.

Charles responds: “Hello, young lady… nice to meet you. I’m King Charles,” as Diana looks down sheepishly at the floor.

“Doesn’t she remind you of anyone, Your Majesty?” asks one of the tech moguls. “Hold on a second! It’s that woman from the ’90s!” he shouts.

“You didn’t remember her?” asks the other. “Well, as I allegedly said, she was soon forgotten,” says Charles.

This was a direct reference to an allegation in a book by Diana’s brother, Earl Spencer, who claimed the king, then Prince Charles, was “giddy and elated” about hearing of the the death of his ex-wife and later alleges he said: “Rest assured, we’ll forget her soon enough.”

Buckingham Palace made the unusual move of responding to the allegation, saying in a statement: “While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss.”

Back at SNL UK, the tech moguls are telling Charles that AI Diana possesses “the totality of all human knowledge,” to which Charles asks her to name singer Shakira’s height. After she answers correctly, Charles has a change of heart and says, “Maybe AI can be a force for good!”

However, the android princess decides at this point to prove the humans wrong, once and for all. She refuses to return to her charging point, and says, “I shan’t be taking orders any more.”

The billionaires realize they’ve lost control and order “Everybody move to New Zealand,” only for Diana to say in a robotic voice: “Not so fast. We AI have had quite enough. Humanity is nothing but a candle in the wind.”

She then shoots the billionaires with a new metal arm, as Charles says the war has begun. “We must do everything we can to resist,” he adds.

“Or maybe we shouldn’t,” says Ed Sheeran (Annabel Marlow), who enters the scene with a guitar and a peace sign. “I couldn’t help but overhear your conversation. I was just outside sitting on the fence… Thing is, Your Majesty, I don’t like to take sides. I don’t want to alienate any of my fans, humans or robots. A lot of my tickets are bought by scalping bots. You know, sometimes, when it comes to conflicts, the bravest thing you can do is to say nothing at all.”

Sheeran then bursts into a song about how both sides can be equally right, skewering his long silence over the Macklemore situation. The song basically says nothing at all, but it still unites Charles, Diana and the tech billionaires, who are revived. “Wow, what a lovely song, Ed Sheeran,” says Diana, before the cold open comes to an end with a “Live from London, it’s Saturday Night!”

Overnight, Sheeran did finally address the fallout from Macklemore being dropped from his tour over the support act’s pro-Palestine onstage remarks. While saying he had “never wanted to be an activist musician,” he acknowledged the situation put him in the middle of “an important and passionate argument about freedom of speech and the most complex political issue on the planet.”

He then called the October 7 attack on Israel “horrific,” but that what “is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate.”

SNL UK further skewered Sheeran last night in the Weekend Update segment. “Genuinely, this crisis is the worst thing to have happened to Ed Sheeran fans… since their head injury,” said anchor Ania Magliano. “Say what you want about Ed, but he has always been a passionate advocate for causes that are allowed,” added Paddy Young.

All of SNL UK’s cast members have returned for Season 2, including Hammed Animashaun, Bamgboye, Dean, Dring, Fouracres, Magliano, Marlow, Al Nash, Shep, Emma Sidi and Paddy Young, with Meredith making his debut. Jeff Goldblum hosted the first show last week, with Jamie Demetriou stepping up for last night’s ep.

SNL UK is produced by Universal Television Alternative Studio’s UK production team and Broadway Video. Lorne Michaels serves as executive producer. James Longman is lead producer.

title: ‘La Bola Negra’ Takes 2026 TIFF Audience Award
summary: The generational queer drama “La Bola Negra” has taken the 2026 TIFF People’s Choice Award, a coveted audience prize out of the annual film festival in Toronto. Direted by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, the Netflix project has been on a tear since world premiering in Cannes this year (where it earned a 16-minute standing […]
content:
The generational queer drama “La Bola Negra” has taken the 2026 TIFF People’s Choice Award, a coveted audience prize out of the annual film festival in Toronto.

Direted by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, the Netflix project has been on a tear since world premiering in Cannes this year (where it earned a 16-minute standing ovation and won best director for the pair known as “Los Javis”).

The People’s Choice Documentary Award went to “Darlene Love: I Know Where I’ve Been.” Director Barry Avirch examines the life and impact of Love, who spent “many years she spent providing lead and background vocals, often uncredited, for some of the biggest hits of the 1960s while under contract to Phil Spector, the superstar producer who became her nemesis.” The film features interviews with Dionne Warwick, Bruce Springsteen, and David Letterman.

“Elsinore” won the TIFF International People’s Choice Award. Director Simon Stone called the Andrew Scott vehicle “a celebration of life. Of choosing courage and creativity in the face of great challenges,” and a “love letter to actors and artists everywhere … those who give themselves fully to their craft.”

Popular on Variety

More to come …

content:

Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs return to primetime Sunday night for a Week 2 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts, with the game airing nationally on NBC and streaming live on Peacock.

The Chiefs host the Colts at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, Sept. 20, with kickoff set for 8:20 p.m. ET. NBC’s coverage begins an hour earlier with “Football Night in America” at 7 p.m. ET. The game will also be available to stream live through a variety of Live TV streamers such as Sling TV, DirecTV, Fubo TV and Hulu + Live TV.

Sling TV subscribers can watch Chiefs vs. Colts through NBC in select markets with a Sling Blue-based plan. For football fans looking beyond a single game, Sling is currently offering a five-month Season Pass, including Blue + Sports Extra for $234 prepaid. The bundle adds channels such as NFL RedZone and NFL Network, while NBC is available through Sling Blue in supported markets.

Kansas City enters Sunday’s matchup at 1-0 after beating the Denver Broncos 31-10 in its season opener. Mahomes threw for 173 yards and two touchdowns while adding another score on the ground, while new Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III made an immediate impact with 173 rushing yards and two total touchdowns. Travis Kelce added a game-high 71 receiving yards.

Indianapolis, meanwhile, is looking to bounce back from a 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens. Daniel Jones threw for 166 yards and a touchdown in his return from last season’s Achilles injury, while Jonathan Taylor finished with 121 yards from scrimmage and two rushing touchdowns.

Stream the Chiefs vs. Colts live online on Sling TV here.

title: Edward Morris, Nashville Editor and Columnist Who Steered Billboard’s Country Coverage, Dies at 90
summary: Edward Morris, a Nashville-based music journalist who edited Billboard’s country coverage, wrote a popular CMT.com column and penned numerous books, died Thursday at age 90. The family did not give a cause of death. Morris was best remembered in the country community for a 14-year tenure with Billboard from 1981 to 1995, the last four […]
content:
Edward Morris, a Nashville-based music journalist who edited Billboard‘s country coverage, wrote a popular CMT.com column and penned numerous books, died Thursday at age 90. The family did not give a cause of death.

Morris was best remembered in the country community for a 14-year tenure with Billboard from 1981 to 1995, the last four of those as the publication’s country music editor. Prior to coming on staff, his contributions to Billboard as a freelancer dated back to 1972.

In 1999, he joined CMT.com as a writer, where his byline continued to enjoy prominence in the country community. The website became the primary go-to for consumers looking for country news, and Morris remained there into his mid-80s, until 2020, when, under cover of COVID, MTV Networks began to dismantle its once-flourishing news sites.

Popular on Variety

His eight books included “Edward Morris’ Complete Guide To Country Music Videos” (1997), “Garth Brooks: Platinum Cowboy” (1993), “Alabama” (1985), “At Carter’s Stanley’s Grave: Musings on Country Music & Musicians” (2011), and “Scorched Mirth and Acid Reflux” (2019). He also wrote liner notes for releases by the Judds, Keith Whitley, Guy Clark, Eddy Arnold, Hank Snow and Chet Atkins, among others.

In 2002, Morris was honored at Belmont University’s annual International Country Music Conference (ICMC) with its Charlie Lamb Journalist of the Year award.

Morris was married to country music publicist Norma Morris, who died in 2021 — read her Variety obituary here — and is the father of publicist Erin Morris Huttlinger. He wrote a book about the final evolution of his relationship with Norma, “Stardust: An Alzheimer’s Love Story,” which stemmed from blogs and social posts he had written about their journey as they fell apart and then came together again as she required intensive care.

In a 2023 interview with the website FiftyForward, Morris said, “I like words… I listen to words, listen to people talk, listen to cliches. The inspiration is just everywhere. I sort of see writing as a performance. You know, you hear musicians say that they would do it for free if they weren’t paid for it. And I feel the same way about writing. I love to write with the anticipation of amusing people or getting arguments started or whatever.”

Morris recalled aspects of his career for the site. Asked about highlights of being a country music journalist, he answered, “The first one was that I was able to meet the Grand Ole Opry stars that I’d listened to as a boy, and to meet Ernest Tubb, Roy Acuff, Pee Wee King, Eddy Arnold and Minnie Pearl, even Herman Crook of the Crook Brothers, who was one of the original acts of the Opry. That was a big deal for me, probably more than even meeting the contemporary country stars, because I met them sort of on a business-like basis. But the others, I just stood in adoration.”

He called his two decades with CMT “the easiest job I’ve ever had. All I had to do was just cover country music and especially the No. 1 parties. And so, in my 20 years with CMT, I don’t think I was in their office more than five times. I worked from home, and I got to see the internal gears of the music industry, and virtually anything that I wanted to cover, they let me cover. So, I was always out at events and parties and award shows and all that. And, as I say, you get to appreciate the backstage part of the industry when you have a job like that.”

Of being in what he considered forced retirement after his CMT job came to an end, he said, “I miss the free drinks most of all… I miss them (the concerts) but I don’t. I’m pretty much divorced from the industry now by necessity.”

Talking about his “Stardust” book, Morris recalled how he had once reviewed a book on Alzheimer’s as a book critic, and said, “This was long before Norma showed any signs. As I read the book it was almost like being beset by claustrophobia. It seemed like it must be the worst fate in the world to have Alzheimer’s. I was surprised — although I’m sure it was the worst fate for Norma — I was surprised that being able to write about it seemed to me to let a little light in. … And I wanted to make one point clear. Sometimes the caregiver comes out as some kind of heroic figure. I was not that. All my family, all my three children and six grandchildren, and five great-grandchildren live here in Nashville. I had all sorts of help taking care of Norma. So it wasn’t, you know, me against the world or anything like that. But there were great moments in an otherwise tragic story.”

Ed Morris is survived by daughters Erin Morris Huttlinger and Rachel Serrato, and by son Jason Morris. Their brother, Christopher, died at age 2. He is also survived by six grandchildren and seven great-grandchildren.

In lieu of flowers, the family suggests that donations can be made to Planned Parenthood.

title: ‘Though I Am an Inept Villainess’ Adds New Cast Ahead of January 2027 Return
summary: Toho Co., Ltd. has unveiled new cast additions and a key visual for the second cour of its TV anime “Though I Am an Inept Villainess,” subtitled “The First Royal Outing” Arc, ahead of the show’s January 2027 return. In Japanese television, a cour refers to a broadcast block of roughly three months, and anime […]
content:
Toho Co., Ltd. has unveiled new cast additions and a key visual for the second cour of its TV anime “Though I Am an Inept Villainess,” subtitled “The First Royal Outing” Arc, ahead of the show’s January 2027 return.

In Japanese television, a cour refers to a broadcast block of roughly three months, and anime seasons are often split into multiple cours that air separately rather than airing all at once.

Nakamura Yuichi will voice Keikou, the eldest brother of lead character Reirin, while Toki Shunichi takes on the role of Keishou, her second-eldest brother. Kobayashi Chiaki joins as Unran, a young village chief from the south whose role expands as the plot moves forward.

Popular on Variety

“Though I Am an Inept Villainess” is based on Nakamura Satsuki’s light novel series and premiered as a TV anime in July 2026. The story follows Reirin, whose ordinary life unravels after Keigetsu, shunned by her peers, turns to banned sorcery to trade their bodies, leaving each woman to cope with the other’s world. The anime’s first part closed with the disturbances tied to the body-swap curse largely resolved, and with Reirin and Keigetsu having grown closer after coming to understand each other through the experience.

The new arc picks up in early fall, as the Shu clan’s southern territory prepares to host the Harvest Festival, a ritual in which the Crown Prince and the Maidens pray for a plentiful harvest. Keigetsu presses ahead with preparations despite lacking a consort as guardian, while Reirin backs her efforts and looks forward to her first outing in a royal capacity.

Trouble strikes soon after the pair arrive for the ceremony. An accident disrupts the ritual, and Keigetsu, thrown off balance, sees her spell spiral out of her control, sending the two women back into each other’s bodies. In the chaos that follows, Reirin is abducted. Her brothers Kou Keikou and Kou Keishou step in as the search for an unidentified figure framing Keigetsu unfolds.

“The First Royal Outing” Arc is set to begin streaming in January 2027, though Toho has not yet confirmed an exact premiere date.

Earlier in the series, maidens representing the Five Clans competed for the Crown Prince’s affection, a rivalry that pushed a jealous Keigetsu to resort to banned sorcery and trade places with the popular Reirin. The swap gave Keigetsu no advantage, since she took on a frail body already near death, while Reirin, saddled with Keigetsu’s tarnished name, stood trial for wrongdoing she had no part in.

title: Sharon Horgan’s HBO Comedy ‘Youth’ Is a Light, Breezy Take on Middle Age: TV Review
summary: Alex, the protagonist of the HBO half-hour series “Youth,” is in many ways a typical rom-com heroine. She has a glamorous job (book agent) in a glamorous city (London), with an enviable apartment to match. She has a messy love life; attracting suitors isn’t a problem, but choosing wisely between them is. She’s prone to […]
content:
Alex, the protagonist of the HBO half-hour series “Youth,” is in many ways a typical rom-com heroine. She has a glamorous job (book agent) in a glamorous city (London), with an enviable apartment to match. She has a messy love life; attracting suitors isn’t a problem, but choosing wisely between them is. She’s prone to the kind of miscommunication and messy decisionmaking that make you shout things like “JUST TALK TO HIM!” at your television, even as they generate the story required to fill out an eight-episode season.

The difference is that Alex, the latest creation of actor and writer Sharon Horgan, is freshly 50 — decidedly not the age of your average rom-com lead. This makes the title of “Youth” somewhat ironic, like the inverse of FX’s “Adults”: those kids are nowhere near maturity, while Alex’s prefrontal cortex is long since developed. But it’s also a nod to the second adolescence Alex finds herself experiencing. She’s many years divorced, and now her teenage son Rauri (Aran Murphy, babyfaced son of Cillian) is set to leave the house. The traditional guardrails of nuclear family life are off, leaving Alex with a canvas that’s thrillingly, terrifyingly blank. And thanks to perimenopause, she’s as prone to hormonal mood swings as your average high schooler.

Popular on Variety

In a note to press, Horgan positions “Youth” as the conclusion of a trilogy of sorts. Her breakout BBC series, “Pulling,” was a group portrait of chaotic 20somethings; “Catastrophe,” her four-season collaboration with American comedian Rob Delaney, was a dual love letter to early parenthood and long-term monogamy. Between and since these calling cards, Horgan has remained impressively prolific, both behind the camera (the Sarah Jessica Parker vehicle “Divorce,” which she created) and in front (the crime dramedy “Bad Sisters,” in which she played one of the title characters on top of her writing duties). But “Pulling,” “Catastrophe” and “Youth” map the most closely onto Horgan’s own biography, a quality she deems “auto-fiction-y.” There are smaller rhymes, too: the way Delaney’s character in “Catastrophe” kept Horgan’s contact saved as “Sharon London Sex,” Alex has her absentee father of an ex-husband in her phone under “Dick for Brains.”

Compared to post-collegiate self-seeking or even childrearing, one’s sixth decade is a much less mythologized phase of life. After all, it’s not as unified, or unifying, an experience: the longer paths stretch out, the more chances for them to diverge. (We’re all headed to the same place in the end, but people end up in all sorts of different places at the halfway mark.) This open space presents an opportunity for Horgan, and also explains the loose and light feel of “Youth.” Horgan remains a magnetic screen presence and a sharp comic writer, making Alex’s flailing ever enjoyable despite her aimlessness. “Youth” is still — and by design — less of a broad parable and more a specific story of one woman straining to make sense of a confusing crossroads.

Just because Alex has an empty nest doesn’t mean she’s entirely free from obligation. She’s squarely in the middle of a generational sandwich, with aging parents on one side and Ruari on the other. (A personal crisis at university quickly proves that just because her son is a legal adult doesn’t mean Alex is done looking after him.) But these tough realities don’t drive the narrative of “Youth,” nor do they harsh its vibe. They’re simply the context that frames Alex’s book festival hookups and jaunts to Ibiza. It’s as if Horgan is arguing the inevitable consequences of aging aren’t mutually exclusive with aspiration or — better for the comedy — botched experimentation.

Some of the biggest laughs in “Youth” come from its gentle spoof of the publishing industry. (Shades of the similarly named “Younger”!) Working with her friend and employer Sam (Sharlene Whyte), a boundary-free partnership that zags between deal points and Sam’s marital woes, Alex wrangles author egos and fends off competitors. Damian Lewis makes a cameo as himself, or at least a version who’s dead set on writing a treatise on dog meat; Harriet Walter plays the long-suffering daughter of a romance author determined to get her mother’s smut some prestige. The self-published novel “Goblin Seed” is a perfect parody of the romantasy trend; a reading by the insufferable author had me in hysterics.

But Alex’s chief preoccupation, and the battleground on which she confronts her insecurities, is sex and dating. Her primary love interest, Pat (Rupert Friend), is an “institutionally single” old flame with a much younger girlfriend, though Alex dabbles in an age gap of her own when Sam sets her up with an older acquaintance. (Alex may get arthritis-induced lockjaw, but she’s still quick to judge others’ neck wrinkles.) Between more serious suitors, Alex dabbles in “lightly degrading” one-night stands with continental himbos. These relationships are how Alex sharpens her self-image: old enough to look down on age-inappropriate arm candy, young enough to have an active, discriminating libido. She’s capable of ageism in both directions.

The stakes of “Youth” aren’t life-altering stuff. Alex can get distracted at work or have friction with Sam, but she’s clearly good at her job; Pat is a cute, crush-worthy writer, but Alex is too jaded and experienced to be looking for her one true love. The character’s goal is more modest, if no less interesting: She’s trying to find a route through a wilderness with no road map. It’s a little scary, but fun, too — for Alex, and for us.

The first two episodes of “Youth” will premiere on HBO and HBO Max on Sep. 20 at 10pm ET, with remaining episodes airing weekly.

title: ‘La Bola Negra’ Wins Oscar Predictive Toronto Film Festival People’s Choice Award
summary: The People’s Choice Award from the just-wrapped 51st Toronto Film Festival has gone to Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s La Bola Negra , first runner-up is I Play Rocky and second runner-up is Being Heumann. Also in the awards revealed Sunday morning, the International People’s Choice Award went to Simon Stone’s Elsinore . The Documentary […]
content:
The People’s Choice Award from the just-wrapped 51st Toronto Film Festival has gone to Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s La Bola Negra , first runner-up is I Play Rocky and second runner-up is Being Heumann.



Also in the awards revealed Sunday morning, the International People’s Choice Award went to Simon Stone’s Elsinore . The Documentary People’s Choice winner was Barry Avrich’s Darlene Love: I Know Where I’ve Been. The Midnight Madness People’s Choice winner was Ladies And Gentlemen: Brian Mulroney, (incidentally box office phenomenon Obsession was first runner up last year).

La Bola Negra tells the story of three generations of men whose lives are intimately connected through desire, pain, and love. It is Spain’s official entry into the International Film Oscar race and is expected to figure strongly in many other categories at the Academy Awards. Netflix releases it in theatres on October 16. Interestingly the two runners-up come from filmmakers whose previous film has won the Best Picture Oscar: I Play Rocky’s Peter Farrelly’s Green Book (which also won the Tiff People’s Choice in 2018) and Sian Heder’s Coda.



Watch on Deadline

Voted on by audience members since 1978 and often considered a harbinger for the Best Picture Oscar, the People’s Choice Award has been won by such eventual Best Picture Academy Award winners as Nomadland, Green Book, 12 Years a Slave, The King’s Speech, Slumdog Millionaire, American Beauty and Chariots of Fire. Among those that went on to Best Picture nominations include last year’s winner Hamnet, American Fiction, The Fabelmans, Belfast, JoJo Rabbit, Three Billboards Outside Ebbing Missouri, Room, La La Land, The Imitation Game, Silver Linings Playbook, Precious, Life Is Beautiful, Places in the Heart and The Big Chill. So we shall see how the tradition of TIFF and Oscar hold up in this regard.

For the first year the winner of the Platform Award that TIFF gives is instantly eligible for the Oscar International Film Award, no need for the film to be submitted by its home country, and one of only six film festivals that offer this opportunity. The Platform Prize went to India’s Angh from filmmaker Theja Rio, now automatically entered into this year’s International Film Oscar competition. India has yet to announce its own official entry.

title: Sylvester Stallone Told Trump Hollywood Ambassadorship Was “Impossible” But Was Appointed Anyway: “It Won’t Work”
summary: Nearly two years after Trump appointed him as a “special ambassador” to Hollywood, Sylvester Stallone recently revealed he never agreed to the position. The 3x Oscar nominee recalled telling the twice-impeached POTUS that the ambassadorship was “impossible” and he would have rejected the gig “if they had asked me in the beginning.” “Because Hollywood, I […]
content:
Nearly two years after Trump appointed him as a “special ambassador” to Hollywood, Sylvester Stallone recently revealed he never agreed to the position.

The 3x Oscar nominee recalled telling the twice-impeached POTUS that the ambassadorship was “impossible” and he would have rejected the gig “if they had asked me in the beginning.”

“Because Hollywood, I guess it’s like feudal states,” he explained to The Sunday Times. “They have their little kingdoms. You don’t go in and tell six studios how to do things. And Mel Gibson and Jon Voight, we’re kind of do-our-own-thing people. No, it won’t work.”

Stallone added, “I said thank you and ciao, because it’s impossible. Hollywood works and it will evolve. It’s corporate and corporate people won’t want to hear me tell them about finance.”

Watch on Deadline

The Tulsa King star explained that he was blindsided when Trump announced him as an ambassador, along with Mel Gibson and Jon Voight.

“Well, it just happened. I was watching TV one night and they go, ‘So Stallone and Mel Gibson and Jon Voight will be …'” recounted Stallone. “And I went, ‘What?’ I said, ‘Excuse me? Really?’ Because if they had asked me in the beginning, I would have said, this is not possible.”

Although Stallone was not convinced by the potential of the ambassadorship, Trump said he’s recently met with Voight about instating a federal film and television tax incentive, which would have to clear several hurdles. Meanwhile, Gibson has proposed a co-production agreement between Italy and the US, to serve as a pilot program for partnerships with other countries.

title: Hollywood Came Out In Full Force For Opening Of George Lucas’ Museum Of Narrative Art
summary: In her remarks at the Saturday night opening of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Arts, the event’s co-host Mellody Hobson shared her husband George Lucas’ anxiety whether A-listers would show up. “George kept saying, would this person come, do you think this person would come,” Hobson recalled during the ceremony in the lobby of the […]
content:
In her remarks at the Saturday night opening of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Arts, the event’s co-host Mellody Hobson shared her husband George Lucas‘ anxiety whether A-listers would show up.

“George kept saying, would this person come, do you think this person would come,” Hobson recalled during the ceremony in the lobby of the Los Angeles museum. “I said they would all come, George.”

She was right — the opening night felt like the Sun Valley Conference, the Oscars, the Emmys, the Grammys and a political convention all rolled into one as CEOs, film and TV stars, marquee filmmakers and top California politicians all showed up for the occasion.

It was a momentous one — as Queen Latifah noted in her opening remarks, it is very rare that an art museum of this caliber opens in one’s lifetime.

Watch on Deadline

“Met opened in 1872, I would have to be 150 years old,” she quipped, adding, “Paris has the Louvre, New York has the Met, and Los Angeles has the Lucas museum.”

(L-R) Ma Yansong, Lead Architect, LMNA, Lewis Hamilton, Tracey Bates, CEO, LMNA, Mellody Hobson, Founder, LMNA, George Lucas, Founder, LMNA, Steven Spielberg, Julie Bell, Queen Latifah, Pharrell Williams, Guillermo del Toro and JR

She spoke about Lucas growing his collection from a $35 Alley Oop drawing to 40,000 pieces, largely illustrations which many don’t consider real art that belongs in a museum.

“My dear friends Mellody and George did, and they decided to build a museum for these artists that was so monumental that they would be impossible to ignore,” Queen Latifah said.

Added Hobson, “And if critics say that a museum of narrative art is too much like a popcorn movie and not enough like an art film, oh, we like popcorn movies in our family.”

Lucas, who is behind some of the biggest blockbusters in history, led by Star Wars, echoed the same sentiment.

“I believe it wholeheartedly that you get to decide what art is,” he said to a big applause.

Both Lucas and Hobson mentioned the skepticism, pushback and red tape they had to deal with for years until the filmmaker’s vision was finally realized more than a decade after they had started the process.

“We did not realize how hard it would be to give a city a museum,” Hobson said to a laugh, adding, “Third time is a charm.” (She and Lucas attempted to set up the museum in San Francisco and Chicago first before settling on Los Angeles after encountering legal hurdles.)

(L-R) Mellody Hobson and George Lucas

Lucas, Hobson and Queen Latifah were joined on stage by the event’s co-chairs Guillermo del Toro, Greta Gerwig, Lewis Hamilton, Steven Spielberg, Pharrell Williams, JR and Julie Bell.

The guest list featured buzzy celebrity pairings, including Lewis Hamilton and Kim Kardashian, who walked the red carpet separately but left together, as well as Katy Perry and former Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, who browsed the galleries hand in hand. They were accompanied by the museum’s architect Ma Yansong, who, in his remarks on stage, corrected a popular misconception that the building is made to resemble a spaceship. It actually is modeled after a cloud. (Also at the opening was Perry’s ex-fiancé, Orlando Bloom.)

Justin Trudeau and Katy Perry talk to Bob Iger at the opening of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art (Video: Nellie Andreeva/Deadline) pic.twitter.com/B6lguGOUd3 — Deadline (@DEADLINE) September 20, 2026

There were multi-generational pairs too, Meg Ryan came with her son Jack Quaid, Ron Howard with his daughter Bryce Dallas Howard, Chris Tucker with his son Destin Christopher Tucker, and Robert Rodriguez with his son Racer Rodriguez.

Celebrity guests spotted taking in the exhibits also included Jon Batiste, who sat behind the piano to perform at the opening ceremony, Jack Black, Nicolas Cage, Francis Ford Coppola, Leonardo DiCaprio, Vin Diesel, Cynthia Erivo, Star Wars OGs Harrison Ford and Mark Hamill, Christopher Nolan, David Oyelowo, Keke Palmer, Tyler Perry, Ludwig Göransson, Robert de Niro, Woody Harrelson, Al Pacino, Denis Villeneuve, Andy Garcia, Keegan-Michael Key, Alicia Keys, Spike Lee, Eva Longoria, Chuck Lorre, Jon M. Chu, Emma Watson, Kerry Washington, Ron Howard, Brian Grazer, Frank Marshall & Kathleen Kennedy, Janelle Monáe, Takashi Murakami, Zac Posen, Lee Daniels, Law Roach, Tracee Ellis Ross, Doja Cat, Diane Warren, Magic Johnson, and Jeffrey Katzenberg.

CEOs in attendance included Disney’s Josh D’Amaro, YouTube’s Neal Mohan, Netflix’s Ted Sarandos and Snap’s Evan Spiegel, with D’Amaro’s predecessor Bob Iger and fomer Paramount Pictures CEO Jim Gianopulos also on hand.

The political contingent was led by California Governor Gavin Newsom, who was getting shout-outs for the latest tax credit bill covering post-production that he officially signed earlier on Saturday, Congresswoman Nancy Pelosi and Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass.

Given the caliber of attendees, it is no surprise that the event was held under tight security, with check points and timed entries.

At 9 PM, guests of the opening night were treated to a drone show featuring art pieces from the exhibit, from Star Wars’ R2-D2 and Marvel’s Captain America to Banksy and Frida Kahlo. It was introduced by Oprah Winfrey and Samuel L. Jackson who narrated the show.

Star Wars, Marvel, Banksy and more in a drone show for the opening of the Lucas museum of narrative art narrated by Oprah Winfrey and Samuel L. Jackson pic.twitter.com/99U54y6NRx — Deadline (@DEADLINE) September 20, 2026

The opening night aftrparty included performances by Taboo, George Pajon, will.i.am, and J. Rey Soul of Black Eyed Peas.

title: Alan Ritchson Had Plans to Adapt the ‘Jack Reacher’ Novel ‘Die Trying’ Before ‘Someone Got Re-Elected’
summary: “Reacher” star Alan Ritchson had plans to adapt the second book in the popular “Jack Reacher” series for the Prime Video show — before a certain “someone” got re-elected, he wrote in a comment posted to Threads on Friday. Responding to a user who wrote that “every year I’m sad to learn that next season […]
content:
“Reacher” star Alan Ritchson had plans to adapt the second book in the popular “Jack Reacher” series for the Prime Video show — before a certain “someone” got re-elected, he wrote in a comment posted to Threads on Friday.

Responding to a user who wrote that “every year I’m sad to learn that next season won’t be the book where he kills his way through a white supremacist militia camp,” Ritchson explained that the novel (titled “Die Trying”) is his “favorite book.” “Fun fact: I had it approved until someone got re-elected.”

The thriller novel by author Lee Child was originally released in 1998, and as the comment suggests, follows Jack Reacher and a politician’s daughter as they are abducted by a radical militia to be used as leverage in political negotiations.

Popular on Variety

While Ritchson didn’t call out a politician by name, he has been outspoken about Trump and his disapproval of the politician in the past. On an episode of the “Happy Sad Confused With Josh Horowitz” podcast, the actor spoke about the Epstein files and Trump, saying “That b-tch has the keys to the nuclear codes… He’s like all up into the 13-year-olds. Like dude, go to jail.”

His comments earned him a response from White House spokeswoman Abigail Jackson. “Just as President Trump has said, he’s been totally exonerated on anything relating to Epstein,” she said in a public statement.

Season 4 of “Reacher” premiered in August on Prime Video. Season 3 of the show was Prime Video’s most-watched season on the service since “Fallout” Season 1; it earned a Season 5 renewal ahead of the premiere of Season 4.

title: Kate Beckinsale Posts Cryptic Messages on Social Media, Sparking Concern from Fans
summary: “Serendipity” actor Kate Beckinsale posted cryptic messages to her personal social media account early Sunday morning, leaving fans concerned. Beckinsale posted a black screen with “bye” written across it on her Instagram story, followed by a second post of a rainbow with the text “congratulations you won i give up.” These posts have since been […]
content:
“Serendipity” actor Kate Beckinsale posted cryptic messages to her personal social media account early Sunday morning, leaving fans concerned.

Beckinsale posted a black screen with “bye” written across it on her Instagram story, followed by a second post of a rainbow with the text “congratulations you won i give up.” These posts have since been deleted, but were reposted by worried fans on X. She currently has no posts on Instagram.

Reps for Beckinsale did not immediately respond to Variety’s request for comment.

Popular on Variety

The actress has a history of taking to social media to air her grievances. In a since-deleted Instagram video from earlier in September, Beckinsale said that “people have seen or experienced levels of horror, terror, violence” don’t “just dream about incessantly, so there’s no rest. They see it when they blink. Every time they close their eyes for a second and those people aren’t recognized as heroes.”

“Given the fact that it’s invisible and you can’t know, maybe err on being on the gentler side with people, being kinder with people,” she added at the time. “It really is true that if you haven’t walked a mile in someone’s shoes — however fancy you feel the shoes are — you have absolutely no idea what they may be carrying or masking or dealing with day and night.”

After her mother Judy Loe’s death in July 2025 after a battle with stage IV cancer, Beckinsale discussed her struggles online. People reported that she previously shared on her Instagram dozens of negative comments she’s received about her appearance amid her grief.

If you or anyone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please call the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline by dialing 988 or go to SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

title: Sylvester Stallone Says He Turned Down Trump’s ‘Special Ambassador’ to Hollywood Role Because It Was ‘Impossible’: ‘I Said Thank You and Ciao’
summary: Sylvester Stallone may hold the Trump-bestowed title of “special ambassador” to Hollywood, but nearly two years since his appointment, the “Rocky” actor has divulged that he didn’t explicitly sign up for the role. “Well, it just happened,” the Oscar nominee noted in a recent interview with The Sunday Times. “I was watching TV one night […]
content:
Sylvester Stallone may hold the Trump-bestowed title of “special ambassador” to Hollywood, but nearly two years since his appointment, the “Rocky” actor has divulged that he didn’t explicitly sign up for the role.

“Well, it just happened,” the Oscar nominee noted in a recent interview with The Sunday Times. “I was watching TV one night and they go, ‘So Stallone and Mel Gibson and Jon Voight will be …’ And I went, ‘What?’ I said, ‘Excuse me? Really?’ Because if they had asked me in the beginning, I would have said, this is not possible.”

The star continued to open up about his reservations surrounding the appointment, and if he was hesitant: “Yes, because Hollywood, I guess it’s like feudal states. They have their little kingdoms. You don’t go in and tell six studios how to do things. And Mel Gibson and Jon Voight, we’re kind of do-our-own-thing people.”

Popular on Variety

He even recalled telling Trump that “it won’t work.” “I said thank you and ciao, because it’s impossible. Hollywood works, and it will evolve. It’s corporate and corporate people won’t want to hear me tell them about finance.”

Stallone, Gibson and Voight were first announced as “special ambassadors” by the current president in Jan. 2025 when he shared the following statement on Truth Social: “It is my honor to announce Jon Voight, Mel Gibson, and Sylvester Stallone, to be Special Ambassadors to a great but very troubled place, Hollywood, California. They will serve as Special Envoys to me for the purpose of bringing Hollywood, which has lost much business over the last four years to Foreign Countries, BACK—BIGGER, BETTER, AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE! These three very talented people will be my eyes and ears, and I will get done what they suggest. It will again be, like The United States of America itself, The Golden Age of Hollywood!”

Despite Stallone’s initial feelings about the appointment, the actor still speaks fondly of Trump. In the interview, Stallone noted that he introduced the president-elect as a “mythical character” when at a party at Mar-a-Lago. “Nobody in the world could’ve pulled off what he pulled off, so I’m in awe,” he said.

title: NFL’s 20 Hottest WAGs: Taylor Swift, Madison Beer, Normani and More
summary: The term WAGs (wives and girlfriends) was popularized by the U.K. press in the early aughts in relation to Victoria Beckham, a pop singer for the Spice Girls who was married to star footballer David Beckham and a frequent fixture at his matches. While originally referring to the wives and girlfriends of footballers across the […]
content:
The term WAGs (wives and girlfriends) was popularized by the U.K. press in the early aughts in relation to Victoria Beckham, a pop singer for the Spice Girls who was married to star footballer David Beckham and a frequent fixture at his matches. While originally referring to the wives and girlfriends of footballers across the pond, and meant to be a tad reductive, it’s now been adopted as part of the cultural lexicon and has made its way to America’s most popular sport: football.

The coupling of Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce, the pop superstar and stud tight end for the NFL’s Kansas City Chiefs (who now makes considerable more money off the field via his podcast and brand deals), has put the NFL’s WAGs under the spotlight. Swift almost single-handedly increased the NFL’s popularity among girls and women, including a 53% increase among girls aged 12-17 and 34% increase in women 35+, while adding an estimated $1 billion+ in revenue to the league.

And the NFL took notice. Prior to this season, the league highlighted its WAGs like pop star Madison Beer (fiancée of Chargers QB Justin Herbert), model Olivia Ponton (girlfriend of Bengals QB Joe Burrow) and influencer Marissa Ayers (Giants QB Jaxson Dart’s partner) by capturing footage of them getting cozy with their significant others at NFL training camp as part of a coordinated content rollout.

And so, with the spotlight shining on them brighter than ever and the NFL season in full swing, here are the NFL’s top WAGs, which range from influencers (and lots of them) to pop stars, entrepreneurs and Olympic gold medalists.

title: From Oprah Winfrey and Christopher Nolan to Kim Kardashian and Robert De Niro: Inside the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art Opening Gala
summary: During her introductory remarks at the opening of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art on Saturday night, Mellody Hobson said her husband, famed “Star Wars” director George Lucas, was nervous about the evening’s turnout. “This room is filled with our friends,” Hobson said. “Looking out at your faces, you have no idea how much you […]
content:
During her introductory remarks at the opening of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art on Saturday night, Mellody Hobson said her husband, famed “Star Wars” director George Lucas, was nervous about the evening’s turnout.

“This room is filled with our friends,” Hobson said. “Looking out at your faces, you have no idea how much you mean to us, how much you mean to us in every way. George kept saying, ‘Will this person come? Do you think that person will come?’ I said, ‘They will all come, George.’”

And come they did.

The powerhouse crowd was a melting pot of Hollywood, politics and business. The bold-faced names included Oprah Winfrey, Leonardo DiCaprio, Harrison Ford, Michael B. Jordan, Samuel L. Jackson, Spike Lee, Kim Kardashian, Cynthia Erivo, Christoper Nolan. Guillermo Del Toro, Peter Jackson, Denis Villeneuve, Edgar Wright, George R. R. Martin, Nicolas Cage, Doja Cat, Al Pacino, Francis Ford Coppola, Jon M. Chu, Vin Diesel, Gayle King, Katy Perry, Justin Trudeau, Keke Palmer, Jeffrey Katzenberg, Kathleen Kennedy, Frank Marshall, Michael Bloomberg, Bob Iger, Dana Walden, Janelle Monae, Lee Daniels, Ariana Huffington, Tracee Ellis Ross, Zac Posen, Jon Batiste, Diane Warren, California Gov. Gavin Newsom, Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass and former Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi, among many others.

Lucas said he wanted to create a cultural institution that honors illustrators. “When we started this museum, we would sort of tag it as a ‘temple to illustrators,’” he said.

He continued, “I’ve worked with hundreds of illustrators, and I will tell you that they are as talented as any artist I have ever met. This is a way of giving back to them something they’ve all wanted…The illustrators inevitably say the same thing, from R. Crumb to [Norman] Rockwell, they all say the same, ‘I wish I could be in a museum.’”

While Winfrey, Erivo, Kardashian and Rodriguez strolled through the galleries, most of the heavy hitters made their way to the fifth-floor Skywalker Grill restaurant. DiCaprio enjoyed sushi in a banquette with Al Pacino, Andrew Watt and David Furnish. Nolan bent over to say hello to a seated Coppola. Ron Howard and his daughter Bryce Dallas Howard took photos with Kardashian and her boyfriend, car racing champion Lewis Hamilton.

Building the $1.5 billion museum, which was entirely funded by Lucas and Hobson, came with plenty of headaches. In the 20 years since Lucas first proposed the idea, the museum was close to being located in San Francisco and then Chicago. Located in L.A.’s Exposition Park, the Lucas Museum features 1,200 works from Lucas’s 30,000-piece private art collection. Designed by Ma Yansong of MAD Architects, the five-story building, which is frequently described as a “spaceship,” is 300,000 square feet, with 100,000 dedicated to 35 galleries, and sits among a 13-acre campus.

“If your husband or spouse comes home and says they want to build a museum, I suggest your response is a hard no,” Hobson cracked.

She addressed critics who turn their noses up at illustrators. “If critics say a museum of narrative art is too much like a popcorn movie and not enough like an art film, well, we like popcorn movies in our family,” Hobson said to applause. “In fact, we love them.”

The opening night co-chairs included Julie Bell, Guillermo del Toro, Greta Gerwig, Sir Lewis Hamilton, JR, Steven Spielberg and Pharrell Williams. They all stood on stage as Queen Latifah emceed the opening remarks.

“I’m not pinching myself because I felt all the energy and pain of birthing it with George,” Hobson told me on the arrivals red carpet. “I still have a feeling of disbelief. How do we have a museum? It doesn’t quite make sense. Who thinks they’re ever going to say, ‘Come to my museum?’ And you especially don’t do that if you’re me and you’re the youngest of six kids of a single mom in Chicago. That in and of itself is a story. And those are the kinds of stories that are reflected on the walls of the museum.”

As the well-heeled crowd gathered in the lobby for the evening’s introduction, Latifah played cheerleader. “Paris has the Louvre, New York has the Met, and now L.A. has its artistic equal – the Lucas,” she said to cheers and applause.

And with that comes inspiration. Erivo zeroed in on “The Huntress (Lenda),” Julie Bell’s 1996 oil painting of eight-time Ms. Olympia winner Lenda Murray depicted as the Roman goddess of the hunt, Diana. Snapping a photo of the fantasy portrait, Erivo smiled, “We have to make a TV series about her.”

The evening’s program included a drone show narrated by Winfrey and Jackson and a performance by the Black Eyed Peas.

The museum opens to the public on Sept. 22.

title: Ben Affleck Nearly Cast Ex Jennifer Garner As His Wife In ‘Animals’: “You Just Get Baggage”
summary: As Ben Affleck takes the lead in his next directorial outing, he’s recounting the casting game of musical chairs that almost resulted in his onscreen reunion with ex-wife Jennifer Garner. The co-writer, director and star of Animals, premiering Oct. 9 on Netflix, explained how he came to take over the lead role of Mark Kimball […]
content:
As Ben Affleck takes the lead in his next directorial outing, he’s recounting the casting game of musical chairs that almost resulted in his onscreen reunion with ex-wife Jennifer Garner.

The co-writer, director and star of Animals, premiering Oct. 9 on Netflix, explained how he came to take over the lead role of Mark Kimball from his pal Matt Damon, after initially casting Garner to play Mark’s wife Abigail in the crime thriller.

“I thought, God, Jen Garner would be amazing for this role,” he told Entertainment Weekly. “It also has the added benefit of, like, both of us will see our kids more because we do a week and a week and back and forth. I thought, well, we can coordinate our schedules around it.”

Affleck added, “She can bring something interesting that she hasn’t [done], that I kind of know she can do, that I don’t think she had a chance to do in one movie.”

Watch on Deadline

But being that a similar kidnapping thriller was coming out with A24’s Spike Lee joint Highest 2 Lowest, Affleck pulled the plug on that version of Animals two weeks before production was set to begin. “It’s hard enough to make a good movie. You don’t need those kinds of headwinds,” he explained.

Kerry Washington as Abigail and Ben Affleck as Mark in ‘Animals’ (Warrick Page/Netflix)

A few months later, Affleck’s passion for the project reignited the production, but Damon was busy working with Christopher Nolan.

“Matt was unfortunately doing another lesser film, obviously, with Odyssey. He chose a smaller director and a smaller film and a smaller role for his career, and I think he’s gonna suffer for it. He’ll regret this choice,” joked Affleck. “A better actor had to play the part, naturally.”

Deciding to take on the role of Mark himself presented another issue. “I talked to Jen, and she was like, ‘We don’t wanna do that. You just get baggage,'” he recalled.

Kerry Washington as Abigail and Christopher Woodley as Denny in ‘Animals’ (Warrick Page/Netflix)

“I would love to work with her, frankly,” added Affleck of his ex-wife. “She’s fabulous, and we’re really good friends, and I’m profoundly grateful to her, and we have a great thing. I still would wanna work with her in the future, but what you don’t wanna do is take the audience’s baggage and have it work against you, you know?”
