In the past, she was “struck by this extraordinary imbalance.”

“The Sherpas did much of the essential work: carrying loads, fixing ropes, setting up camps and making repeated journeys through some of the most dangerous terrain. When something went wrong, they were often the ones who went back up to rescue others. Yet the heroic narrative still tended to belong to the Western climber,” she stresses.

“These were elite mountaineers, often with multiple Everest summits [under their belts], doing some of the most dangerous and skilled work. Yet, outside of Nepal, almost nobody knew their names.”

Celebrated for her documentaries, Peedom felt that this time, the story demanded something else.

“So much of Tenzing’s journey is internal. It’s about faith, family, ambition and identity, and private moments for which no camera was present. Documentary could tell me what happened, and I had spent years gathering that history, but drama allowed us to get closer to what those experiences might have felt like,” she says.

“I didn’t want to portray Tenzing from the outside. I wanted the audience to experience the expedition from his perspective. I wanted them to understand what was at stake for him personally and how it felt to enter this very British world while carrying an entirely different relationship to the mountain.”

His is a spiritual journey, too.

“Very much so. Tenzing was Buddhist, and the mountain had spiritual meaning for him. As a boy, he herded his father’s yaks on the Tibetan high plateau beneath Everest. I think the journey was, in some sense, a journey home,” notes Peedom.

When he finally reached the summit, he prayed and left offerings there.

“In many Western mountaineering stories, the mountain is an adversary, something to defeat or conquer. For Tenzing, the relationship was much more complex. There was ambition, certainly. But there was also reverence.”

Peedom’s film tackles complicated questions around identity.

“I’m not sure I would say he never belonged anywhere. He belonged very deeply to his family, his faith and the Himalayan world he came from. But after Everest, his identity became politicized, and different countries wanted to claim him,” she says. However, the film ends before all that begins.

“We leave him coming back down the mountain before the fame and politics take hold. There’s something very poignant about that moment. He has finally achieved this thing he has dreamed about and worked towards for so many years, and for that brief moment, the achievement simply belongs to him.”

Peedom spent more than 20 years around mountaineers. When asked about what drives them, she’s not sure if there’s only one answer.

“People climb for completely different reasons. What I do understand better is the extraordinary clarity that extreme environments can provide. Everything extraneous falls away. A breath matters. A decision matters. The person on the other end of the rope matters. You become intensely present in a way that ordinary life rarely demands,” she says.

“I understand that pull better now, but I don’t think you can ever fully explain it. Perhaps that mystery is part of the attraction.”

title: Judge Orders Trump White House to Restore Access to CNN, MS NOW, Politico Immediately
summary: A federal judge has ordered the White House to immediate reinstate access to CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists, after President Donald Trump summarily banned them last Friday. U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly of the D.C. Circuit, a Trump appointee, granted the news orgs’ motion for a temporary restraining order in the lawsuit they filed […]
content:
A federal judge has ordered the White House to immediate reinstate access to CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists, after President Donald Trump summarily banned them last Friday.

U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly of the D.C. Circuit, a Trump appointee, granted the news orgs’ motion for a temporary restraining order in the lawsuit they filed against Trump and three White House officials, alleging the ban violated the First Amendment. The TRO will remain in effect for 14 days.

The White House must “immediately return, reinstate, and restore the White House ‘hard pass’ press credentials held by employees of CNN, MS NOW, and POLITICO that were revoked on or about September 18, 2026, until further Order of the Court or the expiration of this Temporary Restraining Order,” Kelly wrote in the ruling issued a little after midnight Thursday.

Popular on Variety

Theodore Boutrous, a lawyer representing the news organizations, said in a statement: “This is a strong ruling vindicating freedom of the press, due process and the rule of law. We greatly appreciate the court’s swift action.”

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A copy of the judge’s ruling is available at this link.

The judge found that CNN, MS NOW and Politico demonstrated they were likely to succeed in proving their claims, “at least on their Fifth Amendment procedural due process claim.” Kelly noted that the White House does not dispute that the news outlets “did not receive notice and an opportunity to be heard before their hard passes were revoked.” He also said the outlets “have shown that they are likely to suffer irreparable harm absent a temporary restraining order.”

Kelly did not address the question of whether the White House’s yanking of press access to CNN, MS NOW and Politico infringed their First Amendment rights. In their lawsuit, the trio said Trump’s ban “brazenly discriminates based on editorial viewpoint.”

In its response to the lawsuit, the White House claimed in court filings that the ban was necessary to prevent the disclosure of “classified and sensitive national security information.” As an example of CNN’s alleged infractions, the White House cited a Jan. 16, 2026, report that “disclosed ‘top-secret’ construction details related to the East Wing bunker, which is designed to protect the President in times of crisis or national security emergency”; the White House did not dispute the accuracy of the CNN report.

“No doubt, protection of the national security is a weighty interest on the [White House’s] part,” Kelly wrote in his TRO order. However, he continued, “Certainly, that is not what President Trump said when he announced that he was ‘banning’ Plaintiffs from the White House — instead, he focused on the alleged lack of truthfulness and negativity of Plaintiffs’ reporting.”

Trump announced last Friday (Sept. 18) that he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico “effective immediately” from the White House because, as he has claimed hundreds of times before about media outlets he doesn’t like, they are “fake news.”

On Monday, CNN, MS NOW and Politico sued Trump and three White House officials over his ban, alleging it violates the First Amendment and “brazenly discriminates based on editorial viewpoint.”

Trump, anticipating that the White House would be defeated in the case, has already suggested he would seek an appeal of an unfavorable ruling. “Almost without question and, as usual, we’ll go for appeal because Fake News people and publications that only write negatively, and who violate our National Security by writing false and defamatory stories with unknown ‘sources,’ shouldn’t be allowed access to the most important Office anywhere in the World,” Trump wrote on Monday on his Truth Social platform.

In protest of Trump’s ban of the news outlets, ABC News, CBS News, NBC News and Fox News — which alongside CNN provide the White House TV pool coverage — announced they were suspending coverage of the president at events because of his ban on the news outlets. The TV pool blackout continued to remain in effect through Thursday.

title: ‘Percy Jackson’ Season 3 Stars Walker Scobell, Leah Sava Jeffries Set to Attend Italy’s Lucca Comics and Games
summary: Disney+ will spotlight Season 3 of “Percy Jackson and the Olympians” at Italy’s Lucca Comics and Games Festival, where stars Walker Scobell, Leah Sava Jeffries and Aryan Simhadri, and the show’s co-creator and executive producer Jonathan E. Steinberg, and executive producer Dan Shotz will be on hand for a dedicated panel presentation that will include […]
content:
Disney+ will spotlight Season 3 of “Percy Jackson and the Olympians” at Italy’s Lucca Comics and Games Festival, where stars Walker Scobell, Leah Sava Jeffries and Aryan Simhadri, and the show’s co-creator and executive producer Jonathan E. Steinberg, and executive producer Dan Shotz will be on hand for a dedicated panel presentation that will include previously unseen footage.

Adapting Rick Riordan’s third book, “The Titan’s Curse,” the third season follows Percy Jackson (Scobell), Grover Underwood (Simhadri) and their fellow campers at Camp Half-Blood — plus some new faces — to save Annabeth Chase (Jeffries) and goddess of the hunt Artemis (Dafne Keen) from the Titan Atlas (Holt McCallany).

Lucca Comics — which will run Oct. 28-Nov. 1 — is a unique geek meet attended by more than 200,000 fans each year and held within the walls of the Tuscan town of Lucca, surrounded by perfectly preserved 16th and 17th century ramparts.

Popular on Variety

Other highlights of this year’s edition include the presence of Aardman Animations’ founder Peter Lord and director Peter Walker for the Italian premiere of “Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom.”

Japanese filmmaker Kore-eda Hirokazu will be making the trek to Lucca to meet fans and discuss adapting Fujimoto Tatsuki’s manga “Look Back,” which blends live-action realism with the creative process behind the manga genre.

Lucca’s so-called Movie Area section will also see Warner Bros. Pictures Animation launch the latest Dr. Seuss adaptation, “The Cat in the Hat,” with directors Erica Rivinoja and Alessandro Carloni in tow.

Seminal writer-graphic artist Frank Miller, creator of the “Dark Knight” Batman comics series, will be returning to Lucca for a screening of the doc “Frank Miller: American Genius,” made by his creative partner Silenn Thomas, who will also be on hand.

Japanese anime producer Hibiki Minagawa is coming to present the international premiere of Toei Animation’s kiddie film “Star Detective Precure – The Movie!”

Also from Japan, director Naoya Ando will be making the trek to present animated feature “Gintama: Yoshiwara in Flames,” which retells the iconic “Gintama” manga arc with brand-new subplots.

Lucca, an event dedicated to fandom, cosplay, role-playing games and the entire cross-media universe of comics, is increasingly becoming an integral part of the Hollywood studios’ promotional push in Europe, ever since the Movie Area strand started 16 years ago.

title: Block the Merger Coalition Files Legal Request to Oppose Paramount-Warner Bros. Deal
summary: A coalition of groups working under the Block the Merger banner have filed an emergency request to oppose Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery ahead of a court hearing in California this morning pertaining to the deal. The motion for an amicus brief – enabling interested parties to present legal arguments relating to a case […]
content:
A coalition of groups working under the Block the Merger banner have filed an emergency request to oppose Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery ahead of a court hearing in California this morning pertaining to the deal.

The motion for an amicus brief – enabling interested parties to present legal arguments relating to a case — was filed Thursday morning in the federal court of California, where Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín is still deciding over whether to approve the $111 billion deal.

In a statement, members of the coalition said they are asking Judge Martínez-Olguín “to grant interested parties the opportunity to formally oppose the weak and unenforceable consent decree that state attorneys general entered into with Paramount on Monday.”

Popular on Variety

The groups participating in the motion are The Committee for the First Amendment, Free Press, Freedom of the Press Foundation, Future Film Coalition and International Documentary Association.

On Monday, Paramount reached a deal with 12 state attorneys general who had filed an antitrust lawsuit, which had been set for a March 2027 trial.

The settlement terms including a commitment from Paramount to release at least 30 movies a year, set up an independent editorial board to oversee the CNN and CBS News operations and hold on to the Paramount Studios or Warner Bros. lots in California for at least five years.

California AG Rob Bonta called the settlement terms “very strong.”

A hearing is set for 11am today for Judge Martínez-Olguín to address “certain outstanding questions” over the merger. Block the Merger said he may also rule on their motion during that hearing.

“Hundreds of thousands of people across the country called on state attorneys general to enforce the law and to protect consumers, workers and free speech,” said Free Press Co-CEO Jessica J. González, co-counsel on the motion. “The weak and unenforceable deal the AGs struck with Paramount leaves us in the lurch. We deserve our day in court.”

title: Gaza Documentary ‘NAZA’ Set to Stream for Free on The Guardian Website After Global Release
summary: “NAZA,” the hot-button documentary about killings in Gaza that won a special jury prize at the recent Venice Film Festival, is set to soon be released theatrically in more than 50 territories and will subsequently be made visible to global audiences for free via the website of British newspaper The Guardian. The Guardian, which produced […]
content:
“NAZA,” the hot-button documentary about killings in Gaza that won a special jury prize at the recent Venice Film Festival, is set to soon be released theatrically in more than 50 territories and will subsequently be made visible to global audiences for free via the website of British newspaper The Guardian.

The Guardian, which produced “NAZA” in tandem with James Wilson (JW Films) and executive producer Jonathan Glazer, has announced that the doc – which was shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv and shows “in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza,” according to its official synopsis – will be screening in cinemas across the world starting Sept. 28, having secured theatrical distribution via French sales company MK2 in 56 territories since its Sept. 10 world premiere in Venice.

As previously announced, “NAZA” has set a distribution rollout for U.S. theaters starting Sept. 30 via an innovative plan that forgoes selling the film to a studio or independent distributor.

Popular on Variety

The U.S. rollout, which kicks off exclusively at the IFC Center in New York City, is “spearheaded by The Guardian and MK2, who have assembled a team of U.S. and international partners and consultants to bring the film to audiences as quickly as possible,” they said.



In addition to the U.S. distribution plan, “NAZA” has now secured unspecified theatrical distributors in the following territories: France, U.K., Italy, Spain, Germany, Belgium, Netherlands, Austria, Switzerland, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Greece, Portugal, Poland, Lithuania, Romania, Bulgaria, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Thailand, Canada, Brazil, Turkey, Central America and the Middle East, according to a statement from The Guardian and MK2.

In Italy, “NAZA” will get a three-day event release on 500 screens via I Wonder distribution between Sept. 28-30.

The film has also “been offered to a number of distributors and cinemas in Israel,” the statement said.

And The Guardian will be exploring other ways to enable the film to be seen in the occupied Palestinian territories, it added.

“NAZA” builds on revelations first published by the Israeli-Palestinian publication +972, Hebrew-language outlet Local Call and The Guardian between 2023 and 2025.

Directors Abraham and Szor said in a statement, “We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of ‘NAZA’s’ producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.”

title: CAPA Deputy Director Unveils Sean Connery Doc; Talks Mission To Expand French Company’s International Reach
summary: EXCLUSIVE: A documentary promising unprecedented behind-the-scenes insight into the life of late Scottish star Sean Connery is in the works at Paris-based factual film and TV production company CAPA. Titled Sean Connery: The Untold Story, it is being developed and directed by French journalist and TV presenter Stéphanie Renouvin, who is the French granddaughter of […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: A documentary promising unprecedented behind-the-scenes insight into the life of late Scottish star Sean Connery is in the works at Paris-based factual film and TV production company CAPA.

Titled Sean Connery: The Untold Story, it is being developed and directed by French journalist and TV presenter Stéphanie Renouvin, who is the French granddaughter of the James Bond star and his second wife, the French Moroccan painter Micheline Roquebrune.

It follows Renouvin’s 2022 mini-series Mme Sean Connery, which focused on her grandmother and was made primarily for a French audience.

Sean Connery: The Untold Story is one of the upcoming titles currently being developed by Sally Blake, the newly appointed Deputy Director of CAPA, which is part of the Studio TFI group.

Watch on Deadline

“We developed it here. It’s a coproduction with Canal Plus and Sky has come onboard in the UK,” says Blake, also citing London-based Embankment and Glasgow-based Boy 313 as coproducers.

Blake, who was appointed to her new role in early September, will work closely with CAPA MD Patrice Lorton, with a mission to “internationalize” the company’s activities and specific goals to connect it with new territories and sources of funding.

She says the upcoming Sean Connery documentary ticks the box of appealing to the company’s home audience in France as well as having wider international.

“Sean Connery is definitely universal while Stéphanie’s connection to the subject gives it a good anchor in France. That’s a perfect example of something that can speak across audiences,” she says, talking to Deadline just days after the announcement of her appointment.

Career highlights & international mission

The Canadian French documentary veteran has been working as a producer with CAPA since 2017, both directly and occasionally under CAPA label, Films à Cinq, the Paris-based factual content production banner she created with Martin de la Fouchardière.

Documentary feature credits across her 20-year career include Su Rynard’s 2015 work The Messenger, exploring environmental threats to songbirds around the world, which she co-wrote, produced and edited. It premiered at Canada’s Hot Docs festival and was then acquired by Kino Lorber for the U.S.

Under the CAPA umbrella, she was a producer on Ron Chapman’s Revival69: The Concert That Rocked the World, as well as Anastasia Trofimova’s Russians at War, which world premiered at the Venice Film Festival in 2024.

More recent credits include the 2025 natural history two-parter 13 Hours to Survive, about how sea creatures tackle the challenge of being left high and dry by the tide, which played on Arte and Blue Ant Studio’s Love Nature platform; 2025 six-part, docu-series Marie Antoinette Confidential, coproduced with Banijay Studios France for Canal Plus, and TV docu-movie Tardigrade, the Indestructible Animal, which she also co-wrote.

“I’ve been a producer with CAPA for a few years and was an independent producer previously, both in Canada and in France, so I have built up a big network for making international coproductions… the main reasons that they’ve given me this job is to push the international angle,” says Blake of her new role.

“CAPA is the largest documentary production company in France. It’s really well known, really well established and producing for all the platforms and all the channels,” she continues.

Blake cites true-crime series From Rock Star to Killer, about rock singer Bertrand Cantat, who killed his partner actress Marie Trintignant in 2003, and 2025 docu-drama November 13, Sonia’s Choice as examples of recent CAPA productions that have moved the dial in France.

“From a Rock Star to a Killer was a Netflix series which did really, really well. It was definitely in the top 10 of Netflix documentary series,” she says of the first title, which was released on the platform on March 2025.

The two-part November 13, Sonia’s Choice recounts the true story of a woman at the heart of the hunt for the culprits of the Paris terror attacks on November 13, 2015, who is now living in hiding.

It was broadcast in a primetime slot by state broadcaster France Télévisions on November 13, 2025, as part of its programming to mark the 10th anniversary of the attacks in which terrorists killed 130 people and injured many more across the French capital.

“It was really interesting because it was an innovative hybrid film.” Blake says of the docu-drama, directed by David André and starring Carima Amarouche in the titular role. “Docu-drama is definitively one of the interesting areas we want to do more in. They’re working really well right now.”

Blake believes strongly that the CAPA has the content, no-how and connections to expand its international footprint.

“I think that the quality of the CAPA programming is something that could travel even more than it does now, and that’s something that I really, really want to make happen,” she says, adding that working with international partners is also becoming a necessity.

“It’s something we all have to do right now when the industry is so difficult. We have to really, really look for those international partnerships and those ‘sneaky’ ways of financing things. You also need a sense of what’s out there, what the trends are, which is something I have, because I travel to all these markets quite a bit.”

Alongside Sean Connery, The Untold Story, other upcoming CAPA productions that Blake feels have strong international potential include Compost.

Being developed as a hybrid for the French market, it delves into the ecosystem and “drama” of a compost heap, exploring its inhabitants and the roles they play in breaking down human leftovers and garden refuse.

“I have a long-standing experience in science, the environment and the natural world and of course that’s something that lends itself to international,” says Blake, citing titles such as 13 Hours to Survive.

“I am currently working on a film, which is going to be primetime feature documentary for France Télévisions. The entire thing is going to be filmed in a compost heap… it will version and adapt very easily to other markets because composting, technically speaking, is something everyone can do,” she says.

“It’s literally about the drama that happens inside a compost heap. Imagine the wooden boxes at the end of gardens, you open them up and it’s absolutely fascinating. It’s like a jungle in there with these tiny, tiny creatures. In the French version, the compost heap is in the back garden of a fictional family to give a human side to it, but the natural history part of the film can travel anywhere.”

In the backdrop, Blake acknowledges it is a complex time for the documentary sector, with the genre making waves on the festival and awards circuit at the same as it faces funding squeezes.

“There have been different waves. There was a contraction of the North American documentary market a few years ago that seems to have settled in the sense we know where we’re at right now. But recently, we’re seeing more and more crisis within public broadcasters in Europe. We’re definitely feeling that in France, but I think that’s happening all over,” she says.

In spite of the challenges, Blake remains confident in the genre.

“People are always looking for keys to decrypt the world, and the world is just getting scarier and more confusing, so I think there’s always going to be an interest in documentary.”

title: BBC Cuts Latest: Around 150 Tech Staff Expected To Take Voluntary Redundancy, Saving Millions
summary: EXCLUSIVE: The drumbeat of BBC cuts continues, with Deadline hearing that roughly 4% of the British broadcaster’s technology unit is expected to take voluntary redundancy. Around 151 employees are set to exit BBC Media Tech, the unit that helps power online services including iPlayer and BBC Sounds. The voluntary redundancies are expected to deliver savings […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: The drumbeat of BBC cuts continues, with Deadline hearing that roughly 4% of the British broadcaster’s technology unit is expected to take voluntary redundancy.

Around 151 employees are set to exit BBC Media Tech, the unit that helps power online services including iPlayer and BBC Sounds. The voluntary redundancies are expected to deliver savings of £14.5 million ($19.8M) over the coming years.

Deadline understands that 11% of staff in BBC Media Tech applied for voluntary redundancy, but only 40% (the 151 figure) can be accepted. The department is set to announce other changes over the coming days, as the BBC reveals further details about its plan to cut 2,000 jobs and save £500M amid a funding crisis.

Deadline revealed on Wednesday that the BBC is expected to announce TV and radio network closures early next week, with speculation that BBC Three could be shut. Also on Wednesday, the BBC Sport unit told employees about plans to make redundancies and cut sports bulletins on its news channel.

Watch on Deadline

The BBC will also consider “bumping” roles in BBC Media Tech, meaning an employee can take voluntary redundancy, but another staff member facing compulsory redundancy can backfill the role.

BBC technology teams have faced uncertainty over the past year amid the corporation drawing up radical plans to outsource thousands of non-content jobs to the private sector. The proposals, codenamed Project Ada, explored spinning off Media Tech into a potential commercial unit. Discussion about Project Ada has gone quiet since the arrival of Matt Brittin, the BBC’s new director general, and the exit of chief operating officer Leigh Tavaziva.

The BBC’s £500M savings target expands on a previous goal worth £1.5 billion. The bigger picture behind the cuts is that 94% of the UK population use the BBC every month, but fewer than 80% pay the £180 annual licence fee. The BBC is attempting to bridge this gap.

The BBC declined to comment.

title: The Guardian To Offer ‘NAZA’ For Free On Website After Theatrical Run & Is Exploring Ways To Show Doc In Israel & Palestinian Territories
summary: The Guardian and mk2 films have announced global release plans for Israeli directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor’s bombshell documentary NAZA. The partners said that The Guardian-produced documentary will be released theatrically from September 28 onwards in more than 50 territories, having secured theatrical distributors in 56 territories since its world premiere at the Venice […]
content:
The Guardian and mk2 films have announced global release plans for Israeli directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor’s bombshell documentary NAZA.

The partners said that The Guardian-produced documentary will be released theatrically from September 28 onwards in more than 50 territories, having secured theatrical distributors in 56 territories since its world premiere at the Venice Film Festival on 10 September.

In an unprecedented move, The Guardian will make NAZA available for global audiences for free on its website, after the theatrical run later this fall. The partners said this move was due to the “worldwide interest” in the documentary as well as The Guardian’s “commitment to fearless, independent journalism”.

The investigative documentary, exposing the calculated targeting of civilians in Gaza in missile strikes by Israeli military through the testimony of intelligence personnel and soldiers involved in the killing, has caused a sensation since its Venice debut.

Watch on Deadline

It landed a record 25-minute ovation its Venice premiere Film, but has since been attacked by Israeli politicians including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has threatened to strip the directors of their Israeli citizenship even though he has no power to do this under the country’s laws.

The Guardian and mk2 said the film has been offered to a number of distributors and cinemas in Israel, and they will be exploring other ways to enable the film to be seen in the occupied Palestinian territories.

They added that, as previously announced, the film will receive its North American premiere on 26 September at New York Film Festival, and will open in U.S. theaters on September 30, launching exclusively at the IFC Center in New York City.

It will expand to Los Angeles and other key markets on October 9, ahead of a national roll out in the weeks to follow.

NAZA is produced by The Guardian and James Wilson (JW Films); and executive produced by Oscar-winning filmmaker Jonathan Glazer.

The documentary builds on a series of revelations first published by the Guardian, +972 Magazine, a Israeli-Palestinian publication, and Hebrew-language outlet, Local Call between 2023-2025, including groundbreaking investigations into how Israel uses AI to identify targets in Gaza.

It follows Abraham and Szor’s No Other Land, winner of the Best Documentary Academy Award in 2025. Co-directed with Palestinian filmmakers Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal, it documented Israeli army-backed efforts to erase the West Bank Palestinian villages of Masafer Yatta, while painting a wider picture of Israeli occupation.

“We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israelis to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible,” said Abraham and Szor in a joint statement as the NAZA release plans were unveiled.

“The threats from the Israeli government to revoke our citizenship and the death threats do not change that and will not stop the film. We thank our colleagues for the solidarity and look forward to sharing NAZA all over the world very soon.”

Harry Davies, a Guardian investigations correspondent and one of NAZA’s producers, added: “NAZA is grounded in rigorous journalism published over the past three years, but it is also a powerful piece of cinema that will soon be available on screens, large and small, around the world.”



“The initial response from those who’ve seen it shows audiences are engaging deeply with the urgent questions the film raises. We’re working with MK2 and international partners to bring the film to global audiences as soon as possible.”

The 56 territories sold by Paris-based mk2 film, which boarded international sales on the documentary ahead of its Venice premiere, include France, UK, Italy, Spain, Germany, Belgium, Netherlands, Austria, Switzerland, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Greece, Portugal, Poland, Lithuania, Romania, Bulgaria, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Thailand, Canada, Brazil, Turkey, Central America, and the Middle East.

title: Paramount UK’s 5 Launches Linear Drama Network With ‘All Creatures Great And Small’, ‘Gilmore Girls’ & ‘Home And Away’ Plus BBC Drama ‘Waterloo Road’
summary: Paramount UK network 5 (formerly Channel 5) is defying linear naysayers once again by launching a drama network airing the likes of All Creatures Great and Small, American hits like Gilmore Girls and the BBC’s Waterloo Road. Replacing the 5Select channel, 5Drama will launch October 21 with a collection of 5 originals, American imports and […]
content:
Paramount UK network 5 (formerly Channel 5) is defying linear naysayers once again by launching a drama network airing the likes of All Creatures Great and Small, American hits like Gilmore Girls and the BBC’s Waterloo Road.

Replacing the 5Select channel, 5Drama will launch October 21 with a collection of 5 originals, American imports and Australian series including popular soap Home and Away.

British drama will air at peak times in the evening including originals like 5’s smash All Creatures Great and Small reboot, which airs on PBS Masterpiece in the U.S., while weekday afternoons will be dedicated to U.S. shows like Gilmore Girls, Columbo and ABC’s A Million Little Things. Home and Away will start from ep 1 in the afternoons.

Intriguingly, the new channel also has rights to the first 10 seasons of long-running BBC school series Waterloo Road, seasons that aired between 2006 and 2014 before it was rebooted in 2023.

Watch on Deadline

5Drama joins a Paramount UK linear roster including the main 5 channel, 5Action, 5Star and 5USA.

Launching a linear channel may feel anachronistic and comes at a time when the BBC is set to close at least one but under maverick content chief Ben Frow, 5 has leaned in to linear. It is the only network to have grown linear share over the past few years and regularly beats rivals Channel 4 and BBC Two in the overnights.

The news comes in the week that Paramount-Warner’s $110B deal terms included divestiture targets for American linear networks like BET, VH1 and Comedy Central. In the UK, David Ellison recently committed to £80M ($105M) of additional 5 investment over three years as a means of getting the deal past the regulators, along with commiting to 5’s public broadcasting remit.

5 boss Reemah Sakaan said: “Award winning drama is increasingly at the heart of what 5 offers viewers, so it’s the right time to give it a dedicated home. This, and the expansion of our portfolio across multiple platforms, is about sharpening our channels and giving viewers a clear offer wherever they’re watching – on linear, 5Streaming, Freely or YouTube.”

Meanwhile on the other end of the digital scale, 5 is launching a YouTube channel for documentaries, joining recently-launched 5 sports, news and kids channels on the platform.

title: Streaming & Local Film Propel Major Asian Markets To $15B Content Spend This Year – MPA
summary: Streaming and local film are set to send spend on content in seven major Asian markets over the $15B mark this year, according to a study. Media Partners Asia (MPA) reports that content investment will rise from $14.8B in 2025 to $15.1B this year and on to $15.4B in 2031. While TV currently accounting for […]
content:
Streaming and local film are set to send spend on content in seven major Asian markets over the $15B mark this year, according to a study.

Media Partners Asia (MPA) reports that content investment will rise from $14.8B in 2025 to $15.1B this year and on to $15.4B in 2031.

While TV currently accounting for 60% of the spend, followed by online video at 30% and film at 10%, MPA’s ‘Asia Video Content Dynamics 2026’ report noted “virtually all incremental growth comes from streaming and film as television budgets decline.”

The report assessed spend in India, Indonesia, Korea, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam, with key findings being that while Asian video industries command large audiences and have valuable brands, this is not always “converting into attractive financial returns” and many “established media companies” are trading “well below equity book value.”

MPA is predicting those that spend wisely, rationalize costs and protect “genuine content advantages” will “increasingly separate” those that don’t.

Watch on Deadline

Within the $14.8B figure from 2025, Korea accounts for $6.9B, with India second at $5B, which is approximately 80% of the total.

MPA noted streaming has overtaken TV in India with online video accounting for 46% of content investment in 2025, compared to 42% in television. Indian audiences streamed 420 billion hours last year, with JioHotstar leading the way with a 58% of the premium VOD viewing. Sports is driving demand, with JioHotstar experiencing a boost in reach during the IPL cricket season.

In Korea, Netflix leads the way with domestic streamer TVING a clear second, while Indonesia’s Vidio, which has been profitable since the fourth quarter of last year, leading that market with six million paying subs. TVING’s extensive baseball rights helped expand its subs base from 5.3 million to 6.5 million, according to MPA.

Local film represents “the region’s clearest growth opportunity,” MPA added. This was evidenced by Vietnam’s box office rising 20% to $213M in 2025 with local titles accounting for 69%. There were similar figures in Indonesia, while India posted a record box office total of $1.41B, and local titles were attributed for a “substantial theatrical recovery” in Korea this year.

TV advertising, on the other hand, fell, with MPA suggesting “several television industries still carry more legacy capacity than their advertising economics can support.”

Stephen Laslocky, Vice President, MPA, said: “Asia’s video industries are not short of audiences or creative capability. They are short of structures that convert both into sustainable returns. As the margin for error narrows, management quality will become decisive.

Companies that rationalise legacy costs through restructuring and the adoption of new technologies such as AI, collaborate where independent investment no longer makes sense and protect the content that gives viewers a reason to stay will increasingly outperform, and the valuation gap between winners and losers will widen.”

Another MPA analyst Myat Pan Phyu (May), added: “The viewership data shows demand is intact. Premium VOD engagement continues to grow across India, Korea and Southeast Asia, streaming now leads content investment in India, and local stories are winning at the box office from Hanoi to Jakarta and Mumbai. This is a story of reallocation rather than retreat as capital moves toward streaming and local film, where both audiences and returns are growing.”

title: ‘Forgotten Island’ Review: A Delightful Animated Celebration of Friendship and Filipino Culture
summary: In Hollywood, parallel thought is a funny thing. As in every other sphere, two or more people can have a similar idea at the same time, but when those ideas bloom into movies, their release can feel like a land rush. Which is more firmly cemented in moviegoers’ memories, “Dante’s Peak” or “Volcano”? “Lambada” or […]
content:
In Hollywood, parallel thought is a funny thing. As in every other sphere, two or more people can have a similar idea at the same time, but when those ideas bloom into movies, their release can feel like a land rush. Which is more firmly cemented in moviegoers’ memories, “Dante’s Peak” or “Volcano”? “Lambada” or “The Forbidden Dance”? “Vice Versa,” “17 Again” or “Like Father, Like Son”? (Trick question: it’s “Big.”) “Forgotten Island” is the second film of at least five this year with a plot that hinges on some kind of magic portal, but Universal’s delightful animated adventure deserves to be remembered more for the creative and cultural elements that set it apart from its competition than those that overlap.

Utilizing a dizzying panorama of Filipino mythology, longtime collaborators and “Puss in Boots: The Last Wish” co-directors Joel Crawford and Januel P. Mercado tell a familiar but moving story about friendship, brought to life through a vivid voice ensemble. Grammy-winning musician H.E.R. plays Josephine “Jo” Yuson, an overzealous elementary school student living in the Philippines, who befriends fellow classmate Raissa Molina (Liza Soberano) when they both get sent to the principal’s office. A dreamer whose father abandoned her, Jo conflates her family history with Filipino lore, tracing the path of her grandmother Lola (Dolly de Leon) through the forgotten island of Nakali and believing fervently in its mythical flora and fauna.

Popular on Variety

Fueled by Lola’s encouragement, the two girls escape into an elaborate but imaginary world during adolescence, but with college looming for Raissa in the U.S., Jo is increasingly afraid of being left behind — especially after her grandmother passes. On the night before Raissa is set to depart for Caltech, Jo convinces her to have one last escapade together, but their celebration is interrupted when she uncovers a magical sand dollar that opens a portal transporting them to the real Nakali.

They awakens on a beach with the portal key gone and no memory of the previous night, although Raissa now has wings and they share a tattoo with Raww (Dave Franco), a were-aspin (a dog-human hybrid from Filipino folklore) who insists they asked him to be their island guide. Raww takes them to Batiba (Jenny Slate), a catlike creature who offers to help them return home — in exchange for the matching bracelets they made as kids, which hold all of the memories of their friendship. Instead, they set out with Raww to recover the magical sand dollar themselves, encountering a series of magical creatures — some helpful, others determined to kill them — as they try to find a way home before Raissa’s flight leaves on the other end of the portal.

Though “Forgotten Island” is rated PG, it not only borrows from more mature sources for inspiration (like “The Hangover”) but is unafraid to be a little bit rude (a gastrointestinal phenomenon called “fire-rrhea” figures into the plot), and occasionally even scary. It’s perfectly appropriate viewing for adults and older teens, but guardians of younger moviegoers — who will be mightily tempted by Truffle Wuffle (Ronny Chieng), the irresistibly cuddly king of the Duwende people — should use discretion. The film’s potty humor, mostly depicted in anime-style 2D, shouldn’t present too many viewers with a challenge, but Manang (Lea Salonga), the fearsome, vampire-like monster who pursues Jo and Raissa throughout the film, is violent and genuinely terrifying.

Yet that mix is exactly what makes the film so powerful, as it gently confronts younger children with some of life’s inevitable realities — including sacrifice and death. Jo has maintained her wrecking-ball momentum since childhood, and now that she’s faced with losing her best friend, the movie zeroes in on how painful it is for her to slow down and come to terms with this devastating change. Raissa, on the other hand, is accused of acquiescing to her parents’ dreams for her by going far away to Caltech — but she hasn’t been honest with Jo about a plan that was actually her decision.

These are conflicts that have been dramatized in any number of coming-of-age films where an ambitious teen realizes they’ve outgrown their troublemaking, underachieving best friend. What sets this particular version apart is the density of the Filipino mythology that Crawford and Mercado, themselves longtime BFFs, use to frame the adventure. Treating nature as a living organism with energy and emotions isn’t especially unusual; including a narcissistic merman (named Mermahn, with the emphasis on the second syllable) is, especially when he has starfish nipple pasties that harmonize. Raww isn’t just a semi-anthropomorphized pup, he’s one of the free-ranging street dogs that roam Filipino cities.

The movie does a lot of table-setting to establish the various creatures that exist in Jo’s imaginary world before we get to meet them in their actual habitat: a visually stunning combination of digital precision and hand-sketched details that read beautifully on screen, like an extreme closeup of the three-color printing process used for comic books. (See it in the best visual format you can find.) If you’re not already familiar with the lore explored here, you may occasionally fall behind. (Sorry, who are these peaceful tree people again?) But each new environment is so unique and visually arresting that it’s easy to let go and just enjoy the ride.

In addition to a lovely score by Nathan Matthew David, Crawford and Mercado frontload the film with classic ’80s and ’90s songs, most crucially INXS’ “Never Tear Us Apart.” H.E.R. and Soberano are exceptionally good as Jo and Raissa, the not-always-calm center of a storm of colorful characters. At 41, Franco still has the right cracked delivery for an adolescent, which fits Raww as naturally as fleas on a stray dog. As Batiba, Slate’s borderline baby voice walks a nimble line between seductive and menacing, but Manny Jacinto is the real scene-stealer as a literal baby demon. As Mermahn, Kevin McCann is perfectly smug, vacuuming the air from most of his scenes, but the collective orbit of these supporting characters serves to externalize, fuel and eventually resolve the conflict between the two principals.

Seemingly intentionally, the film leaves some details unresolved — where’s Jo’s absentee father, and exactly what made Manang so bitterly angry? But whether or not they’re breadcrumbs leading to another adventure, thankfully they’re not what you remember on the way out of “Forgotten Island.” Deeply felt and fully satisfying, Crawford and Mercado’s odyssey is a wonderful cinematic experience — but for best results, watch it with a friend.

title: ‘Beast in Me’ Renewed for Season 2 With Claire Danes Returning
summary: “The Beast in Me” has been renewed for Season 2 at Netflix, Variety has learned. Claire Danes will return to star as Aggie Wiggs and executive produce as she did in Season 1. In addition, Season 1 showrunner Howard Gordon has signed an overall TV deal with Netflix under his Teakwood Lane Productions banner, through […]
content:
“The Beast in Me” has been renewed for Season 2 at Netflix, Variety has learned.

Claire Danes will return to star as Aggie Wiggs and executive produce as she did in Season 1. In addition, Season 1 showrunner Howard Gordon has signed an overall TV deal with Netflix under his Teakwood Lane Productions banner, through which he will develop new series for the streamer. Gordon remains attached to “The Beast in Me,” but he will serve as co-showrunner on Season 2 alongside Season 1 executive producer Daniel Pearle.

“We always told ourselves we’d only do a second season of ‘The Beast in Me’ if we found a story that was worthy of the first – and I’m thrilled to say we found it,” Gordon said. “We loved making this show and our audience seemed to love watching it, so we’re enormously grateful to Jinny Howe and Netflix, and to Karey Burke and 20th Television for giving us the chance to get the band back together and do it again.”

Popular on Variety

“The Beast in Me” was originally announced as a limited series when it was picked up in 2024. It also campaigned as a limited series at this year’s Emmy Awards, for which Season 1 star Matthew Rhys won the award for outstanding lead actor in a limited or anthology series. The series also won the Emmy for outstanding music composition for a limited or anthology series, movie or special (original dramatic score).

But in the tradition of “Big Little Lies” and other “limited series” before it, Netflix and “The Beast in Me” team began exploring the possibility of a second season and opened a writers’ room earlier this year. Not surprising, in the end, given the show’s critical acclaim and love from audiences. Aside from the attention it received on the awards circuit, “The Beast in Me” debuted at number one on the Netflix global top 10 chart the week it debuted and stayed in the top 10 for five weeks. It racked up over 43 million views in just seven weeks, per Netflix.

“We are thrilled to bring back ‘The Beast in Me’ and to welcome Howard Gordon to the Netflix family with this creative partnership,” said Netflix Head of Scripted Series Jinny Howe. “The series captivated global audiences, delivered extraordinary performances led by Claire Danes, and earned Matthew Rhys a historic Emmy win. We are incredibly proud of what Howard Gordon, Gabe Rotter, and the entire cast and crew achieved. We can’t wait for audiences to see what Howard and Daniel Pearle have in store for the next season.”

Gabe Rotter is the creator and an executive producer of “The Beast in Me.” As mentioned above, both Gordon and Pearle will serve as co-showrunners and executive producers on Season 2, with Danes again executive producing. Antonio Campos, Caroline Baron, Amy Lippman, Conan O’Brien, David Kissinger, Jeff Ross, Claire Danes and Jodie Foster also executive produce. The series is produced by 20th Television.

title: John Malkovich to Receive Outstanding Performer of the Year Award at Santa Barbara International Film Festival
summary: John Malkovich will be honored with the Outstanding Performer of the Year Award for his performance in Martin McDonagh’s “Wild Horse Nine” at the 42nd annual Santa Barbara International Film Festival, which will take place Feb. 3-13. The film recently screened at the Telluride, Toronto and Venice film festivals, the latter of which awarded Malkovich […]
content:
John Malkovich will be honored with the Outstanding Performer of the Year Award for his performance in Martin McDonagh’s “Wild Horse Nine” at the 42nd annual Santa Barbara International Film Festival, which will take place Feb. 3-13.

The film recently screened at the Telluride, Toronto and Venice film festivals, the latter of which awarded Malkovich with the Best Actor award. Releasing in theaters Nov. 6, Malkovich stars alongside Sam Rockwell as two CIA agents traveling from Santiago to Easter Island the day before the 1973 Chilean coup.

“A legendary actor gives this year in ‘Wild Horse Nine’ his best performance to date in which he combines pathos, volatility, vulnerability and tenderness,” said Roger Durling, the executive director of SBIFF. “It’s a high wire act that shows us what a commanding artist he is and we are thrilled to be honoring him with our Outstanding Performer of the Year Award.”

Popular on Variety

Malkovich recently starred in “Sacrifice” alongside Salma Hayak and Anya Taylor-Joy and “In the Hand of Dante” with Oscar Isaac and Al Pacino. The actor, director and producer has also recently appeared in the Apple TV series “Bad Monkey” and is currently in production of the Amazon Prime thriller “Bishop.” He previously earned an Emmy Award for “Death of a Salesman” and received two Academy Award nominations for Best Supporting Actor in “Places in the Heart” and “In the Line of Fire.”

The Outstanding Performer of the Year award celebrates individuals who have given exceptional performances in film. Past recipients of the award include Michael B. Jordan, Ralph Fiennes, Bradley Cooper, Margot Robbie, Ryan Gosling, Emma Stone, Jennifer Lawrence, Viola Davis, Angelina Jolie, Helen Mirren and Heath Ledger.

title: ‘Sesame Street’ Movie Set at Netflix, Plus ‘Gabby’s Dollhouse’ Spinoff and ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ Game
summary: After kids and family content brought Netflix 15% of its viewership in the first half of 2026, the streamer is doubling down on its children’s slate. Netflix announced several family-oriented projects on Thursday, beginning with “Sesame Street,” which it began streaming last year. A new “Sesame Street” film is in development, produced by Sesame Workshop […]
content:
After kids and family content brought Netflix 15% of its viewership in the first half of 2026, the streamer is doubling down on its children’s slate.

Netflix announced several family-oriented projects on Thursday, beginning with “Sesame Street,” which it began streaming last year. A new “Sesame Street” film is in development, produced by Sesame Workshop and Netflix film chairman Dan Lin’s company Rideback. The flagship series has been renewed through Season 62, with Volume 4 of Season 57 set to begin streaming on Nov. 23, followed by Volymes 5 and 6 next year. Spinoff series “Mecha Builders,” originally released in 2022, will land on Netflix on Oct. 26.

Netflix is also expanding some of its own children’s IP. Popular preschool series “Gabby’s Dollhouse” is getting a spinoff called “Doozie’s Doghouse,” which follows Gabby’s sister. Premiering on Nov. 9, the project is described as a “mixed-media companion series” featuring imaginative animal-themed play. Unscripted spinoff “Gabby’s Dollhouse: Makers and Bakers” will debut on Dec. 9 with four holiday-themed episodes followed by additional episodes next year. Hosted by Laila Lockhart Kraner as Gabby, multiple duos will complete baking and crafting challenges judged by Aidy Bryant, Justin Willman and Melissa Villaseñor.

Popular on Variety

A new preschool series called “Puppy Pirates” has also been greenlit. Created by Matthew Fernandez, the series follows “four heroic hounds who sail the high seas fetching whatever’s been lost — treasure, stuffies, you name it.” And “Bad Dinosaurs,” created by Joel Veitch, Alex Mallinson and David Shute has been renewed for seasons 2 and 3.

Netflix Playground, the company’s kids gaming arm, will release “KPop Demon Hunters: Ready, Set Shine” on Sept. 29. Counting game “Numberblocks: Hide and Seek” will also debut that day, followed by a “Trash Truck” game on Oct. 27.

“We’re curating a slate of favorite-worthy series, films and games to serve kids at every age and stage of their development. Whether that’s spending more time with Gabby and her adorable sister Doozie, meeting the crew of ‘Puppy Pirates’ for the first time, or growing up alongside more ‘Sesame Street,’ we’re building a place parents can feel good about,” reads a statement from Heather Tilert, vice president of kids and preschool animation series. “A place filled with great stories, beloved characters, and enriching games kids will want to come back to again and again.”

title: ‘Musk’ Trailer: Alex Gibney Dissects the Legacy of the World’s Richest Man in Sprawling Documentary
summary: Bleecker Street has released the trailer for “Musk,” Alex Gibney’s new documentary about the world’s richest man, tech mogul Elon Musk. “Musk” premiered out of competition at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival on Sept. 8, where it received a four-minute standing ovation, and then screened at the Toronto International Film Festival. The sprawling exposé […]
content:
Bleecker Street has released the trailer for “Musk,” Alex Gibney’s new documentary about the world’s richest man, tech mogul Elon Musk.

“Musk” premiered out of competition at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival on Sept. 8, where it received a four-minute standing ovation, and then screened at the Toronto International Film Festival. The sprawling exposé about one of the most divisive figures across popular culture has a runtime of almost four hours.

Musk has no involvement in the film, and recently let his thoughts be known about Gibney’s work in a series of replies on X, his own social media platform.

Popular on Variety

Under a video of Gibney at a press conference for “Musk,” he wrote that “dogshit is worth more respect” than the director. In a separate reply, he claimed that Gibney “just assembled a hit list of people who either have an axe to grind or don’t even know me (but still have an axe to grind),” adding: “He has ZERO integrity. Horrible human.”

“Musk” opens in theaters Oct. 9 from Bleecker Street.

title: Bowen Yang And Reece Weaver Extend Broadway Engagements In ‘Oh, Mary! And ‘Chicago’ Due To Popular Demand
summary: With their box office spiking, Bowen Yang and Reece Weaver have extended their Broadway runs in, respectively, Oh, Mary! and Chicago. Ticket sales have been very strong for both shows with the new, TV-famous cast members leading the way. Yang will extend his run as Mary Todd Lincoln in Cole Escola’s Tony Award-winning comedy through […]
content:
With their box office spiking, Bowen Yang and Reece Weaver have extended their Broadway runs in, respectively, Oh, Mary! and Chicago.

Ticket sales have been very strong for both shows with the new, TV-famous cast members leading the way.

Yang will extend his run as Mary Todd Lincoln in Cole Escola’s Tony Award-winning comedy through January 17, 2027 (his limited engagement had been set to end December 6). The ex-SNL player made his Broadway debut in the role on September 15. (Yang’s co-stars are Phillip James Brannon, Barrett Foa, Bianca Leigh and Tony Macht).

Weaver, best known for her breakout participation in Netflix’s reality show America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, will continue playing Chicago‘s Roxie Hart through Sunday, November 1. She had initially been scheduled through Sunday, October 18. She made her Broadway debut in the role on September 7.

Watch on Deadline

The current cast of Chicago also includes Lissa deGuzman, NaTasha Yvette Williams, Max von Essen, Red Concepción and J. Workman.

Oh, Mary!, which has been a strong Broadway draw since its opening in 2024, saw its biggest gross in months last week after Yang’s arrival: The show sold out and took in $1,517,701, it’s top draw this season other than the $1,576,984 gross when then-star Maya Rudolph neared the end of her popular engagement in the title role.

Likewise, Weaver’s first two weeks in Chicago were sell-outs, with grosses for her first week at $997,133 and her second week at $995,132. Those takes were by far the largest since May when Mormon Wives star Whitney Leavitt concluded her run as Roxie with a weekly gross of $1,688,129.

title: ‘The Beast In Me’ Renewed For Season 2 With Claire Danes Reprising Role; Howard Gordon Back With Netflix Overall Deal
summary: Aggie Wiggs may be writing a sequel to her The Beast In Me book. Netflix has ordered a second season of breakout limited series The Beast In Me, with Claire Danes back reprising her Emmy-nominated role and executive producing. Also returning are Season 1 writers/executive producers Howard Gordon and Daniel Pearle. Gordon, who served as […]
content:
Aggie Wiggs may be writing a sequel to her The Beast In Me book. Netflix has ordered a second season of breakout limited series The Beast In Me, with Claire Danes back reprising her Emmy-nominated role and executive producing. Also returning are Season 1 writers/executive producers Howard Gordon and Daniel Pearle.

Gordon, who served as showrunner, will share co-showrunner responsibilities with Pearle in Season 2. (He previously elevated Pearle to co-showrunner for Season 2 of his Fox’s series Accused.) Additionally, Gordon has signed an overall deal with Netflix to develop new series exclusively for the global streamer through his Teakwood Lane Productions banner.

The Beast In Me comes from an outside studio, 20th Television, where Gordon and Danes had deals stemming from their joint tenure on Homeland and Gordon’s on 24 before that.

Watch on Deadline

Gordon, Pearle and Danes will executive produce Season 2 alongside series creator Gabe Rotter and fellow Season 1 executive producers Antonio Campos, who directed half of the S1 episodes, Caroline Baron, Amy Lippman, Gabe Rotter, Conan O’Brien, David Kissinger, Jeff Ross and Jodie Foster.

This is the latest Netflix limited series to be extended following the success of its original installment. The Beast In Me follows the blueprint of Untamed, which also became a drama series with its lead character, played by Eric Bana, continuing his journey in a new location with a new story. Netflix took the anthology route with Beef, which came back for a second season featuring all new cast of characters with no ties to Season 1.

In an interview with Deadline at the time of The Beast In Me’s launch last November, Gordon left the door open to a followup.

“It was meant to be a limited series. It certainly is possible, because whoever is left standing at the end of this is still around, and I think if there’s a story, we’d be up for it,” Gordon said, adding, “I do think that there’s certainly room for another chapter.”

In a statement accompanying the Season 2 announcement, Gordon reflected on the decision to continue Aggie’s story, acknowledging Netflix Head of Scripted Series Jinny Howe and 20th Television President Karey Burke.

“We always told ourselves we’d only do a second season of The Beast in Me if we found a story that was worthy of the first – and I’m thrilled to say we found it,” he said. “We loved making this show and our audience seemed to love watching it, so we’re enormously grateful to Jinny Howe and Netflix, and to Karey Burke and 20th Television for giving us the chance to get the band back together and do it again.”

Season 1 of The Beast In Me followed the cat-and-mouse game between acclaimed author Aggie Wiggs (Danes), grieving the tragic death of her young son, and her charming and scary new neighbor Nile Sheldon (Rhys) who was the prime suspect in his first wife’s disappearance. The installment ended with Sheldon’s murder in prison, Aggie taking responsibilities for her actions and publishing her book The Beast In Me.

Conversations about a potential second season started shortly after The Beast in Me debuted at #1 in the Netflix Global Top 10 shows, reaching the top 10 in 88 countries, en route to garnering 43M views in its first seven weeks. The development process for the new installment is well underway, with casting for the new leads alongside Danes in advanced stages.

Since The Beast In Me‘s Season 2 renewal was not confirmed until now, the first season competed as a limited series throughout its awards run, including at the Emmys, where it earned nine nominations, including for Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series, Lead Actress In a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie (Danes) and Lead Actor (Rhys). It won two, for Lead Actor and Original Dramatic Score. Rhys became the first performer to win two lead acting categories in the same year (He also won the Lead Comedy Actor trophy for Apple TV’s Widow’s Bay) and the first with a career sweep of all three lead acting categories. (He previously won Lead Drama Actor for FX’s The Americans.)

“We are thrilled to bring back The Beast in Me and to welcome Howard Gordon to the Netflix family with this creative partnership,” Howe said. “The series captivated global audiences, delivered extraordinary performances led by Claire Danes, and earned Matthew Rhys a historic Emmy win. We are incredibly proud of what Howard Gordon, Gabe Rotter, and the entire cast and crew achieved. We can’t wait for audiences to see what Howard and Daniel Pearle have in store for the next season.”

With Season 2, The Beast In Me will transition to Drama Series awards contention, similar to HBO’s Big Little Lies and The While Lotus, which also made the switch after Season 1.

title: Santa Barbara Film Festival Awards: ‘Wild Horse Nine’ Star John Malkovich To Get Performer Of The Year Honor
summary: John Malkovich, a two-time Oscar nominee who won the Best Actor prize at this year’s Venice Film Festival for his work in Martin McDonagh’s upcoming Wild Horse Nine, has been selected to receive the Santa Barbara Film Festival’s Outstanding Performer of the Year Award. The honor will be bestowed during the 42nd annual SBIFF, which […]
content:
John Malkovich, a two-time Oscar nominee who won the Best Actor prize at this year’s Venice Film Festival for his work in Martin McDonagh’s upcoming Wild Horse Nine, has been selected to receive the Santa Barbara Film Festival‘s Outstanding Performer of the Year Award.

The honor will be bestowed during the 42nd annual SBIFF, which runs February 3-13, 2027.

Malkovich leads off the awards announcements from the fest, which has become a valued stop on the movie-awards circuit. Last year, Michael B. Jordan won the same award ahead of his eventual Best Actor Oscar win for Sinners.

Other SBIFF honorees in the category include Ralph Fiennes, Bradley Cooper, Cate Blanchett, Will Smith, Aunjanue Ellis, Sacha Baron Cohen, Adam Driver, Rami Malek, Margot Robbie and Allison Janney, Ryan Gosling and Emma Stone, Brie Larson and Saoirse Ronan, Steve Carell, Cate Blanchett, Jennifer Lawrence, Viola Davis, James Franco, Colin Firth, Penélope Cruz, Angelina Jolie, Helen Mirren, Heath Ledger, Kate Winslet and Charlize Theron.

Watch on Deadline

In the black comedy Wild Horse Nine, Malkovich stars with Sam Rockwell as a pair of CIA agents who travel from Santiago to Easter Island on the eve of the 1973 Chilean coup, confronting their dark pasts and becoming entangled in present-day conspiracies. The Searchlight Pictures pic hits theaters November 6.

“A legendary actor gives this year in Wild Horse Nine his best performance to date in which he combines pathos, volatility, vulnerability and tenderness,” SBIFF executive director Roger Durling said Thursday in a release announcing the award. “It’s a high-wire act that shows us what a commanding artist he is, and we are thrilled to be honoring him with our Outstanding Performer of the Year Award.”

title: New ‘Sesame Street’ Film In Works, More ‘Gabby’s  Dollhouse’, ‘Bad Dinosaurs’ In Netflix’s Kids Slate
summary: Netflix unveiled its preschool and kids slate Thursday, which includes more Sesame Street, a new Gabby’s Dollhouse series and more. The streamer revealed it is currently in development on a new Sesame Street film with Rideback and Sesame Workshop. No details were disclosed. The last Sesame Street feature film was The Adventures of Elmo in […]
content:
Netflix unveiled its preschool and kids slate Thursday, which includes more Sesame Street, a new Gabby’s Dollhouse series and more.

The streamer revealed it is currently in development on a new Sesame Street film with Rideback and Sesame Workshop. No details were disclosed. The last Sesame Street feature film was The Adventures of Elmo in Grouchland, which was released in October 1999. It was preceded by Sesame Street Presents: Follow That Bird, released in August 1985.

Netflix and Sesame Workshop also announced they’ve extended their deal on the series side, which will bring additional seasons of the show through Season 62. Season 57 Volume 4 premieres November 23 with Volumes 5 and 6 coming in 2027. The licensed CGI animated series Mecha Builders will premiere on October 26.

The world of Gabby’s Dollhouse also is expanding with new mixed-media companion series Doozie’s Doghouse, starring Gabby’s sister Doozie, premiering November 9. Gabby’s Dollhouse: Makers and Bakers premieres December 9 with four holiday episodes hosted by Laila Lockhart Kraner as Gabby and judges Aidy Bryant, Justin Willman and Melissa Villaseñor. It will continue with new episodes in 2027.

Watch on Deadline

Netflix announced new preschool series Puppy Pirates, from creator Matthew Fernandes. In it, four heroic hounds sail the high seas fetching whatever’s been lost — treasure, stuffies, you name it. Premiere date TBA. Additionally, Bad Dinosaurs, from creators Joel Veitch, Alex Mallinson and David Shute, has been renewed for seasons 2 and 3, with eight episodes each.

Three new games also are joining Netflix Playground’s library – Trash Truck, featuring Hank and the crew, launching October 27; Numberblocks: Hide and Seek, which tests kids’ counting skills, on September 29; and KPop Demon Hunters: Ready, Set, Shine also on September 29.

title: Zazie Beetz, Ben Foster, Stella Baker & John Hoogenakker Join Paramount+ Series ‘Discretion’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Zazie Beetz (Atlanta, Joker), Ben Foster (Hell or High Water, Emancipation), Stella Baker (Scarpetta, Tell Me Your Secrets) and John Hoogenakker (One Battle After Another, The Morning Show) have joined as recurring cast members of the new Paramount+ series, Discretion. Character descriptions are under wraps. They join the previously announced lead cast: Nicole Kidman, […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Zazie Beetz (Atlanta, Joker), Ben Foster (Hell or High Water, Emancipation), Stella Baker (Scarpetta, Tell Me Your Secrets) and John Hoogenakker (One Battle After Another, The Morning Show) have joined as recurring cast members of the new Paramount+ series, Discretion. Character descriptions are under wraps.

They join the previously announced lead cast: Nicole Kidman, Elle Fanning, Josh Lucas, Colton Ryan, and Stephan James. Production is currently underway with an expected premiere in 2027.

The eight-episode legal thriller, adapted from bestselling author Chandler Baker’s short story, Discretion, is a legal thriller about a summer associate, Lenny (Fanning), at a prestigious Dallas law firm who uncovers a web of NDAs masking a dark truth. When she realizes she signed the same agreement, her discoveries put her in the crosshairs of the firm’s most powerful female partner, Sharon (Kidman)—upending their mentor-protégé dynamic and raising the question: who gets to keep secrets, and at what cost?

The series is executive produced and written by Baker and executive produced by Susannah Grant. Kidman and Per Saari (Blossom Films), Elle Fanning, Dakota Fanning and Brittany Kahan Ward (Lewellen Pictures), Joe Hipps (Cut To) and Jordan Cerf (Linden Entertainment) also serve as executive producers along with A24. Matt Shakman, who also serves as executive producer, will direct the first four episodes.

Watch on Deadline

Beetz is repped by WME, Entertainment 360, and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern. Foster is repped by Range Media Partners and Toczek Suddleson Law Group. Baker is repped by Gersh, Untitled Entertainment, and United Management (Aus). Hoogenakker is repped by Industry Entertainment, Paradigm, and Hanson Jacobson.

title: ‘Avengers: Endgame Encore’ Adds 4 New Scenes Tying to ‘Doomsday’: [SPOILER] Fights Doctor Doom, [SPOILER] Travels to the Past and the Multiverse Collapses
summary: SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for “Avengers: Endgame Encore,” now playing in theaters. In the lead-up to “Avengers: Doomsday,” Marvel has re-released “Avengers: Endgame” in theaters with four brand new scenes that tie directly into the sprawling team-up film releasing on Dec. 18. Retitled “Avengers: Endgame Encore,” this slightly longer version of the 2019 […]
content:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for “Avengers: Endgame Encore,” now playing in theaters.

In the lead-up to “Avengers: Doomsday,” Marvel has re-released “Avengers: Endgame” in theaters with four brand new scenes that tie directly into the sprawling team-up film releasing on Dec. 18. Retitled “Avengers: Endgame Encore,” this slightly longer version of the 2019 blockbuster adds four minutes of new footage with characters like Robert Downey Jr.’s mega-villain Doctor Doom, Tom Hiddleston’s Loki and Mark Ruffalo’s Bruce Banner to the already jam-packed movie.

Marvel started building the hype for “Doomsday” a year ahead of its release with four short teasers attached to last year’s “Avatar: Fire and Ash.” The first revealed that Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) and Peggy Carter (Hayley Atwell) have a son; the second focused on Thor (Chris Hemsworth) and his adopted daughter; the third showed Prof. Xavier (Patrick Stewart), Magneto (Ian McKellen) and Cyclops (James Marsden) from Fox’s “X-Men” universe crossing into the MCU; and the fourth brought together Black Panther (Letitia Wright) and the Wakandans with the Fantastic Four, who traveled from their universe.

Popular on Variety

These new “Endgame Encore” scenes were shot during “Doomsday” production and added to the re-release to bridge the two massive “Avengers” stories. The first scene takes place during Steve and Peggy’s dance in the closing of “Endgame.” As fans saw in the original movie, Steve has hung up his Captain America costume, passed the star-spangled shield down to Sam Wilson (Anthony Mackie) and finally settled down with his long-lost love Peggy after traveling back in time. But now, they get a surprising knock at their door from none other than the Norse trickster god, Loki. The last time we saw the reformed villain was in the finale of “Loki” Season 2, where he resigned himself to holding up the entire multiverse for the rest of time. But before that, it seems that Loki, in his Time Variance Authority uniform, pays Steve and Peggy a visit, perhaps to discuss how they’ve created an unstable branch in the multiverse with Steve’s time travel.

“Loki” gets another look with a fellow scene that takes place in the Time Variance Authority with Mobius (Owen Wilson), Casey (Eugene Cordero), Ouroboros (Ke Huy Quan) and Miss Minutes (Tara Strong). They notice that two Earths are about to collide in an incursion and begin firing on each other. More alternate worlds start colliding and terminating, and it’s revealed that the entire multiverse is collapsing. Could those two Earths be Fox’s “X-Men” universe and the mainline MCU world? We already know that Prof. Xavier, Magneto, Cyclops, Mystique (Rebecca Romijn), Nightcrawler (Alan Cumming) and Gambit (Channing Tatum) will cross into the MCU, so this may set up their clash with the Avengers that was teased in the “Doomsday” trailer.

Another new scene with Bruce Banner pops up during the credits and takes place after he’s apprehended in “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” In this summer’s record-breaking blockbuster, Bruce loses control and is unable to stop from transforming into the Hulk when his mind is controlled by Jean Grey (Sadie Sink). Spider-Man (Tom Holland) beats the super-strong, green giant, and Bruce is taken to a secure medical facility. In the new “Endgame Encore” credits scene, Bruce is in an underground bunker tinkering on a serum to suppress his Hulking out. All of a sudden, Doctor Doom breaks into Bruce’s facility and Bruce turns into the roaring Hulk to face him, but we don’t see what happens next. Does this mean Bruce and/or Hulk will reappear in “Doomsday, and will he be under Doctor Doom’s control?

The final new scene appears at the very end of the credits, when the original “Endgame” had a mysterious, metal-clanging sound in the closing moments. When “Endgame” first released, diehard fans realized that the noise was from “Iron Man” when Downey Jr. was forging his powerful suit of armor. Now, we see a flashes of Doctor Doom making his metal mask with the same sound being played. It’s a dark twist and seems to hint that Doom and Iron Man, while both played by Downey Jr., may also have their origins mirrored.

“Avengers: Doomsday” hits theaters on Dec. 18 — the same day as “Dune: Part 3,” setting up a “Dunesday” showdown. With all of the new scenes, advance teasers and year-long countdown clock, Marvel and Disney are hoping “Doomsday” ends up being another smash hit in the wake of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s” record-setting run.

title: Letterboxd Suitors Include A24 and New York Times; Sale Could Value Social Movie Platform at $300 Million: Report
summary: A bidding war may be in full flower for Letterboxd, the popular film-reviews and social service that has been fielding inbound acquisition offers for several months. Indie studio A24 and the New York Times are the latest to express an interest in buying Letterboxd, according to a New York Times report citing anonymous sources. Any […]
content:
A bidding war may be in full flower for Letterboxd, the popular film-reviews and social service that has been fielding inbound acquisition offers for several months.

Indie studio A24 and the New York Times are the latest to express an interest in buying Letterboxd, according to a New York Times report citing anonymous sources. Any deal is “expected to value Letterboxd at more than $300 million,” per the report. That would be about 20 times its projected earnings in 2026 of roughly $15 million, according to the Times.

There’s been broad interest in Letterboxd: Those said to have explored a possible acquisition include Netflix, Sony Pictures Entertainment, Paramount Skydance, private-equity giant TPG and Reddit co-creator Alexis Ohanian.

Popular on Variety

Asked for comment, Katie Hill, the New York Times’ SVP, global head of communications and external affairs, said, “The company regularly reviews potential investments, and it’s our policy not to comment on speculation about potential acquisitions or divestitures.”

A24 declined to comment. Reps for Letterboxd did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

If a studio or streamer acquired Letterboxd, it would introduce at least the perception of a conflict of interest, as users might wonder if such an owner would favor its own titles on the service. Rotten Tomatoes was part of NBCUniversal for years, raising questions of its independence from the entertainment division. (Rotten Tomatoes is now part of Versant Media, which spun off from NBCU earlier this year.)

In a statement in July, a Letterboxd spokesperson said about reports of potential buyers: “As Letterboxd has grown, it’s natural there will be interest in what we do next. There’s nothing specific for us to share at this time. Any decision about Letterboxd’s future would involve the founders.”

Letterboxd, founded in 2011 and based in New Zealand, has been shopping itself to interested parties in recent months. It is majority-owned by Canadian holding company Tiny, which acquired a 60% stake in Letterboxd in 2023 at a valuation of $50 million-$60 million. Letterboxd co-founders Matthew Buchanan and Karl von Randow own the remaining 40% share.

Letterboxd has more than 30 million members globally and serves a passionate base of movie lovers. The company also has launched an online video-rental service stocked with indie films including previously unreleased titles.

title: Tamera Mowry-Housley Joins ‘Scrubs’ Reboot Season 2
summary: Tamera Mowry-Housley is checking into Season 2 of the “Scrubs” reboot. The “Sister, Sister” and “Twitches” star has boarded the ABC sitcom as a guest star. She will play Dr. Steffie, a pediatric doctor who tries to persuade Tosh (Ava Bunn) to choose peds as her specialty. Season 2 premieres with two episodes on Wednesday, […]
content:
Tamera Mowry-Housley is checking into Season 2 of the “Scrubs” reboot.

The “Sister, Sister” and “Twitches” star has boarded the ABC sitcom as a guest star. She will play Dr. Steffie, a pediatric doctor who tries to persuade Tosh (Ava Bunn) to choose peds as her specialty. Season 2 premieres with two episodes on Wednesday, Sept. 30, at 8 p.m. on ABC. Episodes stream on Hulu and Disney+ the next day.

Mowry-Housley joins the 30-minute revival comedy alongside Zach Braff as John “J.D.” Dorian, Donald Faison as Christopher Turk, Sarah Chalke as Elliot Reid and Ava Bunn as Sam Tosh.

Popular on Variety

The second iteration of the series finds J.D., Turk and Elliot after they’ve leveled up from interns to icons at Sacred Heart. Per the logline, “Now, the respected doctors inspire the next generation while balancing the ups and downs of working in a hospital. Together with characters new and old, they are navigating this next chapter with laughter, heart and some surprises along the way.”

Bill Lawrence of Doozer Productions created the original series and serves as executive producer of the reboot alongside Jeff Ingold and Liza Katzer also of Doozer Productions. Braff, Faison and Chalke star and executive produce. Aseem Batra serves as executive producer and showrunner; Mike Royce, Mathew Harawitz, Randall Keenan Winston and Michael Spiller also executive produce.
